### E2E-TPL-02 · A template built in the editor is saved with its sections, {{variables}} (key, type, label, required), contract type and publish state

**Covers:** `/templates` · `POST /templates`, `GET /templates/:id` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in as counsel-a on `/templates`. No template named "QA Services Agreement".

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click **New Template**. | A full-screen dialog "New Template": at the top a **Published** checkbox (unchecked), **Save Template** (disabled) and an X. Left: "Template Name *" (placeholder "e.g. Mutual NDA — Standard"), "Description", "Contract Type" showing "Generic (all types)"; "Sections" with **+ Add** and one entry "Section 1"; "Variables" with **+ Add**. Right: the section title "Section 1" and an empty editor. No **Preview** button (a new template has nothing saved to preview). |
| 2 | Name `QA Services Agreement`; Description `QA fixture: services with an annual fee`; Contract Type **MSA**. | **Save Template** becomes enabled. |
| 3 | Change the section title to `Parties`. In the editor type: `This Services Agreement is made between {{customer_name}} and {{provider_name}}, effective {{effective_date}}.` | The Sections list now reads "Parties". |
| 4 | Sections → **+ Add**. | "Section 2" is added and selected (dark). Known bug: the editor still shows the Parties text. Select all in the editor (Cmd/Ctrl+A) and delete it, then title the section `Fees` and type `The Customer pays {{fee_amount}} per year. {{payment_terms}}` |
| 5 | Click "Parties", then "Fees", in the Sections list. | The editor switches to each section's own text. |
| 6 | Variables → **+ Add** four times and fill: `customer_name` / text / `Customer name` / **Req.** ticked; `provider_name` / text / `Provider name` / Req. ticked; `effective_date` / date / `Effective date` / Req. ticked; `fee_amount` / number / `Annual fee` / Req. not ticked. Leave `payment_terms` undeclared. | Each row: a key box ("variable_key"), a type list (text, number, date, boolean, select), a label box ("Display label"), **Req.** and an X that removes the row. In a fifth row, typing `Fee Amount` in the key box shows `_ee__mount`: every character other than a–z, 0–9 and _ becomes "_" (Known limits). Remove that fifth row with its X. |
| 7 | Tick **Published**. Click **Save Template**. | A spinner, then the dialog closes. A new card "QA Services Agreement": "MSA", "Published", "v1 · 2 sections · 4 variables · updated today". |
| 8 | Run command A. | The saved template: contractType "MSA", isPublished true, version 1, usageCount 0; the 4 variables with their labels, types and `required` true/true/true/false; sections "Parties" (sortOrder 0) and "Fees" (1) with your text and `{{…}}` tokens, `clauseRefs: []`, `conditionalLogic: null`. |

Command A:
```bash
export T_QA=$(tid "QA Services Agreement")
curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{name, description, contractType, isPublished, version, usageCount, variables, sections: [.sections[] | {title, sortOrder, content, clauseRefs, conditionalLogic}]}'
```
Command B (validation):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA bad key","variables":[{"key":"Fee","label":"Fee","type":"text"}]}' | jq '{status, detail, first: .errors[0].message}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA bad type","variables":[{"key":"fee","label":"Fee","type":"string"}]}' | jq '{status, path: .errors[0].path}'
```

**Also check**
- **Save Template** stays disabled while "Template Name *" is empty.
- A variable row left with an empty key or label, or a key starting with a digit or "_": **Save Template** does nothing
  visible and the dialog stays open (defect: no message). The request answers 422 "Request body failed validation".
- Command B: `{"status":422,"detail":"Request body failed validation","first":"Variable key must be snake_case"}`, then
  `{"status":422,"path":["variables",0,"type"]}`. Nothing is created.
- The X closes the builder without asking and discards what you typed.
- contracts-a (edit but no create) and viewer-a: **Save Template** does nothing visible (TPL-09).

**Known limits**
- There is no Duplicate, in the UI or the API. To copy a template, GET it and POST its name (changed), description,
  contractType, variables and sections; this fails with 422 for the seeded and pack templates (TPL-04, step 9).
- The builder can't delete or reorder sections, set a variable's default value or a select's options, set a section's
  condition, or reference a library clause. These are API-only: TPL-05, TPL-06 and CLS-04.
- **Req.** is only a label: nothing checks that required variables are filled (TPL-05 step 8).

### E2E-TPL-03 · The section editor's tools work while writing a template: formatting, clause insert, find and replace, AI suggestions and export

**Covers:** `/templates` · (from the editor: `GET /clauses`, `POST /agent/assist`, `POST /agent/complete`, `POST /contracts/export`) · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key for steps 7–9; Gotenberg (part of the stack) for step 10 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$T_QA` from TPL-02. You will close the builder without saving at the end, so the fixture doesn't change.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open "QA Services Agreement" (click its title) and select "Fees". | The editor toolbar, by hover title: Undo, Redo, Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3, Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough, Align Left, Align Center, Align Right, Bullet List, Numbered List, Insert Table, Clause Library, Find & Replace, the AI group (✏️ Rewrite, 🧹 Simplify, 🔍 Expand, ⚖️ Check Compliance, 🔄 Suggest Alternative), **Doc AI ▾**, Export PDF, Export DOCX, and "N words" at the end. There is no **Save Draft** in the template builder. |
| 2 | Select "per year" and click Bold; put the cursor on the text and click Heading 2; click Undo twice. | Bold, then a heading, then both undone. |
| 3 | Click Insert Table. | A 3 × 3 table with a header row is inserted. Undo removes it. |
| 4 | Click Find & Replace. | A bar with "Find...", "Replace...", **Find**, **Replace All** and an X. Enter `Customer` / `Client`, click **Replace All**: every "Customer" in this section becomes "Client". One Undo reverts all of them. Close the bar. |
| 5 | Click Clause Library. | A right panel "Clause Library" with "Search clauses..." and up to 30 clauses, each with its category and rating. Type `carve`: "Excluded Claims (Carve-Outs)" is listed. Click it: its text is inserted at the cursor and the panel closes. (CLS-04 tests this in depth.) |
| 6 | Pause typing for a second after a word. | A grey suggestion may appear after the cursor (ghost completion). Tab accepts it; Esc or any other key dismisses it. |
| 7 | Select a sentence and click ✏️ Rewrite. | "Thinking…", then a banner "AI Suggestion" with the original struck out, the proposed text and an explanation, and **Apply** / **Dismiss**. **Apply** replaces the selection and briefly highlights it. With nothing selected, the button shows the tip "Select text first" for about 2 s. |
| 8 | Stop the agents service and click ✏️ Rewrite on a selection. | A red bar "AI request failed — please try again." (or the server's reason) for about 4 s. Start the agents service again. |
| 9 | Click **Doc AI ▾**. | A menu: "✨ Fix Layout" / "Clean up PDF extraction artifacts" and "📝 Rewrite Document" / "AI rewrites full document". Rewrite Document opens "Rewrite entire document?" with **Cancel** / **Rewrite**. After a rewrite, an amber bar says "Doc AI updated the document — click **Save Draft** to keep the changes." (there is no Save Draft here; the template saves with **Save Template**: wording defect). |
| 10 | Click Export PDF, then Export DOCX. | The browser saves `contract.pdf` and `contract.docx` holding this section's text only. With Gotenberg stopped, Export PDF shows a red bar "Could not export as PDF: …" with **Dismiss**. |
| 11 | On a window at least 1024 px wide, add a Heading 2 line. | A "Sections" outline appears left of the editor listing this section's own H2/H3 headings; clicking one scrolls to it. |
| 12 | Close the builder with the X. Reopen "QA Services Agreement". | Nothing from this journey was saved: the Fees text is as in TPL-02. |

**Also check**
- viewer-a can use every tool here (they only need view permissions); only saving is refused (TPL-09).

**Known limits**
- Export and AI act on the selected section's text, not the whole template.

### E2E-TPL-04 · Editing a template saves its details and sections, bumps its version, and publishing decides whether anyone can draft from it

**Covers:** `/templates` · `PATCH /templates/:id`, `PUT /templates/:id/sections`, `GET /templates/:id`, `GET /templates` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, contracts-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$T_QA` from TPL-02, published. Open DevTools → Network before step 2.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click the title "QA Services Agreement". | "Edit Template" with every field filled in, **Published** ticked, sections "Parties" and "Fees", the 4 variables, and a **Preview** button (it previews the saved template, not unsaved changes). |
| 2 | Description → `QA fixture v2`; untick **Published**; at the end of the "Fees" text add ` Fees are due annually in advance.`; click **Save Template**. | Intended: the dialog closes; the card shows "Draft — not usable yet" and "v3 · 2 sections · 4 variables" (one save sends two requests, each adds 1 to the version). Network shows `PATCH /templates/<id>` → 200 and `PUT /templates/<id>/sections` → 200, sent in parallel; the sections request carries `"conditionalLogic": null` for a section with no condition, which is stored as no condition. After a reload the added sentence is there. |
| 3 | Close the dialog, reload `/templates`, set **All Status** → **Draft**. | "QA Services Agreement" is listed as "Draft — not usable yet". |
| 4 | Left rail → Contracts → **Draft new**. | The "Select Template" picker does not list "QA Services Agreement": only published templates can be drafted from. Close it. |
| 5 | Run command A (publish again through the API). Reload `/templates`. | `{"isPublished":true,"version":<one more>}`. The card shows "Published". |
| 6 | Run command B (replace the sections through the API, back to TPL-02's text). | 200 with the two sections (new ids, sortOrder 0 and 1) and the version one higher. |
| 7 | Run command C. | A blank name: 422, `path` `["name"]`. The seeded Mutual NDA sent back with its own variables: 422, messages including "Variable key must be snake_case" (its keys are camelCase, its types "string"/"enum", some defaults numbers). |
| 8 | Run command D. | `PUT …/sections` with `{}`: 500 (the route validates nothing; defect). |
| 9 | Open "Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement", untick **Published**, click **Save Template**. | Nothing visible changes and the dialog stays open: the PATCH is refused with 422 as in step 7. Seeded and pack templates can't be saved from the builder (defect). Close the dialog without saving. |
| 10 | Change a seeded template's publish state alone through the API: `curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$M_NDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"isPublished":false}' \| jq .isPublished`, then the same with `true`. | `false`, then `true`: a body without `variables` passes. |
| 11 | As contracts-a (edit, no create): open "QA Services Agreement", change the description, **Save Template**. | The PATCH is accepted (200); the sections request behaves as in step 2. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"isPublished":true}' | jq '{isPublished, version}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X PUT "$API/templates/$T_QA/sections" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"sections":[
 {"title":"Parties","content":"<p>This Services Agreement is made between {{customer_name}} and {{provider_name}}, effective {{effective_date}}.</p>"},
 {"title":"Fees","content":"<p>The Customer pays {{fee_amount}} per year. {{payment_terms}}</p>"}]}'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":""}' | jq '{status, path: .errors[0].path}'
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$M_NDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "$(curl -s "$API/templates/$M_NDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -c '{name, variables}')" | jq '{status, messages: ([.errors[].message] | unique)}'
```
Command D:
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X PUT "$API/templates/$T_QA/sections" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

**Also check**
- rep-a, procurement-a and viewer-a: **Save Template** does nothing visible; the API answers 403 `Missing permission: edit:template`.
- `PATCH` with a `sections` field ignores it (200, sections unchanged): sections change only through `PUT …/sections`.
- Editing a template never changes contracts already drafted from it (their text is stored on the contract).

**Known limits**
- One builder save raises the version by two.
- A template's Preview (card or builder) can show the rendering from before your edit for up to 5 minutes: reload the
  page before previewing an edited template (defect: the preview isn't refreshed on save).
- The Assistant drafts from the most recently updated published template of a type, so even toggling **Published** on
  an older template makes it the one used (DRAFT-03).
- Template edits write no audit-log entry.

### E2E-TPL-05 · Preview fills variables with samples or defaults, generate fills your values and marks blanks as [[key]], and only generating counts as a use

**Covers:** `/templates` · `POST /templates/:id/preview`, `POST /templates/:id/generate`, `PATCH /templates/:id` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** nothing extra (no model) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `$T_QA` published, sections as in TPL-02 (TPL-04 command B restores them). Reload `/templates`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click the eye (Preview) on "QA Services Agreement". | A dialog "Template Preview (Sample Data)" ("Loading preview..." first): heading "Parties", "This Services Agreement is made between [customer_name] and [provider_name], effective <today as YYYY-MM-DD>."; heading "Fees", "The Customer pays 100000 per year. [[payment_terms]]". Samples: text → `[key]`, number → 100000, date → today, boolean → true, select → `[key]`. The undeclared `payment_terms` shows as `[[payment_terms]]`, as plain text (no highlight; Known limits). Esc or a click outside closes it. |
| 2 | Run command A. | `{"isSample":true,"sectionsIncluded":2,"sectionsExcluded":0,"unfilledVariables":["payment_terms"]}`; the override prints `between Preview Co and [provider_name]`; usageCount 0 — previews don't count. |
| 3 | Run command B (declare defaults: `fee_amount` 25000 and `payment_terms` "Net 30"; API only). Reload, Preview again. | "The Customer pays 25000 per year. Net 30". The card reads "5 variables". |
| 4 | Run command C (generate with three values). | `sectionsIncluded` 2 and `unfilledVariables` `["fee_amount","payment_terms"]`: generate does **not** apply declared defaults. The HTML has "between Acme Corp and Demo Org, Inc., effective 2026-10-01" and `<span class="template-variable-unfilled" data-key="fee_amount">[[fee_amount]]</span>`. |
| 5 | Reload `/templates`. | The card shows "Used 1 time". With **Most used** sort it comes before templates with no use. |
| 6 | Run command D (four more generates). Reload. | usageCount 5; the card shows "Used 5 times" and the pill "★ Most used" (hover: "Used 5 times — frequently used template"). |
| 7 | As viewer-a, preview "QA Services Agreement" in the UI, and run `code -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'`. | Preview works. Generate answers 200 and adds a use (Known limits). |
| 8 | Generate with `{}` (as in command D). | 200; every variable left as `[[key]]`: required variables are not enforced. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq -c '{isSample, sectionsIncluded, sectionsExcluded, unfilledVariables}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"variables":{"customer_name":"Preview Co"}}' | jq -r .html | grep -o 'between [^,]*'
curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .usageCount
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"variables":[
 {"key":"customer_name","label":"Customer name","type":"text","required":true},
 {"key":"provider_name","label":"Provider name","type":"text","required":true},
 {"key":"effective_date","label":"Effective date","type":"date","required":true},
 {"key":"fee_amount","label":"Annual fee","type":"number","defaultValue":"25000"},
 {"key":"payment_terms","label":"Payment terms","type":"text","defaultValue":"Net 30"}]}' | jq -c '[.variables[] | {key, defaultValue}]'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"variables":{"customer_name":"Acme Corp","provider_name":"Demo Org, Inc.","effective_date":"2026-10-01"}}' | jq '{sectionsIncluded, unfilledVariables, html}'
```
Command D:
```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'; done
curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .usageCount
```

**Also check**
- finance-a: preview and generate answer 403 `Missing permission: view:template`.
- Another org's or a deleted template's id: 404 `{"detail":"Template not found"}` (TPL-08, TPL-09).

**Known limits**
- Declared defaults are used by Preview and by the Assistant's drafting plan (DRAFT-03), not by generate and not by
  **Draft new** (there the model decides; DRAFT-01).
- "Used N times" counts generate calls: **Draft new**, the Assistant's Apply and direct API calls, including a viewer's.
  Previews and the Assistant's planning don't count; Undo doesn't subtract.
- Blanks (`[[key]]`) are not highlighted anywhere: the only style for them is inside the section editor, which never
  receives them (defect).

### E2E-TPL-06 · Conditional sections are included or left out by their rule (API)

**Covers:** `/templates` · `POST /templates`, `PUT /templates/:id/sections`, `POST /templates/:id/preview`, `POST /templates/:id/generate` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra (no model) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- None. Conditions exist only in the API: the builder neither shows nor edits them.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run command A (create "QA Conditional Terms"). Reload `/templates`. | An id is printed. The card: "MSA", "Draft — not usable yet", "v1 · 5 sections · 4 variables". |
| 2 | Run command B (preview with samples). | `{"sectionsIncluded":4,"sectionsExcluded":1}` and titles Parties, Service levels, Large deal terms, EU data. Samples make `include_sla` true, `fee` 100000 (≥ 100000) and `region` "EU" (its default); `special_terms` is not declared, so "Special terms" (`not_empty`) is left out. |
| 3 | Run command C (preview with your values). | `{"sectionsIncluded":2,"sectionsExcluded":3}`: Parties and Special terms ("Net 45 payment."). |
| 4 | Run command D (generate with only a name). | `{"sectionsIncluded":1,"sectionsExcluded":4}`: only Parties. Generate uses no samples or defaults, so `region` is empty and "EU data" drops out. |
| 5 | Run command E (replace the sections; every section has a condition). | 200, two sections. Generating with `{"customer_name":"ACME Ltd"}` includes both: `contains` ignores case, and `empty` is true for an unset `region`. |
| 6 | Run command F (replace with one section that has no condition). | 200, and the template now has the one section, with no condition. |
| 7 | Run command G (an unknown operator on create). | 422 "Request body failed validation"; nothing created. |

Command A:
```bash
export T_COND=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
 "name":"QA Conditional Terms","contractType":"MSA","isPublished":false,
 "variables":[{"key":"customer_name","label":"Customer name","type":"text","required":true},
  {"key":"include_sla","label":"Include SLA","type":"boolean"},
  {"key":"fee","label":"Annual fee","type":"number"},
  {"key":"region","label":"Region","type":"select","options":["EU","US"],"defaultValue":"EU"}],
 "sections":[{"title":"Parties","content":"<p>Services for {{customer_name}}.</p>"},
  {"title":"Service levels","content":"<p>99.9% monthly uptime.</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"include_sla","operator":"eq","value":true}},
  {"title":"Large deal terms","content":"<p>Quarterly business reviews.</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"fee","operator":"gte","value":100000}},
  {"title":"EU data","content":"<p>Customer data stays in the EU.</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"region","operator":"eq","value":"EU"}},
  {"title":"Special terms","content":"<p>{{special_terms}}</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"special_terms","operator":"not_empty"}}]}' | jq -r .id); echo $T_COND
```
Commands B–D (`sec` prints the counts and the included section titles):
```bash
sec() { jq -r '"included \(.sectionsIncluded) excluded \(.sectionsExcluded)", (.html | scan("section-title\">([^<]*)") | .[0])'; }
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_COND/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | sec
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_COND/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"variables":{"include_sla":false,"fee":5000,"region":"US","special_terms":"Net 45 payment."}}' | sec
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_COND/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"variables":{"customer_name":"Acme"}}' | sec
```
Command E:
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X PUT "$API/templates/$T_COND/sections" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"sections":[
 {"title":"Parties","content":"<p>Services for {{customer_name}}.</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"customer_name","operator":"contains","value":"acme"}},
 {"title":"No region","content":"<p>Region to be agreed.</p>","conditionalLogic":{"field":"region","operator":"empty"}}]}' | tail -1
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_COND/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"variables":{"customer_name":"ACME Ltd"}}' | sec
```
Command F:
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X PUT "$API/templates/$T_COND/sections" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"sections":[{"title":"Always","content":"<p>Always here.</p>"}]}' | tail -1
```
Command G:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA bad rule","sections":[{"title":"x","conditionalLogic":{"field":"fee","operator":"between","value":1}}]}' | jq '{status, detail}'
```

**Also check**
- The other operators behave as named: `neq`, `gt`, `lt`, `lte` compare numbers (`gt`/`lt`/`lte`) or text (`neq`).
- Opening "QA Conditional Terms" in the builder and saving sends its conditions back unchanged.

**Known limits**
- A condition sees only the values given (generate) or the preview samples; declared defaults count in Preview only.
- A section whose condition can't be read is included.

### E2E-TPL-07 · A Word .docx becomes an unpublished template split on its headings, and bad files are refused with a reason

**Covers:** `/templates` · `POST /templates/upload` · docs/38: TC-DOC-07 (P4, N4–N6), TC-DOC-08 (N6)
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Files: `D-NDA.docx` and `D-MSA.pdf` (§0), plus these, made in Word or Google Docs and saved as .docx:
  - `D-TPL.docx`: a normal paragraph "This template is for QA."; then "Definitions" in the Heading 1 style, followed by
    "Terms have their usual meaning."; then "Payment" in the Heading 2 style, followed by
    "The Customer pays {{fee}} within 30 days."
  - `D-EMPTY.docx`: an empty document. `D-ZIP.docx`: any .zip file renamed to .docx.
  - Optional: `D-BIG.docx`, a .docx over 10 MB (paste in several large photos).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `/templates` → **Upload .docx** → pick `D-TPL.docx`. | The button reads "Converting…" with a spinner, then the builder opens as "Edit Template": name "D TPL" (the file name, dashes and underscores made spaces), Contract Type "Generic (all types)", **Published** unticked, sections "D TPL" (the text before the first heading), "Definitions" and "Payment". Each heading became its section's title and is not repeated in the text. No variables. |
| 2 | Close the builder (X). | Card "D TPL": "Draft — not usable yet", "v1 · 3 sections · 0 variables". |
| 3 | Preview "D TPL". | "Payment" reads "The Customer pays [[fee]] within 30 days.": upload doesn't declare the `{{fee}}` it finds (Known limits). |
| 4 | Upload `D-NDA.docx`. | A template "D NDA", unpublished. If the document uses Word heading styles, one section per heading; if not, one section titled "D NDA" holding the whole text. Close the builder. |
| 5 | Upload `D-MSA.pdf` (switch the file picker to all files). | A red bar under the page header: "Only .docx files can be converted into a template. Save your document as .docx and try again." No template. |
| 6 | Upload `D-ZIP.docx`. | The bar reads "Could not read that .docx — it may be corrupted or password-protected." |
| 7 | Upload `D-EMPTY.docx`. | "That document appears to be empty — there is nothing to turn into a template." |
| 8 | Upload `D-BIG.docx` (optional). | "File too large (10MB limit)". |
| 9 | Run command A (name, description and type are API-only fields; and a request without a file). | 201: name "QA Uploaded MSA", contractType "MSA", isPublished false, section titles as in step 1 (the first titled "QA Uploaded MSA"). Then 400 `{"detail":"No file uploaded"}`. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@D-TPL.docx" -F "name=QA Uploaded MSA" \
  -F "contractType=MSA" -F "description=From Word" | jq '{name, contractType, isPublished, sections: [.sections[].title]}'
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/templates/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "name=x"
```

**Also check**
- As viewer-a (also contracts-a, rep-a): **Upload .docx** → pick a file → the red bar reads "You don't have permission to
  create templates." and no request is sent. The API answers 403 `Missing permission: create:template` (TC-DOC-07 N6).
- A DOCX that inflates past 100 MB is refused quickly with the "Could not read that .docx…" message (TC-DOC-08 N6).
- Uploading the same file twice makes two templates.

**Known limits**
- Only .docx. Only Heading 1 and Heading 2 split sections; lower headings stay inside a section.
- `{{tokens}}` in the document are not declared as variables: add them in the builder.
- Saving the builder after an upload hits the section-save issue in TPL-04 step 2.

### E2E-TPL-08 · Deleting a template takes it out of the library and out of drafting, and leaves contracts already drafted from it

**Covers:** `/templates` · `DELETE /templates/:id`, `GET /templates/:id`, `GET /templates` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, legalops-a · **Needs:** nothing extra (no model) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- "D TPL" and "D NDA" from TPL-07. Run command A as legalops-a: it drafts a contract from "D NDA" through the Assistant's
  Apply call (no model needed; Apply doesn't check the publish state, DRAFT-03) and exports `$C_DEL`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a (LEGAL_COUNSEL: no delete:template), click the trash on "D TPL". | A dialog "Delete this template?" with "D TPL will no longer be available for drafting. Contracts already drafted from it are unaffected. This can't be undone." and **Cancel** / **Delete template**. |
| 2 | Click **Delete template**. | Nothing happens and the dialog stays open: the browser refuses the request, with no message (defect). `code -X DELETE "$API/templates/$(tid 'D TPL')" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` → 403. Click **Cancel**. |
| 3 | Sign in as legalops-a. Trash on "D NDA": press Esc; open it again and click outside; open it again and click **Delete template**. | Esc and the outside click close the dialog. **Delete template** shows a spinner, the dialog closes, the card is gone and the count drops by one. |
| 4 | Run command B. | 404 `{"detail":"Template not found"}` for GET and for a second DELETE; the list no longer has "D NDA". |
| 5 | Run command C. | The contract drafted before the delete still opens: status "DRAFT", its text intact. |
| 6 | Run command D. | The drafting planner refuses the deleted id: 404 `{"error":"TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND",…}`. |

Command A (as legalops-a; uses §3's `draftapply`):
```bash
export T_DNDA=$(tid "D NDA")
R=$(draftapply $LEGALOPS_A '{"templateId":"'$T_DNDA'","variables":{},"title":"QA drafted from D NDA"}'); echo "$R" | jq -c '{ok, contractId: .result.contractId}'
export C_DEL=$(echo "$R" | jq -r .result.contractId)
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/templates/$T_DNDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/templates/$T_DNDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
curl -s "$API/templates?q=D%20NDA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A" | jq '[.data[].name]'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_DEL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A" | jq '{title, status, text: .versions[0].plainText[0:80]}'
```
Command D:
```bash
tj contract_draft '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","userMessage":"nda","templateId":"'$T_DNDA'"}' | jq -c '{error, detail}'
```

**Also check**
- A deleted template's name still counts for re-seeding: a pack or standard-library install never adds a template back
  whose name matches a deleted one (PACK-01 step 9).

**Known limits**
- The delete is permanent from the product's side: no restore in the UI or the API.
- Template deletes write no audit-log entry.

### E2E-TPL-09 · Each role gets exactly its template rights, and Org B can't see or change Org A's templates

**Covers:** `/templates` · `GET /templates`, `POST /templates`, `PATCH /templates/:id`, `DELETE /templates/:id`, `POST /templates/:id/preview` (and by the same permissions `PUT /templates/:id/sections`, `POST /templates/:id/generate`, `POST /templates/upload`) · docs/38: —
**Roles:** all Org A accounts, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$T_QA` from TPL-02. Define command A. It probes each permission with requests that change nothing: an allowed create
  fails validation (422), an allowed edit, delete or preview finds no template (404), a refused one answers 403.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run `tplperm` for each token. | admin-a `view 200 create 422 edit 404 delete 404 preview 404`; counsel-a `200 422 404 403 404`; legalops-a `200 422 404 404 404`; contracts-a `200 403 404 403 404`; rep-a, procurement-a and viewer-a `200 403 403 403 404`; finance-a and approver-a `403 403 403 403 403`. |
| 2 | As viewer-a on `/templates`: **New Template**, type a name, **Save Template**. | The builder stays open and nothing is created. No request is sent (DevTools → Network); the console shows an uncaught "You don't have permission to create templates." Defect: the button is offered and the refusal is silent. |
| 3 | As viewer-a: trash on any card → **Delete template**. | The dialog stays open; nothing is deleted; no message. |
| 4 | As finance-a: open `/templates`. | "No templates yet" (the list request was refused with 403; defect: shown as an empty library). |
| 5 | Run command B (admin-b against Org A). | Org B's list doesn't contain "QA Services Agreement" (`null`); then `get 404 patch 404 put 404 delete 404 preview 404 generate 404`. Afterwards Org A's `$T_QA` has the same version and description as before. |

Command A:
```bash
tplperm() { echo "view $(code "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1")" \
  "create $(code -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}')" \
  "edit $(code -X PATCH "$API/templates/qa-none" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}')" \
  "delete $(code -X DELETE "$API/templates/qa-none" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1")" \
  "preview $(code -X POST "$API/templates/qa-none/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}')"; }
for t in "$ADMIN_A" "$COUNSEL_A" "$LEGALOPS_A" "$CONTRACTS_A" "$REP_A" "$PROCUREMENT_A" "$FINANCE_A" "$APPROVER_A" "$VIEWER_A"; do tplperm "$t"; done
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s "$API/templates?limit=200" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq '[.data[].name] | index("QA Services Agreement")'
B="Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B"; J='content-type: application/json'
echo "get $(code "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "$B")" \
  "patch $(code -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "$B" -H "$J" -d '{"description":"B"}')" \
  "put $(code -X PUT "$API/templates/$T_QA/sections" -H "$B" -H "$J" -d '{"sections":[]}')" \
  "delete $(code -X DELETE "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "$B")" \
  "preview $(code -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/preview" -H "$B" -H "$J" -d '{}')" \
  "generate $(code -X POST "$API/templates/$T_QA/generate" -H "$B" -H "$J" -d '{}')"
curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '{version, description}'
```

**Also check**
- Org B has its own library (seeded at registration, plus any pack chosen in its onboarding) with different ids.

### E2E-CLS-01 · The clause library lists, searches and filters the org's clauses by category, approval and risk

**Covers:** `/clauses` · `GET /clauses/categories`, `GET /clauses`, `GET /clauses/:id` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, finance-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in as counsel-a. Fresh counts as in "Before you start".

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Left rail → Library → **Clauses**. | Three columns. Left: "Categories" with a **+**, "All Clauses" selected (dark), then the 18 categories from "Definitions & Interpretation" to "Service Levels & Performance". Middle: "Search clauses...", **New clause**, the chips **Not approved** and **Unfavourable**, the clause list grouped by category (each row names its category under the title), a **Load 6 more** button at the end, and the footer "Showing 100 of 106 clauses". Right: "Select a clause to edit, or create a new one." with **New clause**. |
| 2 | Click **Load 6 more**. | The button goes; the footer reads "106 clauses". |
| 3 | Find "No Termination for Convenience (Vendor-Favorable)". | Pills "Not approved" and "Unfavourable"; tags "termination", "no-convenience"; a hollow circle (hover "Not approved — click to approve") and a trash (hover "Delete clause"). An approved clause shows a filled check (hover "Approved — click to withdraw approval") and its rating as a plain tag ("Favorable", "Neutral" or "Standard"). |
| 4 | Click the chip **Not approved**. | 3 clauses: "Confidentiality Term — 3 Years", "No Termination for Convenience (Vendor-Favorable)", "Self-Insurance (Vendor Pushback)"; footer "3 clauses". Add **Unfavourable**: still 3. Only **Unfavourable**: 8. |
| 5 | Chips off. Select category "Insurance". | Its 4 clauses, without the category line. With **Not approved** on: only "Self-Insurance (Vendor Pushback)". |
| 6 | Select "Definitions & Interpretation" with **Not approved** on. | "Nothing matches" / "Every clause here is approved and none is marked unfavourable." |
| 7 | Chips off, "All Clauses", search `carve`. | After a short pause: "Excluded Claims (Carve-Outs)" (search reads titles and text, any case). Search `zzqq`: "Nothing matches" / "Try a different term, or clear the search." |
| 8 | Clear the search; click a seeded clause. | The right panel "Edit Clause" with its title, Risk Rating, Tags and text; footer "0 version(s) · used 0×" (Known limits). Click **Cancel**. |
| 9 | Run command A. | 18 categories; `{"total":3,…}` for not approved; total 8 for unfavorable; the `tag=termination` list (tag filter is API-only); `q=insurance&limit=2` gives 2 items with the full total; an item has `category.name`; a missing id answers 404 `{"detail":"Clause not found"}`. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s "$API/clauses/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.data | length'
curl -s "$API/clauses?approved=false" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{total, titles: [.data[].title]}'
curl -s "$API/clauses?riskRating=unfavorable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .total
curl -s "$API/clauses?tag=termination" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '[.data[].title]'
curl -s "$API/clauses?q=insurance&limit=2&offset=0" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{total, n: (.data | length), first: .data[0] | {title, category: .category.name}}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/clauses/qa-missing" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"
```

**Also check**
- finance-a and approver-a (no view:clause): the page shows "No clauses in this category", "0 clauses" and a disabled
  **New clause** (hover "Create a category first, then add clauses to it") instead of a permission message (defect); the
  API answers 403 `Missing permission: view:clause`.

**Known limits**
- The "Nothing matches" text for chips always says "approved and none is marked unfavourable", even with one chip on.
- The tag filter exists only in the API.

### E2E-CLS-02 · Categories can be added and nested on the page, renamed, moved and deleted through the API, and a category in use can't be deleted

**Covers:** `/clauses` · `POST /clauses/categories`, `GET /clauses/categories`, `PATCH /clauses/categories/:id`, `DELETE /clauses/categories/:id` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, legalops-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B for the last check · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in as counsel-a on `/clauses`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click the **+** next to "Categories". In the browser prompt "Category name:" enter `QA Category`, OK. | "QA Category" appears at the top of the list: new categories get sort order 0, the standard ones start at 10. |
| 2 | Click **+** again and cancel the prompt, or OK it empty. | Nothing is created. |
| 3 | Hover "QA Category": a **+** appears at the row's right. Click it; enter `QA Sub`. | "QA Category" gets a chevron and "QA Sub" is nested, indented, under it. |
| 4 | Click "QA Category" twice. | The first click selects it and collapses it; the second expands it. The list: "No clauses in this category" / "Add the language your team reuses so drafting can pull from it." |
| 5 | Left rail → Library → **Playbook**. | "QA Category" is listed there too: the clause library and the playbook share one category list. Go back to Clauses. |
| 6 | Run command A. | `CAT_QA` and `CAT_SUB` set; `{"sortOrder":0,"children":["QA Sub"]}`. |
| 7 | Run command B (rename, move to top level, move back; API only). Reload after each. | 200 each. "QA Sub (renamed)" shows; after the move it is a top-level category; after moving back it is under "QA Category" again. |
| 8 | As legalops-a, run command C. | Deleting the parent: 409 `{"detail":"Cannot delete category with 1 sub-categories and 0 clauses"}`. Then the child: 204. Then the parent: 204. Both are gone after a reload. |
| 9 | Run command D (a seeded category). | 409 `{"detail":"Cannot delete category with 0 sub-categories and 4 clauses"}` (5 once the Manufacturing pack is installed). |
| 10 | Make `QA Cat 2` with the **+**, select it, **New clause** titled `QA temp` (text: click **Save Draft** in the editor, then **Save**; see CLS-03). As legalops-a run command E. | With the clause: 409 "…0 sub-categories and 1 clauses". After deleting the clause (trash → **Delete clause**): intended 204. **Verify (defect, reported):** the deleted clause still references the category and the database refuses the delete, so it answers 500 "An unexpected error occurred…". The same happens for any category that has playbook positions. |

Command A:
```bash
cats() { curl -s "$API/clauses/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"; }
export CAT_QA=$(cats | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA Category") | .id')
export CAT_SUB=$(cats | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA Category") | .children[] | select(.name=="QA Sub") | .id')
cats | jq -c '.data[] | select(.name=="QA Category") | {sortOrder, children: [.children[].name]}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -o /dev/null -X PATCH "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_SUB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"QA Sub (renamed)","description":"QA"}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -o /dev/null -X PATCH "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_SUB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"parentCategoryId":null}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -o /dev/null -X PATCH "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_SUB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"parentCategoryId":"'$CAT_QA'"}'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_SUB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/$CAT_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
```
Command D:
```bash
FM=$(curl -s "$API/clauses/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="Force Majeure & Excused Events") | .id')
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/$FM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
```
Command E (run it before and after deleting "QA temp"):
```bash
C2=$(curl -s "$API/clauses/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA Cat 2") | .id')
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/$C2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
```

**Also check**
- counsel-a deleting a category: 403 `Missing permission: delete:clause`.
- viewer-a: **+** opens the prompt, but after OK nothing appears (refused in the browser, no message; defect). The API
  answers 403 `Missing permission: create:clause`.
- A name over 128 characters: 422.
- `PATCH` with `"parentCategoryId"` set to the category's own id is accepted (200) and the category disappears from the
  tree; so does one whose parent is an Org B category id (no check that the parent is a different category in the same
  org; defect). Set `"parentCategoryId":null` to bring it back.
- admin-b: PATCH or DELETE of an Org A category → 404 `{"detail":"Category not found"}`.

**Known limits**
- The page can add categories but not rename, move, reorder or delete them: the API only.
- A category with playbook positions or with deleted clauses can't be deleted (500 today, see step 10).

### E2E-CLS-03 · A clause is created, edited with a version history, approved, withdrawn and deleted

**Covers:** `/clauses` · `POST /clauses`, `GET /clauses/:id`, `PATCH /clauses/:id`, `POST /clauses/:id/approve`, `DELETE /clauses/:id`, `GET /clauses` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, legalops-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in as counsel-a on `/clauses`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Select category "Limitation of Liability"; click **New clause**. | The right panel "New Clause" with **Save** and **Cancel**; "Clause title..."; "Risk Rating" = None (None, Favorable, Neutral, Unfavorable, Standard); "Tags (comma-separated)" ("e.g. mutual, standard"); an editor whose toolbar ends with **Save Draft**. |
| 2 | Title `QA Mutual Cap — 12 Months`; Risk Rating **Standard**; Tags `qa, cap, mutual`; in the editor type `Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid in the {{cap_months}} months before the claim.` Click **Save Draft** in the editor toolbar (it reads "Saved!"), then **Save**. | The panel closes. The list shows "QA Mutual Cap — 12 Months" with "Not approved", "Standard" and the tags qa, cap, mutual; the footer count is one higher. |
| 3 | Run command A. | riskRating "standard", tags `["qa","cap","mutual"]`, isApproved false, category "Limitation of Liability", one version `{"version":1,"note":"Initial version"}`. |
| 4 | Click the hollow circle on the row. | The "Not approved" pill goes and the icon fills (hover "Approved — click to withdraw approval"). The **Not approved** chip no longer lists it. |
| 5 | Click the row. | "Edit Clause" with the saved values; footer "1 version(s) · used 0×". |
| 6 | Change the text to end `…before the claim, except for data breaches.`, click **Save Draft**, then **Save**. Click the row again. | Footer "2 version(s) · used 0×". |
| 7 | Change only the tags, **Save**. | The version count stays at 2. |
| 8 | Set Risk Rating **Unfavorable**, **Save**. | The row shows the "Unfavourable" pill; the **Unfavourable** chip lists it. |
| 9 | Click the filled check. | "Not approved" is back. |
| 10 | Run command B. | Version 3 with note "QA tightened"; then `isApproved` false, then true (`{}` approves by default). |
| 11 | As legalops-a: trash on the row. Press Esc; open it again and click **Delete clause**. | "Delete this clause?" with "QA Mutual Cap — 12 Months will be removed from the library, along with its version history. This can't be undone." Esc closes it. **Delete clause**: the row is gone and the count drops by one. |
| 12 | Run command C. | GET and a second DELETE: 404 `{"detail":"Clause not found"}`. |

Command A:
```bash
export CL_QA=$(curl -s "$API/clauses?q=QA%20Mutual%20Cap" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.data[0].id')
curl -s "$API/clauses/$CL_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{title, riskRating, tags, isApproved, category: .category.name, versions: [.versions[] | {version, note}]}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/clauses/$CL_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content":"<p>The total liability of each party is capped at {{cap_months}} months of fees.</p>","changeNote":"QA tightened"}' | jq -c '.versions[-1] | {version, note}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/clauses/$CL_QA/approve" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"approved":false}' | jq .isApproved
curl -s -X POST "$API/clauses/$CL_QA/approve" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq .isApproved
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/clauses/$CL_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/clauses/$CL_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEGALOPS_A"
```

**Also check**
- Typing new text and clicking **Save** without **Save Draft** keeps the old text (defect; Known limits).
- **Save** with an empty title does nothing. **Cancel** closes without saving.
- With "All Clauses" selected, **New clause** first selects the top category in the list and the clause lands there.
- API: `"riskRating":"high"` → 422; a title over 256 characters → 422; a `categoryId` from Org B → 404
  `{"detail":"Category not found"}`; a `categoryId` in a PATCH is ignored (clauses can't change category).
- counsel-a deleting: the dialog's **Delete clause** does nothing (no message); API 403 `Missing permission: delete:clause`.

**Known limits**
- The clause text is kept only after **Save Draft** in the editor toolbar; **Save** alone saves title, rating and tags.
- "used N×" never goes above 0: nothing counts clause uses.
- Seeded clauses have no version history ("0 version(s)").
- No restore after delete; clause changes write no audit-log entry.

### E2E-CLS-04 · A clause is used in a template: inserted as text in the editor, or referenced so drafts pick up its current wording

**Covers:** `/clauses`, `/templates` · `POST /clauses`, `PATCH /clauses/:id`, `DELETE /clauses/:id`, `GET /clauses`, `POST /templates`, `POST /templates/:id/preview`, `POST /templates/:id/generate` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, legalops-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B for step 9 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Run command A: it makes the approved clause "QA Ref Clause" in "Limitation of Liability" (`$CL_REF`).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|

Click in the editor, then the toolbar's Clause Library; search `QA Ref`; click "QA Ref Clause". | Its text "Liability is capped at {{cap_months}} months of fees." is inserted at the cursor and the panel closes. **Save Template**. |
| 2 | Preview "QA Clause Insert". | The Liability section contains the clause text as ordinary text: "Liability is capped at [[cap_months]] months of fees." (`{{cap_months}}` isn't declared on this template, so it shows as a blank). |

The preview HTML has `<div class="clause-library-ref" data-clause-id="<$CL_REF>">` after "The following cap applies." with the clause text; `unfilledVariables` `["cap_months"]` (a referenced clause's own variables count). |

Command A:

```bash
  -d '{"name":"QA Clause Ref","contractType":"MSA","isPublished":true,"sections":[{"title":"Liability","content":"<p>The following cap applies.</p>","clauseRefs":["'$CL_REF'"]}]}' | jq -r .id)
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_REF/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq '{unfilledVariables, html}'
```

Command D:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/clauses/$CL_REF" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content":"<p>Liability is capped at {{cap_months}} months of fees, excluding data breaches.</p>"}' | jq -c '{versions: (.versions | length)}'
```
Command E:
```bash
tj contract_draft '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","userMessage":"msa","templateId":"'$T_REF'"}' | jq -c '{templateVariables, unfilledVariables}'
```
Command F:
```bash
CL_B=$(curl -s "$API/clauses?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq -r '.data[0].id')
T_FOREIGN=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA Foreign Ref","sections":[{"title":"X","content":"<p>Own text.</p>","clauseRefs":["'$CL_B'"]}]}' | jq -r .id)
curl -s -X POST "$API/templates/$T_FOREIGN/preview" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq -r .html | grep -c clause-library-ref
```

- viewer-a can open the editor's Clause Library panel and see clauses (view:clause); only saving is refused.

**Known limits**
- Referencing a library clause (live wording) is API-only; the editor's Clause Library inserts a copy.
- The builder doesn't show referenced clauses; only Preview, generate and drafts include them.
- Deleting a referenced clause silently drops it from later drafts.

### E2E-CLS-05 · Each role gets exactly its clause rights, and Org B can't see or change Org A's clauses

**Covers:** `/clauses` · `GET /clauses`, `POST /clauses`, `PATCH /clauses/:id`, `POST /clauses/:id/approve`, `DELETE /clauses/:id`, `POST /clauses/categories`, `PATCH /clauses/categories/:id`, `DELETE /clauses/categories/:id`, `GET /clauses/:id`, `GET /clauses/categories` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** all Org A accounts, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Define command A (same idea as TPL-09: allowed calls fail validation (422) or find nothing (404), refused ones 403).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run `clsperm` for each token. | Columns: view, create, edit, approve, delete, category create, category edit, category delete. admin-a and legalops-a `200 422 404 404 404 422 404 404`; counsel-a `200 422 404 404 403 422 404 403`; contracts-a, rep-a, procurement-a and viewer-a `200 403 403 403 403 403 403 403`; finance-a and approver-a `403` eight times. |
| 2 | As viewer-a on `/clauses`: click a row's approve circle; **New clause** → type a title → **Save**; trash → **Delete clause**. | Nothing changes and no message appears (defect); no request is sent. |
| 3 | Run command B (admin-b against Org A). | GET, PATCH, approve and DELETE of an Org A clause: 404 each; a new clause in an Org A category: 404 `{"detail":"Category not found"}`; Org B's search for "QA Ref" finds 0. |

Command A:
```bash
clsperm() { local h="Authorization: Bearer $1" j='content-type: application/json'; echo \
  "$(code "$API/clauses" -H "$h") $(code -X POST "$API/clauses" -H "$h" -H "$j" -d '{}')" \
  "$(code -X PATCH "$API/clauses/qa-none" -H "$h" -H "$j" -d '{}') $(code -X POST "$API/clauses/qa-none/approve" -H "$h" -H "$j" -d '{}')" \
  "$(code -X DELETE "$API/clauses/qa-none" -H "$h") $(code -X POST "$API/clauses/categories" -H "$h" -H "$j" -d '{}')" \
  "$(code -X PATCH "$API/clauses/categories/qa-none" -H "$h" -H "$j" -d '{}') $(code -X DELETE "$API/clauses/categories/qa-none" -H "$h")"; }
for t in "$ADMIN_A" "$COUNSEL_A" "$LEGALOPS_A" "$CONTRACTS_A" "$REP_A" "$PROCUREMENT_A" "$FINANCE_A" "$APPROVER_A" "$VIEWER_A"; do clsperm "$t"; done
```
Command B:
```bash
A_CL=$(curl -s "$API/clauses?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[0].id')
A_CAT=$(curl -s "$API/clauses/categories" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[0].id')
echo "get $(code "$API/clauses/$A_CL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B")" \
 "patch $(code -X PATCH "$API/clauses/$A_CL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"B"}')" \
 "approve $(code -X POST "$API/clauses/$A_CL/approve" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}')" \
 "delete $(code -X DELETE "$API/clauses/$A_CL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B")"
curl -s -X POST "$API/clauses" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"categoryId":"'$A_CAT'","title":"B in A"}'; echo
curl -s "$API/clauses?q=QA%20Ref" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq .total
```

### E2E-PACK-01 · Installing an industry pack from Settings adds its template, clauses and playbook positions once, and marks it installed

**Covers:** (Settings → Industry packs) · `GET /organization/industry-packs`, `POST /organization/install-industry-pack`, `GET /templates`, `GET /clauses`, `PATCH /templates/:id` · docs/38: TC-WF-13 (P1, P4, N5)
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a, counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Healthcare not installed: `curl -s "$API/organization" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq .settings.installedIndustryPacks`
  prints `null` or a list without "healthcare". Note `counts $ADMIN_A`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: left rail (bottom) → **Settings** → **Industry packs** (or open `$WEB/settings?tab=industry-packs`). | Heading "Industry packs" and "Add contract types, templates, clauses and playbook positions for your industry, on top of the standard library. Installing is safe to repeat: nothing you've changed is overwritten." Five rows, each with a description and **Install**: SaaS, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Biotech, Logistics. Each description ends "Adds N clauses, 1 template, 6 playbook positions." (7 clauses for Biotech, 8 for the others). |
| 2 | Click **Install** on Healthcare. | It reads "Installing…" and the other Install buttons are disabled; then a toast "Industry pack installed" / "Healthcare", and the row shows "Installed" with a check (no button). |
| 3 | `counts $ADMIN_A`; `curl -s "$API/organization" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq .settings.installedIndustryPacks`. | templates +1, clauses +8, positions +6 (more if standard playbook positions were deleted earlier: see step 10). The list contains "healthcare". |
| 4 | `/templates`. | A card "Business Associate Agreement (BAA)": "BAA", "Published", "v1 · 10 sections · 4 variables". |
| 5 | `/clauses` → "Data Protection & Privacy". | New, approved clauses: "HIPAA — Business Associate Status", "HIPAA — Minimum Necessary", "HIPAA Breach Notification — 60 Days", "De-Identification", "Patient Access to PHI". "Information Security" has "HIPAA Security Rule Safeguards" and "HITRUST or SOC 2 + HITECH Certification"; "Compliance with Laws" has "Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law Compliance". |
| 6 | Library → **Playbook** → "Data Protection & Privacy". | Three more positions, e.g. the walkaway "Vendor refuses to sign BAA or insists on terms materially weaker than HHS sample BAA, OR breach notification longer than 60 days." Its note reads "[seed-key:hc-no-baa-walkaway] Reject — HIPAA non-compliant.": the install's marker is shown to users (defect). |
| 7 | Run command A (install Healthcare again through the Settings endpoint). | `{"ok":true,"packId":"healthcare","label":"Healthcare"}`; `counts` unchanged; "healthcare" appears once in installedIndustryPacks. |
| 8 | Run command B (rename the pack's template, install again). Reload `/templates`. | A second "Business Associate Agreement (BAA)" card appears next to "BAA (QA renamed)": matching is by name, so a renamed template comes back as a new copy (templates +1). |
| 9 | Delete the new copy (as admin-a or legalops-a: trash → **Delete template**), then run command A again. | Nothing is added: a deleted template's name still counts. Rename "BAA (QA renamed)" back with `-d '{"name":"Business Associate Agreement (BAA)"}'` if you want the original name. |
| 10 | Library → **Playbook**: open any category, click the trash on one standard position, then **Delete position** in "Delete this position?". Run command A. | The deleted standard position is back (positions +1): installing from Settings also re-runs the standard library, and deleted playbook positions are re-created. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/organization/install-industry-pack" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"packId":"healthcare"}'; echo
counts $ADMIN_A
curl -s "$API/organization" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -c .settings.installedIndustryPacks
```
Command B:
```bash
BAA=$(tid "Business Associate Agreement (BAA)")
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$BAA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"BAA (QA renamed)"}' | jq -r .name
curl -s -X POST "$API/organization/install-industry-pack" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"packId":"healthcare"}' >/dev/null; counts $ADMIN_A
```

**Also check**
- legalops-a sees the **Industry packs** tab and can install. counsel-a, contracts-a, rep-a and viewer-a have no
  Industry packs tab; opening `?tab=industry-packs` shows an empty content area. The API as viewer-a:
  403 `Missing permission: configure:integration`.
- An unknown pack (`{"packId":"fintech"}`): 422 "Request body failed validation"; nothing installed (TC-WF-13 N5).
- An install racing another admin's settings change doesn't undo it (TC-WF-13 P1).
- Org B's counts (`counts $ADMIN_B`) don't change.
- If the install fails, the toast reads "Install failed" with the server's reason or "Try again in a moment.".

**Known limits**
- A pack can't be uninstalled. Once a row shows "Installed" there's no button: install again through the API.
- Matching is by template name, clause title and the playbook marker: renamed items come back as copies; deleted
  templates and clauses don't; deleted playbook positions do.
- Packs add templates, clauses and playbook positions, not contract types (the tab's first sentence says otherwise).
- Pack installs write no audit-log entry (by design).
- The Manufacturing pack adds "Master Supply Agreement" (type "Supply"), which the Assistant may use for supply and
  purchase requests (DRAFT-05): install it after DRAFT-05 or expect that.

### E2E-PACK-02 · The admin packs API lists the packs with their counts, installs one, reports what it added, and adds nothing the second time

**Covers:** `GET /admin/packs`, `POST /admin/packs/install` · (Settings → Industry packs) · docs/38: —
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a, counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Biotech not installed in Org A or Org B. Note `counts $ADMIN_A` and `counts $ADMIN_B`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run command A. | Five packs with counts: saas, healthcare, manufacturing and logistics `{"clauses":8,"templates":1,"playbookPositions":6}`; biotech `{"clauses":7,"templates":1,"playbookPositions":6}`. Labels and descriptions as on the Settings tab. |
| 2 | Run command B. | `{"pack":"biotech","installed":{"clausesCreated":7,"templatesCreated":1,"playbookPositionsCreated":6}}`; counts +1 / +7 / +6. |
| 3 | `/templates`. | "Material Transfer Agreement (Research)": "MTA", "Published", "v1 · 8 sections · 5 variables". |
| 4 | Run command B again. | `{"clausesCreated":0,"templatesCreated":0,"playbookPositionsCreated":0}`; counts unchanged. |
| 5 | Settings → **Industry packs**. | Biotech still shows **Install**: this endpoint doesn't record the pack as installed (inconsistency, reported), and `installedIndustryPacks` has no "biotech". Click **Install**: toast "Industry pack installed" / "Biotech", the row shows "Installed", and counts don't change unless standard items were deleted (PACK-01 step 10). |
| 6 | Run command C (bad bodies). | Each: 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request","issues":[…]}`. Note `{"packId":"biotech"}` is refused: this endpoint takes `pack`, the Settings one takes `packId`. |
| 7 | Run command D (other roles). | legalops-a, counsel-a and viewer-a: 403 `Missing permission: configure:organization` on both routes, although legalops-a can install from Settings. |
| 8 | Run command E (Org B). | admin-b gets the same catalogue and can install Biotech into Org B (its counts +1/+7/+6); Org A's counts don't change. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/packs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -c '.packs[] | {id, label, counts}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/packs/install" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pack":"biotech"}'; echo; counts $ADMIN_A
```
Command C:
```bash
for b in '{}' '{"pack":"fintech"}' '{"packId":"biotech"}'; do curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/admin/packs/install" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$b"; done
```
Command D:
```bash
for t in "$LEGALOPS_A" "$COUNSEL_A" "$VIEWER_A"; do echo "list $(code "$API/admin/packs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $t")" \
  "install $(code -X POST "$API/admin/packs/install" -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pack":"saas"}')"; done
```
Command E:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/packs/install" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pack":"biotech"}'; echo
counts $ADMIN_B; counts $ADMIN_A
```

**Known limits**
- Two install endpoints do the same seeding with different permissions (`configure:organization` here,
  `configure:integration` in Settings) and different bodies, and only the Settings one records the pack as installed.
- This endpoint seeds only the pack (and any missing standard categories); the Settings one also re-runs the standard
  library.

### E2E-DRAFT-01 · Contracts → Draft new picks a published template, drafts with AI and opens the new Draft contract

**Covers:** (`/contracts`, `/counterparties/:id`) · `POST /agent/draft`, `GET /templates`, `POST /templates/:id/generate` · agent service `draft` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, viewer-a, admin-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key; the workers, for the analysis that follows · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$T_QA` "QA Services Agreement" published (TPL-02/04). Note its usage count:
  `curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .usageCount`.
- Signed in as counsel-a.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Left rail → Workspace → **Contracts** → **Draft new** (top right; hover "Start a new contract from a template"). | A dialog "Select Template" / "Choose a template to start your contract draft", with "Search templates...", **All Types**, the published templates only (each: name, one line of description, type pill, "N sections", plus " · used N×" once used), and at the bottom "N templates available" and **Cancel**. "Mutual Idea Submission Agreement" and other drafts are not listed. |
| 2 | Search `QA`; then pick **MSA** in All Types; then clear both. Press Esc; click **Draft new** again. | The list narrows to matching names, then MSA-typed templates. Esc closes the picker. |
| 3 | Click "QA Services Agreement". | "Draft Details" with "Template: QA Services Agreement", a back arrow (hover "Back to templates") and an X. Fields: "Contract title *" filled with "QA Services Agreement", "Counterparty name" ("e.g. Acme Corporation"), "Additional context for AI" ("e.g. 2-year term, mutual NDA, governing law Delaware, SaaS licensing deal..."). **Cancel** and **Generate Draft**. |
| 4 | Clear "Contract title *". | **Generate Draft** is disabled. |
| 5 | Title `QA Acme services draft`; Counterparty `Acme Corporation`; context `Annual fee 50000, effective 2026-10-01, New York law.`; click **Generate Draft**. | "Generating draft with AI… this takes 20–40 seconds" and the button disabled. |
| 6 | Wait. | The new contract's page opens: title "QA Acme services draft", status "Draft", a type chip (the model's reading of the request, e.g. "MSA"). A blue bar "Identifying contract type…" and the steps Queue · Parse · Classify · Extract · Analyze · Index while the analysis runs. The Styled view shows "Parties" and "Fees" filled by the model; any term it couldn't fill shows as `[[key]]`. **Original** is disabled (hover "No original file — this contract was created from text or a template."). The right rail's History reads "v1 AI-generated draft (QA Services Agreement)". |
| 7 | Run command A with the id from the page URL. | status "DRAFT", owner legal@demo.com, counterpartyName `null` (the typed name isn't saved; Known limits), note "AI-generated draft (QA Services Agreement)". The template's usage count is one higher. |
| 8 | As admin-a run command B. | A `CONTRACT_CREATED` event for the contract by legal@demo.com with `{"source":"agent_draft","template":"QA Services Agreement"}`. |
| 9 | Workspace → **Counterparties** → "Globex Industries" → **New contract**. | The Contracts page opens with the "Select Template" picker. Pick "QA Services Agreement": "Counterparty name" is already "Globex Industries". **Generate Draft**. The new contract names Globex Industries, and it is listed on Globex Industries' page. (Change the name before generating and the contract is not linked.) |
| 10 | Run command C (the agents service's draft route directly). | Without the secret: 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}`. With it: `usedTemplateName` "QA Services Agreement", `error` null, plus `unfilledVariables`, `completenessScore`, `missingFields` and `reviewNotes`, which the UI never shows. An empty message: 400 `{"detail":"user_message is required"}`. |
| 11 | Run command D (the API route behind the dialog). | An empty `userMessage`: 400 `{"detail":"userMessage is required"}`. Org B's contract as `saveAs.contractId`: 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`; Org B's counterparty as `saveAs.counterpartyId`: 404 `{"detail":"Counterparty not found"}`. viewer-a with `saveAs.title`: 403 `Missing permission: create:contract`; viewer-a without `saveAs`: 200 with the HTML and nothing saved (the usage count still rises; Known limits). |
| 12 | Stop the agents service; try **Generate Draft** again. | Under the form: "Agent service unavailable" (HTTP 502). Nothing is created. Start the service again. |

Command A:
```bash
C_NEW=<id from the contract page URL>
curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_NEW" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{title, status, type, counterpartyName, owner: .owner.email, analysisStatus, note: .versions[0].changeNote}'
curl -s "$API/templates/$T_QA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .usageCount
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=CONTRACT_CREATED&resourceId=$C_NEW" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -c '.events[] | {action, actor: .actor.email, metadata}'
```
Command C (the agents service listens on `AGENTS_PORT`, 8002 by default):
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:8002/draft -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"user_message":"x","org_id":"'$ORG_A'"}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8002/draft -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user_message":"Draft an MSA for Acme Corporation","org_id":"'$ORG_A'","user_id":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","context":{"template_id":"'$T_QA'"}}' \
  | jq '{usedTemplateName, contractType, sectionsIncluded, unfilledVariables, completenessScore, missingFields, reviewNotes, error}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:8002/draft -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"user_message":"  ","org_id":"'$ORG_A'"}'
```
Command D (get an Org B contract id and counterparty id first: `C_B=$(curl -s "$API/contracts?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq -r '.data[0].id')`,
`CP_B=$(curl -s "$API/counterparties" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq -r '.data[0].id')`; create one of each in Org B if empty):
```bash
d() { curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/agent/draft" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2"; }
d $COUNSEL_A '{"userMessage":" "}'
d $COUNSEL_A '{"userMessage":"Draft an MSA","templateId":"'$T_QA'","saveAs":{"contractId":"'$C_B'"}}'
d $COUNSEL_A '{"userMessage":"Draft an MSA","templateId":"'$T_QA'","saveAs":{"title":"QA x","counterpartyId":"'$CP_B'"}}'
d $VIEWER_A  '{"userMessage":"Draft an MSA","templateId":"'$T_QA'","saveAs":{"title":"QA viewer"}}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/agent/draft" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"userMessage":"Draft an MSA","templateId":"'$T_QA'"}' | jq '{usedTemplateName, contractId, html: (.html[0:60])}'
```

**Also check**
- viewer-a, finance-a and approver-a have no **Draft new** button; opening `$WEB/contracts?new=1` opens nothing.
- rep-a (sales rep, own scope) can use **Draft new**; the contract is rep-a's and appears in rep-a's list.
- With no published template in the org, the picker says "No published templates found" / "Create and publish a
  template first" and "0 templates available".

**Known limits**
- The model fills whatever blanks it can infer and may fill unstated ones (its instructions default governing law to
  Delaware and ask for "reasonable values"); the Assistant's drafting never guesses (DRAFT-03, DRAFT-04).
- The dialog never tells you which terms were left blank.
- The counterparty name you type is only used for drafting: it is saved on the contract only when you started from that
  counterparty's page.
- The contract's type is the model's reading ("Draft a <template type> contract titled …"); a template typed outside
  the drafting codes (e.g. "SaaS") gives OTHER or the nearest code.
- If the chosen template is unpublished or deleted meanwhile, the drafting service silently uses another published
  template of the type it reads from the request, or fails with "No template matches this contract type. Create a
  template for this type first, then retry."
- The usage count rises when the text is generated, even if the contract isn't saved (and for viewers previewing
  drafts through the API).

### E2E-DRAFT-02 · The Assistant answers "what can I draft from?" from the template list, within the caller's permission

**Covers:** (`/agent`) · `POST /agent/chat` · tool `template_list` · docs/38: TC-ACC-14 (the `template_list` rule)
**Roles:** counsel-a, finance-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key for steps 1–2 and 5 · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- The QA templates from earlier journeys exist. Signed in as counsel-a.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Left rail → **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Send `What templates can I draft from?` | A `template_list` chip with "N results" (up to 20); expand it: "Args" and "Result". The answer lists templates by name with their type and whether each is published; unless you asked for published ones only, drafts such as "Mutual Idea Submission Agreement" may appear, marked as not published. No card and no contract. |
| 2 | Send `Do we have a published NDA template?` | Another `template_list` call (with an NDA type and/or published only). The answer names published NDA templates ("QA Mutual NDA" once DRAFT-03 has run, "Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement", "One-Way Non-Disclosure Agreement (Inbound)") and not the unpublished "Mutual Idea Submission Agreement". |
| 3 | Run command A (the tool's endpoint, no model). | Published NDAs only; `{"total":3,…}` for `query` "statement" (name or description); each item has id, name, description, contractType, isPublished, version, usageCount, variableKeys and updatedAt, and no sections; items are ordered by usage, then name. `limit` 51: 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request",…}`. |
| 4 | Run command B. | As finance-a: 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:template permission"}`. As admin-b in Org B: only Org B's templates (no "QA …" names). |
| 5 | Sign in as finance-a; on `/agent` send `What templates can I draft from?` | The `template_list` chip shows "permission denied" in red; the answer says this user can't see templates, rather than claiming there are none. |

Command A:
```bash
tj template_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractType":"NDA","publishedOnly":true}' | jq -c '{total, names: [.items[].name]}'
tj template_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","query":"statement"}' | jq -c '{total, first: .items[0]}'
tjs template_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","limit":51}'
```
Command B:
```bash
tj template_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$FINANCE_A_ID'"}'; echo
tj template_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_B'","userId":"'$ADMIN_B_ID'","limit":50}' | jq '[.items[].name | select(startswith("QA"))]'
```

**Known limits**
- `template_list` returns names and variable keys only, never template text: the Assistant can say what exists, not
  quote it.
