**Covers:** `POST /templates`, `POST /agent/threads`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/apply`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/:toolCallId/undo`, `GET /admin/audit` · tool `contract_create_from_template` (its plan and apply endpoints) · docs/38: TC-AI-05 (P2, P5–P7, N5, N6), TC-DRAFT-01 (N4), TC-ACC-16
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, viewer-a, finance-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B; no agents service · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Run command A: the fixtures "QA Mutual NDA" (`$T_NDA`, NDA, published; declares a default `purpose` and a Delaware
  default for `governing_law`), the counterparty "Hooli" with an address, and "QA Offer Letter" (`$T_OFFER`, no type,
  published). `curl -s "$API/contracts?search=Hooli" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq .total` prints `0`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run command B (plan an NDA: counterparty, New York law, 3 years). | templateName "QA Mutual NDA", contractType "NDA", title "Hooli — NDA", counterpartyName "Hooli", variables `counterparty_name` "Hooli", `governing_law` "New York" (your term beats the template default), `term_years` "3", `purpose` "evaluating a possible business relationship" (the template's default), `our_company` "Demo Org, Inc." (the org's name); unfilledVariables `["effective_date"]` (never today's date); persisted false. Contracts matching "Hooli": still 0 — planning creates nothing. |
| 2 | Run command C (which NDA template wins). | "QA Mutual NDA"; after touching the seeded "Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement" (publishing it again) the plan uses it; after touching `$T_NDA` again, "QA Mutual NDA" again. The planner takes the **most recently updated** published template of the type (Known limits). |
| 3 | Run command D (the seeded Mutual NDA by id). | templateName "Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement". We take the customer role: `customerName` "Demo Org, Inc.", `providerName` "Hooli", `customerEntity` "a Delaware corporation" (the template default, our side); `providerAddress` "1 Hooli Way, Palo Alto, CA" from the counterparty record; `governingLaw` "New York", `confidentialityYears` "3". unfilledVariables `["effectiveDate","customerAddress","providerEntity","purpose","venueLocation"]`: their entity type isn't guessed from a default, and the venue default ("Wilmington, Delaware") is dropped because the law changed. |
| 4 | Run command E (a request typed only by its words). | "QA Offer Letter" is used for "offer letter for Jane Doe": the words make it EMPLOYMENT, no published template is typed `EMPLOYMENT` (the seeded one is "Employment"), so the planner takes an untyped template whose name or description has "offer letter" or "employment". `company_name` "Demo Org, Inc.", `candidate_name` "Jane Doe"; unfilled `["job_title"]`; title "Jane Doe — Employment Agreement". |
| 5 | Run command F (refusals). | No type found in the words: 422 `CONTRACT_TYPE_AMBIGUOUS`, "Could not tell which contract to draft. Pass contract_type (NDA \| MSA \| SOW \| VENDOR_AGREEMENT \| LICENSE \| EMPLOYMENT \| DATA_PROCESSING) or a template_id from template_list." No LICENSE template: 422 `NO_TEMPLATE_MATCH`, "No published LICENSE template. Pick one of the org's published templates by id, or create a LICENSE template in Templates first." with `templates` (at most 20, most recently updated first). The unpublished "Mutual Idea Submission Agreement" by id, and `$T_NDA` asked for from Org B: 404 `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`, "No published template with that id in this organization." |
| 6 | Run command G (Apply as counsel-a, with step 1's plan). | ok true, a toolCallId; result title "Hooli — NDA", type "NDA", subtitle "Draft NDA for Hooli", unfilledVariables `["effective_date"]`, diff title / type / status (DRAFT). |
| 7 | Run command H (the new contract). | status "DRAFT", type "NDA", tags `["template-draft"]`, counterpartyName "Hooli" but counterpartyId `null` (named, not linked to the "Hooli" record), owner legal@demo.com, analysisStatus "PENDING", note `Generated from template "QA Mutual NDA"`, and the stored HTML holds `data-key="effective_date"`. `$T_NDA`'s usage count went up by one. |
| 8 | Run command I (Undo, twice). | First: 200 `{"ok":true,"toolCallId":…,"rolledBackAt":…}`; the contract answers 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` and "Hooli" contracts are 0 again. Second: 409 `{"detail":"Already undone",…}`. |
| 9 | As admin-a run command J. | Newest first: `AGENT_TOOL_UNDONE` (resource = the toolCallId), `CONTRACT_CREATED` (resource = the contract; metadata `source` "agent_tool", `tool` "contract_create_from_template", `template` "QA Mutual NDA") and `AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED` (metadata `toolName` contract_create_from_template, `status` success), all by legal@demo.com. |
| 10 | Run command K (refusals at Apply). | viewer-a and finance-a: 403 `{"detail":"Missing permission: create:contract"}` (before any thread lookup). admin-b applying Org A's template in an Org B thread: `{"ok":false,…,"error":{"detail":"Template not found in this org"}}` (HTTP 404); nothing is created in either org. counsel-a applying into admin-a's thread: 404 `{"detail":"Thread not found"}`. |
| 11 | Run command L (Apply with an unpublished template id). | 200 and a contract: Apply doesn't check the publish state that planning does (reported). Undo it: run command I's first line with the `threadId` and `toolCallId` that command L printed. |
| 12 | Optional: Apply once more and wait 16 minutes, then Undo. | 410 `{"detail":"Undo window expired (15 minutes)",…}`; the contract stays. |

Command A (fixtures):

```bash
 "variables":[{"key":"purpose","label":"Purpose","type":"text","required":true,"defaultValue":"evaluating a possible business relationship"},
              {"key":"governing_law","label":"Governing law","type":"text","required":true,"defaultValue":"Delaware"}],
 "sections":[{"title":"Parties","content":"<p>This Mutual NDA is made on {{effective_date}} between {{our_company}} and {{counterparty_name}}.</p>"},
             {"title":"Purpose","content":"<p>Purpose: {{purpose}}.</p>"},

echo $T_NDA $T_OFFER
```

**Also check**
- rep-a (own-scope create) can apply; the contract is rep-a's, and rep-a's Undo works only while rep-a still owns it
  (TC-ACC-16 P5, N5).

**Known limits**
- The planner uses the most recently updated published template of a type; there is no "default template per type".
- Its own fallback only considers templates with no type; others are reached through the model's retry (DRAFT-05).
- `NO_TEMPLATE_MATCH` lists at most 20 published templates; its `detail` names the type by code ("a LICENSE template").
- An Assistant draft sets the counterparty's name but doesn't link the counterparty record.
- An Assistant draft is left with analysis status PENDING and nothing queued, so its page shows "Processing starting…"
  (DRAFT-04 step 8; reported).

### E2E-DRAFT-04 · Drafting in the Assistant shows a confirm card with the stated terms and the blanks, creates the Draft contract only on Apply, and Undo removes it

**Covers:** (`/agent`, `/contracts/:id`) · `POST /agent/chat`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/apply`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/:toolCallId/undo` · tool `contract_create_from_template` · docs/38: TC-AI-05
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- DRAFT-03 command A ran (`$T_NDA`, counterparty "Hooli") and "QA Mutual NDA" is the newest published NDA template
  (DRAFT-03 command C's `pick` prints "QA Mutual NDA"). No contract matches "Hooli" (DRAFT-03 step 8).
- Signed in as counsel-a. The demo org already has an "Initech" contract and counterparty, so this journey uses "Hooli".

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Left rail → **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Send `draft an NDA with Hooli, New York law, 3 years` | Tool chips appear first: `contract_search`, `counterparty_memory`, then `contract_create_from_template` with a pause icon. The right pane may first show a "Hooli" card ("No prior deals on file") or search results. Then an amber card: "About to run" `contract_create_from_template` and the badge "Undoable", with the summary `Create a draft NDA for Hooli from the template "QA Mutual NDA" — 1 term(s) left blank to fill in: effective_date`, and **Cancel**, **Edit**, **Apply**. |
| 2 | Read the reply. | It opens with one line on what the agreement is for, names "QA Mutual NDA" and the terms it applied (New York law, 3 years), names the blank (effective date), and doesn't say the contract is saved. |
| 3 | Before clicking anything: `curl -s "$API/contracts?search=Hooli" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq .total` | `0`. |
| 4 | Click **Edit**. | "Arguments" with editable JSON: `templateId` = `$T_NDA`, `contractType` "NDA", a `title` (e.g. "Hooli — Mutual NDA"; "Hooli — NDA" if the model gave none), `counterpartyName` "Hooli", `variables` with `counterparty_name`, `governing_law` "New York", `term_years` "3", `purpose` and `our_company`, and no `effective_date`. The button now reads **Review**. |
| 5 | Replace the `"title"` value with `"Hooli — Mutual NDA (QA)"`; click **Review**. | The editor closes and the card says "Arguments edited: Apply uses your version." with **Discard edit**. |
| 6 | Click **Edit**, delete a closing brace, click **Apply**. | "Invalid JSON: …" under the editor; nothing is sent. Restore the brace (or **Discard edit** and redo step 5), click **Review**. |
| 7 | When the reply has finished, click **Apply**. | "Applying…", then the receipt "Applied · Create a draft NDA for Hooli from the template "QA Mutual NDA" — …" with **Undo** (hover "Undo this action (within 15 minutes)"). The right pane opens a document titled "Hooli — Mutual NDA (QA)", subtitle "Draft NDA for Hooli", reading "This Mutual NDA is made on [[effective_date]] between Demo Org, Inc. and Hooli.", "Purpose: evaluating a possible business relationship.", "Confidentiality lasts 3 years.", "…governed by the laws of New York.", and **Open in Contracts** at the bottom; its X (hover "Close artifact (Esc)") closes the pane. |
| 8 | Keep this tab. In a second tab open `$WEB/contracts` and click "Hooli — Mutual NDA (QA)". | The contract page: status "Draft", type chip "NDA". The Styled view shows the four section headings and the text, with "[[effective_date]]" as plain text (not highlighted; reported). Right rail: History "v1 Generated from template "QA Mutual NDA"". **Original** is disabled (no file). A blue bar "Processing starting…" stays, and after 3 minutes adds "Taking too long?" with **Cancel** and **Retry** (the draft is saved as PENDING with nothing queued; reported). |
| 9 | Check the API and the template. | `curl -s "$API/contracts?search=Hooli" …` total 1; the contract's owner is legal@demo.com; `/templates` shows "QA Mutual NDA" "Used N time(s)" one higher; the audit log has `CONTRACT_CREATED` and `AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED` by legal@demo.com (DRAFT-03 command J). |
| 10 | Back in the `/agent` tab, click **Undo** on the receipt (within 15 minutes). Reload the second tab. | The receipt reads "Undone · …". The contract is gone: its page no longer loads it (the API answers 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`), and it is gone from Contracts and from search; the audit log has `AGENT_TOOL_UNDONE`. The usage count stays. |
| 11 | Send the step-1 message again; **Apply** the new card; in the document pane click **Open in Contracts**. | The browser loads the new contract's page in this tab (same checks as step 8). |
| 12 | Press the browser's Back button. | The conversation reloads with its messages and tool chips, but without the "Applied" receipt and its **Undo**: receipts live only in the open page (Known limits). Undo this draft through the API with command A: `{"ok":true,…}`, and the contract is gone. |
| 13 | Send the step-1 message once more; on the new card click **Cancel**. | "Cancelled · …"; nothing is created. |

Command A (thread id from the `/agent` URL, `?thread=<id>`):
```bash
T_UI=<thread id>
TC_UI=$(curl -s "$API/agent/threads/$T_UI" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '[.toolCalls[] | select(.toolName=="contract_create_from_template" and .reversible and .rolledBackAt==null)][-1].id')
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/agent/threads/$T_UI/actions/$TC_UI/undo" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"
```

**Also check**
- Clicking **Apply** on a brand-new conversation before the reply has finished can show "Failed · … · Thread not
  persisted yet — try again in a moment.": the conversation is saved when the reply ends. Send again.
- 15 minutes after Apply the **Undo** button disappears (the receipt checks every 10 seconds); the API answers 410.
- viewer-a sends the same request: no "About to run `contract_create_from_template`" card (the tool isn't offered to a
  role without create:contract); the reply may say it can't create contracts; no contract (TC-AI-05 N4).
- Start a request, and before applying click **New conversation**, then reopen it from the left list: the card is not
  restored (TC-AI-05 N2); ask again.
- Terms you didn't state are never filled with guesses: no California law, no "2 years", no today's date (TC-AI-05 N1).

**Known limits**
- The draft comes from the most recently updated published template of the type (DRAFT-03 step 2).
- **Open in Contracts** loads a new page, and a reloaded conversation shows no receipts, so after it the only Undo is
  the API (step 12). Check the draft in a second tab if you still want the Undo button.
- The document pane's subtitle uses the type code (e.g. "Draft VENDOR_AGREEMENT for …" in DRAFT-05; reported).
- Blanks are not highlighted in the pane or on the contract page.
- The `contract_create_from_template` chip keeps its pause icon after Apply.

### E2E-DRAFT-05 · (GG1) The Assistant works out the type from the agreement's purpose, names it in words, drafts from the newest template of that type, and falls back to a template whose name fits

**Covers:** (`/agent`) · `POST /agent/chat`, `PATCH /templates/:id`, `POST /contracts/bulk-import` · tool `contract_create_from_template` · docs/38: TC-DRAFT-01, TC-DRAFT-02
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- Run command A (as admin-a: "QA Supply Agreement" typed VENDOR_AGREEMENT, published; as counsel-a: an executed NDA
  with QA Meridian Foods, so that counterparty's history points to the wrong type). No other published template is
  typed VENDOR_AGREEMENT, and the Manufacturing pack is not installed (its "Master Supply Agreement" would fit steps
  7–9; PACK-01).
- Command B prints templateName "QA Supply Agreement", contractType "VENDOR_AGREEMENT", title "QA Meridian Foods —
  Vendor Agreement" and unfilledVariables `["effective_date","goods","payment_terms","term","governing_law"]`.
- No Org A contract names QA Kestrel Packaging. Signed in as counsel-a on `/agent`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | **New conversation**; send `We supply raw materials to QA Meridian Foods for their bakery lines. Draft the agreement, New York law.` | Chips `contract_search`, `counterparty_memory`, `contract_create_from_template`; a card "About to run" `contract_create_from_template`, "Undoable", summary `Create a draft vendor agreement for QA Meridian Foods from the template "QA Supply Agreement" — N term(s) left blank to fill in: …` — the type in words, never `VENDOR_AGREEMENT`. |
| 2 | Read the reply. | It opens with one line on what the agreement is for (e.g. "We're supplying raw materials to QA Meridian Foods, so this is a supply agreement."), then names the template and New York law, and lists the blanks. It doesn't say the contract is saved. |
| 3 | **Edit** and read the Arguments. | `contractType` "VENDOR_AGREEMENT" and `templateId` = `$T_SUPPLY` (codes live only here); `title` says what it is (e.g. "QA Meridian Foods — Raw Material Supply Agreement"; without one from the model, "QA Meridian Foods — Vendor Agreement"); `variables` has `our_company` "Demo Org, Inc.", `counterparty_name` "QA Meridian Foods", `governing_law` "New York" (and `goods` only if the model passed it), and no `effective_date`, `payment_terms` or `term`. |
| 4 | **Review**, **Apply**; then **Undo**. | "Applied · Create a draft vendor agreement for QA Meridian Foods…" with **Undo**; the document shows New York and `[[effective_date]]`, `[[payment_terms]]`, `[[term]]` (and `[[goods]]` unless the model filled it); its subtitle reads "Draft VENDOR_AGREEMENT for QA Meridian Foods" (a type code; reported). After Undo: "Undone" and the contract is gone. |
| 5 | **New conversation**; send `We're buying 40 tonnes a month of recycled cardboard packaging from QA Kestrel Packaging. Draft the agreement.` | A card `Create a draft vendor agreement for QA Kestrel Packaging from the template "QA Supply Agreement" — …`; the reply's first line says we're buying packaging from them. **Cancel**. |
| 6 | In step 1's conversation, expand the `contract_search` and `counterparty_memory` chips. Search the text of steps 1, 2 and 5 (answers and card summaries) for `VENDOR_AGREEMENT`, `OTHER`, `ORDER_FORM` and `$T_SUPPLY`'s id. | The chips found the NDA with QA Meridian Foods, and the draft is still a vendor agreement: the purpose decides, past deals are context. No codes or ids in the answers or summaries. |
| 7 | Run command C (retype the fixture so no template has the type), then command B. | `error` "NO_TEMPLATE_MATCH", templateName null, `templates` starting "QA Supply Agreement" (just updated, so newest). |
| 8 | **New conversation**; send step 1's message. Expand the first `contract_create_from_template` chip. | Its row shows "NO TEMPLATE MATCH" in red and its Result lists "QA Supply Agreement". Without asking you anything, the Assistant calls the tool again with that template and shows a card: "a draft vendor agreement" (or "a draft Supply Agreement", the template's own type, when only the template is passed). The reply gives the purpose line, then the template; no question like "Your org doesn't have a vendor agreement template yet — I can use …" comes before the card. **Cancel**. |
| 9 | Run command D (unpublish the fixture). **New conversation**; send step 1's message. | No card. The reply says in plain words that the org has no supply or vendor agreement template and offers the closest templates by name, or suggests creating one in Templates. No template ids, no type codes. A card for an unrelated template (an MSA, say) is the failure this guards against. |
| 10 | Run command E (restore the fixture). | `{"contractType":"VENDOR_AGREEMENT","isPublished":true}`. |
| 11 | Command B without `contractType`, with step 1's message as `userMessage`. | 422 `CONTRACT_TYPE_AMBIGUOUS`: no keyword in "we supply raw materials" names a type; the vendor agreement in step 1 is the model's reading of the purpose. |

Command A:
```bash
export T_SUPPLY=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"QA Supply Agreement","contractType":"VENDOR_AGREEMENT","isPublished":true,"sections":[{"title":"Supply Agreement","content":"<p>This Supply Agreement is made between {{our_company}} and {{counterparty_name}}, effective {{effective_date}}.</p><p>1. Goods. {{goods}}.</p><p>2. Payment. {{payment_terms}}.</p><p>3. Term. {{term}}.</p><p>4. Governing law. The laws of {{governing_law}}.</p>"}]}' | jq -r .id)
printf 'title,type,status,counterpartyname\nQA Meridian Foods — Mutual NDA,NDA,executed,QA Meridian Foods\n' > qa-gg1.csv
curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/bulk-import" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@qa-gg1.csv;type=text/csv" | jq -c .results
echo $T_SUPPLY
```
Command B:
```bash
tj contract_draft '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","userMessage":"supply agreement","contractType":"VENDOR_AGREEMENT","counterpartyName":"QA Meridian Foods"}' \
  | jq '{templateName, contractType, title, unfilledVariables, error, templates: [.templates[]?.name]}'
```

Commands C, D and E:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_SUPPLY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"contractType":"Supply Agreement"}' | jq .contractType
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_SUPPLY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"isPublished":false}' | jq .isPublished
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/templates/$T_SUPPLY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"contractType":"VENDOR_AGREEMENT","isPublished":true}' | jq -c '{contractType, isPublished}'
```

**Also check**
- `draft an offer letter for Jane Doe` reaches the seeded "Employment Offer Letter (At-Will)" (typed "Employment") or
  "QA Offer Letter" (DRAFT-03): the planner's word match or the model's retry picks a template whose name fits.

**Known limits**
- The type from the purpose, the opening line and the retry after `NO_TEMPLATE_MATCH` are the model's behaviour (the
  orchestrator's DRAFT REQUESTS rule): wording varies. Check the card's structure and the absence of codes.
- The planner takes the most recently updated published template of a type: a second VENDOR_AGREEMENT template updated
  later would be used instead of "QA Supply Agreement".
- The retry can only choose among the 20 most recently updated published templates.

**Covers:** (the Assistant side panel on any page; `/admin/skills`) · `POST /agent/threads`, `POST /agent/chat`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/apply`, `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/:toolCallId/undo`, `GET /skills` · tool `contract_create_from_template` · docs/38: —
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

- `$T_NDA` and "Hooli" from DRAFT-03; no Hooli contract. Built-in skills seeded (by `pnpm dev:setup`). Signed in as
  counsel-a on `/templates` (any page that isn't a contract, matter or counterparty page).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click the thin strip at the right edge ("Ask · ⌘K"; hover "Open Ask · ⌘K"). If the panel is already open, click **New thread** in its header instead. | The side panel opens: header "Ask" / "New thread", buttons titled "New thread" and "Collapse rail"; under the header a strip of chips **Draft from scratch** and **Draft from template**; the composer "Ask anything · @ for skills · / for actions". |
| 2 | Hover **Draft from template**. | Tooltip "Wizard-style: pick a template + fill variables → draft a new contract." |
| 3 | Click it. | The composer holds `@draft-from-template ` (nothing is sent). |
| 4 | Type `draft an NDA with Hooli, New York law` after it and press Enter. | Your message shows the chip `@draft-from-template` above it. The reply asks one question at a time (counterparty, value, term, effective date) or describes what it would fill; any tool chips are only `contract_search` or `clause_search`. No "About to run `contract_create_from_template`" card. `curl -s "$API/contracts?search=Hooli" …` → 0. The chip is search-only: the skill allows only those two tools, so it can never draft. |
| 5 | As admin-a: Admin → **Skills**. | The row "@draft-from-template" "Draft from template" (badge "Built-in", scope "dashboard") shows "Tools: contract_search, clause_search". "Draft from scratch" shows "Tools: clause_search, contract_search". |
| 6 | Back as counsel-a: click **New thread** in the panel; send `draft an NDA with Hooli, New York law` (no chip). | Chips `contract_search`, `counterparty_memory`, `contract_create_from_template`, and the card "About to run" … "Undoable" `Create a draft NDA for Hooli from the template "QA Mutual NDA" — …`. |
| 7 | Click **Apply**. | Only the receipt "Applied · Create a draft NDA for Hooli…" with **Undo**. No document pane opens, there is no link to the new contract, and the page underneath doesn't change. |
| 8 | Left rail → Contracts. | "Hooli — NDA" (or the model's title) with status "Draft". |
| 9 | In the panel, click **Undo**. | "Undone · …"; the contract is gone from Contracts (reload). |

**Also check**
- On `/agent`, typing `@` in the composer offers the same skills (picker `@draft-from-template`); with it the reply is
  search-only too.
- On a contract page the panel's chips are the contract skills instead (e.g. Review contract); the two drafting chips
  show only on pages without a contract, matter or counterparty.

**Known limits**
- The side panel shows only a receipt after Apply; open the draft from Contracts, or draft on `/agent` to get the
  document and **Open in Contracts**.
- "Draft from template" and "Draft from scratch" can't produce a draft; to draft, ask without the chip.
## 4. Playbooks, review and negotiation

This section tests how Draft Legal records an organization's negotiating positions and uses them on real contracts. **PB** covers the Playbook page and its API: clause categories, the four positions (preferred, acceptable, fallback, walkaway) with their notes, the contract types a position applies to, the structured limits behind the liability cap, and the "Test playbook" panel. **REV** covers review: the Extraction Queue at `/review-queue` (low-confidence extracted fields), the automatic playbook review of every analysed contract, liability caps measured from the contract's words (DD1), the clause review drawer and its decisions (EE1), "Suggest alternative language" with Apply, and the Assistant's clause tools. **NEG** covers redlining and negotiation: the playbook redline, clause rewrites from the Assistant, version comparison and its Word export, the redline risk analysis (FF1), the counterparty's own Word file with our changes tracked (BB2), and the Google Docs round trip with its lock (BB3, BB4). **PORT** covers the counterparty's side: share links, the external portal, emailed returns, and last the whole third-party-paper flow end to end. Do the setup below first, then run the journeys in the order written: PB, REV, NEG, PORT. Later journeys reuse contracts and links made earlier, and E2E-PORT-04 assumes the pieces before it pass. For depth, journeys cite cases in `docs/38-QA-TEST-CASES-fix-audit-2026-09-22.md` (for example TC-REVQ-01..04 and TC-RISK-01..02) and fix ids in `FIX_TRACKER.md` (AA, BB, CC, DD, EE1, FF1).

### Section 4 setup

**Services and settings**
- The local stack from §0, with the agents service running and a model key set. A journey that calls a model says "Needs: agents service + model key". Model wording changes from run to run, so those steps check structure, fixed text and numbers, not the model's prose.
- The API's background workers run inside the API process that `pnpm dev` starts. Nothing else to start.
- Mailpit (§0). Share-link emails and the owner's "revised version" emails arrive there.
- For E2E-PORT-03 and E2E-PORT-04, inbound email must be switched on: in the repo-root `.env` set `INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET=qa-inbound-secret-123` and `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN=inbound.test`, then restart `pnpm dev` (the API reads `.env` at start). `$INBOUND_SECRET` below means `qa-inbound-secret-123`.
- A browser window at least 1280 px wide unless a step says otherwise. Below 1280 px the contract page's right rail becomes a drawer (open it with the floating **Details** button), the header's **Compare** moves into **Actions → Compare versions**, and the clause review drawer opens as a panel over the page.
- Word, LibreOffice Writer or Google Docs, to open and edit `.docx` files.

**Helpers.** Define these once in the shell you use for API steps (§0 defines `$API`, `$WEB`, the tokens and `$ORG_A`):
```bash
INTERNAL=http://localhost:3001/api/internal/ai    # the tool routes the agents service calls
AGENTS=http://localhost:8002                       # the agents service
COUNSEL_A_ID=$(curl -s $API/users/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r .id)
upload()   { curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${3:-$COUNSEL_A}" -F "file=@$1" -F "title=$2" | jq -r .id; }
status()   { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -c '{title, status, analysisStatus, currentVersionId, versions: (.versions | length)}'; }
versions() { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.data[] | [.versionNumber, .id, .mimeType, .createdByName, .changeNote] | @tsv'; }
clauses()  { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1/clauses" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.data[] | [.id, (.sectionRef // "-"), .clauseType, (.riskRating // "-"), .reviewState] | @tsv'; }
audit()    { curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=$1${2:+&resourceId=$2}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -c '.events[] | {action, at: .createdAt, by: .actor.email, metadata}'; }
catid()    { curl -s $API/clauses/categories -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r --arg n "$1" '.. | objects | select(.name? == $n) | .id' | head -1; }
CAT_LIAB=$(catid "Limitation of Liability"); CAT_INS=$(catid "Insurance")
```

**Files.** Besides §0's `D-MSA.pdf`, `D-NDA.docx` and `D-MARKUP.docx`, make these:
- `D-SUPPLY.docx`: a supplier's services agreement. In Word (or LibreOffice, or Google Docs → File → Download → Microsoft Word), paste this text, one paragraph per line, with the section headings ("1. Services." and so on) in bold, and save it as `D-SUPPLY.docx`:
  ```
  SERVICES AGREEMENT
  This Services Agreement is made on 1 October 2026 between Northwind Supplies Ltd (Supplier) and Demo Org, Inc. (Customer).
  1. Services. Supplier will provide the implementation services described in Schedule 1.
  2. Fees and Payment. Customer shall pay Supplier a fee of USD 12,500 per month. Invoices are payable within fifteen (15) days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month.
  3. Term and Termination. This Agreement starts on the Effective Date and continues for one (1) year. It renews automatically for further one-year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the term. Neither party may terminate for convenience.
  4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the Confidential Information of the other party confidential for two (2) years after termination.
  5. Limitation of Liability. Each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed two (2) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
  6. Indemnification. Customer shall indemnify Supplier against all claims arising from the use of the services by Customer.
  7. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of London have exclusive jurisdiction.
  ```
  §5 is a mutual cap of 24 months' fees with no exclusion of consequential damages; §2 (Net 15), §3 (30 days' non-renewal notice), §4, §6 and §7 sit away from the seeded playbook's preferred positions.
- `D-SUPPLY-v2.docx`: the other side's markup. Copy `D-SUPPLY.docx` and, with Track Changes **off**, make three edits: in §2 change "USD 12,500" to "USD 14,000" and "fifteen (15) days" to "seven (7) days"; at the end of §4 add the sentence "Supplier may use Confidential Information of Customer to improve its products."; in §5 replace "two (2) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months" with "the fees paid or payable in the three (3) months". Sections 2, 4 and 5 change; nothing else does.
- `fake.pdf`: an HTML page with a PDF name: `printf '<html><body>not a pdf</body></html>' > fake.pdf`.
- `img.png`: any small PNG image.

**Contracts.** Upload these as counsel-a at the start; they analyse in parallel (1–3 minutes each). Each is ready when `status <id>` shows `"analysisStatus":"DONE"`. The playbook review of each runs about a minute after that.
```bash
C_SUP=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply A")      # reading and checking: REV-02, REV-03, REV-06, NEG-05
C_REV=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply B")      # the clause review drawer: REV-04, REV-05
C_PBR=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply C")      # the playbook redline: NEG-01, NEG-02
C_RISK=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply D")     # two versions: NEG-03, NEG-04
C_GD=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply E")       # Google Docs: NEG-06
C_SHARE=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply F")    # sharing and the portal: PORT-01, PORT-02
C_MAIL=$(upload D-SUPPLY.docx "E2E Supply G")     # emailed returns: NEG-05 (untouched), PORT-03
C_PDF=$(upload D-MSA.pdf "E2E MSA PDF")           # a PDF upload: REV-06, NEG-05, NEG-06
```
When `C_RISK` is analysed, add its second version (there is no upload-a-version button on the contract page; this is the API behind it) and wait for DONE again:
```bash
curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_RISK/versions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@D-SUPPLY-v2.docx" | jq '{versionNumber}'
```
- The first analysis can rename a contract after its document ("Services Agreement – Northwind Supplies", say). The variables hold ids; steps say "open `$C_SUP`" meaning `$WEB/contracts/$C_SUP`.
- counsel-a owns all of them, so counsel-a receives their owner notifications.

**Org C (optional, throwaway).** Two checks need an organization with no playbook positions. Register it at `$WEB/register` as for Org B in §0 (for example `qa-empty-playbook@example.test`, org "QA Empty Playbook"); `$ADMIN_C` is its token. Registration seeds the standard playbook a few seconds later; then delete every position:
```bash
for id in $(curl -s $API/playbook/positions -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_C" | jq -r '.data[].id'); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$id %{http_code}\n" -X DELETE $API/playbook/positions/$id -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_C"; done
```

**Who can do what in this section** (system roles, `apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts`):

| Role | See the playbook, Test playbook | Add and edit positions | Delete positions | Change contracts: drawer decisions, Suggest/Apply, redlines, Google Docs, Extraction Queue fixes | Share links | See contracts, diffs, Word downloads, playbook review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ADMIN (admin-a) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| LEGAL_COUNSEL (counsel-a) | yes | yes | no | yes | no | yes |
| LEGAL_OPS (legalops-a) | yes | yes | no | yes | no | yes |
| CONTRACT_MANAGER (contracts-a) | yes | no | no | yes | no | yes |
| PROCUREMENT (procurement-a) | no | no | no | yes | no | yes |
| VIEWER (viewer-a) | yes | no | no | no | no | yes |
| FINANCE, APPROVER | no | no | no | no | no | yes |
| SALES_REP (rep-a) | no | no | no | no | no | own contracts only |

The API refuses a missing permission with 403 and `detail` "Missing permission: <action>:<resource>". The web app hides some controls from users who can't use them (Share, Edit in Google Docs, the drawer's decision buttons). For the others it shows the control and refuses the request in the browser before sending it, with the message "You don't have permission to <action> <resource>s." Several screens in this section never display that message; the journeys say where.

**Two different "queues".** The sidebar's **Queues → Extraction Queue** (`/review-queue`) lists low-confidence AI-extracted fields across contracts (E2E-REV-01). The clause review drawer on a contract page steps through that contract's flagged clauses still waiting on a decision (E2E-REV-04). They are unrelated.

**Labels.** Rail section titles, eyebrow labels and a few badges are drawn in capitals by the stylesheet. This section writes them as the code does ("Playbook review"); on screen they read PLAYBOOK REVIEW.

**Audit checks.** The `audit` helper (it runs as admin-a) is the reliable check. Events about one contract also appear on that contract's Activity: open any tab other than the document (for example rail **Clauses** → **View all**) and click **Activity** in the tab bar, where each event is listed in capitals ("LINK SHARED") with the acting user's id. The rail's own **Activity** section shows only the latest eight. Every load of the contract, including the page's automatic refresh every 4 seconds while an analysis or redline runs, adds a "CONTRACT VIEWED" row, so look through the list rather than at its top.

### E2E-PB-01 · Each clause category shows how much of its ladder is written, and every position on it can be read

**Covers:** /playbook · `GET /playbook/positions` · `GET /playbook/positions/:id`
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, finance-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra (Org C for one check) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Org A as `pnpm dev:setup` seeds it: the standard playbook (18 clause categories; most have three or four positions), with structured rules on the Limitation of Liability positions.
- `$CAT_LIAB` from the section setup.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Sign in as counsel-a. Left rail → **Library** → **Playbook**. | `/playbook` opens. The left column has the heading "Playbook", the line "Negotiation positions per clause type", and the categories in order: Definitions & Interpretation, Scope of Services, Fees & Payment, Term & Termination, Confidentiality, Intellectual Property, … Service Levels & Performance (plus any category another section added). Each row ends in four small ticks, filled for each rung that has a position; hovering them shows "N of 4 positions defined". The first category with positions (Definitions & Interpretation) is already selected. |
| 2 | Read the right side for Definitions & Interpretation. | The heading "Definitions & Interpretation", the line "3 of 4 positions defined — missing acceptable", the tip "Tip: paste a clause into Test playbook to see which position it matches.", and the buttons **Test playbook** and **Add Position** "(1 left)". Below, the ladder in order: a PREFERRED card, a dashed ACCEPTABLE card reading "What we sign without escalating." and "Define this position", a FALLBACK card, a WALKAWAY card. |
| 3 | Click **Limitation of Liability**. | "All 4 positions defined · 4 in total". Four cards: PREFERRED ("Liability cap of 2x annual fees. Super-cap of 3x for data breach. Carve-outs: …"), ACCEPTABLE ("Liability cap of 12 months fees. …"), FALLBACK, WALKAWAY ("Liability cap < 6 months fees, OR …"). Each card shows its language, its notes in italics, a short bar and "matches at 70%+" / "50%+" / "40%+" / "20%+". The card colours run brand, neutral, amber, red down the ladder. The Limitation of Liability row's ticks are all filled. |
| 4 | Click **Intellectual Property**. | "3 of 4 positions defined — missing fallback". Two ACCEPTABLE cards are both listed (the category has two positions on that rung), then a dashed FALLBACK card "What we concede, reluctantly." **Add Position** reads "Add Position (1 left)" with the tooltip "Add fallback position". |
| 5 | Click **Insurance**, then **Fees & Payment**. | Insurance: "3 of 4 positions defined — missing fallback". Fees & Payment: all four, with the fallback "Net 15 payment terms with dispute right. Annual escalation cap of 7%." The empty-rung texts are preferred "What we open with.", acceptable "What we sign without escalating.", fallback "What we concede, reluctantly.", walkaway "What we refuse." |
| 6 | Command A. | Four positions, one per rung, each with `contractTypes: []` (applies to every contract type). `preferred` and `walkaway` have rules; the others have none. `grouped` has one entry, for Limitation of Liability. |
| 7 | Command B with the preferred position's id from step 6. | 200: the position with its `clauseCategory` (name "Limitation of Liability"), `content`, `notes`, `riskThreshold` 0.7, `contractTypes` [] and `rules` (see E2E-PB-03). |
| 8 | Command B with a made-up id. | 404 `{"detail":"Position not found"}`. |

Command A (the Limitation of Liability positions):
```bash
curl -s "$API/playbook/positions?clauseCategoryId=$CAT_LIAB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \
  | jq '{positions: [.data[] | {id, positionType, riskThreshold, contractTypes, hasRules: (.rules != null)}], grouped: [.grouped[].category.name]}'
```
Command B (one position): `curl -s "$API/playbook/positions/<id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{positionType, category: .clauseCategory.name, riskThreshold, contractTypes, notes, hasRules: (.rules != null)}'`

**Also check**
- Nested categories. Command C creates a child of Limitation of Liability (counsel-a may create clause categories). Reload `/playbook`. The Limitation of Liability row now has a chevron. Clicking the row selects it and expands it; the child "E2E Data-breach liability" appears indented under a left border with its own ticks. Selecting the child titles the panel "E2E Data-breach liability" with "0 of 4 positions defined — missing preferred, acceptable, fallback, walkaway", four dashed cards and no tip line. Clicking the parent again collapses it. Keep the child for E2E-PB-04.
- Filters: `curl -s "$API/playbook/positions?positionType=walkaway" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '[.data[].positionType] | unique'` → `["walkaway"]`.
- rep-a (SALES_REP, no `view:playbook`): `/playbook` shows the empty-playbook explainer: "What's a playbook?", the paragraph "A playbook captures your preferred, acceptable, and reject-worthy positions for each clause type. …", the button **Start with your first clause category**, and four faded sample cards under "Example — Limitation of Liability", with "Preview — pick a category on the left to start defining your own positions." Picking a category shows "0 of 4 positions defined — missing preferred, acceptable, fallback, walkaway". Nothing says the playbook is hidden from this role (known defect, reported). The API: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' $API/playbook/positions -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A"` → 403, `detail` "Missing permission: view:playbook". procurement-a sees the same.
- finance-a (FINANCE: no `view:clause`, no `view:playbook`): the category list is empty and the explainer has no button.
- The explainer in its intended place: in Org C (every position deleted), `/playbook` shows the same explainer, and **Start with your first clause category** selects Definitions & Interpretation with four dashed cards.
- admin-b (Org B): `/playbook` lists Org B's own seeded playbook. Command B as admin-b with an Org A position id → 404 `{"detail":"Position not found"}`.

Command C (a child category): 
```bash
CAT_CHILD=$(curl -s -X POST $API/clauses/categories -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"E2E Data-breach liability","parentCategoryId":"'$CAT_LIAB'"}' | jq -r .id)
```

**Known limits**
- The page never shows which contract types a position applies to, or its structured rules. Use the API (E2E-PB-03).
- Known defect, reported: every seeded position's notes begin with an internal marker, for example "[seed-key:pb-liab-cap-preferred] Buy-side preferred — wide carve-outs." The marker also shows in the review drawer's "Playbook comparison".
- Known defect, reported: a role without playbook access sees an empty-looking playbook instead of a refusal.

### E2E-PB-02 · Legal adds and edits positions, only an admin can delete one, and other roles are refused

**Covers:** /playbook · `POST /playbook/positions` · `PATCH /playbook/positions/:id` · `DELETE /playbook/positions/:id` · `GET /playbook/positions/:id`
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, legalops-a, contracts-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra (Org C for one check) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Org A's Insurance category has preferred, acceptable and walkaway positions and no fallback (as seeded). `$CAT_INS` from the setup.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|

Click **Add Position (1 left)**. | A modal "New Position": "Position Type" with four buttons (preferred, acceptable, fallback, walkaway), **fallback** selected; "Position Language" (a text editor); "Legal Team Notes" with placeholder "Guidance for the legal team..."; "Risk Threshold: 50%" with a slider running from "Walk away" to "Preferred"; **Cancel** and **Save Position**. |
| 2 | Type in Position Language: `CGL $1M/$2M and Cyber $1M; certificates of insurance on request.` Notes: `E2E fallback for low-risk vendors`. Move the slider to 40%. Click **Save Position**. | The modal closes. A FALLBACK card shows the language, the notes in italics and "matches at 40%+". The heading line reads "All 4 positions defined · 4 in total", **Add Position** loses its "(1 left)", and Insurance's ticks in the left column are all filled. |
| 3 | Command A. Note the new position's `id` as `$POS`. | `content` `<p>CGL $1M/$2M and Cyber $1M; certificates of insurance on request.</p>`, `notes` "E2E fallback for low-risk vendors", `riskThreshold` 0.4, `contractTypes` [], `createdById` = `$COUNSEL_A_ID`. |
| 4 | Click the pencil on the new card. | "Edit Position", with fallback selected, the saved language and notes, and "Risk Threshold: 40%". |
| 5 | Change the type to **acceptable** and the notes to `E2E edited`. **Save Position**. | The card moves to the acceptable rung (two ACCEPTABLE cards now) with the new notes. The fallback rung is a dashed "Define this position" card again, and the line reads "3 of 4 positions defined — missing fallback". |
| 6 | Pencil on it again → type **fallback** → **Save Position**. | Back on the fallback rung; "All 4 positions defined · 4 in total". |
| 7 | Click **Add Position** (tooltip "Add another position to this category"). | "New Position" opens on **preferred**: a full ladder still takes a second position on a rung. |
| 8 | Language `E2E second preferred`, **Save Position**. | Two PREFERRED cards; "All 4 positions defined · 5 in total". |
| 9 | Click the bin icon on "E2E second preferred". Press Esc. | A dialog "Delete this position?": "The Preferred position for Insurance will be removed, and drafting and review will stop scoring against it. This can't be undone." with **Cancel** and **Delete position**. Esc closes it; nothing is deleted. Clicking outside the dialog also closes it. |
| 10 | Bin again → **Delete position**. | The dialog closes and the card is still there. counsel-a (LEGAL_COUNSEL) has no `delete:playbook`; the browser refuses the request and nothing on screen says so (known defect, reported). |
| 11 | `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE $API/playbook/positions/<id of E2E second preferred> -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` | 403, `detail` "Missing permission: delete:playbook". |
| 12 | Sign in as admin-a → Playbook → Insurance → bin on "E2E second preferred" → **Delete position**. | The card disappears; "All 4 positions defined · 4 in total". Command B with its id → 404 `{"detail":"Position not found"}`. |
| 13 | As admin-a delete the E2E fallback (`$POS`) the same way. | The fallback rung is "Define this position" again; "3 of 4 positions defined — missing fallback"; Insurance shows three of four ticks. |

Command A: `curl -s "$API/playbook/positions?clauseCategoryId=$CAT_INS" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.data[] | {id, positionType, content, notes, riskThreshold, contractTypes, createdById}'`
Command B: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' "$API/playbook/positions/<id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"`

**Also check**
- legalops-a: adding and editing work as for counsel-a; deleting is refused the same way, silently in the page and 403 "Missing permission: delete:playbook" from the API.
- contracts-a and viewer-a (view only): the cards, **Add Position**, pencils and bins all show. **Save Position** leaves the modal open and saves nothing, with no message (the browser console shows "You don't have permission to create playbooks."; known defect, reported). API: `POST /playbook/positions` as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: create:playbook"; `PATCH /playbook/positions/<id>` as contracts-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:playbook".
- rep-a and procurement-a: `GET /playbook/positions/<id>` → 403 "Missing permission: view:playbook".
- admin-b (Org B): `PATCH` or `DELETE` an Org A position → 404 `{"detail":"Position not found"}`; `POST` with `"clauseCategoryId":"$CAT_INS"` (Org A's) → 404 `{"detail":"Clause category not found"}`.
- Validation (as counsel-a, `POST $API/playbook/positions`): `"positionType":"ideal"`, `"riskThreshold":1.5`, notes longer than 2,048 characters, or no `clauseCategoryId` → 422, `detail` "Request body failed validation". A `PATCH` carrying `"clauseCategoryId"` ignores it: a position can't move to another category.
- The audit log records nothing for any playbook change: `audit` finds no event, and the category has no activity feed (known limit).
- Re-seeding (Org C only; it adds industry content, and Org C starts with an empty playbook from the setup): as admin-c run `curl -s -X POST $API/organization/install-industry-pack -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_C" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"packId":"saas"}'`. Reload `/playbook`: every standard position deleted in the setup is back, next to the pack's own. Then open Insurance, edit its preferred position and replace the whole notes text with `E2E edited` (this drops the "[seed-key:…]" marker), and install a second pack the same way with `{"packId":"healthcare"}`. Insurance now shows two PREFERRED cards: the edited one and a fresh copy of the standard one (known defect, reported: installing a pack re-runs the standard seed, which recognises its positions only by the marker in their notes). Afterwards run the setup's delete loop again, so Org C's playbook is empty for E2E-REV-02.

**Known limits**
- Playbook changes are not in the audit log.
- The editor has no field for contract types or rules; see E2E-PB-03.
- Known defect, reported: refused saves and deletes give no message on this page.

### E2E-PB-03 · A position applies only to the contract types it names, and the liability positions carry measured limits

**Covers:** `POST /playbook/positions` · `PATCH /playbook/positions/:id` · `GET /playbook/positions` · `GET /playbook/positions/:id` · `DELETE /playbook/positions/:id` · `POST /playbook/test`
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `$CAT_LIAB`. There is no screen for contract types or rules: every step here is an API call, plus one look at the Playbook page.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Command A (creates an NDA-only fallback on Limitation of Liability). Save its `id` as `$POS_NDA`. | 201 with `"contractTypes":["NDA"]`. |
| 2 | Command B with `NDA`, then with `MSA`. | NDA: five positions, the four seeded ones (`contractTypes` []) and `$POS_NDA`. MSA: the four seeded ones only. A position with no contract types applies to every type; one with types applies only to those. |
| 3 | Open **Playbook** → **Limitation of Liability**. | A second FALLBACK card "E2E NDA-only: cap of 6 months' fees." Nothing on it says it applies only to NDAs (known limit). |
| 4 | Command C (every seeded position pinned to types). | Scope of Services `["MSA","SOW"]`, Term & Termination acceptable `["SaaS","Subscription"]`, Intellectual Property `["SOW","Professional Services"]` and `["SaaS","Subscription"]`, Representations & Warranties `["SOW","Professional Services"]`, and all four Service Levels & Performance positions `["SaaS","Subscription"]`. A contract's type is one of NDA, MSA, SOW, SLA, VENDOR_AGREEMENT, EMPLOYMENT, PARTNERSHIP, LICENSE, DATA_PROCESSING, ORDER_FORM, OTHER, so the positions pinned only to "SaaS", "Subscription" or "Professional Services" apply to no contract (known defect, reported). |
| 5 | Command D (the liability rules). | `preferred`: must-have `lol.mutual_cap`, `lol.consequential_damages_carveout`, `lol.cap_is_stated`; must-not `lol.uncapped`, `lol.uncapped_2`; bounds `liability_cap_months` {min 6, max 24, units "months of fees", severity "high"} and `cap_multiplier_of_annual` {max 3, units "x annual contract value", severity "walkaway"}. `walkaway`: the two must-not rules only. If both are null, run `pnpm --filter api exec tsx scripts/seed-playbook-rules.ts` from the repo root and repeat. E2E-REV-03 shows these limits applied to a contract. |
| 6 | `curl -s -X PATCH $API/playbook/positions/$POS_NDA -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"rules":{"bounds":{}},"notes":"E2E types (edited)"}' \| jq '{notes, rules}'` | 200 with the new notes and `"rules": null`: rules can't be written through the API; only the seed script sets them. |
| 7 | Command E with the Service Levels & Performance category (`CAT_SLA=$(catid "Service Levels & Performance")`) and `"contractType":"MSA"`. No model is called for this answer. | 404 `{"detail":"No playbook positions found for this category"}`: all four of that category's positions are pinned to types an MSA isn't. (With `$CAT_LIAB` and a running agents service, the same call scores the clause against the positions that apply to MSAs.) |
| 8 | `PATCH $POS_NDA` with `{"contractTypes":[]}`, then Command B with `MSA`. | Five positions: with no types it applies to every contract. |
| 9 | As admin-a: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE $API/playbook/positions/$POS_NDA -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` | 204. The extra fallback card is gone from the page. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST $API/playbook/positions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"clauseCategoryId":"'$CAT_LIAB'","positionType":"fallback","content":"<p>E2E NDA-only: cap of 6 months'"'"' fees.</p>","notes":"E2E types","contractTypes":["NDA"]}' | jq '{id, contractTypes}'
```
Command B: `curl -s "$API/playbook/positions?clauseCategoryId=$CAT_LIAB&contractType=<TYPE>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '[.data[] | {positionType, contractTypes, content: .content[0:50]}]'`
Command C: `curl -s $API/playbook/positions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '[.data[] | select(.contractTypes | length > 0) | {category: .clauseCategory.name, positionType, contractTypes}]'`
Command D: `curl -s "$API/playbook/positions?clauseCategoryId=$CAT_LIAB" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.data[] | select(.rules != null) | {positionType, mustHave: [.rules.must_have[]?.id], mustNot: [.rules.must_not[]?.id], bounds: .rules.bounds}'`
Command E: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/playbook/test -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"clauseText":"Each party'"'"'s liability is capped at 12 months of fees.","clauseCategoryId":"<category id>","contractType":"MSA"}'`

**Also check**
- `contractTypes` takes any strings, including ones no contract can have (`["Anything"]` → 201); nothing warns (known defect, reported, with step 4).
- The same type filter decides which positions reach the automatic playbook review (E2E-REV-02), the redline analysis (E2E-NEG-04) and `playbook_check` (E2E-REV-03). `POST /playbook/test` from the page sends no contract type, so it compares every position in the category.

**Known limits**
- Contract types and rules are invisible on the Playbook page; rules can only be set by `scripts/seed-playbook-rules.ts`, and only the Limitation of Liability positions have them.

### E2E-PB-04 · "Test playbook" scores a pasted clause against a category's positions

**Covers:** /playbook · `POST /playbook/test` · agent service: `assist` (its `/compare` endpoint)
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `$CAT_CHILD` "E2E Data-breach liability" from E2E-PB-01 (a category with no positions).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: **Playbook** → **Limitation of Liability** → **Test playbook**. | The button now reads **Hide test panel** and looks pressed; the tip line goes. A "Test Mode" panel opens with a text box ("Paste a clause to test against your playbook...") and **Test Clause**, disabled while the box is empty. |
| 2 | Paste `Each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid in the three (3) months preceding the claim, including consequential damages.` → **Test Clause**. | The button reads "Analyzing..." and then the result appears: a pill "<RUNG> MATCH" (for a 3-month cap, normally "WALKAWAY MATCH"), "Score: NN%", a two- or three-sentence explanation, and a list of deviations, each "<Position type>: <difference>", tinted red (high), amber (medium) or grey (low). |
| 3 | Replace the text with `Liability is capped at two times the annual fees, with a super-cap of three times the annual fees for data breach. The cap does not apply to confidentiality, IP indemnification, payment obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct.` → **Test Clause**. | Normally "PREFERRED MATCH" with a higher score than step 2. The pill always names one of the four rungs, or reads "NO CLEAR MATCH" when the answer names none. |
| 4 | Click **Hide test panel**. | The panel closes and the tip line returns. |
| 5 | Expand Limitation of Liability, select **E2E Data-breach liability** → **Test playbook** → paste any clause → **Test Clause**. | A red box "No playbook positions found for this category". |
| 6 | `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/playbook/test -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"clauseText":"   ","clauseCategoryId":"'$CAT_LIAB'"}'` | 400 `{"detail":"clauseText is required"}`. |

**Also check**
- viewer-a can run the test (`view:playbook`) and gets a result.
- rep-a: the page shows no positions (E2E-PB-01). If rep-a opens the panel on a category and tests, the red box reads "You don't have permission to view playbooks." The API: `POST /playbook/test` as rep-a → 403 "Missing permission: view:playbook".
- Agents service stopped: **Test Clause** shows "NO CLEAR MATCH" and "Score: 0%" with no explanation. The API answered 200 with `"comparison":null` and `"warning":"Agent service unavailable — returning positions without AI comparison"`, which the panel doesn't show (known defect, reported). Start the agents service again.
- The agents service's endpoint refuses callers without the shared secret: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/compare -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` → `{"error":"unauthorized"} 401`. With `-H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET"` and `-d '{"clauseText":"x","positions":[]}'` → 400 `{"detail":"positions are required"}` (no model call).
- Personal data in the pasted clause reaches the model masked, and the result reads with the real values (TC-PII-09).

**Known limits**
- The page's test compares every position in the category, whatever contract types they name.
- The explanation and score are the model's; they vary between runs.

### E2E-REV-01 · Low-confidence extracted fields land in the Extraction Queue and are verified, corrected or rejected

**Covers:** /review-queue · `GET /review-queue` · `POST /review-queue/:contractId/verify` · `POST /review-queue/:contractId/reject` · docs/38 TC-WF-09
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**What lands here.** When the analysis extracts a key field (counterparty, dates, value, currency, governing law, jurisdiction, auto-renew, renewal term, notice period, liability cap, exclusivity, IP ownership, indemnification, termination) it records a confidence for it. Every field under the chosen threshold, on a contract whose analysis is DONE (or INDEXING), that nobody has verified or rejected yet, is listed here, lowest confidence first.

**Preconditions**
- Fixture `$C_Q` (Command A): a contract with six low-confidence fields, written the way the extraction writes them. No model needed.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: left rail → **Queues** → **Extraction Queue**. | `/review-queue` opens: heading "Extraction Queue"; the line "AI-extracted fields below the confidence threshold. Verify (keep the value), correct (set a new value), or reject (clear the value) — each contract stops carrying a silent low-confidence extraction."; top right "<N> items · threshold 70%"; a filter box "Filter by contract, field, value or quote…"; a dropdown set to "Legal bar (<0.7)". |
| 2 | Find the "E2E extraction queue" group. | A header with the contract title (a link), "OTHER", "6 flagged fields" and **Open contract**. Rows, lowest confidence first: Counterparty (`counterpartyName`) "Wrong Co" “Wrong Co” 30%; Notice period (`noticePeriod`) "(nothing extracted)" 35%; Expiry date "2026-12-31" 40%; Effective date "2026-01-01" 45%; Contract value "1000" 50%; Governing law "Delaware" 60%. Each row shows the quote in italics, a confidence chip (tooltip "Extractor confidence: 30%"), and **Correct**, **Reject** and **Verify**. The Notice period row has **Correct** and **Not present** only: there is nothing to reject. |
| 3 | Set the dropdown to **Risky only (<0.5)**, then **High bar (<0.9)**, then back to **Legal bar (<0.7)**. | Under 50% the group keeps Counterparty, Notice period, Expiry date and Effective date, and the header says "threshold 50%". Under 90% all six show (and other contracts' fields up to 89%). |
| 4 | Type `Delaware` in the filter; then `zzz`; then clear it. | `Delaware`: only rows whose contract, field, value or quote contains it (Governing law). `zzz`: `Nothing matches "zzz" at this threshold.` and "Clear the filter, or widen the threshold." |
| 5 | Open `$WEB/review-queue?contractId=$C_Q`. Click **Showing one contract — show all**. | Only the E2E group, with the link "Showing one contract — show all" under the description; after the click, every contract's fields again. |
| 6 | Expiry date → **Correct**. Replace the value with `2031-03-31` → **Save**. | The input opened with "2026-12-31" and **Save** / **Cancel**. After Save the row leaves the queue and the count drops by one. Command B: `expiryDate` "2031-03-31T00:00:00.000Z", `keyTerms.expiryDate` "2031-03-31", `fieldConfidence.expiryDate.confidence` 1 with `verifiedAt` and `verifiedBy` = `$COUNSEL_A_ID`. |
| 7 | Effective date → **Correct** → type `next spring` → press Enter. | A toast "Correction not saved" with "Enter the date as YYYY-MM-DD."; the input stays open and the row stays. Esc closes the input. |
| 8 | Contract value → **Correct** → `12,500` → **Save**. Governing law → **Correct** → `New York` → **Save**. | Both rows leave. Command B: `value` "12500" (the column is a decimal, sent as a string) and `keyTerms.value` 12500; `jurisdiction` "New York" and `keyTerms.governingLaw` "New York" (governing law is where the jurisdiction column comes from). |
| 9 | Counterparty → **Reject**. | The row leaves. Command B: `counterpartyName` null, no `counterpartyName` in `keyTerms`, and `fieldConfidence.counterpartyName` with `confidence` 0, `rejectedAt` and `rejectedBy`. Opening the contract shows "—" for Counterparty in the rail's Key Terms. |
| 10 | Notice period → **Not present**; Effective date → **Verify**. | Both rows leave; the effective date keeps "2026-01-01". |
| 11 | Reload `$WEB/review-queue?contractId=$C_Q`. | "Nothing to review at this threshold." with "Try widening it to surface more." Verified and rejected fields never come back. |
| 12 | `audit CONTRACT_UPDATED $C_Q` | One event per action, each naming the field but not the value: `{"source":"review_queue","action":"corrected","field":"expiryDate"}`, `…"corrected","field":"value"`, `…"corrected","field":"governingLaw"`, `…"rejected","field":"counterpartyName"`, `…"verified","field":"noticePeriod"`, `…"verified","field":"effectiveDate"`. The contract's Activity lists them as "CONTRACT UPDATED". |

Command A (fixture `$C_Q`, owned by counsel-a):
```bash
C_Q=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"E2E extraction queue","type":"OTHER","counterpartyName":"Wrong Co","value":1000,"currency":"USD","effectiveDate":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","expiryDate":"2026-12-31T00:00:00.000Z"}' | jq -r .id)
curl -s -X PATCH $API/contracts/$C_Q -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jurisdiction":"Delaware",
  "keyTerms":{"counterpartyName":"Wrong Co","effectiveDate":"2026-01-01","expiryDate":"2026-12-31","value":1000,"governingLaw":"Delaware"},
  "fieldConfidence":{"counterpartyName":{"confidence":0.3,"quote":"Wrong Co"},"noticePeriod":{"confidence":0.35,"quote":null},
    "expiryDate":{"confidence":0.4,"quote":"ends on 31 December 2026"},"effectiveDate":{"confidence":0.45,"quote":"starts on 1 January 2026"},
    "value":{"confidence":0.5,"quote":"a fee of USD 1,000"},"governingLaw":{"confidence":0.6,"quote":"the laws of Delaware"}}}' | jq -c '{id, fields: (.fieldConfidence | keys)}'
```
Command B: `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_Q -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{counterpartyName, expiryDate, value, jurisdiction, keyTerms, fieldConfidence}'`

**Also check**
- From a contract: on an analysed upload whose Key Terms include a field under 70% (for example `$C_SUP`, if it has one), open the contract → rail **Clauses** → **View all** → tab bar **Overview** → the **Key Terms** card shows "Review N low-confidence fields" → it opens `/review-queue?contractId=<id>` with those N fields.
- viewer-a sees the page (it needs only `view:contract`). **Verify** gives the toast "Correction not saved" with "You don't have permission to edit contracts."; **Reject** gives "Could not clear the value" with the same text. The rows stay. API: `POST /review-queue/$C_Q/reject` as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract".
- rep-a sees only fields of contracts rep-a owns: `curl -s $API/review-queue -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" | jq '[.items[].contractId] | index("'$C_Q'")'` → `null`. Verifying `$C_Q` as rep-a → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- admin-b: the Org A group isn't listed; `POST /review-queue/$C_Q/verify` → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- Validation: a value correction `{"field":"value","value":"twelve"}` → 400 `{"detail":"Enter the value as a number, e.g. 250000."}`; `?threshold=2` or a body without `field` → 422 "Request body failed validation".
- On an APPROVED contract, correcting or rejecting Contract value or Currency sends it back to DRAFT, and the audit event adds `statusFrom`/`statusTo` (TC-WF-04).
- Diligence-room contracts stay out of this queue unless `?diligenceRoomId=<room>` is given (TC-WF-15).

**Known limits**
- The page lists at most 200 items; the header's count is the full total.
- This queue is about extracted fields. Clause-by-clause review is the drawer on the contract page (E2E-REV-04).

### E2E-REV-02 · Every analysed contract is reviewed against the playbook, and the rail lists the findings in document order

**Covers:** `GET /contracts/:id/playbook-review` · agent service: `playbook_review` · background: the `playbook-review` job queued when extraction finishes, and again after an edit · docs/38 TC-AI-08
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key (Org C for one check) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_SUP` analysed, and its review stored: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $API/contracts/$C_SUP/playbook-review -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` prints 200. The review starts when the analysis finishes and takes up to a minute or two; until then the call returns 404 with `"reason":"not_run"`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_SUP`. In the right rail find **Playbook review** (below "Playbook redline", above "Compliance"); it is open by default. | Its header count equals the number of findings. Inside: a summary "N of M clause(s) deviate from the playbook (<n> high, <n> medium, …)." (M is the number of clauses extraction found, about 7 for `D-SUPPLY.docx`); an ordered list of findings; a footer "M clauses reviewed · <date>". When any clause is at a walkaway position, outside the playbook, or critical, a red banner reads "Legal review required — a clause is at a walkaway position, outside the playbook, or critical." |
| 2 | Read the findings. | Each shows a severity chip (critical, high, medium, low), the clause type, "§<section>", the recommendation on the right (accept, negotiate, reject), the alignment in words ("preferred", "acceptable", "fallback position", "walkaway position", "outside the playbook", "no playbook position") and a one-sentence reason. On `D-SUPPLY.docx` the findings normally include §3 (30 days' non-renewal notice), §4 (two years, no trade-secret carve-out), §6 (one-sided indemnity) and §7 (English law); the model decides the exact set. Any finding for §5 is about the missing exclusion of consequential damages, not the size of the cap (E2E-REV-03). |
| 3 | Command A. | Findings in ascending `sortOrder` (document order, not the model's), each with `sectionRef` and `excerpt` (at most 240 characters of the clause). `versionId` equals the contract's `currentVersionId`; `clausesReviewed` M; `playbookPositions` is the number of positions that apply to the contract's type. |
| 4 | Click a finding (tooltip "Go to this clause"). | If the clause is marked in the document (a red or blue underline in the Styled view), the page scrolls to it and outlines it for a moment. Otherwise the clause review drawer opens on it (E2E-REV-04). |
| 5 | Header **Edit** → in §7 change "England and Wales" to "the State of New York" → wait for "Saved ✓" → **Done**. Reload the page and run Command A. | The rail still shows the old review. In the API, the §7 finding (if there is one) now points at the clause in the new version and carries `"changedSinceReview": true`. |
| 6 | Wait about two minutes after the edit, reload, run Command A again. | The review has been redone on the new version: `versionId` is the new `currentVersionId`, `reviewedAt` is newer, and §7 is normally no longer flagged for its governing law. |

Command A: `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_SUP/playbook-review -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{summary, requiresHumanGate, clausesReviewed, playbookPositions, versionId, reviewedAt, findings: [.findings[] | {sortOrder, sectionRef, clauseType, severity, recommendation, playbookAlignment, changedSinceReview, excerpt: (.excerpt // "")[0:60]}]}'`

**Also check**
- A contract with nothing to score against (Org C, every position deleted): as admin-c upload `D-NDA.docx` and wait for the analysis. Its **Playbook review** reads "No playbook positions apply to <type> contracts, so there is nothing to score this contract against." with the link **Add positions in Playbook** (opens `/playbook`). The API: 404 with `"reason":"no_positions"`, `"playbookPositionCount":0`, `contractType`, and `detail` "No playbook positions apply to <TYPE> contracts, so this contract has not been reviewed against a playbook." Add one position on the Playbook page and reload: "Not reviewed yet. The playbook review runs automatically once the contract has been analysed."; the API gives `"reason":"not_run"`, `playbookPositionCount` ≥ 1 and "No playbook review has been run for this contract yet. It runs automatically after extraction."
- When a review finds nothing, the rail says "Every reviewed clause matches a preferred position."
- rep-a on a contract rep-a doesn't own, and admin-b on `$C_SUP`: 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`, with no `reason` or counts.
- The agents service endpoint itself, without a model: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/playbook-review -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"contractId":"qa"}'` → `{"error":"unauthorized"} 401`. With `-H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET"`: `{"contractId":"qa","clauses":[]}` → 200 with `"summary":"No clauses were extracted for this contract."`; `{"contractId":"qa","clauses":[{"id":"c1","clauseType":"payment","content":"Pay within 15 days."}],"playbookPositions":[]}` → `"summary":"No playbook positions are configured for this org, so the contract could not be scored against one."`, `"clausesReviewed":1`.
- The API process log shows `[agent-worker] playbook-review done contractId=<id> findings=N gate=<true|false>` when a review is stored.
- The clauses reach the model with personal data masked (TC-PII-01).

**Known limits**
- The rail doesn't refresh when a review finishes; reload the page.
- There is no button or route to run the review by hand. It runs when extraction finishes, and two minutes after an edit that changes a clause's words (at most once per contract every two minutes). Re-analysing the same version does not run it again.
- The summary counts findings, and a finding can recommend "accept" at "preferred" (TC-AI-08 P1).

### E2E-REV-03 · A liability cap is measured from its words and judged against the playbook's limits (DD1)

**Covers:** tool: `playbook_check` (its route `POST /api/internal/ai/tools/playbook_check`) · `GET /contracts/:id/playbook-review` · FIX_TRACKER DD1, DD2
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** steps 1–2 and 5–8 nothing extra; steps 3–4 agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_SUP` analysed, with §5 as written in `D-SUPPLY.docx` (if E2E-REV-02 changed only §7, that's fine). The liability rules are seeded (E2E-PB-03 step 5). `$COUNSEL_A_ID` and `$INTERNAL_SECRET`.
- Command A, which calls the tool route as the agents service does for a chat about this contract:
```bash
pbcheck() { curl -s -X POST $INTERNAL/tools/playbook_check -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'x-internal-service: agents' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$1'","maxClauses":100}'; }
pbcheck $C_SUP | jq '.checks[] | select(.category.name == "Limitation of Liability") | {sectionRef, capAnalysis, worstSeverity, passed, violations: [.violations[] | {kind, rule: (.ruleId // .boundKey), passed, severity, reason}]}'
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Command A. | One check, §5. `capAnalysis`: ["Each party's cap: 2 × the fees of the 12 months before the claim = 24 months of fees, 2 times a year's fees."]. Violations: `lol.mutual_cap` passed true ("each party's aggregate liability" counts as mutual); `lol.cap_is_stated` true ("two (2) times … twelve (12) months" counts as stated); `lol.consequential_damages_carveout` **false**, severity high; `lol.uncapped` and `lol.uncapped_2` true, each listed once although two positions carry them; bound `liability_cap_months` true with reason "Each party's cap: … That is 24 months of fees, within the limit. The playbook's limit is 6–24 months of fees."; bound `cap_multiplier_of_annual` true with "… That is 2 times a year's fees, within the limit. The playbook's limit is at most 3 x annual contract value." `worstSeverity` "high", not "walkaway". |
| 2 | `pbcheck $C_SUP \| jq .summary` | `worstSeverity` "high", `requiresHumanGate` false, `deviationCount` ≥ 1, `totalClauses` = the extracted count, `truncated` false, and `uncoveredClauses` = clauses that no position with rules could judge. |
| 3 | Open `$C_SUP` → the Ask strip on the right edge (**Ask · ⌘K**, or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K). Send: `What is the liability cap in this contract, and is it within our playbook?` | The rail shows "Context: <title>" above the composer and one or more tool chips (for example `playbook_check`, `contract_get`). The answer gives the cap as 24 months of fees (2 times a year's fees), says it is within the playbook's limits (6–24 months; at most 3 times annual value), and may point out the missing exclusion of consequential damages. It does not speculate that the cap "could exceed" a limit depending on the payment schedule. |
| 4 | Read the rail's **Playbook review** (E2E-REV-02). | No finding faults §5 for the size of its cap. A §5 finding, if any, is about consequential damages. |
| 5 | Add a super-cap. **Edit** → at the end of §5 add: `For breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed three (3) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.` → "Saved ✓" → **Done**. Command A. | `capAnalysis` now lists two caps: the general one as before, and "For breaches of Section 4: 3 × the fees of the 12 months before the claim = 36 months of fees, 3 times a year's fees." The two bounds are still judged on the general cap (passed true), and each reason adds "Separately, a cap for some claims is 36 months of fees (3 times a year's fees)." The edit's new version already carries §5 with its new words (DD2), so the check reads them at once. |
| 6 | **Edit** → in §5's first sentence replace "two (2) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months" with "the fees paid or payable in the three (3) months" → **Done**. Command A. | The general cap reads "Each party's cap: 1 × the fees of the 3 months before the claim = 3 months of fees, 0.25 times a year's fees." `liability_cap_months` passed **false**: "… That is 3 months of fees, outside the limit. …". `cap_multiplier_of_annual` passed true. |
| 7 | **Edit** → make that first sentence end "shall not exceed the greater of USD 1,000,000 and the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim." → **Done**. Command A. | "Each party's cap: the greater of USD 1,000,000 and 1 × the fees of the 12 months before the claim." Both bounds `passed` null, with "… Its size in months of fees can't be worked out from the words. …" (and "…in times a year's fees…" for the other): nothing is estimated. |
| 8 | Put §5 back exactly as in `D-SUPPLY.docx` (remove the super-cap sentence too) → **Done**. Command A. | Step 1's result again. Later journeys expect the original §5. |

**Also check**
- A cap on one party only ("Supplier's aggregate liability shall not exceed …") is named for that party: "Supplier's cap: …", and `lol.mutual_cap` fails.
- The same measured figures reach `contract_get` and `portfolio_compare` as `liabilityCaps` (TC-FAMILY-01 covers `contract_get`), and the automatic review gets them as each clause's `facts`.
- Without the secret: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST $INTERNAL/tools/playbook_check -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` → `{"detail":"Internal endpoint — bad secret"} 401`.
- A caller without `view:playbook` (rep-a's id as `userId`, on a contract rep-a owns) → 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:playbook permission"}` (TC-ACC-14).

**Known limits**
- Only the Limitation of Liability positions have structured rules, so only liability clauses are measured; other clauses are judged by the model (the automatic review) or reported as not covered (`uncovered`).
- A super-cap is reported, not judged: the playbook's limits apply to the general cap.

### E2E-REV-04 · Every decision in the clause review drawer takes the clause out of the queue, and Reopen puts it back (EE1)

**Covers:** `PATCH /contracts/clauses/:clauseId/review-state` · the contract page's **Review progress** checklist and clause review drawer · docs/38 TC-REVQ-01, TC-REVQ-03, TC-REVQ-04 · FIX_TRACKER EE1
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra once `$C_REV` is analysed · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_REV` analysed. For a known set of flagged clauses, run Command C: it replaces the version's extracted clauses with seven rows matching `D-SUPPLY.docx`, five of them flagged (§2, §4, §6 unfavorable, shown as risks; §3, §5 unusual, shown as deviations). Then reload the contract page.
- DevTools → Network, filtered on `review-state`.

Command C (the clause rows; `$VID` is the current version):
```bash
VID=$(curl -s $API/contracts/$C_REV -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r .currentVersionId)
curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_REV/versions/$VID/clauses -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- <<'JSON' | jq .
{"clauseSegments":[
 {"sortOrder":1,"sectionRef":"1","clauseType":"scope","riskRating":"favorable","interpretation":"E2E: scope by schedule.","content":"Supplier will provide the implementation services described in Schedule 1."},
```
