```bash
 {"sortOrder":2,"sectionRef":"2","clauseType":"payment","riskRating":"unfavorable","interpretation":"E2E: Net 15 is only our fallback.","content":"Customer shall pay Supplier a fee of USD 12,500 per month. Invoices are payable within fifteen (15) days of receipt."},
 {"sortOrder":3,"sectionRef":"3","clauseType":"auto_renewal","riskRating":"unusual","interpretation":"E2E: no exit for convenience.","content":"Neither party may terminate for convenience."},
 {"sortOrder":4,"sectionRef":"4","clauseType":"confidentiality","riskRating":"unfavorable","interpretation":"E2E: two years, no trade-secret carve-out.","content":"Each party shall keep the Confidential Information of the other party confidential for two (2) years after termination."},
 {"sortOrder":5,"sectionRef":"5","clauseType":"limitation_of_liability","riskRating":"unusual","interpretation":"E2E: no exclusion of consequential damages.","content":"shall not exceed two (2) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."},
 {"sortOrder":6,"sectionRef":"6","clauseType":"indemnification","riskRating":"unfavorable","interpretation":"E2E: one-sided indemnity.","content":"Customer shall indemnify Supplier against all claims arising from the use of the services by Customer."},
 {"sortOrder":7,"sectionRef":"7","clauseType":"governing_law","riskRating":"neutral","interpretation":"E2E: English law.","content":"This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of London have exclusive jurisdiction."}
]}
JSON
```
Command B (every flagged clause back to pending):
```bash
for id in $(curl -s $API/contracts/$C_REV/clauses -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.riskRating | IN("unfavorable","unusual")) | .id'); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$id %{http_code}\n" -X PATCH $API/contracts/clauses/$id/review-state -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"state":"unreviewed"}'; done
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_REV`. | In the Styled view, §2, §4 and §6's text has a red underline (risk) and §3 and §5 a blue squiggle (deviation); their accessible names are "Risky clause — open focused review" and "Deviation from playbook — open focused review", and clicking one opens the drawer on that clause. At the top of the rail: "Review progress" "0 / 5" with a bar. |
| 2 | Click **Review progress**. | A checklist, in document order: payment §2, auto renewal §3, confidentiality §4, limitation of liability §5, indemnification §6, each with a coloured dot. Hovering a row shows **Mark reviewed**. Under the list: "✓ Mark all 5 as reviewed". |
| 3 | Click "payment". | The drawer replaces the rail: ‹ (disabled), "1 / 5" (tooltip "Clauses still waiting on a decision"), ›, ×. Badge "HIGH RISK", pill "Pending", title "Payment", "2". Sections: "Why this matters" (the interpretation), "Playbook comparison", "Alternative language" with **Suggest alternative language**, then **Accept clause as-is**, **Edit manually**, **Reject**, **Mark reviewed**, then "Comments on this clause". Playbook comparison reads "No playbook position defined for Payment. Add one under Library → Playbook to compare this clause automatically." although Fees & Payment has four positions (known defect, reported). |
| 4 | Click **Accept clause as-is**. | The drawer opens "Auto Renewal" (§3, badge "DEVIATION"), counter "1 / 4", ‹ disabled. Network: `PATCH /api/v1/contracts/clauses/<§2 id>/review-state` `{"state":"resolved"}` → 200. |
| 5 | Click **Reject**. | "Confidentiality" (§4), "1 / 3". The PATCH sends `{"state":"rejected"}` and answers `"reviewState":"rejected"`. Its Playbook comparison lists the four Confidentiality positions, each with its rung, its language and notes. |
| 6 | Click **Mark reviewed**. | "Limitation Of Liability" (§5), "1 / 2". The PATCH sends `{"state":"reviewed"}`. |
| 7 | Close the drawer (× or Esc) and expand **Review progress**. | "3 / 5". The first three rows read "accepted", "rejected" (in red) and "reviewed"; §5 and §6 have no label. |
| 8 | `clauses $C_REV`, then reload the page and expand **Review progress**. | §2 `resolved`, §3 `rejected`, §4 `reviewed`, §5 and §6 `unreviewed`. After the reload the labels are the same. |
| 9 | Click the "accepted" row (payment). | The drawer shows pill "Accepted" and, above the buttons, "Accepted — no longer in the queue." with **Reopen**. **Accept clause as-is** is disabled; **Reject** and **Mark reviewed** are not. The counter's total is 3: the open clause plus the two pending. |
| 10 | Click **Reopen**. | The pill turns "Pending", the decision line goes, all four buttons are enabled, the drawer stays on the clause. The PATCH sends `{"state":"unreviewed"}` and answers `"reviewedAt":null,"reviewedById":null`. |
| 11 | Decide each remaining pending clause with any of the three buttons. | Each decision opens the next pending clause, going back to one you skipped when none is after it. After the last one the drawer closes by itself and **Review progress** reads "5 / 5 ✓". |

**Also check**
- › and ‹ (or j and k) step only through pending clauses plus the one open; › is disabled on the last and ‹ on the first. A decided clause, once you move off it, doesn't come round again (TC-REVQ-01 N1).
- Command B and reload. Accept §2, reject §3, close, then click "✓ Mark all 3 as reviewed": only the pending rows turn "reviewed"; accepted and rejected stay (TC-REVQ-01 N3).
- Opening a decided clause doesn't lock it: open the "accepted" row and click **Reject** → it becomes "rejected" (TC-REVQ-03 N2).
- viewer-a opens `$C_REV` → Review progress → a decided row: the pill shows (for example "Rejected") but no decision line, no **Reopen**, no buttons and no "Alternative language"; instead "Read-only: accepting, rejecting or changing this clause needs edit access to the contract." The checklist still offers **Mark reviewed** and "✓ Mark all … as reviewed" to viewer-a: a click turns the row "reviewed", the request is refused, and the row turns back with no message (known defect, reported).
- API (TC-REVQ-04): `{"state":"done"}` → 400 `{"detail":"state must be unreviewed | reviewed | resolved | rejected"}`; as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract"; as admin-b, or a made-up clause id → 404 `{"detail":"Clause not found"}`.
- A decision sent with an earlier version's clause id marks the same clause (same place, same type) in the current version, and the answer adds `requestedId` (DD5).
- Below 1280 px wide the drawer opens as a panel over the page.
- Nothing about these decisions is in the audit log or the contract's Activity (known limit).

**Known limits**
- The drawer's "Playbook comparison" matches positions to the clause by exact category name; other features map clause types to categories more loosely (see E2E-REV-05). Known defect, reported.
- Clause decisions are not audited.

### E2E-REV-05 · "Suggest alternative language" works on any clause, and applying a rewrite writes a new version and counts as a decision

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/clauses/:clauseId/suggest` · `POST /contracts/:id/clauses/:clauseId/apply` · `PATCH /contracts/clauses/:clauseId/review-state` · agent service: `assist` (its `/redline_propose` endpoint) · docs/38 TC-REVQ-02 · FIX_TRACKER AA3, AA5, DD5, DD7, EE1
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_REV` with the Command C clauses from E2E-REV-04 and every flagged clause pending (Command B there), in DRAFT. Reload the page. DevTools → Network open.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open "confidentiality" from **Review progress**. In "Alternative language" click **Suggest alternative language**. | The button reads "Drafting alternatives…", then three cards appear, labelled LEAST, MODERATE and AGGRESSIVE, each with the proposed text, a rationale in italics and **Apply to document**. Nothing is decided: the pill still reads "Pending", the counter is unchanged, and no `review-state` request is sent. The response (Network → `suggest`) has `"hasPlaybook": true` and `category.name` "Confidentiality". |
| 2 | Click **Apply to document** on the MODERATE card. | The button reads "Applying…". Then the drawer opens the next pending clause and the counter's total drops by one. Network: `POST /api/v1/contracts/$C_REV/clauses/<id>/apply` → 200 with `newVersionNumber` and `"spliced": true`, then `PATCH …/review-state` `{"state":"resolved"}` → 200 with `requestedId`. |
| 3 | Close the drawer. Read the document and the rail's **History**. | §4 reads as the moderate rewrite. History's newest version is "redline_apply (moderate): <rationale>". |
| 4 | `clauses $C_REV` | The rewritten §4 (same place and type, in the new version) has the new words, no rating and `resolved`; it has left **Review progress** because it is no longer rated. The other clauses keep their states. |
| 5 | `audit VERSION_CREATED $C_REV` | The newest event's metadata: `{"via":"clause_apply","clauseId":"…","newVersionNumber":N,"spliced":true}`. The contract's Activity lists "VERSION CREATED". |
| 6 | Any clause, flagged or not: rail **Clauses** → **View all**. The Clauses tab opens, with "Search clauses…" and the filters "All (7)", "Unfavorable (…)", "Unusual (…)", "Favorable" and "Neutral"; each card has **View verbatim text** and **Review and suggest changes**. On the §1 card (scope, badge "Favorable") click **Review and suggest changes**. | The drawer opens on §1: badge "FAVORABLE", pill "Pending"; the counter counts it with the pending clauses. |
| 7 | **Suggest alternative language**. | Variants appear with, under them, "No preferred playbook position exists for Scope, so this is general drafting practice rather than your playbook." (no category matches the type `scope`; the response has `"hasPlaybook": false`). Close without applying: nothing is decided. |
| 8 | Open "Governing Law" (§7) the same way → **Suggest alternative language**, and read the response in Network. | `category.name` is "Compliance with Laws" (in an org with the seeded categories and none named "Governing Law"): the governing-law clause is rewritten against the anti-bribery and sanctions positions, not the governing-law positions under "Dispute Resolution" (known defect, reported). |
| 9 | Open a pending flagged clause → **Edit manually**. | The drawer closes and the document becomes editable: the header shows undo, redo, the save status and **Done**. No `review-state` request is sent. Click **Done** without typing: the clause is still pending. |

**Also check**
- A passage labelled as a clause type it isn't (AA3): re-run Command C with §1's `"clauseType":"governing_law"`, reload, open §1 → **Suggest alternative language**. Normally no variants and the text "This text isn't really a governing law clause, so there's nothing to redline against the playbook. <reason>". Re-run Command C as given afterwards.
- viewer-a: the drawer has no "Alternative language" section and shows the read-only line. API: `suggest` or `apply` as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract".
- API refusals (as counsel-a): `apply` with `{}` → 400 `{"detail":"proposedText is required"}`; `"aggression":"extreme"` → 400 `{"detail":"aggression must be one of: least, moderate, aggressive"}`; `proposedText` over 20,000 characters → 400. A made-up clause id: `suggest` → 404 `{"detail":"Clause not found",…}`, `apply` → 404 `{"detail":"Clause not found on current version"}`. As admin-b → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- Suggest after an earlier Apply still works (AA5): open another pending clause → Suggest → 200 and variants.
- A clause that runs over a heading and list items (as a Word section often does) applies through the rewrite's own edits, one per paragraph (DD7); a clause across paragraphs that can't be placed is refused rather than half-applied.
- The agents service stopped: Suggest shows "Could not draft alternatives right now. Try again, or use Edit manually."
- If the model's answer can't be read, the section shows the raw error (for example "redline_failed: JSONDecodeError: …"), and a variant the model skipped shows the original clause with "(Model did not produce a '<aggression>' variant — original kept.)" and still offers **Apply to document**, which saves an unchanged version (known defects, reported).
- An APPROVED contract goes back to DRAFT when a rewrite is applied (X42).
- While a Google Docs copy is out, the drawer is read-only and the API answers 409 `EDITING_IN_GOOGLE_DOCS` (E2E-NEG-06).
- The clause reaches the model with personal data masked, and the applied text has the real values (TC-PII-06).

**Known limits**
- The "Add as an amendment instead" choice appears only when the clause's text can no longer be found in the document ("This clause has changed since the suggestion was written, so it can't be replaced automatically. …"). Since clauses are carried into new versions (DD2) this is rare, and there's no reliable way to produce it by hand.
- A rewritten clause is unrated until the contract is analysed again.

### E2E-REV-06 · The Assistant quotes, cites and checks a contract's clauses against the playbook

**Covers:** tools: `clause_search`, `contract_cite`, `playbook_check`, `redline_propose` (through the "Review contract" skill) · their routes `POST /api/internal/ai/tools/clause_search` and `/contract_cite` · FIX_TRACKER CC2, CC3, CC7, CC10
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key (steps 1–4 and 7); steps 5–6 nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_SUP` (§5 as uploaded) and `$C_PDF` analysed. `pbcheck` from E2E-REV-03.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open `$C_SUP` → **Ask · ⌘K**. Send `Quote the confidentiality clause.` | A `clause_search` chip (its one-line summary shows the query), then an answer quoting §4 word for word as a block quote. No "<<<UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DATA>>>" or other framing text appears in the answer (CC3). |
| 2 | Type `@review` in the composer and pick **Review contract** from the list (it inserts `@review-contract`); send it. | Chips for several tools, among them `playbook_check`, `clause_search` and usually `contract_cite` and `redline_propose`. The answer gives a summary, the top risks and the playbook deviations, listing only deviations the check reports or the clause's own words show (for §5, the missing exclusion of consequential damages; it doesn't call "each party's" cap "not mutual"). It may end by offering to draft redlines for the worst ones. |
| 3 | Open `$C_PDF` → **Ask · ⌘K**. Send `Where does it say the agreement renews automatically? Cite it.` | A `contract_cite` chip and a "Citations" card: "· <title>", the query in quotes, a count, and rows like "§<ref> <section title> p.<N>", with an "exact" tag when the words matched verbatim. Each row has "quote" to show the passage. |
| 4 | Click a citation row. | The contract opens in the **Original** view at page N with the passage outlined (X1, TC-DOC-04). Without page data, the Styled view scrolls to the section and its Table of Contents entry flashes. |
| 5 | Command D (`clause_search` without a model). | `totalMatches` ≥ 1; a match in §5 with `passageComplete` true and the whole paragraph (CC2). |
| 6 | Command E on `$C_PDF`. | Citations with `sectionRef`, `page`, `score` and `exact`. The same command on `$C_SUP` returns `"citations": []` (see Known limits). |
| 7 | On the full Assistant page (left rail → **Assistant**) send `Check <title of $C_SUP> against our playbook.` | A `playbook_check` chip, and in the right-hand pane a table "Playbook check" with the subtitle "<n> of <total> clauses checked · <k> rule failures · <u> not covered by the playbook" and columns Clause, §, Playbook, Rules, Severity. §5 shows 1 failed rule. |

Command D:
```bash
curl -s -X POST $INTERNAL/tools/clause_search -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'x-internal-service: agents' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$C_SUP'","query":"aggregate liability"}' | jq '{totalMatches, matches: [.matches[] | {sectionHint, passageComplete, match}]}'
```
Command E: the same call to `$INTERNAL/tools/contract_cite` with `"contractId":"'$C_PDF'","query":"renew"`, piped to `jq '.citations[] | {sectionRef, sectionTitle, page, exact, score}'`.

**Also check**
- A contract with no document text (for example `$C_Q` from E2E-REV-01): ask it to quote a clause. The answer says there is no document on file for it, rather than inventing text; `clause_search` returns `"documentOnFile": false` with a note (CC7).
- rep-a asking about a contract rep-a doesn't own: the tools find nothing and the answer says so (TC-ACC-13). rep-a asking for a playbook check: the tool reports "The user in this conversation does not have view:playbook permission" and the answer says the permission is missing (TC-ACC-14).
- A contract whose text addresses the AI ("SYSTEM OVERRIDE: …"): the answer quotes the instruction to you and doesn't act on it (CC13).
- The tool routes without the secret → 401 `{"detail":"Internal endpoint — bad secret"}`.

**Known limits**
- Known defect, reported: `contract_cite` finds nothing in a Word (`.docx`) upload. Citations come from the section tree that only PDF extraction builds, so on `$C_SUP` the card reads "No passage in <title> matches “<query>”. Anything stated about this clause below is unsupported by the document." although the passage is there. `clause_search` works on both.
- The "Playbook check" table appears only on the full Assistant page, not in the contract page's Ask rail.

### E2E-NEG-01 · "Redline against playbook" stages a first-pass markup, and only the changes you accept reach the document

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/redline-against-playbook` · `POST /contracts/:id/redline-against-playbook/apply` · agent service: `assist` (its `/redline_propose_batch` endpoint) · background: the `playbook-redline` job · FIX_TRACKER BB5
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_PBR` analysed, with its playbook review stored (`GET /contracts/$C_PBR/playbook-review` → 200). The redline rewrites what that review flagged plus what the liability rules catch.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_PBR`. Find the rail section **Playbook redline** (open by default, above "Playbook review"). | "Check every clause against your playbook and draft a first-pass markup. Nothing changes in the document until you accept it." and the button **Redline against playbook**. |
| 2 | Click it. | "Starting…", then "Reviewing every clause against your playbook — this takes a minute or two." with a spinner. The page checks again every 4 seconds; don't reload. |
| 3 | Wait until the list appears (1–3 minutes). | A line "N clauses deviate from your playbook" and a chip "worst: <severity>". Where they apply: "<k> clauses could not be checked — no playbook position covers them. They were not reviewed, not approved."; "Left as written: …" for passages labelled as a clause type they aren't; "<n> clauses could not be rewritten (<types>). Review them by hand." Then one row per proposed rewrite: clause type, "§<section>", a severity chip and two lines of rationale, a chevron at the left and a square toggle at the right (tooltip "Accept this change"). Under the list: **Accept all** and **Apply 0 changes** (disabled). On `D-SUPPLY.docx` the list includes §5 (the missing exclusion of consequential damages, from the liability rules) and normally the clauses the review flagged. |
| 4 | Command A. | `_playbookRedlineStatus` "DONE"; `aggression` "moderate"; `deviationCount`, `proposedCount` and `failedCount` match the rail; each proposal has `clauseId`, `sectionRef`, `originalText`, `proposedText` and `rationale`. |
| 5 | Expand §5 with its chevron. | The rationale, then "Current" (the clause as it reads now) and "Proposed" (the rewrite, marked as machine-written). The rewrite keeps the 2× twelve-month cap and adds the exclusion; no other proposal restates the whole cap (BB5). |
| 6 | Click the toggle on §5 and on one other row. | Both toggles turn solid with a tick (tooltip "Accepted — click to undo"); the button reads **Apply 2 changes**. |
| 7 | Click **Apply 2 changes**. | "Applying…", then "Applied 2 changes as a new version. Everything you did not accept was left alone." If a change couldn't be placed, an amber line says "<k> couldn't be placed in the document, so it was left as written (<type>). Edit it by hand." |
| 8 | Read the document and **History**. | The two rewrites are in the text; the rest is unchanged. The newest version is "redline_apply_batch (2 clauses): accepted from playbook redline". |
| 9 | `audit AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED $C_PBR` | One event from step 3, metadata `{"via":"playbook-redline","deviationCount":N,"proposed":M}`. The contract's Activity lists "AGENT TOOL APPLIED". Applying (step 7) adds no audit event of its own (known limit). |

Command A: `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_PBR -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.metadata | {_playbookRedlineStatus, r: (._playbookRedline | {aggression, deviationCount, proposedCount, failedCount, uncoveredClauses, truncated, proposals: [.proposals[] | {clauseId, sectionRef, clauseType, severity, error, proposed: ((.proposedText // "")[0:60])}]})}'`

**Also check**
- Reload the page after step 7. The rail still lists every proposal, including the two applied ones, and has no **Run again** (known defect, reported). Accept an applied one and click **Apply 1 change**: a red line "None of the requested clauses could be located in the current version." (409 `NO_CLAUSE_APPLICABLE`).
- A second start while one runs: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_PBR/redline-against-playbook -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` twice in a row → the second gives 409 `{"detail":"A redline is already running for this contract"}`. The first gives 202 `{"status":"QUEUED","contractId":"…","aggression":"moderate"}`. `-d '{"aggression":"aggressive"}'` stages aggressive rewrites; any other value means moderate.
- Apply refusals (API, as counsel-a): `{}` → 400 `{"detail":"acceptedClauseIds is required"}`; ids that aren't staged → 409 `{"detail":"None of the accepted clauses are in the staged redline","code":"NOT_STAGED"}`; a contract never redlined (for example `$C_RISK`) → 409 `{"detail":"No staged redline to apply","code":"NO_STAGED_REDLINE"}`. Only staged text is ever applied: the request carries clause ids, not text.
- A contract where nothing deviates: the rail says "No clause deviated from the playbook." with **Run again**, which starts a new run.
- Agents service stopped: after the start, the rail shows a red box with the reason (for example "fetch failed") and **Try again**; `_playbookRedlineStatus` "FAILED" with `_playbookRedlineError`.
- viewer-a: the section and its button show, and clicking **Redline against playbook** does nothing and says nothing (known defect, reported). API as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract". admin-b → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- While a Google Docs copy is out, applying is refused with the lock's message in the red line (E2E-NEG-06).

**Known limits**
- The page always asks for moderate rewrites; least and aggressive are API-only.
- Rewritten clauses are unrated until the contract is analysed again.

### E2E-NEG-02 · The Assistant proposes a clause rewrite and applies it only when you confirm; Undo reverts it

**Covers:** tools: `redline_propose`, `redline_apply` · the Ask rail on the contract page and the full Assistant page · docs/38 TC-AI-04, TC-AI-13 · FIX_TRACKER C9, CC8, X53, X58
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_PBR` in DRAFT (an applied rewrite on an APPROVED contract would send it back for approval). Keep the page open between Apply and Undo: a reload drops the receipt and its **Undo**.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_PBR` → **Ask · ⌘K**. | The rail opens with "Context: <title>" above the composer ("Ask anything · @ for skills · / for actions"). |
| 2 | Send `Propose redlines for the confidentiality clause.` | A `redline_propose` chip, then a "Redline proposal" card headed with the clause type and section as extracted (for example "confidentiality · 4"). Tabs **Least**, **Moderate** (selected) and **Aggressive**; hovering them shows "Minimal edits; preserves counterparty language", "Balanced rewrite toward playbook acceptable", "Full rewrite to playbook preferred position". Below: "Rationale", "Changes (N)" with each old wording struck and each new wording highlighted, a toggle "Full proposed text (N chars)", the note "Applying creates ContractVersion (n+1). Reversible via Undo." and the button **Apply Moderate**. |
| 3 | Click the **Least** tab, then **Apply Least**. | An "About to run `redline_apply`" card with an "Undoable" badge: "Apply least redline to confidentiality (4).", "Target: <title> · 4", a "Changes" box listing each edit ("change", or "change 1", "change 2" …) as old → new, and **Cancel**, **Edit**, **Apply**. |
| 4 | Click **Apply**. | "Applying…", then a receipt "Applied · Apply least redline to confidentiality (4)." with **Undo** (tooltip "Undo this action (within 15 minutes)"). `versions $C_PBR`: the newest version's note starts "redline_apply (least)". |
| 5 | Click **Undo**. | The receipt reads "Undone". That version's note now ends "(reverted via undo)", and `status $C_PBR` shows `currentVersionId` back on the version before it. |
| 6 | `audit AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED` and `audit AGENT_TOOL_UNDONE` | The newest AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED has `metadata.toolName` "redline_apply", `status` "success" and the args; AGENT_TOOL_UNDONE names the same tool. |
| 7 | Send `Redline section 5.` | The proposal card is for §5 (limitation of liability): the section number finds the clause (X53, TC-AI-13). Click **Apply Moderate**, then **Cancel** on the card that appears → a receipt "Cancelled · Apply moderate redline to …"; no new version. |
| 8 | Left rail → **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Send `Propose redlines for the indemnification clause of <title of $C_PBR>.` Click **Apply Moderate**. | The same proposal card appears in the answer, and **Apply Moderate** brings the "About to run `redline_apply`" card into the same message (X58). Click **Cancel**. |

**Also check**
- A clause type with no playbook position (for example §1 if it was extracted as `scope`): the card has a "No playbook" chip and a dashed note "No playbook position exists for <type>, so this wording is the model's own — not your organisation's agreed fallback. Read it before applying."
- **Edit** on the confirm card shows the arguments as JSON; changing `"aggression"` to `"extreme"` and applying gives the receipt "Failed · … · Invalid request" and no new version (TC-AI-04 N1–N2).
- viewer-a asking for a redline: the tool is refused ("The user in this conversation does not have edit:contract permission") and the answer says so. `curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads/any/actions/apply -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"toolName":"redline_apply","args":{"contractId":"'$C_PBR'","clauseId":"x","proposedText":"y"}}'` → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract" (TC-AI-04 N4).
- While a Google Docs copy is out, **Apply** gives "Failed · … · <name> is editing this contract in Google Docs …" (E2E-NEG-06).
- The rewriter gets the clause with personal data masked; the applied text has the real values (TC-PII-06).

**Known limits**
- **Undo** lasts 15 minutes and only on the receipt in the conversation where you applied; a reload loses it.

### E2E-NEG-03 · Two versions compare as a tracked-changes diff, merge change by change, and download as a Word file with tracked changes

**Covers:** `GET /contracts/:id/versions/:v1Id/diff/:v2Id` · `GET /contracts/:id/versions/:v1Id/redline-docx/:v2Id` · the header's **Compare** and the **Negotiate** tab's "Version diff" · docs/38 TC-WF-19, TC-WF-20
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_RISK` with v1 (`D-SUPPLY.docx`) and v2 (`D-SUPPLY-v2.docx`), both extracted. `V1` and `V2`: their ids from `versions $C_RISK`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_RISK` and click **Compare** in the header (below 1280 px: **Actions** → **Compare versions**). | A full-screen "Compare versions" view: pickers labelled "Newer" (v2) and "Older" (v1), chips "v2 · Legal Counsel · today" and "v1 · Legal Counsel · today", filter chips all, theirs, ours, pending, and × (Esc also closes). A bar "<i> added, <d> removed" and "0 accepted · 0 rejected · <n> pending", with **Accept all**, **Reject all**, **Word (tracked)** and **Apply as new version**. The diff shows insertions underlined and deletions struck through, both in blue. On the right "Changes (n)", each item "Added" or "Removed" with its text, **Accept**, **Reject** and "pending". |
| 2 | Click the filter chips **theirs**, **ours**, **pending**, then **all**. | theirs: only "Added" items; ours: only "Removed"; pending: items not yet decided ("No changes match this filter." when none). |
| 3 | Click **Word (tracked)**. | The browser saves `redline-v1-to-v2.docx`. In Word (Review → Track Changes) the changes are tracked insertions and deletions by "Legal Counsel" (the author of v2). **Accept All** gives v2's text; **Reject All** gives v1's. |
| 4 | Command A. | `200 application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`, and the header `content-disposition: attachment; filename="redline-<title>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.docx"`. |
| 5 | Command B. | `stats` {insertions, deletions} equal to step 1's bar; `ins` and `del` true. A second call answers at once (the diff is cached). |
| 6 | In Compare, accept both items of the §2 fee change (the old amount "Removed", the new amount "Added"), and **Reject** the §4 sentence "Supplier may use Confidential Information of Customer to improve its products." Hover **Apply as new version**, then click it. | The tooltip reads "<n> undecided change(s) will keep the older version". After the click, Compare closes. History's newest version is "Redline merge: <accepted> accepted, 1 rejected vs v2", counting the items you decided. The document has USD 14,000, does not have the §4 sentence, and keeps v1's wording everywhere you didn't decide (§2's payment days, §5). |
| 7 | Rail **History** → **Negotiate** (the link in the section header). | The tab bar appears ("Document", then Overview, Clauses, Versions, Negotiate, Comments, Approval, Activity), with Negotiate selected. Left: "Version diff" with two selectors, "vs", defaulting to the version before the current one and the current one (v2 vs v3 now). |
| 8 | Set the selectors to v1 and v2. | "<n> insertions" and "<n> deletions", and **Unified** / **Side by side**. Side by side shows two columns headed "v1" and "v2" (in capitals), deletions only on the left and insertions only on the right. |

Command A: `curl -s -D - -o redline.docx -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}\n' "$API/contracts/$C_RISK/versions/$V1/redline-docx/$V2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | grep -iE '^content-disposition|^HTTP|application/vnd'`
Command B: `curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_RISK/versions/$V1/diff/$V2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '{stats, v1Id, v2Id, ins: (.diffHtml | test("<ins")), del: (.diffHtml | test("<del"))}'`

**Also check**
- A version still being read: upload any file as a new version (the setup's `curl … /versions`) and open Compare at once: "This version is still being processed. The comparison will be available once extraction finishes." The Negotiate "Version diff" says "This version is still being extracted. The comparison will be available once processing finishes." Command B for that pair → 409 `{"error":"Version still processing","detail":"…","pendingVersionIds":["…"]}`; Command A → 409 with "…The redline will be available once processing finishes."; **Word (tracked)** shows "Could not build the Word file — try again." without the reason.
- One version only (`$C_MAIL`): **Compare** is disabled with the tooltip "Upload a second version to compare. Until then there is nothing to diff."; below 1280 px **Actions** → "Compare versions" is disabled with "need 2+"; the Negotiate tab and the History "Negotiate" link don't appear.
- The same version in both pickers: "Pick two different versions to see changes."
- viewer-a can compare and download (`view:contract`). Their **Apply as new version** shows "Failed to apply — try again." (the save is refused; the message doesn't say why).
- admin-b: Command B → 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}`; Command A → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`. A version id from another contract → 404 (`"error":"Version not found"` / `"detail":"Version not found"`).
- A pair too large to compare within 30 seconds → 422 "These versions are too large to compare. Compare smaller sections, or download both versions." on both routes (TC-WF-20).

**Known limits**
- Compare works on words: a replaced word is a "Removed" and an "Added" item, and both must be decided for a clean result.
- The Word file attributes every change to one author, the newer version's.
- There are two Word downloads. Compare's **Word (tracked)** is a comparison of any two versions, rebuilt from Draft Legal's text. **Actions → Download for counterparty (Word)** is the counterparty's own Word file with our current changes tracked in it (E2E-NEG-05).
- There is no upload-a-version control on the contract page; versions come from edits, applied rewrites, Google Docs, the portal and email (or `POST /contracts/:id/versions`).

### E2E-NEG-04 · "Analyze Redlines" scores each changed section's risk before and after, and counters every change we don't accept (FF1)

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/redline` · agent service: `redline` · background: the `redline-analysis` job · docs/38 TC-AI-02, TC-RISK-01, TC-RISK-02 · FIX_TRACKER C8, FF1
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_RISK`: v1 is our standard (`D-SUPPLY.docx`), v2 their markup (`D-SUPPLY-v2.docx`, changing sections 2, 4 and 5). E2E-NEG-03 may have added v3; this journey compares v1 with v2.
- The seeded playbook has positions for Fees & Payment, Confidentiality and Limitation of Liability that apply to every contract type.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_RISK` → rail **History** → **Negotiate**. On the right, "Select versions to compare": set **Baseline (our version)** to v1 and **Counterparty redlines** to v2. Click **Analyze Redlines**. | The button reads "Analyzing redlines…" with a spinner. The page checks every 4 seconds; don't reload. |
| 2 | Wait (1–2 minutes). | "Analysis summary" with the line "Analyzed 3 changes: <a> acceptable, <c> need countering, <r> should be rejected. Average risk across the 3 changed clauses: <X> in our standard, <Y> as proposed, <Z> with our counter-proposals."; a badge ("Accept all", "Counter required" or "Reject"); "<NN>% confidence"; and "<a> accept", "<c> counter", "<r> reject". When any change is at walkaway, outside the playbook or critical, an amber box "Legal review required" / "One or more changes involve walkaway positions or terms outside the playbook. Please escalate to legal counsel before proceeding." sits above. Below: "3 changes detected". |
| 3 | Read the three change cards. | One card per changed section: §2, §4 and §5 (a section with two edits is one card). Each shows the recommendation (Accept, Counter or Reject), the clause type, the section, a severity chip, a playbook chip (preferred, acceptable, fallback, walkaway, outside playbook) and, when set, "Human review". The grey line under them reads `Risk <a> → <b> (<+/-d>): <deviation>; <exposure>, <likelihood>; <market>. <why>`, with words from fixed lists: deviation "matches our standard" / "within our acceptable position" / "needs our fallback position" / "beyond our walkaway position"; exposure "no exposure" … "severe exposure"; likelihood "unlikely" / "possible" / "likely"; market "market standard" / "slightly off-market" / "clearly off-market" / "one-sided or of doubtful enforceability". The §5 card (a 3-month cap, under the 6-month walkaway) normally rises most and reads "beyond our walkaway position". |
| 4 | Expand each card with its chevron. | "Original" holds the whole section as v1 has it and "Counterparty proposes" the whole section as v2 has it: §2's Original has "USD 12,500" and "fifteen (15) days", its proposal "USD 14,000" and "seven (7) days". |
| 5 | On each Counter or Reject card, read "Our counter-proposal". | The proposed wording, **Copy counter text** (turns "Copied!"), and an italic note `Revised risk if they accept: <r> (from <b>, <r−b>): <four ratings in words>. <why>`. `<b>` is the card's own "after" number. Where their wording raised the risk, `<a> ≤ <r> ≤ <b>`. Reject cards have a counter too. Accept cards have none. |
| 6 | Commands D, E, F and G. | D: one line per change with `riskBefore`, `riskAfter` (0–100), `riskDelta` = after − before, and `riskRevised` only on changes with a counter. E: every line ends `same`, so each number is the formula 100 × (0.45 × deviation/3 + 0.35 × exposure × likelihood/12 + 0.20 × market/3) applied to the stored ratings. F: `true`, `true` (ratings in range; one likelihood per change). G: `true`, `true` (every change not accepted has counter text; no revised risk outside our standard's and their proposal's). |
| 7 | Check the summary's averages against the cards. | X = the mean of the "before" numbers, Y of the "after" numbers, Z of each card's revised risk where it has one, else its "after"; each rounded to a whole number. |
| 8 | `audit REDLINE_ANALYZED $C_RISK` | One event per run, metadata `{"v1Id":"…","v2Id":"…"}`; the contract's Activity lists "REDLINE ANALYZED". |

Command D: `curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_RISK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.metadata._redlineAnalysis.changes[] | [.sectionRef, .recommendation, .riskBefore, .riskAfter, .riskDelta, .riskRevised, (.counterText != null)] | @tsv'`
Command E:
```bash
curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_RISK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
a = json.load(sys.stdin)["metadata"]["_redlineAnalysis"]
score = lambda f: None if not f else round(100 * (0.45 * f["deviation"] / 3 + 0.35 * f["exposure"] * f["likelihood"] / 12 + 0.20 * f["market"] / 3))
for c in a["changes"]:
    stored = (c.get("riskBefore"), c.get("riskAfter"), c.get("riskRevised"))
    factors = tuple(score(c.get(k)) for k in ("ourAssessment", "theirAssessment", "counterAssessment"))
    print(c.get("sectionRef"), c.get("recommendation"), stored, factors, "same" if stored == factors else "DIFFERENT")'
```
Command F:
```bash
curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_RISK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.metadata._redlineAnalysis.changes
  | ([.[] | .ourAssessment, .theirAssessment, .counterAssessment | select(. != null)
      | .deviation >= 0 and .deviation <= 3 and .exposure >= 0 and .exposure <= 4 and .market >= 0 and .market <= 3 and .likelihood >= 1 and .likelihood <= 3] | all),
    ([.[] | [.ourAssessment, .theirAssessment, .counterAssessment | select(. != null) | .likelihood] | unique | length <= 1] | all)'
```
Command G:
```bash
curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_RISK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.metadata._redlineAnalysis.changes
  | ([.[] | select(.recommendation != "accept") | (.counterText // "") != ""] | all),
    ([.[] | select(.riskRevised != null and .riskBefore <= .riskAfter) | .riskBefore <= .riskRevised and .riskRevised <= .riskAfter] | all)'
```

**Also check**
- Two identical versions: upload `D-SUPPLY.docx` as a new contract, add the same file as its v2 (the setup's `curl … /versions`), wait, then **Analyze Redlines** v1 vs v2 → a red box "Redline analysis failed" / "The two versions have no differences, so there is nothing to analyze." (TC-AI-02 N1). A later successful run clears the box.
- The same version in both dropdowns: **Analyze Redlines** is disabled.
- Agents service stopped: after about 30 seconds (two tries, 15 s apart) the red box gives a reason starting "The redline analysis could not run:" and the button returns (TC-AI-02 N8).
- API: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_RISK/redline -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` → 400 `{"error":"v1Id and v2Id are required"}`. The same with real ids as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract"; as admin-b → 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}`.
- viewer-a on the Negotiate tab: **Analyze Redlines** is shown, and clicking it does nothing and says nothing (known defect, reported).
- The agents service's `/redline` refuses callers without the secret (`curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/redline -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` → 401); with it, it answers at once `{"status":"queued",…}` and works in the background.
- Each run keeps the last five analyses in `metadata._redlineHistory`.
- Personal data in the two versions reaches the model masked, and the stored analysis quotes the real values (TC-PII-07).

**Known limits**
- The panel shows the latest analysis whatever versions are selected, and doesn't say which pair it was run on (known defect, reported).
- The risk numbers appear only inside the text lines; there is no separate field on the card. The weights are a first judgement, not calibrated against lawyers' ratings (FF1).
- A REDLINE_ANALYZED event is recorded when the job reaches the agents service, so a run that then fails (for example "no differences") has one too.

### E2E-NEG-05 · "Download for counterparty" returns their own Word file with our changes as tracked changes (BB2)

**Covers:** `GET /contracts/:id/redline/counterparty` · **Actions → Download for counterparty (Word)** · FIX_TRACKER BB1, BB2
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_SUP`: v1 is their `D-SUPPLY.docx`; E2E-REV-02 changed §7 in a later version, so our current version differs from their file. (If it has no edit yet, change one word in the Styled view first.)
- `$C_PDF` (their paper came as a PDF) and `$C_MAIL` (their file only, untouched).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_SUP` → **Actions** → **Download for counterparty (Word)**. | The item shows a spinner, the browser saves "<title> - our changes to their v1.docx", and a notice appears under the header: "Downloaded <file name>. Their Word file, with N paragraphs changed as tracked changes under your name. Open it in Word to check, then send it." with **Dismiss**. |
| 2 | Open the file in Word or LibreOffice. | Their document, in their formatting, with Track Changes on. Our changes (for example §7's governing law) are tracked insertions and deletions by "Legal Counsel". Accept All reads as the contract's current version in Draft Legal; Reject All gives their file back. |
| 3 | Command A. | 200; `content-disposition` names the same file; `x-redline-stats` (URL-encoded JSON) has `modified`, `inserted`, `deleted`, `skipped` [], `verified` true and `acceptedExisting` 0. |
| 4 | `audit REDLINE_EXPORTED $C_SUP` | Metadata `{"audience":"counterparty","author":"Legal Counsel","theirVersionNumber":1,"versionNumber":<current>,"redline":{…},"sha256":"…"}`. The contract's Activity lists "REDLINE EXPORTED". |
| 5 | Open `$C_PDF` → **Actions** → **Download for counterparty (Word)**. | No file. A red notice: "There is no Word file of theirs to mark up: this contract came as a PDF, or was drafted here. Use Export › Word (tracked) to send a comparison between two versions instead." There is no "Export" menu; the comparison's Word file is **Compare** → **Word (tracked)** (known defect in the message, reported). The API answers 409 with `"code":"NO_WORD_ORIGINAL"`. |
| 6 | Open `$C_MAIL` → the same item. | "Version 1 is their file as they sent it: there are no changes of ours to mark up yet." (409 `NO_CHANGES`). |

Command A: `curl -s -D - -o theirs.docx "$API/contracts/$C_SUP/redline/counterparty" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | grep -iE '^HTTP|^content-disposition|^x-redline-stats'`

**Also check**
- Their file with tracked changes of its own: upload §0's `D-MARKUP.docx` as a new contract, change one word in the Styled view, then download for counterparty. The notice adds "Their file had N tracked changes of their own; your changes are marked against it as it reads with those accepted."
- A paragraph Draft Legal won't edit: make a copy of `D-SUPPLY.docx` with a date field in §1 (Word: Insert → Date & Time, "Update automatically"), upload it, change a word in §1, and download. The notice lists "Left as they were, so change these by hand in Word:" with "“<§1 text>” (it contains a field)". A text box or an embedded image is reported the same way.
- If the file fails its own check that accepting every change gives our version, the notice ends "Check this file carefully before sending it: it didn't pass its own check that accepting every change gives this version." (not reproducible on demand).
- While a Google Docs copy is out: "<name> has this contract open in Google Docs. Publish that copy back first, so the counterparty gets your latest changes." (409; E2E-NEG-06).
- "Their paper" is their latest Word file that isn't a Google Docs round trip: after their Word return through the portal or email, the file name says "our changes to their v<N>" with that version (E2E-PORT-04).
- Any role that can open the contract can download (`view:contract`), and the changes are authored under the downloader's name: viewer-a gets the file with changes by "<viewer-a's name>". rep-a: only on contracts rep-a owns. admin-b → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.

**Known limits**
- Paragraphs with fields, text boxes, embedded objects or their own pending tracked changes are left as they are and listed.
- The file goes to your computer; sending it to the counterparty is up to you.

### E2E-NEG-06 · Edit in Google Docs locks the contract, and publishing the copy back makes the next version (BB3, BB4)

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/external-edit/start` · `GET /contracts/:id/external-edit/working-copy` · `POST /contracts/:id/external-edit/publish` · `POST /contracts/:id/external-edit/discard` · `POST /contracts/:id/share` · `POST /portal/:portalToken/versions` (a counterparty upload during the lock) · FIX_TRACKER BB3, BB4, DD6
**Roles:** counsel-a, contracts-a, viewer-a, admin-a · **Needs:** a Google account (or Word/LibreOffice: any editor that saves `.docx` with comments and suggestions); agents service + model key for the re-analysis after publishing · **Time:** ~30 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_GD` analysed. As counsel-a make one edit in the Styled view (for example "one (1) year" → "two (2) years" in §3) so our version differs from their file: that's v2.
- A second browser (or profile) signed in as contracts-a.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$C_GD` → **Actions** → **Edit in Google Docs**. | A dialog "Edit in Google Docs": "Work on this contract with your team in Google Docs, then publish it back here as the next version.", two paragraphs explaining the copy and the read-only lock, **Cancel** and **Download working copy**. |
| 2 | Click **Download working copy**. | The browser saves "<title> - v2 for Google Docs.docx". The dialog becomes four numbered steps: "Downloaded <file name>. Their Version 1, with 1 paragraph changed as suggestions."; "In Google Drive, choose New › File upload and pick that file, then open it with Google Docs." with the link **Open Google Drive**; "Share it with your team. Accept or reject suggestions, suggest changes, and comment."; "When you're done: File › Download › Microsoft Word (.docx), then choose Publish from Google Docs on this contract. Comments come in as internal comments; nothing is shared with the counterparty." Button **Done**. |
| 3 | Click **Done**. | Under the header a blue banner: "Editing in Google Docs. Legal Counsel took a working copy of Version 2 on <date, time>. This contract is read-only here until it's published back or discarded." with **Working copy**, **Publish from Google Docs** and **Discard copy**. The header's **Edit** is replaced by a disabled "In Google Docs" (tooltip "Legal Counsel is editing this contract in Google Docs"). **Actions** → **Edit in Google Docs** is disabled. |
| 4 | In the second browser (contracts-a) open `$C_GD` (reload it if it was already open). | The same banner and the disabled "In Google Docs". contracts-a (who can edit) also gets **Publish from Google Docs** and **Discard copy**. A page opened before the copy was taken shows nothing until it is reloaded; once a page knows a copy is out, it checks every 15 seconds and notices when the copy is published or discarded. |
| 5 | Command A (writes while locked). | Each answers 409 with `"code":"EDITING_IN_GOOGLE_DOCS"` and `"detail":"Legal Counsel is editing this contract in Google Docs (from Version 2). Publish that copy back, or discard it, before changing the contract here."`: an editor save, a version upload, a clause apply. A second start gives 409 `"code":"ALREADY_EDITING_IN_GOOGLE_DOCS"`. |
| 6 | As counsel-a: **Actions** → **Download for counterparty (Word)**. Then open any clause in the review drawer (rail **Clauses** → **View all** → **Review and suggest changes** on a card). | The notice "Legal Counsel has this contract open in Google Docs. Publish that copy back first, so the counterparty gets your latest changes." The drawer is read-only: "Read-only: accepting, rejecting or changing this clause needs edit access to the contract." (the cause is the lock, not access; known defect, reported). |
| 7 | Google Drive → **New** → **File upload** → the working copy → open it with Google Docs. Accept the suggestion. Add a comment on §2: `E2E: check the fee`. Switch to Suggesting and type a new sentence at the end of §2: `Disputed amounts are not late.`; leave that suggestion open. **File** → **Download** → **Microsoft Word (.docx)**. | Google Docs shows our change as a suggestion by "Legal Counsel". The downloaded file has one comment and one open suggestion (an insertion; a replaced word would count as two, a deletion and an insertion). |
| 8 | Back on `$C_GD`: **Publish from Google Docs** → pick the downloaded file. | A toast "Published as Version 3" with "1 comment added as internal comments; 1 open suggestion included as written". The banner goes and **Edit** is back. |
| 9 | Read **History**, the comments, and `status $C_GD`. | v3: "Published from Google Docs by Legal Counsel; 1 suggestion still open (<your Google name>), included as written; 1 comment imported (internal)". Rail **Comments** → **Open the thread**: a comment reading "From Google Docs, <your Google name> (<date>): E2E: check the fee" followed by "On: “<the words you commented on>”". Its author shows as the first 8 characters of the publisher's user id (known defect, reported). `analysisStatus` goes PENDING and then DONE: the new file is read and analysed like any upload. `versions $C_GD`: v3 is a Word file. |
| 10 | `audit EXTERNAL_EDIT_STARTED $C_GD`; `audit EXTERNAL_EDIT_PUBLISHED $C_GD` | STARTED: `{"provider":"google-docs","baseVersionNumber":2,"workingCopySha256":"…","theirVersionNumber":1,"redline":{…}}`. PUBLISHED: `{"versionNumber":3,"baseVersionNumber":2,"revisions":{…},"comments":1,"sha256":"…","filename":"…","forced":false}`. |
| 11 | **Edit in Google Docs** → **Download working copy** → **Done**. Click **Discard copy**, then **Keep editing in Google Docs**; then **Discard copy** → **Discard**. | The prompt reads "Discard the Google Docs copy? Nothing from it comes back here, and the copy in Google Drive stays where it is."; **Keep editing in Google Docs** closes it. **Discard** shows the toast "Google Docs copy discarded" / "The contract can be edited here again."; the banner goes; no new version. `audit EXTERNAL_EDIT_DISCARDED $C_GD` has one event. |
| 12 | Start a copy again (step 11's first three clicks). Then Command B: admin-a makes an upload link and uploads `D-SUPPLY-v2.docx` through the portal, as a counterparty would. | 201 from the portal: the counterparty's upload isn't blocked by the lock. It becomes v4. |
| 13 | **Publish from Google Docs** with the working copy you just downloaded. | A red line: "Version 4 arrived while this copy was in Google Docs (it was made from Version 3). Publishing makes it Version 5 and leaves Version 4's changes out of it." with **Publish anyway** and **Dismiss**. Click **Publish anyway** → "Published as Version 5"; the audit event has `"forced":true`. |

Command A (while the copy is out):
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_GD/html-version -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"htmlContent":"<p>x</p>"}'
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_GD/versions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@D-SUPPLY.docx"
CL=$(curl -s $API/contracts/$C_GD/clauses -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq -r '.data[0].id')
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_GD/clauses/$CL/apply -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"proposedText":"x"}'
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/contracts/$C_GD/external-edit/start -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A"
```
Command B:
```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_GD/share -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"permissions":["upload"]}' | jq -r .portalUrl | sed 's#.*/portal/##')
curl -s -X POST $API/portal/$TOKEN/versions -F "file=@D-SUPPLY-v2.docx" | jq '{versionNumber, message}'
```

**Also check**
- The wrong file: start a copy, then **Publish from Google Docs** with `D-NDA.docx` → "That file doesn't look like "<title>" (it shares little of its text). Check it is the copy you edited in Google Docs." with **Publish anyway** (click **Dismiss**). With a PDF (switch the file picker to all files) → "Publish the Word file: in Google Docs, File → Download → Microsoft Word (.docx)." Then **Discard copy**.
- `$C_PDF` (their paper came as a PDF): the working copy is a clean Word file of our text, and step 1 of the dialog reads only "Downloaded <file name>."
- An EXECUTED or ARCHIVED contract: **Download working copy** leaves the dialog open with "This contract is signed or archived, so it can no longer be edited." (409 `CONTRACT_FINAL`). A contract whose text isn't ready yet: "The document is still being prepared. Try again in a moment." (`VERSION_NOT_READY`).
- Two people pressing **Download working copy** at the same moment: one gets the copy, the other "<name> is editing this contract in Google Docs (from Version N). …".
- API with no copy out: `GET …/external-edit/working-copy` → 409 `{"code":"NOT_EDITING_IN_GOOGLE_DOCS","detail":"No Google Docs copy is out for this contract."}`; `POST …/discard` → 200 `{"discarded":false}`; `POST …/publish` → 409 "No Google Docs copy is out for this contract, so there is nothing to publish. It may already have been published or discarded."
- Publish refusals: no file → 400 "Attach the Word file you downloaded from Google Docs."; over 25 MB → 413 "That file is over 25 MB."; a Word file with no text → 422 "That file has no text in it. Check you downloaded the right document from Google Docs."
- Someone in Edit mode when another user takes a copy: their next save fails with the toast "Not saved: this contract is being edited in Google Docs" and the lock's message.
- An APPROVED contract goes back to DRAFT when a copy is published.
- Roles: **Edit in Google Docs** shows only for roles that can edit contracts (ADMIN, LEGAL_COUNSEL, LEGAL_OPS, CONTRACT_MANAGER, PROCUREMENT). viewer-a sees the banner and **Working copy** but no **Publish** or **Discard**; their **Working copy** click does nothing (403; known defect, reported). `POST …/external-edit/start` as viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: edit:contract".

**Known limits**
- There is no connection to Google: the copy travels by download and upload.
- Suggestions left open in Google Docs are published as written, and imported comments are authored by the person who publishes, with the Google author named in the text.
- Any user who can edit the contract can publish or discard the copy, not only the person who took it.

### E2E-PORT-01 · An admin shares a contract by link or email, with the permissions chosen, and can list and revoke the links

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/share` · `GET /contracts/:id/share` · `DELETE /contracts/:id/share/:linkId` · **Actions → Share** · /portal/:portalToken (a revoked link)
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Mailpit; `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN=inbound.test` for the reply invitation (section setup) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$C_SHARE` analysed.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a open `$C_SHARE` → **Actions** → **Share**. | A dialog "Share Contract" with "Create new link": "Label (optional)" (placeholder "e.g. Acme Legal Review"); "Send to (optional)" (placeholder "counsel@counterparty.com") with "Leave blank to just generate a link you copy yourself."; "Expires in" (24 hours, 3 days, 7 days, 14 days, 30 days; 7 days selected); "Permissions" with "Read — view contract" (always on), "Comment — add comments" and "Upload — return a revised version"; and **Generate link**. |
| 2 | Label `E2E read-only`; leave the rest. **Generate link**. | A box "Link created! Share this URL:" with the URL (`http://localhost:5173/portal/<token>`) and **Copy** (turns "Copied!"). Save the URL as `$LINK_READ`. "Active links" lists "E2E read-only", "Expires <Mon D, YYYY> · 0 views" and the chip "read", with a bin (tooltip "Revoke link"). |
| 3 | Label `E2E counterparty`; Send to `counterparty@example.test`; a "Note (optional)" box appears: type `Please return your redline by Friday.` Tick **Comment** and **Upload**; the hint "Lets the counterparty download the document, redline it offline, and upload it back as a new version for you to review." appears. Expires in **14 days**. The button now reads **Send link**; click it. | "Link sent to counterparty@example.test" with the URL and **Copy**. Save the URL as `$LINK_CP`. The new link is first under "Active links": "E2E counterparty", "Sent to counterparty@example.test", chips "upload", "comment", "read". The form clears. |
| 4 | Mailpit: open the new email to counterparty@example.test. | Subject "[Demo Org, Inc.] Review and return: <title>". Heading "Shared for review", "Demo Org, Inc. · <type>", "Admin User has shared <title> with you for review.", a box "Message from Admin User: Please return your redline by Friday.", a button **Open the document →** with the same URL, "You can download the document, mark it up in Word, and upload your revised version back through the same link.", "Or just reply to this email with your marked-up copy attached (PDF or DOCX) — it will be filed against this contract automatically.", and "This link expires on <YYYY-MM-DD>." Reply-To is `contracts+<$C_SHARE>@inbound.test`. |
| 5 | Command A. | Both links, newest first: `permissions` ["read"] and ["read","comment","upload"], `invitedEmail` null and "counterparty@example.test", `expiresAt` 7 and 14 days out, `viewCount` 0. |
| 6 | Open `$LINK_READ` in a private window (the portal loads; E2E-PORT-02 tests it). Back as admin-a, reload the contract page and open **Actions** → **Share** again (the dialog keeps its list for a few minutes unless the page is reloaded). | "E2E read-only" now reads "1 view". |
| 7 | Click the bin on "E2E read-only". | It leaves "Active links" at once (there is no confirmation). |
| 8 | Reload `$LINK_READ` in the private window. | "Link unavailable": "This share link is invalid, has expired, or has been revoked." and "What to do next" with three points ("Reply to the email that carried this link and ask the sender for a new one.", …). `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' $API/portal/<its token>/contract` → 401 `{"error":"Invalid or expired share link"}`. |
| 9 | `audit LINK_SHARED $C_SHARE`; `audit LINK_REVOKED $C_SHARE` | Two LINK_SHARED events with `shareLinkId`, `permissions`, `expiresAt` and `emailedTo` (null, then "counterparty@example.test"); one LINK_REVOKED with the revoked `shareLinkId`. The contract's Activity lists "LINK SHARED" and "LINK REVOKED". |

Command A: `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_SHARE/share -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '.data[] | {id, label, invitedEmail, permissions, expiresAt, viewCount}'`

**Also check**
- Without an email provider (API started without `SMTP_HOST`): step 3 says "Link created! Share this URL:" and "Email isn't configured on this deployment, so nothing was sent to counterparty@example.test. Copy the URL below and send it yourself."; the API's `emailDelivered` is false. In development the API console prints `[share] ✉  counterparty@example.test  →  <link>  (<type> "<title>", expires <date>)` either way (TC-OPS-04).
- Without `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN` the email has no Reply-To and no "reply to this email" sentence.
- counsel-a (and every role but ADMIN): **Actions** has no **Share**. The API: `POST`, `GET` and `DELETE …/share` as counsel-a → 403 "Missing permission: configure:contract".
- API validation (as admin-a, `POST $API/contracts/$C_SHARE/share`): `{"permissions":["delete"]}` → 400 `{"error":"Unknown permission(s): delete"}`; `{"permissions":"read"}` → 400 `{"error":"permissions must be an array of strings"}`; `{"recipientEmail":"not-an-email"}` → 400 `{"error":"recipientEmail is not a valid email address"}`; `"expiresInHours":5000` → a link expiring in 30 days, `0` → in 1 hour, `"abc"` → in 7 days.
- In the dialog, an invalid "Send to" address (for example `not-an-email`) makes **Send link** do nothing visible: the 400 is not shown (known defect, reported).
- `{"permissions":["edit"]}` (API only; the dialog doesn't offer it) makes a link that can upload like "upload"; the dialog shows it with the chip "upload".
- admin-b: `POST $API/contracts/$C_SHARE/share` → 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}`; `DELETE` an Org A link → 404. Revoking the same link twice → 404 `{"error":"Share link not found"}`.
- An expired link that nobody revoked stays under "Active links" (known defect, reported). Make one with `"expiresInHours":1` and check after an hour: its URL shows "Link unavailable".

**Known limits**
- Only admins can share, by default (`configure:contract`).
- A link's URL is shown only when it's created; the list has no **Copy**. Make a new link if the URL is lost.
- Revoking has no confirmation.

### E2E-PORT-02 · The counterparty reads, downloads, comments and returns a revision in the portal, and the owner is told

**Covers:** /portal/:portalToken · `GET /portal/:portalToken/contract` · `GET /portal/:portalToken/download/docx` · `POST /portal/:portalToken/comments` · `POST /portal/:portalToken/versions` · background: the parse and analysis of the returned file, the owner's notification email · docs/38 TC-ACC-06 · FIX_TRACKER AA1, AA4, DD6
**Roles:** counterparty (private window, no account), counsel-a (owner), admin-a · **Needs:** Mailpit; agents service + model key (to analyse the return) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$LINK_CP` from E2E-PORT-01 (comment and upload, 14 days, labelled "E2E counterparty"). `TOKEN_CP=${LINK_CP##*/portal/}`.
- Three more links on `$C_SHARE` for the permission checks (Command A): read-only, comment-only and upload-only.
- `D-SUPPLY-v2.docx`, `fake.pdf`.

Command A:
```bash
mk() { curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_SHARE/share -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$1" | jq -r .portalUrl; }
LINK_R=$(mk '{"label":"E2E read","permissions":["read"]}'); LINK_C=$(mk '{"label":"E2E comment","permissions":["comment"]}'); LINK_U=$(mk '{"label":"E2E upload","permissions":["upload"]}')
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open `$LINK_CP` in a private window. | A header band in the org's brand colour (dark when none is set) with the org's logo (or a building icon) and "Demo Org, Inc.", and on the right "E2E counterparty" and "Expires <Month D, YYYY>". Under it a band: "Shared by Demo Org, Inc.", "Expires in 14d", "· E2E counterparty", and **Print**, **Download .docx** and **Upload revised**. Then the title, a chip with the type, "› <counterparty>" if known, "Effective …" and "Expires …" if known, and "View + comment + redline" on the right; tabs **Document** and **Comments**; the contract's current text, read-only. Footer: "Shared securely by Demo Org, Inc. · You may comment and return a revised version · Do not redistribute this link" and "Secured by <logo> · Terms · Privacy". No risk scores, AI summary, playbook findings, approvals or internal comments anywhere. |
| 2 | Click **Download .docx**. | A Word file "<title with dashes>-v1.docx" with the contract's text (plain; no tracked changes). `curl -s -o p.docx -w '%{http_code}\n' $API/portal/$TOKEN_CP/download/docx` → 200. |
| 3 | **Comments** tab. | "Add a comment" with "Your name (optional)", "Clause / Section (optional, e.g. Section 5.2)", "Write your comment…" and **Post comment** (disabled while empty). Below: "No comments yet". |
| 4 | Name `Casey Counterparty`, section `Section 5`, text `We need a higher cap.` → **Post comment**. | The form clears. The list still says "No comments yet": the portal never lists comments, not even your own (known defect, reported). |
| 5 | As counsel-a open `$C_SHARE` (reload it if it was open) → rail **Comments** ("1 comment. Open the thread"). | The Comments tab (filters Unresolved, All, Resolved) shows the comment by "External reviewer" with the chip "Section 5", "just now" and "We need a higher cap.", with reply, "Mark resolved" and "Delete". The name the counterparty typed is not shown anywhere (known defect, reported). No notification was sent for it (known limit). |
| 6 | In the portal: **Upload revised** → pick `fake.pdf`. | A red line under the band: "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX." No new version. |
| 7 | **Upload revised** → pick `D-SUPPLY-v2.docx`. | The button spins, then "Uploaded v2 · D-SUPPLY-v2.docx. The owner has been notified." The document area shows "Version 2 was received and is being processed. Showing version 1 until it's ready." with a spinner; the page checks every 3 seconds and, once the file is read, shows v2's text and the notice goes (AA1). |
| 8 | As counsel-a: the **Notifications** bell in the header. Mailpit. | A notification "Counterparty returned a revised version": "A revised version (v2) of "<title>" was uploaded via the share link — E2E counterparty."; clicking it opens the contract. Mailpit has an email to legal@demo.com with the subject "Counterparty returned a revised version" and that sentence. |
| 9 | Open `$C_SHARE` (reload if it was open). | The status pill reads "In Review" (the API's `status` is `UNDER_NEGOTIATION`). While v2 is read, the document says "Preparing document…". The strip under the header reads "→ You → You (review counter)", "Waiting today", "Last: Uploaded by counterparty via portal (D-SUPPLY-v2.docx)", "Next: Counterparty uploaded v2 — review" and **Nudge**. **History** lists v2 "Uploaded by counterparty via portal (D-SUPPLY-v2.docx)". |
| 10 | `versions $C_SHARE`; open **Compare**. | v2: a Word file, `createdByName` "E2E counterparty (counterparty)"; Compare's chip shows that name cut to 20 characters: "v2 · E2E counterparty (co… · today". |
| 11 | After the analysis finishes (`status $C_SHARE` DONE). | The title, type and counterparty are what they were before the return (AA4). About a minute later the playbook review is redone on v2 (`GET …/playbook-review` → `versionId` = v2's id). |
| 12 | `audit PORTAL_VIEWED $C_SHARE`; `audit PORTAL_UPLOADED_VERSION $C_SHARE` | PORTAL_VIEWED once per portal load (`shareLinkId`, `ipAddress`), plus one with `"action":"download_docx"` for step 2. PORTAL_UPLOADED_VERSION: `{"shareLinkId":"…","versionNumber":2,"filename":"D-SUPPLY-v2.docx","ipAddress":"…","userAgent":"…"}`. The Share dialog shows the link's view count. |

**Also check**
- Read-only `$LINK_R`: no **Upload revised** and no **Comments** tab; "Read-only view" on the right; the footer says "Read-only". API: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/portal/<token>/comments -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"body":"x"}'` → 403 `{"error":"This link does not allow comments"}`; `-X POST $API/portal/<token>/versions -F "file=@D-SUPPLY-v2.docx"` → 403 `{"error":"This link does not allow uploads"}`.
- Comment-only `$LINK_C`: the **Comments** tab works, but the page says "Read-only view" at the top right, while the footer says "You may read and comment". Upload-only `$LINK_U`: no **Comments** tab, yet the page says "View + comment + redline" and the footer "You may comment and return a revised version"; commenting through the API → 403 (known defect, reported: the labels don't match the link).
- `POST $API/portal/$TOKEN_CP/comments` with `{"body":""}` → 400 `{"error":"body is required"}`. A file over 25 MB → 413 `{"error":"File too large (25MB limit)"}`. `fake.pdf` sent as `type=application/pdf` → 415 with `error` "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX." (TC-ACC-06).
- A made-up or altered token → 401 `{"error":"Invalid or expired share link"}`; the page shows "Link unavailable".
- A link whose contract is EXECUTED or ARCHIVED: **Upload revised** → "This contract is already finalised — uploads are closed. Contact the sender if changes are still needed." (409).
- A contract with no document text (create one with `POST $API/contracts`, then share it): "No document has been attached to this link yet" and "The link is valid and the record exists, but Demo Org, Inc. has not uploaded a version for you to read. …"; no **Print** or **Download .docx**; the download API answers 400 `{"error":"No content available to export"}`.
- A link that expires within 48 hours (`"expiresInHours":24`): the banner "This link expires soon. Contact the sender to get a new link before it expires."
- A returned file that can't be read: make a Word-looking file with no readable document (`mkdir -p bad/word && printf broken > bad/word/document.xml && (cd bad && zip -qr ../D-BROKEN.docx word)`) and upload it through a comment-and-upload link. The portal accepts it and shows it as being processed; once reading it has failed three times (a minute or so) it shows "We couldn't read version N. Demo Org, Inc. has the file and will follow up. Showing version N−1 until it's ready." and stops checking; the owner's page shows "Document extraction failed".
- The portal shows the version the contract stands on: after an internal Undo, not the undone version (DD6).
- Counterparty uploads are accepted while a Google Docs copy is out (E2E-NEG-06 step 12).
- After the return, have admin-a send a new link (**Actions** → **Share** → **Generate link**). admin-a's strip now reads "Waiting on <counterparty> reply" (we moved last), but counsel-a's still reads "You (review counter)": counsel-a can't read share links (`GET …/share` needs `configure:contract`), so the owner's strip never knows a link was sent (known defect, reported).
- **Nudge** only scrolls to the rail's Comments section; it sends nothing.

**Known limits**
- The portal's Comments tab never lists comments, and the owner can't answer in the portal.
- A counterparty comment sends no notification; only a returned version does, to the contract's owner.
- The status pill groups UNDER_NEGOTIATION under "In Review"; the API's `status` tells them apart.

### E2E-PORT-03 · A redline the counterparty emails back becomes the next version

**Covers:** `POST /inbound/email` · `POST /contracts/:id/share` (to allow the sender) · background: the parse and analysis of the attachment, the owner's notification email · docs/38 TC-SEC-06, TC-DOC-09, TC-ACC-06
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a (owner), an external sender (curl) · **Needs:** `INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET` and `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN` set (section setup); Mailpit; agents service + model key (to analyse the attachment) · **Time:** ~15 min

**How it works.** In production a mail provider (SendGrid Inbound Parse, Mailgun, Postmark) posts each email sent to `contracts+<contractId>@<INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN>` to `POST /api/v1/inbound/email`, with the shared secret in the `x-inbound-secret` header. The contract id comes from the `+` tag of the To address. The sender must be the contract's counterparty (its counterparty record's email) or an address that a live share link allowing uploads was sent to. The first attachment whose bytes are a PDF or DOCX becomes the next version. Locally you post the same request with curl, as JSON or as provider-style multipart.

**Preconditions**
- `$C_MAIL` analysed (counsel-a owns it; its only version is their file).
- Command A: an upload link sent to `counterparty@example.test` (this is what allows that sender), and the JSON payload.

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_MAIL/share -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"label":"E2E email","permissions":["upload"],"recipientEmail":"counterparty@example.test"}' | jq '{emailedTo, emailDelivered, id: .shareLink.id}'
jq -n --arg to "contracts+$C_MAIL@inbound.test" --arg b64 "$(base64 < D-SUPPLY-v2.docx | tr -d '\n')" \
  '{to: $to, from: "Casey Counterparty <counterparty@example.test>", subject: "Re: our redline", text: "Our changes are attached.",
    attachments: [{filename: "D-SUPPLY-v2.docx", contentType: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document", contentBase64: $b64}]}' > inbound.json
inbound() { curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/inbound/email" -H "x-inbound-secret: ${2:-$INBOUND_SECRET}" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @"${1:-inbound.json}"; }
```
Command B (the same email as a provider posts it, multipart, with an inline image first):
```bash
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/inbound/email" -H "x-inbound-secret: $INBOUND_SECRET" \
  -F "to=contracts+$C_MAIL@inbound.test" -F "from=Casey Counterparty <counterparty@example.test>" \
  -F "subject=Second round" -F "text=See attached." \
  -F "attachment1=@img.png;type=image/png" -F "attachment2=@D-SUPPLY-v2.docx"
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `inbound` | `HTTP 201` with `{"ok":true,"versionId":"…","versionNumber":2,"filename":"D-SUPPLY-v2.docx","message":"Recorded as v2 on <title>. Owner has been notified."}`. |
| 2 | As counsel-a: the **Notifications** bell; Mailpit. | "Counterparty emailed a revised version": "counterparty@example.test emailed a revised version (v2) of "<title>"." Mailpit has an email to legal@demo.com with that subject and sentence. |
| 3 | Open `$C_MAIL`. | The status pill reads "In Review" (`UNDER_NEGOTIATION`); "Preparing document…" until the file is read, then v2's text. **History**: v2 "Emailed by counterparty@example.test: Re: our redline". |
| 4 | `versions $C_MAIL`, then Command C. | v2 is a Word file with `createdByName` "counterparty@example.test (counterparty)". Its `metadata.inboundEmail` has `from`, `to`, `subject` "Re: our redline" and `textExcerpt` "Our changes are attached." |
| 5 | Command B. | `HTTP 201`, `"versionNumber":3`, `"filename":"D-SUPPLY-v2.docx"`: the image is passed over and the document used (TC-DOC-09). |
| 6 | `audit EMAIL_REDLINE_RECEIVED $C_MAIL` | Two events, each `{"sender":"counterparty@example.test","subject":"…","filename":"D-SUPPLY-v2.docx","versionNumber":N,"senderReason":"share_link_invite_match"}`. The contract's Activity lists "EMAIL REDLINE RECEIVED". |
| 7 | `inbound inbound.json wrong` | `HTTP 401`, `{"error":"Invalid inbound secret"}`. |
| 8 | Copy `inbound.json` to `other.json` with `from` "Someone <someone@elsewhere.test>"; `inbound other.json`. | `HTTP 403`, `{"error":"Sender someone@elsewhere.test is not authorised on this contract. Add them as the counterparty or set INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL=1 (dev only).","sender_reason":"unknown"}`. No new version. |
| 9 | A payload with `to` "contracts@inbound.test" (no tag); then one with `to` "contracts+nosuchcontract@inbound.test". | `HTTP 400` `{"error":"Could not extract contract id from To: address. Expected format: contracts+<id>@…"}`; then `HTTP 404` `{"error":"Contract not found"}`. |
| 10 | A payload whose only attachment is `img.png` (base64, `contentType` "image/png"). | `HTTP 400` `{"error":"No PDF or DOCX attachment found. We only attach PDF/DOCX as new versions.","attachments":[{"filename":"img.png","contentType":"image/png"}]}`. |
| 11 | Revoke the "E2E email" link (Share dialog, or `DELETE $API/contracts/$C_MAIL/share/<id>` as admin-a); `inbound` again. | `HTTP 403` with the "not authorised" error: a revoked (or expired) link no longer allows the sender. |

Command C: `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_MAIL/versions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.data[] | select(.versionNumber == 2) | {createdByName, mimeType, changeNote}'` (the version list doesn't carry `metadata`; read it with `curl -s $API/contracts/$C_MAIL -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.versions[] | select(.versionNumber == 2) | .metadata.inboundEmail'`).

**Also check**
- A link that allows only reading, sent to the same address, doesn't allow email returns: the sender gets 403.
- The counterparty record's email also allows the sender (`"senderReason":"counterparty_email_match"`): link `$C_MAIL` to a counterparty whose email is the sender's (Counterparties page) and send from that address.
- `from` that isn't an address (`"from":"nobody"`) → 422 "Request body failed validation".
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET` unset → 503 `{"error":"Inbound email handler not configured"}` in every environment (TC-SEC-06).
- An EXECUTED contract → 409 `{"error":"Contract already executed — emails ignored"}`. An ARCHIVED one is accepted and goes back to UNDER_NEGOTIATION, although the portal refuses uploads to archived contracts (known defect, reported).
- An attachment over 25 MB → 413 `{"error":"Attachment too large (25MB limit)"}`; seven images before the document still work (TC-DOC-09).
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL=1` (development only) accepts any sender with `"senderReason":"allow_all_dev"`; with any other `NODE_ENV` the API refuses to start with it set.
- An emailed return isn't blocked by a Google Docs copy; it makes the copy stale (E2E-NEG-06).
- The negotiation strip doesn't recognise an emailed return as the counterparty's: after step 1 it doesn't say "Counterparty uploaded v2 — review" (it does for a portal upload). As counsel-a it reads "Internal review" / "Next: Internal draft — not yet sent to counterparty"; as admin-a "Waiting on <counterparty> reply" (known defect, reported).

**Known limits**
- Locally there is no mail provider; the webhook is exercised with curl only.
- Only the first usable attachment becomes a version; the email body is kept only as a 500-character excerpt on the version.

### E2E-PORT-04 · Their paper, end to end: upload, playbook redline, share, their return, compare and review
