**Covers:** the whole third-party-paper flow across /contracts/:id and /portal/:portalToken · `GET /contracts/:id/playbook-review` · `POST /contracts/:id/redline-against-playbook` · `POST /contracts/:id/redline-against-playbook/apply` · `GET /contracts/:id/redline/counterparty` · `POST /contracts/:id/share` · `GET /portal/:portalToken/contract` · `POST /portal/:portalToken/comments` · `POST /portal/:portalToken/versions` · `GET /contracts/:id/versions/:v1Id/diff/:v2Id` · `POST /contracts/:id/redline` · `POST /contracts/:id/clauses/:clauseId/suggest` · `POST /contracts/:id/clauses/:clauseId/apply` · `PATCH /contracts/clauses/:clauseId/review-state` · FIX_TRACKER AA1–AA5, BB1–BB5
**Roles:** counsel-a (owner), admin-a (shares), the counterparty (private window) · **Needs:** agents service + model key; Mailpit; Word or LibreOffice (or Google Docs) · **Time:** ~45 min

**Preconditions**
- `D-SUPPLY.docx`. Nothing else: this journey makes its own contract. Run it after the journeys above pass; each step points at the journey that tests that piece in depth.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: left rail → **Contracts** → **Upload PDF**. In "Upload Contracts" drop `D-SUPPLY.docx` (the box reads "Drag & drop or click to browse" / "PDF, DOCX, or TXT · up to 50 MB each · multiple files supported"), set the title `E2E Northwind — their paper`, click **Upload contract**. | "Uploaded — AI analysis queued in background", then "1 contract uploaded successfully" with **View Contract**. Click it and save the id from the URL as `$C_E2E`. |
| 2 | Wait for the analysis (1–3 minutes), then about a minute more, and reload. | The document shows their text; the rail's **Playbook review** lists findings (E2E-REV-02); **Review progress** counts the flagged clauses. |
| 3 | **Playbook redline** → **Redline against playbook**; wait; **Accept all** → **Apply N changes**. | "Applied N changes as a new version. Everything you did not accept was left alone." **History** v2 "redline_apply_batch (N clauses): accepted from playbook redline" (E2E-NEG-01). |
| 4 | **Actions** → **Download for counterparty (Word)**. Open the file. | "<title> - our changes to their v1.docx": their Word file, in their formatting, with our playbook changes tracked under "Legal Counsel"; the notice counts the changed paragraphs (E2E-NEG-05). |
| 5 | As admin-a: **Actions** → **Share** → Label `Northwind`, Send to `counterparty@example.test`, tick **Comment** and **Upload** → **Send link**. | "Link sent to counterparty@example.test". Mailpit: "[Demo Org, Inc.] Review and return: <title>" (E2E-PORT-01). Send them the step 4 file yourself; the app doesn't. |
| 6 | As the counterparty (private window, the link from Mailpit): read the document; **Comments** → section `Section 5`, `Please add a super-cap for data breach.` → **Post comment**. | The portal shows v2, our redlined text. The comment reaches counsel-a's Comments tab as "External reviewer" (E2E-PORT-02). |
| 7 | As the counterparty: open the step 4 Word file, **Accept All** tracked changes, then with Track Changes off change §2's "fifteen (15)" to "seven (7)" and §5's "two (2) times the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months" to "the fees paid or payable in the three (3) months". Save as `D-RETURN.docx`. Portal → **Upload revised** → `D-RETURN.docx`. | "Uploaded v3 · D-RETURN.docx. The owner has been notified."; "Version 3 was received and is being processed. Showing version 2 until it's ready." until it's read. |
| 8 | As counsel-a: the bell, Mailpit, then open `$C_E2E`. | "Counterparty returned a revised version" in both. The strip: "You (review counter)" and "Next: Counterparty uploaded v3 — review". After the analysis the title is still "E2E Northwind — their paper" (AA4). |
| 9 | **Compare**: Newer v3, Older v2. | Only their edits show (§2's days, §5's cap), not dozens of list-bullet changes from the Word round trip (AA2). The v3 chip reads "v3 · Northwind (counterpa… · today" (the author "Northwind (counterparty)" cut to 20 characters; E2E-NEG-03). |
| 10 | **History** → **Negotiate**: Baseline v2, Counterparty redlines v3 → **Analyze Redlines**; wait. | The summary with the three average risks; the §5 card is normally "Reject" or "Counter", "beyond our walkaway position", with a counter-proposal and "Revised risk if they accept: …" (E2E-NEG-04). |
| 11 | After v3's analysis and playbook review (reload): open §5 from **Review progress** or its **Playbook review** finding → **Suggest alternative language** → **Apply to document** on the variant that restores a compliant cap. | A new version v4 "redline_apply (<aggression>): …"; the drawer moves to the next pending clause; §5 is recorded as accepted (`resolved`) (E2E-REV-05). |
| 12 | **Clauses** tab → on a clause nobody flagged (for example Governing Law) → **Review and suggest changes** → **Suggest alternative language**, then close the drawer. | Variants appear (or, for a passage labelled as a clause type it isn't, "This text isn't really a … clause, so there's nothing to redline against the playbook." with the reason; AA3). Nothing is decided or applied (AA5). |
| 13 | **Actions** → **Download for counterparty (Word)** again. | "<title> - our changes to their v3.docx": their returned file is now "their paper", with only our v4 change tracked; the notice counts that paragraph. |
| 14 | The contract's Activity tab (or `audit <ACTION> $C_E2E` for each). | Among the "CONTRACT VIEWED" rows: "AGENT TOOL APPLIED" (the staged redline), "REDLINE EXPORTED" (twice), "LINK SHARED", "PORTAL VIEWED", "PORTAL UPLOADED VERSION", "REDLINE ANALYZED", "VERSION CREATED". |

**Also check**
- The counterparty's email return instead of the portal (E2E-PORT-03): with `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN` set, the share email's Reply-To is `contracts+<$C_E2E>@inbound.test`, and posting `D-RETURN.docx` to the webhook from `counterparty@example.test` makes the same kind of version.
- Taking the contract to Google Docs between steps 3 and 5 (E2E-NEG-06) and publishing it back: step 13's file is still based on their Word file, never on the Google Docs round trip.

**Known limits**
- The app never sends the Word file with tracked changes to the counterparty: you download it and send it. The portal's **Download .docx** is a plain Word file of our current text.
- The Negotiate analysis and the playbook review are the model's; their exact findings vary from run to run.

## 5. Approvals, signatures and sealing

This section tests how a contract gets from Draft to Executed. It covers the approval workflows an admin builds
(**Approvals → Manage Workflows**) and how a contract is sent for review and routed to the right workflow. Then every way
an approval is decided: the **My Queue** cards, the decision strip on the contract page, bulk decisions, delegation,
out-of-office, escalation of an overdue step, the assistant and Slack. It also covers the org-wide **All approvals**
view and what happens when an approved contract changes. The second half sends contracts for signature and follows
the public signer portal (sign, decline, turn order, expiry), reminders and voids, and the **Signatures** page. It ends
with the sealed PDF: its certificate page and its PAdES/X.509 signature. The last journeys check the notifications these
flows produce: email in Mailpit, the in-app bell, the daily digest, Slack and Teams. Run the section setup first, then
the journeys in this order: E2E-WFB-01 to 04 (they create the workflows later journeys use), E2E-APPR-01 to 13,
E2E-SIGN-01 to 10, then E2E-NOTIF-01 to 06. Most journeys need only the local stack and Mailpit. The ones that need
the agents service, a Slack workspace or a Teams channel say so.

### Before you start: section 5 setup

- §0 is done: Org A is seeded, the five invited Org A accounts exist, Org B ("QA Org B") is registered, the §0.5
  variables are set, Mailpit runs and `.env` has the SMTP lines. Emails come from `qa@draftlegal.local` (`EMAIL_FROM`).
- **One API process only** (§0.2). This section's background jobs run inside it: **notification.worker** (in-app
  notifications and their emails, escalation timers, signing reminders), **signing.worker** (the sealed PDF) and
  scan.worker (the daily digest).
- Gotenberg and MinIO are running (`docker compose ps`). Sealing a Word or text contract renders a PDF in Gotenberg.
- Use a browser window at least **1280 px wide**. Below that, the contract page's right-hand rail (its **Approval** and
  **Signatures** sections) becomes a drawer you open with the floating button.
- Seeded display names: admin-a "Admin User", counsel-a "Legal Counsel", contracts-a "Casey Contracts", rep-a "Sam
  Sales". The invited users have the names given at invite time; the steps say "approver-a's name" and so on.
- Remember §0.5: signing in with `curl` signs that user out of the browser. The helpers below never sign in; they use
  the tokens you already have.

Paste these helpers once per shell, from the repo root, after the §0.5 lines:

```bash
# ── Section 5 helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INTERNAL_SECRET=${INTERNAL_SECRET:-$(grep '^INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)}
TOOLS=http://localhost:3001/api/internal/ai/tools            # the agents service's tool endpoints
uid() { curl -s "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" | jq -r .id; }      # a user's id, without signing in
ADMIN_A_ID=$(uid "$ADMIN_A");        COUNSEL_A_ID=$(uid "$COUNSEL_A");  CONTRACTS_A_ID=$(uid "$CONTRACTS_A")
LEGALOPS_A_ID=$(uid "$LEGALOPS_A");  FINANCE_A_ID=$(uid "$FINANCE_A");  APPROVER_A_ID=$(uid "$APPROVER_A")
VIEWER_A_ID=$(uid "$VIEWER_A");      REP_A_ID=$(uid "$REP_A");          ADMIN_B_ID=$(uid "$ADMIN_B")

# mk <token> <title> <TYPE> [value] [currency] → id of a new DRAFT contract with one text version.
# The token must be able to edit contracts when a value is given (admin-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, legalops-a).
mk() {
  local f="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/qa-$RANDOM.txt" id
  printf '%s\n1. Services. The Supplier shall provide the services in Schedule 1.\n2. Fees. 1,000 per month, payable within 30 days of invoice.\n3. Term. 12 months, renewing automatically unless either party gives 60 days notice.\n4. Liability. The liability of each party is capped at the fees paid in the prior 12 months.\n' "$2" > "$f"
  id=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
       -F "file=@$f;type=text/plain" -F "title=$2" -F "type=$3" | jq -r .id)
  [ -n "$4" ] && curl -s -o /dev/null -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$id" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
       -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"value\":$4,\"currency\":\"${5:-USD}\"}"
  echo "$id"
}
st()   { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r .status; }         # contract status
wfid() { curl -s "$API/approvals/workflows" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r --arg n "$1" '.[] | select(.name==$n) | .id'; }

# submit <token> <contractId> [workflowId] → prints the answer and HTTP code; sets INST and STEP (first step)
submit() {
  local body='{}' r
  [ -n "$3" ] && body="{\"workflowDefinitionId\":\"$3\"}"
  r=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$2/submit-approval" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
       -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$body" -w '\n%{http_code}')
  echo "$r"
  INST=$(echo "$r" | head -1 | jq -r '.instanceId // empty'); STEP=$(echo "$r" | head -1 | jq -r '.steps[0].id // empty')
}
# qstep <token> <contractId> → sets INST and STEP from that user's My Queue item for the contract
qstep() {
  read -r INST STEP <<< "$(curl -s "$API/approvals/my-queue" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
    | jq -r --arg c "$2" '[.data[] | select(.contract.id==$c)][0] | "\(.instanceId) \(.stepId)"')"
  echo "INST=$INST STEP=$STEP"
}
# decide <token> <instanceId> <stepId> APPROVED|REJECTED|DELEGATED [comment] [delegateToUserId]
decide() {
  curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/approvals/$2/decide" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d "$(jq -nc --arg s "$3" --arg d "$4" --arg c "${5:-}" --arg t "${6:-}" \
      '{stepId:$s, decision:$d} + (if $c != "" then {comment:$c} else {} end) + (if $t != "" then {delegateTo:$t} else {} end)')"
}
# inst <instanceId> → the approval as admin-a sees it
inst() { curl -s "$API/approvals/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '{status, currentStepOrder,
  workflow: .definition.name, aiSummary, approvalRecommendation,
  steps: [.steps[] | {stepOrder, stepName, approverName, status, decision, comment}]}'; }
# approve_now <contractId> → routes it through "QA quick approval" (admin-a) and approves it: the contract ends Approved
approve_now() { submit "$ADMIN_A" "$1" "$W_QUICK" > /dev/null; decide "$ADMIN_A" "$INST" "$STEP" APPROVED; }
# notes <token> → that user's newest in-app notifications (the bell)
notes() { curl -s "$API/approvals/notifications?limit=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
  | jq '{unreadCount, latest: [.data[] | {type, title, body, read}]}'; }
# audit <ACTION[,ACTION]> [resourceId] → newest matching audit events (as admin-a)
audit() { curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=$1&limit=5${2:+&resourceId=$2}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \
  | jq '[.events[] | {action, resourceType, resourceId, actor: .actor.name, metadata, createdAt}]'; }
# mail <address> → the newest messages to that address in Mailpit (the web UI at :8025 shows the same)
mail() { curl -s -G http://localhost:8025/api/v1/search --data-urlencode "query=to:$1" --data-urlencode limit=5 \
  | jq '[.messages[] | {Subject, Snippet, Created}]'; }
# sql "<statement>" → local development database only
sql() { docker exec -i clm_postgres psql -U clm -d clm_dev -c "$1"; }

# ── Signing ──
# sfs <token> <contractId> '<signers JSON>' [ANY|SEQUENTIAL] [days] [message] → the new request (201) or the refusal
sfs() {
  curl -s -w '\n  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/$2/send-for-signature" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d "$(jq -nc --argjson s "$3" --arg o "${4:-ANY}" --argjson d "${5:-14}" --arg m "${6:-}" \
      '{signers:$s, signOrder:$o, expiresInDays:$d} + (if $m != "" then {message:$m} else {} end)')"
}
srq() { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1/signature-requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" | jq '.data[0]'; }  # newest request, with tokens
tok() { srq "$1" | jq -r --arg e "$2" '.signers[] | select(.email==$e) | .token'; }                            # one signer's token
sign()    { curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/sign/$1/sign" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
            -d "{\"signedName\":\"$2\",\"consent\":true}"; }
decline() { curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/sign/$1/decline" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
            -d "{\"reason\":\"$2\"}"; }
```

Then create the helper workflow, **once** (in a later shell, get it back with `W_QUICK=$(wfid "QA quick approval")`):

```bash
W_QUICK=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/approvals/workflows" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"name\":\"QA quick approval\",\"description\":\"One step: admin-a. Used by the section 5 helpers.\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":0,\"name\":\"Admin check\",\"approverId\":\"$ADMIN_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":48}]}" \
  | jq -r .id); echo "W_QUICK=$W_QUICK"
```

The workflows this section uses. Which workflow a contract goes to depends on every active workflow in the org, so
the journeys pick contract types that keep them apart: **SOW** and **OTHER** go to *Standard approval*, **NDA** to *QA
NDAs*, and **MSA** worth USD 100,000 or more (or with no value) to *QA large MSAs*.

| Variable | Name | Made in | Rules ("Used for") | Steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | Standard approval (**Default**, seeded) | `pnpm dev:setup` | Every type; approves NDA up to USD 10,000 at once | Legal review: role LEGAL_COUNSEL (counsel-a), due 48 h |
| `$W_QUICK` | QA quick approval | the setup above | Every type (never picked automatically: the default, which names no type or value either, ranks first) | Admin check: admin-a |
| `$W_SEQ` | QA three steps | E2E-WFB-02 | Every type | Legal review: counsel-a, 24 h, escalate to legalops-a → Finance approval: role FINANCE → Final sign-off: approver-a |
| `$W_PAR` | QA parallel | E2E-WFB-02 | Every type | Finance and approver: parallel, finance-a + approver-a, 1 required |
| `$W_NDA` | QA NDAs | E2E-WFB-03 | NDA; approves NDA up to USD 10,000 at once | NDA review: approver-a |
| `$W_BIG` | QA large MSAs | E2E-WFB-03 | MSA from USD 100,000 | Deal desk: finance-a |

### E2E-WFB-01 · The seeded default workflow is in place, and an org without workflows is told where to make one

**Covers:** /approvals · `GET /approvals/workflows` · — · — · TC-SMK-08
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~5 min

**Preconditions**
- A fresh `pnpm dev:setup` (§0). If `pnpm demo:seed` was also run, more workflows are listed; that is expected.
- The section setup is done, so "QA quick approval" also exists.
- Org B has no workflows: `curl -s $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq length` prints `0`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a, left rail → **Queues** → **Approvals**. | Title **Approvals**. Subtitle "Decisions routed to you, and the org-wide view of everything in flight." (it reads "N contracts waiting on your decision." once admin-a has items). Tabs **My Queue**, **All approvals**, **Manage Workflows**. No yellow "No approval workflows defined yet." banner. |
| 2 | Click **Manage Workflows**. | Text "Workflow definitions control how contracts are routed for approval. Set a default workflow so contracts are auto-routed on submission." Heading **Workflow Definitions** and a **New Workflow** button. Table columns **Name**, **Used for**, **Steps**, **Status** (shown in capitals). Default first. |
| 3 | Read the **Standard approval** row. | A **Default** chip with a star. Description "Legal reviews each contract sent for approval. NDAs up to USD 10,000 are approved at once." Used for: "Every type · approves NDA up to USD 10,000 at once". Steps: "1 step". Status: **Active**. At the right: a pencil icon and a trash icon, but no star (it is already the default). The "QA quick approval" row reads "Every type", "1 step", **Active**, with a star icon (tooltip "Set as default"). |
| 4 | Click the pencil on **Standard approval**. | A side panel **Edit Workflow**. **Workflow name *** "Standard approval"; **Description** as above; **Set as default workflow** ticked, with "Used when no other workflow's rules fit a contract." **When to use this workflow**: no **Contract types** chip pressed ("None selected: every type."), **Only for contracts worth at least** empty (placeholder "Any value"), currency **USD**. **Approve automatically**: one row "NDA", "up to", "10000", "USD", with a remove ×. **Approval steps ***: step 1 "Legal review", its header showing "LEGAL_COUNSEL". Expanded: **Step name** "Legal review", **Specific approver** "— None —", **Or by role** "LEGAL_COUNSEL", **Due in (hours)** 48, **Escalate to (on timeout)** "— No escalation —", **Execution mode** "Sequential". Footer: **Save Changes**, **Cancel**. |
| 5 | Click **Cancel**. | The panel closes. Nothing changed. |
| 6 | `curl -s $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.[] \| {name, isDefault, isActive, triggerRules, steps}'` | 200, a plain array, default first. Standard approval: `isDefault: true`, `isActive: true`, `triggerRules` `{"currency":"USD","autoApproveRules":[{"contractType":"NDA","maxValue":10000}]}`, `steps` `[{"order":0,"name":"Legal review","roleRequired":"LEGAL_COUNSEL","executionMode":"sequential","requiredApprovals":1,"dueSoonHours":48}]`. |
| 7 | As counsel-a (who may view workflows but not configure them), **Approvals** → **Manage Workflows**. | The same list. The tabs are **My Queue** and **Manage Workflows** only; **All approvals** is not shown. |
| 8 | As admin-b (Org B), open **Approvals**. | A yellow banner on every tab: "No approval workflows defined yet." and "Until someone creates a workflow, the "Submit for Approval" button on contracts won't know where to route decisions and will fail quietly. Create one to unblock your team.", with a **Create workflow →** link. |
| 9 | Click **Create workflow →**. | The **Manage Workflows** tab opens: a dashed box "No workflows yet. Create one to route approvals." and a **Create Workflow** button. Org A's workflows are not listed anywhere in Org B. |

**Also check**
- `GET /approvals/workflows` needs `view:workflow`: admin, counsel, legalops, contracts, finance and approver get 200.
  rep-a, procurement-a and viewer-a get 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: view:workflow"`. In the UI those three see
  **Manage Workflows** with "No workflows yet. Create one to route approvals." because their list request was
  refused. That text is wrong for them (reported).
- The **Dashboard**'s welcome checklist item "Configure an approval workflow" is ticked in Org A and not in Org B (§1).

**Known limits**
- The seeded workflow is named **Standard approval**; "Legal review" is the name of its only step.
- The banner in step 8 names a "Submit for Approval" button and says a submission "will fail quietly". The button is
  called **Send for Review**, and without a workflow its dialog says "No workflows configured" (E2E-APPR-01).

### E2E-WFB-02 · An admin builds a three-step sequential workflow and a parallel one, and they save exactly as built

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/workflows` · — · — · TC-WF-06
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- The five invited Org A users exist (§0.4).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: **Approvals** → **Manage Workflows** → **New Workflow**. | A side panel **New Workflow** with empty fields. **Approval steps *** shows "No approval steps yet" and **Add First Step**. **Create Workflow** is disabled (no name, no step). |
| 2 | **Workflow name *** "QA three steps"; **Description** "Legal, then finance, then final sign-off". Click **Add First Step**. | Step 1 appears, expanded, with the header "1" and "Untitled step". **Create Workflow** is now enabled. |
| 3 | Click **Create Workflow** now, with no approver on the step. | The panel stays open. A red line above the buttons: `Step 1 ("Untitled") has no approver — pick a user or role.` Nothing is saved. |
| 4 | Step 1: **Step name** "Legal review"; **Specific approver** "Legal Counsel"; **Due in (hours)** 24; **Escalate to (on timeout)** legalops-a's name; **Execution mode** "Sequential". | **Or by role** becomes disabled once a specific approver is chosen. The step header shows "Legal review" and "Legal Counsel". |
| 5 | Click **Add Step**. Step 2: **Step name** "Finance approval"; **Specific approver** "— None —"; **Or by role** "FINANCE". Leave **Due in (hours)** at 48. | Step 2's header shows "Finance approval" and "FINANCE". Only one step is expanded at a time; clicking a header opens or closes it. The role list offers ADMIN, LEGAL_COUNSEL, LEGAL_OPS, CONTRACT_MANAGER, FINANCE and APPROVER. |
| 6 | **Add Step**. Step 3: "Final sign-off", **Specific approver** approver-a's name. | Header "3", "Final sign-off", approver-a's name. |
| 7 | Reorder: click step 3's up arrow, then the same step's down arrow. | It moves to position 2 (renumbered "2"), then back to 3. Step 1's up arrow and the last step's down arrow are greyed out. |
| 8 | **Add Step** to make a step 4, then click step 4's red trash icon. | Step 4 disappears at once (there is no confirmation). |
| 9 | Click **Create Workflow**. | The panel closes. A new row "QA three steps": Used for "Every type", "3 steps", **Active**, no Default chip. |
| 10 | `W_SEQ=$(wfid "QA three steps"); curl -s $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq --arg id $W_SEQ '.[] \| select(.id==$id) \| {isDefault, triggerRules, steps}'` | `isDefault: false`, `triggerRules: {}`. Steps in order 0, 1, 2: `{"order":0,"name":"Legal review","approverId":"<COUNSEL_A_ID>","executionMode":"sequential","requiredApprovals":1,"dueSoonHours":24,"escalateTo":"<LEGALOPS_A_ID>"}`, `{"order":1,"name":"Finance approval","roleRequired":"FINANCE",…,"dueSoonHours":48}`, `{"order":2,"name":"Final sign-off","approverId":"<APPROVER_A_ID>",…}`. |
| 11 | **New Workflow** → name "QA parallel" → **Add First Step** → **Step name** "Finance and approver" → **Execution mode** "Parallel". | The approver fields change to a list headed "Approvers (all run concurrently — every user who holds a selected role is included)", with a checkbox per org user, and role chips below it. Next to the mode: "Required approvals:" 1 "of 0". |
| 12 | Tick finance-a and approver-a. | "of 2". The step header reads "2 approvers · 1 required". |
| 13 | Type 5 in **Required approvals**. | It becomes 2: with only named approvers, the field is capped at their number. Set it back to 1. |
| 14 | Click the **LEGAL_OPS** role chip, then click it again. | Pressed: it turns dark, the counter reads "of 2 + role members" and the header "2 approvers + LEGAL_OPS · 1 required". Pressed again: back to "of 2". Leave it unpressed. |
| 15 | **Create Workflow**, then `W_PAR=$(wfid "QA parallel")` and read it as in step 10. | Row "QA parallel", "1 step", **Active**. API: `{"order":0,"name":"Finance and approver","executionMode":"parallel","requiredApprovals":1,"approverIds":["<FINANCE_A_ID>","<APPROVER_A_ID>"],"roleRequireds":[],…}`. |
| 16 | Mode switch keeps the pick: **New Workflow**, add a step, pick a **Specific approver**, then switch **Execution mode** to "Parallel". Then close the panel with **Cancel**. | In parallel mode that user is already ticked. **Cancel** (or the ✕, or a click outside the panel) closes it and saves nothing. |
| 17 | As legalops-a (LEGAL_OPS may configure workflows): **New Workflow**, name "QA legal ops check", one step with **Specific approver** admin-a → **Create Workflow**. Then delete it with its trash icon and confirm. | Created and deleted like admin-a's. |

**Also check**
- API validation (as admin-a, `POST $API/approvals/workflows`):
  - no `name` → 400 `{"error":"name is required"}`;
  - `"steps":[]` → 400 `{"error":"steps must be a non-empty array"}`;
  - a step with no `approverId`, `roleRequired`, `approverIds` or `roleRequireds` → 400 `{"error":"Step 1 (\"<name>\") has no approver — pick a user or role."}`;
  - a parallel step with `"requiredApprovals":3` and two `approverIds` → 400 `{"error":"Step 1 requires 3 approvals but only 2 approver(s) are named."}`;
  - `"requiredApprovals":0` on a parallel step → 400 `{"error":"Step 1 requiredApprovals must be at least 1."}`.
- The API accepts any role name, even one no user holds (`"roleRequired":"NO_SUCH_ROLE"`). E2E-APPR-10 uses that to
  strand an approval.
- **Due in (hours)** can't go below 1 in the builder. Typing 0 (or 0.5) sets it to 48, not 1. Through the API any
  positive number works; E2E-APPR-11 uses 0.01 hours.
- The builder offers every org user as an approver or escalation target, and CONTRACT_MANAGER as a role. A contract
  manager, procurement user, viewer or deactivated user can't decide approvals, so a step routed to them can never be
  decided. The builder doesn't warn (reported).

**Known limits**
- Steps are ordered with the arrows only; there is no drag and drop. A step's number is its position, counted from 0
  in the saved JSON.
- A sequential step "by role" goes to **one** user who holds that role, not to all of them. Use a parallel step to ask
  everyone who holds a role.

### E2E-WFB-03 · Trigger rules send contracts to a workflow by type and value, and auto-approve rules are saved as set

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/workflows` · — · — · —
**Roles:** admin-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-WFB-02 done.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | **Manage Workflows** → **New Workflow** → name "QA NDAs". Under **When to use this workflow**, read the help text. | "A contract sent without choosing a workflow goes to the one whose rules fit it most closely. When none fits, it goes to the default." **Contract types** shows one chip per type: NDA, MSA, SOW, SLA, VENDOR AGREEMENT, EMPLOYMENT, PARTNERSHIP, LICENSE, DATA PROCESSING, ORDER FORM, OTHER. |
| 2 | Click the **NDA** chip. | It turns dark (pressed). |
| 3 | **Only for contracts worth at least**: type "lots". | A red line: "The minimum value must be a number, 0 or more." **Create Workflow** is disabled. Clear the field; the line goes. |
| 4 | Under **Approve automatically**, click **Add a rule**. | A row appears: a type list preset to "NDA" (the first pressed type; "Any type" when none is pressed), "up to", an empty **Limit** box, and "USD". A red line: "Give each automatic approval a limit: a number, 0 or more." |
| 5 | Type 10000 in the limit. Read the hint under the rules. | The red line goes. Hint: "A contract at or under the limit is approved when it is sent, with no review. One with no value set, or in another currency, always goes to a person." |
| 6 | **Add First Step**: "NDA review", **Specific approver** approver-a → **Create Workflow**. | Row "QA NDAs", Used for "NDA · approves NDA up to USD 10,000 at once", "1 step", **Active**. |
| 7 | **New Workflow** → "QA large MSAs": press **MSA**; **Only for contracts worth at least** "100,000" (commas are fine); currency **USD**; step "Deal desk", **Specific approver** finance-a → **Create Workflow**. | Row "QA large MSAs", Used for "MSA · from USD 100,000". |
| 8 | `W_NDA=$(wfid "QA NDAs"); W_BIG=$(wfid "QA large MSAs")`, then `curl -s $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.[] \| select(.name \| test("QA NDAs\|QA large")) \| {name, triggerRules}'` | QA NDAs: `{"contractTypes":["NDA"],"currency":"USD","autoApproveRules":[{"contractType":"NDA","maxValue":10000}]}`. QA large MSAs: `{"contractTypes":["MSA"],"valueThreshold":100000,"currency":"USD"}`. An empty field saves no rule. |
| 9 | Open "QA NDAs" with its pencil. Change the currency list to **EUR** (it offers USD, EUR, GBP, INR, JPY, CAD, AUD, SGD, CHF). | The auto-approve row now ends "EUR". Click **Cancel**: nothing is saved (the list still reads USD 10,000). |

**Also check**
- The API checks the rules. Each of these answers 400 with an `error` that starts with the path of the problem
  (`POST $API/approvals/workflows` as admin-a, with a valid step):
  - `"triggerRules":{"contractTypes":["NOT_A_TYPE"]}` → `triggerRules.contractTypes.0: …` (an invalid-value message);
  - `"triggerRules":{"currency":"dollars"}` → `triggerRules.currency: a three-letter currency code, such as USD`;
  - `"triggerRules":{"autoApproveRules":[{"contractType":"NDA"}]}` → `triggerRules.autoApproveRules.0.maxValue: …`;
  - `"triggerRules":{"autoApproveRules":[{"contractType":"NDA","maxValue":-5}]}` → `triggerRules.autoApproveRules.0.maxValue: …`;
  - `"triggerRules":{"contractType":"NDA"}` (a misspelt key) → `triggerRules: …` (unrecognised key);
  - `"triggerRules":{"valueThreshold":"lots"}` → `triggerRules.valueThreshold: …`.
  After all six, no new workflow exists.
- At most 20 auto-approve rules per workflow (a 21st is refused with a `triggerRules.autoApproveRules` error).

**Known limits**
- Rules compare values only in the rules' currency. A contract in another currency counts as meeting a value floor
  and is never approved automatically. There is no currency conversion.
- The routing itself is tested in E2E-APPR-02 and the auto-approval in E2E-APPR-03.

### E2E-WFB-04 · Edit, make default, switch off and delete a workflow; only workflow admins can

**Covers:** /approvals · `PATCH /approvals/workflows/:workflowId`, `DELETE /approvals/workflows/:workflowId`, `POST /approvals/workflows` · — · — · —
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, rep-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-WFB-03 done. A DRAFT SOW contract for the dialog check: `C_WF4=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA WFB-04 default check" SOW 5000)`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: **New Workflow** "QA scratch", one step "Scratch step" with **Specific approver** admin-a → **Create Workflow**. | Row "QA scratch", **Active**, with a star icon. |
| 2 | Click its pencil. The panel is titled **Edit Workflow** and the button **Save Changes**. Change **Description** to "edited" and the step's **Due in (hours)** to 72 → **Save Changes**. | The panel closes. The row shows "edited" under the name. `curl -s $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.[] \| select(.name=="QA scratch") \| .steps[0].dueSoonHours'` → `72`. |
| 3 | Click the star (tooltip "Set as default") on "QA scratch". | "QA scratch" moves to the top with the **Default** chip. **Standard approval** loses its chip and now shows a star. Only one workflow is ever the default. |
| 4 | As contracts-a, open `$WEB/contracts/$C_WF4` → **Send for Review**. | The **Workflow** list preselects "QA scratch (default) — fits this contract". Close the dialog with **Cancel**. |
| 5 | As admin-a, open **Standard approval** with its pencil, tick **Set as default workflow** → **Save Changes**. | Standard approval is the default again; "QA scratch" has its star back. |
| 6 | Switch "QA scratch" off (there is no UI control for this): `S=$(wfid "QA scratch"); curl -s -X PATCH $API/approvals/workflows/$S -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"isActive":false}' \| jq .isActive` | `false`. Reload **Manage Workflows**: the row's status reads **Inactive**. As contracts-a, **Send for Review** on `$C_WF4` no longer lists "QA scratch". |
| 7 | Submit with the inactive workflow: `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$C_WF4" "$S"` | 422 `{"error":"That workflow is inactive or no longer exists. Choose another."}`. `st $C_WF4` → `DRAFT`. |
| 8 | Switch it back on with the same call and `{"isActive":true}`. | The row reads **Active** again. |
| 9 | Click the trash icon on "QA scratch". Click **Cancel** in the browser's confirm box "Delete "QA scratch"?". Then click the trash icon again and **OK**. | Cancel keeps the row. OK removes it (the request answered 204). |
| 10 | `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE $API/approvals/workflows/$S -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"`; then the same with `-X PATCH … -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x"}'`; then `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$C_WF4" "$S"`. | Delete and PATCH: 404 `{"error":"Workflow not found"}`. Submit: 422 `{"error":"That workflow is inactive or no longer exists. Choose another."}`. A deleted workflow is gone for good. |
| 11 | As legalops-a: **New Workflow** "QA legal ops 2" (one step, admin-a) → **Create Workflow**; its pencil → rename to "QA legal ops 2b" → **Save Changes**; its trash icon → **OK**. | Each change is saved; LEGAL_OPS holds `configure:workflow`. |
| 12 | As counsel-a (no `configure:workflow`): **Manage Workflows** → **New Workflow**, name "QA counsel try", one step with admin-a → **Create Workflow**. | Nothing visible happens: the panel stays open with no message, and no row appears. The web app refused the request itself ("You don't have permission to configure workflows.") but the panel doesn't show that reason (reported). Close the panel. |
| 13 | As counsel-a, the API: `curl -s -X POST $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x","steps":[{"order":0,"name":"s","approverId":"'$ADMIN_A_ID'","executionMode":"sequential","requiredApprovals":1,"dueSoonHours":48}]}'` | 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: configure:workflow"`. The same for PATCH and DELETE of any workflow, and for contracts-a, finance-a and approver-a. |
| 14 | As admin-b: `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X PATCH $API/approvals/workflows/$W_NDA -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"hijack"}'` | 404 `{"error":"Workflow not found"}`. Org A's workflow is unchanged. |

**Also check**
- rep-a and viewer-a: every workflow route answers 403 (`view:workflow` to list, `configure:workflow` to change).
- Editing a workflow that has approvals in flight changes their **remaining** steps: the engine reads the saved
  steps each time it moves an approval on. Verify: submit a contract with `$W_SEQ`, rename its step "Finance approval"
  while step 1 is pending, approve step 1, and the new name appears on finance-a's card.
- Deleting the default leaves the org without one. Contracts then go to the best-fitting remaining workflow; among
  workflows without rules, the oldest (here "QA quick approval"). An org with no active workflow at all gets 422
  (E2E-APPR-01, Org B). Don't delete Standard approval in Org A: later journeys rely on it.

**Known limits**
- There is no on/off switch in the UI: **Inactive** can only be set through the API.
- The pencil and trash icons have no tooltip or label; only the star does.
- Users who may view workflows but not change them (counsel-a, contracts-a, finance-a, approver-a) still see **New
  Workflow**, the pencil, the star and the trash icon. Their saves fail without a message (reported).

|---|----|--------|

With "QA three steps": First reviewer "Legal review" and "Then 2 more steps in sequence." |
| 4 | Type "Please review by Friday" in **Message** → **Send**. | The button shows "Sending…", then the dialog closes. The pill reads **Approval**. **Send for Review** is gone and **Send for Signature** is now dark. `st $C1` → `PENDING_APPROVAL`. |

| 6 | Mailpit. | One email to legal@demo.com from qa@draftlegal.local. Subject "Contract awaiting your approval". Body: `"QA APPR-01 services" has been submitted for approval (Legal review).` Plain text, no link. |
| 7 | As counsel-a, reload the app. | The left rail's **Approvals** item has a count badge (one more than before). The header bell shows an unread count; its panel lists "Contract awaiting your approval" with the same sentence and "just now". |
| 8 | **Approvals** → **My Queue**. | Subtitle "N contracts waiting on your decision." (singular for one). The **My Queue** tab has a count. Then "AI summary is being generated…" with a spinner (E2E-APPR-04 covers the summary). Buttons **Approve**, **Reject**, **Delegate**. |
| 9 | Click the card's title. | The contract opens. Above the document is the decision strip "AWAITING YOUR DECISION" (E2E-APPR-05). The rail's **Approval** section is open: "Waiting on you: Legal review" and **Review & Decide**, which scrolls to the strip. The rail also has a **Precedents** section (approver mode, §2). |
| 10 | As contracts-a, reload `$C1`. | No decision strip. A thin status line under the header: "→ You → Approver", "Last: …", "Next: Waiting on review" and **Nudge** (it only scrolls to the Comments rail). The rail's **Approval** section says "Not yet submitted for approval." That is wrong: the approval data that section needs never loads (reported). |
| 11 | Look for the message typed in step 4. | It appears nowhere: not on the card, the email, the notification, or `GET /approvals/:instanceId`. The API drops it (reported). |
| 12 | `audit APPROVAL_SUBMITTED $C1` | One event: resourceType "contract", actor "Casey Contracts", metadata `{"instanceId":"<INST>","workflowId":"<Standard approval's id>","approverCount":1}`. The contract's Activity tab lists "APPROVAL SUBMITTED". |
| 13 | Submit again: `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$C1"` | 409 `{"error":"Contract already has an active approval workflow","instanceId":"<INST>"}`. |

Leave `$C1` pending: E2E-APPR-10 and NOTIF-04 use it.

**Also check**
- **Send for Review** needs `edit:contract` (admin, counsel, legalops, contracts, procurement) and a contract in Draft, In
  Review or In Negotiation. rep-a, finance-a, approver-a and viewer-a see no button;
  `submit "$VIEWER_A" "$C1"` → 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- procurement-a can submit (`edit:contract`) but can't list workflows (`view:workflow`). On a Draft contract its
  dialog says "No workflows configured" and **Send** stays disabled, although the API accepts its submission
  (`submit "$PROCUREMENT_A" <id>` → 201). Reported.
- Status: submitting an Approved, Signing or Executed contract → 409
  `{"error":"Cannot submit a contract with status APPROVED for approval"}` (the status name varies). The header shows no
  **Send for Review** for those statuses.
- Org B has no workflows. As admin-b:
  `CB=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA no workflow","type":"NDA"}' | jq -r .id)`.
  Open it → **Send for Review** → "No workflows configured" and "An admin needs to create one first, under Approvals →
  Manage Workflows."; **Send** disabled. `submit "$ADMIN_B" "$CB"` → 422
  `{"error":"No active approval workflow found for this org. Create one in Approvals → Manage Workflows."}`.
- A workflow id that is unknown or from the other org → 422
  `{"error":"That workflow is inactive or no longer exists. Choose another."}`.
- A first step nobody can take: create a workflow through the API whose only step has `"roleRequired":"NO_SUCH_ROLE"`
  and submit with it → 422 `{"error":"Cannot resolve approver for step \"<step name>\". Check the workflow configuration."}`;
  the contract stays Draft. Delete that workflow afterwards.
- Cross-org and roles: admin-b submitting `$C1` → 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}`; `GET /approvals/$INST` as
  admin-b → 404 `{"error":"Approval instance not found"}`, as viewer-a → 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: view:workflow"`.
- The dialog closes without sending on **Cancel**, the × or a click outside. A server refusal shows in a red box inside
  the dialog: open the dialog in two tabs and send from both; the second says "Contract already has an active approval
  workflow".
- On an analysed Draft contract, the **Approval** tab (in the tab bar, §2) shows "Not yet in review", "Send this
  contract to the approval workflow to start the review." and an outlined **Send for Review**. That button submits at
  once with the automatically chosen workflow, without the dialog; a refusal shows in red under it.

**Known limits**
- The approval request email has no link to the app.
- An approver is told once, when the step is assigned. There are no reminders before the escalation deadline.
- A submitter can't withdraw a pending approval.

### E2E-APPR-02 · Each contract goes to the workflow whose rules fit it best, and a workflow the sender picks always wins

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval` · — · — · —
**Roles:** contracts-a, admin-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-WFB-03 done: active workflows are Standard approval (default), QA quick approval, QA three steps, QA parallel,
  QA NDAs and QA large MSAs.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |

R6 preselects "Standard approval (default) — fits this contract", First reviewer "Legal review". The dialog uses the same rule as the server. |
| 3 | Submit all nine without choosing a workflow: `for c in $R1 $R2 $R3 $R4 $R5 $R6 $R7 $R8 $R9; do submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $c > /dev/null; inst $INST \| jq -c '{workflow, status, approver: .steps[0].approverName}'; done` | One line per contract, as in the table below. |

| R7 MSA, no value | QA large MSAs | PENDING, finance-a: a contract of unknown size gets the more careful review |
| R8 MSA, EUR 40,000 | QA large MSAs | PENDING, finance-a: a value in another currency counts as meeting the floor |
| R9 SOW, USD 1,000 | Standard approval | PENDING, Legal Counsel |

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 4 | The sender's choice wins: `R10=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA route R10 MSA 40k chosen" MSA 40000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $R10 $W_BIG; inst $INST \| jq -c '{workflow, approver: .steps[0].approverName}'` | "QA large MSAs", finance-a, although R10 is below that workflow's floor. |
| 5 | The same in the dialog: `R11=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA route R11 dialog" MSA 40000)`; open it → **Send for Review** → pick "QA large MSAs" → **Send**. | finance-a's My Queue lists R11 ("DEAL DESK"). |
| 6 | Only the chosen workflow's rules can approve at once: `R12=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA route R12 NDA 5k chosen" NDA 5000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $R12 $W_QUICK` | `"status":"PENDING"`, approver admin-a: QA quick approval has no auto-approve rule, so a person decides. |
| 7 | Each approver's **My Queue**. | approver-a: R2, R3, R4. finance-a: R5, R7, R8, R10, R11. counsel-a: R6, R9 (and `$C1`). admin-a: R12. |

**Also check**
- Ties: among the workflows that fit, one that names the contract's type beats one for every type; then the higher
  value floor wins; then the default; then the oldest. Verify with a second NDA workflow "QA NDAs 20k" (types NDA,
  from USD 20,000, one step admin-a): an NDA worth USD 50,000 now goes to it, one worth USD 15,000 still to QA NDAs.
  Delete it afterwards.
- Inactive and deleted workflows are never picked (E2E-WFB-04).

**Known limits**
- There is no currency conversion.
- The workflow is picked once, at submission. Changing a workflow's rules later doesn't re-route approvals in flight.

### E2E-APPR-03 · A contract under the auto-approve limit is approved the moment it is sent; one without a value never is

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval` · — · notification.worker · —
**Roles:** contracts-a, approver-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~8 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-WFB-03 done (without it, the seeded Standard approval also approves NDAs up to USD 10,000).
- `A1=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA auto NDA 8k" NDA 8000)`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As contracts-a, open A1 → **Send for Review**. | Workflow "QA NDAs — fits this contract". In place of the First reviewer box, a grey box: "This workflow's rules approve this contract as soon as you send it, with no review." |
| 2 | **Send**. | A toast "Approved automatically" with "The workflow's rules approve this contract without a review." The dialog closes. The pill reads **Approved**; the header offers **Mark as Executed** and **Send for Signature**. |
| 3 | `audit APPROVAL_SUBMITTED $A1`, then `inst <metadata.instanceId>` | Metadata `{"instanceId":"…","autoApproved":true}`. The approval: status "AUTO_APPROVED", no steps, aiSummary "Auto-approved based on org rules.", approvalRecommendation "approve". |
| 4 | approver-a's My Queue; Mailpit. | Nothing for A1: no queue item, no email to any approver. |
| 5 | contracts-a's bell. | "Contract auto-approved": `"QA auto NDA 8k" was auto-approved based on your org's rules.` No email to contracts@demo.com. |
| 6 | The limit is inclusive: `A2=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA auto NDA 10k" NDA 10000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $A2`; `A3=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA auto NDA 10001" NDA 10001); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $A3` | A2: 201 `{"instanceId":"…","status":"AUTO_APPROVED","autoApproved":true}`. A3: 201 with `"status":"PENDING","autoApproved":false`, approver approver-a. |
| 7 | It fails closed: open a Draft NDA with no value, and one worth EUR 5,000, in the dialog. | Both show the **FIRST REVIEWER** box ("NDA review"), not the auto-approval box (E2E-APPR-02 R3 and R4). |

**Also check**
- The contract's **Approval** tab would show an "Auto-approved" card ("Approved automatically based on org rules on
  <date>"), but that history doesn't load (reported).
- An auto-approval sends no `approval.submitted` webhook, so no Slack or Teams card (E2E-NOTIF-05/06).

**Known limits**
- The submitter is told only in the bell, not by email.

### E2E-APPR-04 · The approver sees the AI summary, risk flags and recommendation, and approves with a comment

**Covers:** /approvals · `GET /approvals/my-queue`, `PATCH /approvals/:instanceId/summary`, `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide` · — · approval (agents service), notification.worker · TC-SEC-04, TC-PII-08
**Roles:** contracts-a, counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key (steps 1–9); steps 10–12 need none · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- The agents service runs with a model key (§0.2).
- Upload D-MSA.pdf as contracts-a and give it a value under QA large MSAs' floor:
  `C4=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -F "file=@$HOME/qa-docs/D-MSA.pdf;type=application/pdf" -F "title=QA APPR-04 Northwind MSA" -F "type=MSA" | jq -r .id)`;
  `curl -s -o /dev/null -X PATCH $API/contracts/$C4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"value":50000,"currency":"USD"}'`.
  Let the analysis finish (§2: the rail's Clauses section fills in). It gives the strip a risk score.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As contracts-a, open C4 → **Send for Review** → Standard approval → **Send**. | Pill **Approval**. |
| 2 | Wait up to a minute. | API log: "[agent-worker] approval-summary queued in agents service instanceId=…". Agents service log: "[approval-summary] DONE instanceId=… recommendation=…". |
| 3 | As counsel-a, reload **Approvals** → **My Queue**. | C4's card has an **AI SUMMARY** block with a small diamond mark and a chip: "AI recommends: Approve", "AI recommends: Review Required" or "AI recommends: Reject". The text summarises this contract in plain words: Northwind Analytics, USD 12,000 a month, the term and automatic renewal, the liability cap. Below it: "N risks identified" (or "1 risk identified") with a warning icon. |
| 4 | Click "N risks identified". | One box per risk: its title in bold and a description. Colour by severity: low grey, medium amber, high red, critical dark red. Then "Non-standard terms:" and a bullet list, when there are any. Click again to collapse. |
| 5 | `qstep "$COUNSEL_A" "$C4"; curl -s $API/approvals/$INST -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{aiSummary, keyRisks, nonStandardTerms, approvalRecommendation}'` | The same text. `keyRisks`: at most 5, each `{title, description, severity}` with severity low, medium, high or critical. `nonStandardTerms`: at most 5. `approvalRecommendation`: approve, review_required or reject_advised. Any personal data the summary quotes (the SSN, card or IBAN in D-MSA) reads with its real value, not a placeholder (TC-PII-08). |
| 6 | As counsel-a, open C4. | The strip shows "Confidence NN%" (90 for approve, 75 for reject advised, 60 for review required, minus 5 per risk), "Risk NN%" from the contract's risk score (or "Risk —"), "AI: Approve", "AI: Review required" or "AI: Reject advised", and "Top blocker: <the first risk's title>" (greyed: the summary's risks aren't tied to a clause, so it doesn't jump). |
| 7 | Back on **My Queue**, on C4's card click **Approve**; click it again; click it once more. | First click: the button turns solid, and a box "Optional comment…" and **Confirm Approval** appear. Second click: it toggles off. Third: on again. |
| 8 | Type "Fine at USD 50k" → **Confirm Approval**. | A spinner, then green "Decision recorded successfully." After a reload the card is gone. `st $C4` → APPROVED; the pill reads **Approved**. contracts-a's bell: "Contract approved", `"QA APPR-04 Northwind MSA" has been fully approved.` No email to contracts@demo.com. |
| 9 | `inst $INST` and `audit APPROVAL_DECIDED` | Status APPROVED; step "Legal review" APPROVED, decision APPROVED, comment "Fine at USD 50k". Audit: an approval_step event by "Legal Counsel", `{"decision":"APPROVED","instanceId":"…"}`, and an approval_instance event with no actor, `{"decision":"APPROVED","contractId":"<C4>"}`. |
| 10 | No summary: stop the agents service. `C4b=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-04 no summary" OTHER 3000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C4b`. As counsel-a, open **My Queue** now, and again after 5 minutes. | For 5 minutes after submission: "AI summary is being generated…" with a spinner. After that: "No AI summary for this submission — review the contract directly." and **Open contract →**. The API log shows the job retried once, then "[worker:agents] ✗ job failed name=approval-summary …". |
| 11 | Write a summary as the agents service would: `qstep "$COUNSEL_A" "$C4b"; curl -s -X PATCH $API/approvals/$INST/summary -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'x-internal-service: agents' -H "x-org-id: $ORG_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"aiSummary":"QA summary: 12-month services, 1,000 a month, liability capped at 12 months of fees.","keyRisks":[{"title":"Auto-renewal","description":"Renews for 12 months unless 60 days notice is given.","severity":"medium"},{"title":"Low liability cap","description":"Capped at 12 months of fees.","severity":"high"}],"nonStandardTerms":["60-day notice period"],"approvalRecommendation":"review_required"}'` | 200 `{"id":"<INST>","status":"summary_updated"}`. Reload **My Queue**: the card shows that text, "AI recommends: Review Required" and "2 risks identified" (amber, then red when expanded). The contract's strip: "Confidence 50%", "AI: Review required", "Top blocker: Auto-renewal". |
| 12 | Refusals: repeat step 11's call (a) without the three internal headers, (b) with `x-internal-secret: wrong`, (c) with `-H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` in place of the internal headers, (d) with `x-org-id: $ORG_B`. | (a)–(c): 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}`. (d): 404 `{"error":"Approval not found"}`. The stored summary is unchanged after all four (TC-SEC-04). |

**Also check**
- viewer-a opening **Approvals**: **My Queue** shows "All clear" / "No contracts are awaiting your approval." because
  the queue request was refused (viewer-a has no `view:workflow`), not because the queue is empty.
- Restart the agents service before moving on.

**Known limits**
- The summary is written once per submission, for the first step's approvers. Later steps show the same summary; it
  isn't redone when the document changes.
- The queue doesn't refresh on its own: reload to see a summary arrive.
- "Confidence" is a display rule computed from the recommendation and the number of risks, not a score from the
  model. The recommendation is advice only.

### E2E-APPR-05 · A three-step approval moves step by step, each approver sees it only on their turn, and the decision strip decides it

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide`, `GET /approvals/:instanceId`, `GET /approvals/my-queue` · — · notification.worker · TC-WF-03, TC-WF-06
**Roles:** contracts-a, counsel-a, finance-a, approver-a, admin-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$W_SEQ` exists (E2E-WFB-02). `C5=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-05 three steps" OTHER 30000)`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As contracts-a: C5 → **Send for Review** → Workflow "QA three steps" → **Send**. Then `qstep "$COUNSEL_A" "$C5"`. | The dialog showed "Legal review" and "Then 2 more steps in sequence." The pill reads **Approval**. INST and STEP are set. |
| 2 | finance-a and approver-a: **Approvals** → **My Queue**; also `curl -s $API/approvals/my-queue -H "Authorization: Bearer $FINANCE_A" \| jq '[.data[].contract.title]'`. | C5 is in neither queue, and their **Approvals** badges didn't change: a later step isn't shown before its turn. |
| 3 | admin-a: **Approvals** → **All approvals**. | C5's row: Current step "Legal review", "step 1 of 3"; Awaiting "Legal Counsel". |
| 4 | As counsel-a: the C5 card reads "Escalates in 1d" (24 hours). Open C5. | The strip: "AWAITING YOUR DECISION", Confidence, Risk, the AI chip, and **Approve**, **Reject**, **Delegate ▾**. |
| 5 | On the strip, click **Approve**, then **Cancel**, then **Approve** again. | A row opens under the strip with a box "Optional note for the audit trail…", **Cancel** and **Confirm Approve**. **Cancel** closes it. |
| 6 | Type "Legal OK" → **Confirm Approve**. | The strip disappears. The pill stays **Approval** (two steps left). |
| 7 | Mailpit, and finance-a's bell and **My Queue**. | An email to finance@qa.test, "Contract awaiting your approval", `"QA APPR-05 three steps" requires your approval (Finance approval).` The same in the bell. The card's eyebrow reads "FINANCE APPROVAL", "Escalates in 2d". admin-a's **All approvals**: "Finance approval", "step 2 of 3", Awaiting finance-a. |
| 8 | finance-a, on the card: **Approve** → "Optional comment…": "Budget OK" → **Confirm Approval**. | "Decision recorded successfully." approver-a now has the card "FINAL SIGN-OFF", and an email at approver@qa.test. |
| 9 | approver-a opens C5 and approves on the strip with no note. | The pill reads **Approved**. C5 leaves **All approvals**. contracts-a's bell: "Contract approved". contracts-a got nothing for the two intermediate steps, and no email at all. |
| 10 | `inst $INST` | Status APPROVED. Three steps, orders 0, 1, 2, all APPROVED, with approver names and comments "Legal OK", "Budget OK" and null. |
| 11 | `audit APPROVAL_DECIDED` | Three approval_step events (actors Legal Counsel, finance-a, approver-a) and one approval_instance event `{"decision":"APPROVED","contractId":"<C5>"}`. |

**Also check**
- Before step 6, finance-a has no step on C5; posting counsel-a's step id as finance-a →
  403 `{"error":"Step not found or not assigned to you"}`. Missing `stepId` → 400 `{"error":"stepId and decision are required"}`;
  `"decision":"MAYBE"` → 400 `{"error":"decision must be APPROVED, REJECTED, or DELEGATED"}`.
- Deciding needs `approve:workflow` (admin, counsel, legalops, finance, approver). viewer-a and contracts-a →
  403 `"detail":"Missing permission: approve:workflow"`. admin-b on an Org A step → 403 `{"error":"Step not found or not assigned to you"}`.
- There is no self-approval block: admin-a submits a contract with QA quick approval and approves its own step.
- A late decision doesn't move a contract that has moved on (TC-WF-03): submit another contract with QA three steps;
  while step 1 is pending, counsel-a clicks **Send for Signature** (it shows at status Approval) and sends it to
  signer1@example.test, so the pill reads **Signing**. Then the three approvers approve: the approval ends APPROVED but
  the contract stays **Signing**.
- When a decision fails on the server (for example, the step was decided in another tab), the card shows "Request
  failed with status code 403" rather than the server's reason, and the strip shows nothing at all (reported).

**Known limits**
- There is no "Request changes" decision. Use **Reject** with a comment (E2E-APPR-06).
- The contract's **Approval** tab doesn't show the step history (reported). Approval comments are visible only
  through `GET /approvals/:instanceId`.
- Only the submitter hears the final outcome, in the bell.

### E2E-APPR-06 · A rejection needs a reason, returns the contract to Draft, and the contract can be sent again

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide`, `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval` · — · notification.worker · TC-SMK-04
**Roles:** contracts-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `C6=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-06 reject" OTHER 15000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C6` (Standard approval, counsel-a).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a, open C6 → on the strip, **Reject**. | A box "Reason for rejection (required) — helps the submitter fix and re-submit…" and **Confirm Reject**, disabled. |
| 2 | Type only spaces. | **Confirm Reject** stays disabled. |
| 3 | Type "Liability cap too low; raise it to 2x fees." → **Confirm Reject**. | The strip goes. The pill reads **Draft** and **Send for Review** is back. |
| 4 | `inst $INST` | Status REJECTED; the step REJECTED, decision REJECTED, comment "Liability cap too low; raise it to 2x fees." |
| 5 | contracts-a's bell; Mailpit. | "Contract approval rejected": `"QA APPR-06 reject" was rejected and returned to Draft.` The reason isn't included. No email to contracts@demo.com. |
| 6 | contracts-a sends C6 again (**Send for Review** → **Send**); `qstep "$COUNSEL_A" "$C6"`. | A new approval with a new instance id. counsel-a's queue has C6 again. |
| 7 | counsel-a, on the C6 card: **Reject** → the box "Reason for rejection (required)…"; **Confirm Rejection** is disabled until text is typed; type "Still too low" → **Confirm Rejection**. | "Decision recorded successfully." C6 is **Draft** again. |
| 8 | Send C6 a third time and reject through the API with no comment: `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C6; decide "$COUNSEL_A" $INST $STEP REJECTED`, then with the comment "   ". | Both 400 `{"error":"comment is required when rejecting"}`. The step stays pending. |
| 9 | `audit APPROVAL_DECIDED` | An approval_step event by Legal Counsel `{"decision":"REJECTED",…}` and an approval_instance event `{"decision":"REJECTED","contractId":"<C6>"}` for each rejection. |

**Also check**
- In a multi-step workflow, a rejection at any step ends the approval; later steps are never created.
- In a parallel step, one rejection rejects the whole approval (E2E-APPR-08).
- Click the header's status pill: a **Lifecycle** popover lists Draft, In Review, Approval, Approved, Signing, Executed,
  with the current state marked.

**Known limits**
- The submitter never sees the reason in the app: the notification leaves it out, and the contract's approval history
  doesn't load (reported).
- There is no "Request changes" decision.

### E2E-APPR-07 · An approver hands a step to a teammate, and an absent approver's steps go to their out-of-office delegate

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide` · — · notification.worker · —
**Roles:** admin-a, approver-a, counsel-a, legalops-a, contracts-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `C7=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-07 delegate" OTHER 12000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C7 $W_QUICK` (step "Admin check", admin-a).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | admin-a: **My Queue** → C7's card → **Delegate**. | A search box "Delegate to which teammate? Search by name or email…" and a box "Reason for delegation (optional)…". **Confirm Delegation** is disabled. |
| 2 | Type part of approver-a's name, pick them, reason "Away this week" → **Confirm Delegation**. | "Decision recorded successfully." C7 leaves admin-a's queue. |
| 3 | approver-a's bell, Mailpit and **My Queue**. | "Contract approval delegated to you": `"QA APPR-07 delegate" approval has been delegated to you (Admin check).` The same email at approver@qa.test. A card "ADMIN CHECK". |
| 4 | `qstep "$APPROVER_A" "$C7"; inst $INST` | Two steps at order 0: admin-a DELEGATED (comment "Away this week"), approver-a PENDING. Status PENDING. |
| 5 | approver-a opens C7 → strip **Delegate ▾** → search box → pick "Legal Counsel" → **Confirm Delegate**. | The strip has no reason box. counsel-a now has C7; approver-a doesn't. |
| 6 | counsel-a approves. | **Approved**. `inst` shows DELEGATED, DELEGATED, APPROVED. |
| 7 | Out of office: admin-a → Admin → **Team** → **Set OOO**. In "Set Out-of-Office": pick counsel-a, tick "Mark as out-of-office", **Return Date** tomorrow, **Delegate To** legalops-a → **Save**. | counsel-a's card on the Team page shows as out of office. |
| 8 | `C7b=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-07 OOO" OTHER 9000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C7b; inst $INST \| jq '.steps[0].approverName'` | legalops-a's name, not "Legal Counsel". legalops-a's queue, bell and email (legalops@qa.test) have it; counsel-a has nothing. |
| 9 | legalops-a approves C7b. Then admin-a: **Team** → **Set OOO** → counsel-a → untick ("Bring Legal back — clears the absence and the delegate") → **Save**. | New Legal review steps go to counsel-a again. |

**Also check**
- API: `"decision":"DELEGATED"` without `delegateTo` → 400 `{"error":"delegateTo is required when delegating"}`;
  `delegateTo` = `$ADMIN_B_ID` → 400 `{"error":"Delegatee user not found in this org"}`.
- Out of office applies when a step is assigned; steps already pending stay with the absent person. A delegate who is
  also away still gets the step (one hop). Out of office with no delegate: the approver keeps the step.
- Delegating to a deactivated member is accepted, and strands the step (reported).

**Known limits**
- A delegated step keeps the original deadline but never escalates (reported).
- The person delegated to needs `approve:workflow` to decide.

### E2E-APPR-09 · An approver decides several contracts at once, and a partial failure names what failed and why

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide`, `GET /approvals/my-queue` · — · — · —
**Roles:** approver-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- approver-a has at least three pending items (R2, R3, R4 from E2E-APPR-02). If not:
  `for n in 1 2 3; do submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA bulk $n" NDA 20000)" $W_NDA > /dev/null; done`.

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | approver-a: **Approvals** → **My Queue**. | Above the cards: "Oldest first · longest wait is 0 days" and **Bulk decision…**. The cards are oldest first. |
| 2 | **Bulk decision…** | Dialog **Bulk decision**: "Apply a single decision (with optional comment) to multiple pending approvals." Two choices: **Approve all selected** (chosen) and **Reject all selected**. A list with every queue item ticked, each with its title and "<TYPE> · <step name> · submitted by <name>". "3 of 3 selected" and **Deselect all**. "Comment (optional)" with the placeholder "Optional note recorded against each decision". Footer: **Cancel** and **Approve 3**. |
| 3 | Untick one item; then **Deselect all**; then **Select all**. | "2 of 3 selected" and **Approve 2**; then "0 of 3 selected" with the button disabled; then all ticked and **Approve 3**. |
| 4 | Click **Reject all selected**. | The label reads "Comment *", the placeholder "Reason for rejection — applied to every selected item", and **Reject 3** is disabled until a comment is typed. Click **Approve all selected** again. |

Back in the dialog, type "Batch OK" → **Approve 3**. | "Processing 1 of 3…", then red "2 of 3 processed · 1 failed", a list naming that contract with "Step not found or not assigned to you", and **Retry 1 failed**. The dialog stays open. The footer's **Cancel** and **Approve** are now greyed out: only the ×, a click outside or **Retry** get you on (reported). |
| 6 | **Retry 1 failed**. | The selection becomes that one item, the progress line and the failure list disappear, and **Cancel** works again. Close the dialog with **Cancel**. |
| 7 | With two or more new items: **Bulk decision…** → **Approve N**. | "✓ N of N processed" in green, then the dialog closes by itself and the queue refreshes. |

**Also check**
- **Reject all selected** needs the comment and writes it on each decision; each contract returns to Draft.
- **Bulk decision…** shows only when the queue has two or more items.

**Known limits**
- Decisions are sent one at a time. A failure doesn't undo the ones that succeeded.

### E2E-APPR-10 · Workflow admins see every approval in flight, oldest wait first, including ones that can no longer move

**Covers:** /approvals · `GET /approvals/all`, `POST /approvals/workflows` · — · — · TC-WF-06, TC-WF-07
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B; the dev database for step 7 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Pending approvals from earlier journeys (`$C1` on counsel-a; R5, R7 on finance-a; R12 on admin-a).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | admin-a: **Approvals** → **All approvals** (its tab shows the number in flight). | "Every approval in flight across the org, oldest wait first." Columns **Contract**, **Current step**, **Awaiting**, **Submitted**, **Waiting** (in capitals), and a last column with **Open →**. Rows sorted by waiting time, longest first. |
| 2 | Read `$C1`'s row. | Title "QA APPR-01 services" (a link) and, under it, "USD 20,000" (the counterparty's name comes first when there is one). Current step "Legal review", "step 1 of 1". Awaiting "Legal Counsel". Submitted "Casey Contracts" and the date. Waiting "today" with a grey dot. **Open →** opens the contract. |
| 3 | R12's row (awaiting admin-a). | Under "Admin User", a small "You" marker. |
| 4 | Strand an approval: `W_STRAND=$(curl -s -X POST $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"name\":\"QA stranded\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":0,\"name\":\"First look\",\"approverId\":\"$COUNSEL_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":48},{\"order\":1,\"name\":\"Second look\",\"roleRequired\":\"NO_SUCH_ROLE\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":48}]}" \| jq -r .id)`; `C10=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-10 stranded" OTHER 7000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $C10 $W_STRAND; decide "$COUNSEL_A" $INST $STEP APPROVED "first look done"` | The decision answers 200 with `"instanceStatus":"PENDING"`. The API log has "[workflow-engine] no approvers found for step 1 … — skipping". `st $C10` → PENDING_APPROVAL. |
| 5 | Reload **All approvals**. | C10's row: Current step "Unrouted" in red with a warning icon (tooltip "This approval is still open but has no pending step, so no decision can be recorded against it. It needs to be re-routed or withdrawn."); Awaiting "nobody" in italics. The line above the table adds "1 is unrouted and cannot move at all." |
| 6 | `curl -s $API/approvals/all -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.data[] \| select(.contract.title=="QA APPR-10 stranded") \| {status, totalSteps, currentStepName, currentApproverName, currentStepPosition, stepCount}'` | `{"status":"PENDING","totalSteps":0,"currentStepName":null,"currentApproverName":null,"currentStepPosition":1,"stepCount":2}`. |
| 7 | A week-old approval (dev database only): `sql "UPDATE approval_instances SET \"submittedAt\" = now() - interval '8 days' WHERE \"contractId\" = '$C1' AND status = 'PENDING';"`, then reload. | `$C1` moves to the top: Waiting "8d" with a red dot. The line adds "1 has been waiting a week or more." counsel-a's C1 card: "Waiting 8 days" in red; the queue line "Oldest first · longest wait is 8 days". |
| 8 | legalops-a: **Approvals**. counsel-a, contracts-a, finance-a, approver-a: **Approvals**. | legalops-a has the **All approvals** tab with the same rows. The others have only **My Queue** and **Manage Workflows**. |
| 9 | `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' $API/approvals/all -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"`, and the same with `$VIEWER_A` and `$REP_A`. | 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: configure:workflow"` each time. |
| 10 | admin-b: **Approvals** → **All approvals**. | "No approvals in flight" / "No contracts are pending approval anywhere in the org." None of Org A's rows. |

**Also check**
- Approvals left in the old ESCALATED state (from before the C2 fix) are listed as Unrouted and counted (TC-WF-07 makes
  one in the database).
- The Dashboard's approval figures (the user's own queue, and **Org Approvals** for admins) and the sidebar's
  **Approvals** badge move with these approvals (§1; TC-WF-06, TC-ACC-20).
- The list shows at most 100 approvals.

**Known limits**
- Nothing in the product moves an Unrouted approval: there is no withdraw or re-route action, and editing the workflow
  doesn't restart it (reported). The contract stays **Approval**; delete it (§2) to clear the row.

### E2E-APPR-11 · An overdue step escalates: with a named target it moves, with none it stays and the admins are told

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /approvals/workflows`, `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide` · — · notification.worker · TC-WF-05
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, legalops-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Exactly one API process (§0.2): the escalation timers run in its notification worker.
- Two workflows due after 0.01 hours (36 seconds). The builder's minimum is 1 hour, so use the API:

```bash
wf() { curl -s -X POST $API/approvals/workflows -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$1" | jq -r .id; }
W_ESC0=$(wf "{\"name\":\"QA overdue no target\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":0,\"name\":\"Legal sign-off\",\"approverId\":\"$COUNSEL_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":0.01}]}")
W_ESCT=$(wf "{\"name\":\"QA overdue to admin\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":0,\"name\":\"Legal sign-off\",\"approverId\":\"$COUNSEL_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":0.01,\"escalateTo\":\"$ADMIN_A_ID\"}]}")
E1=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA overdue no target" OTHER 4000); E2=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA overdue named target" OTHER 4000)
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $E1 $W_ESC0; IE1=$INST; SE1=$STEP`, then wait about a minute. | counsel-a first gets the usual "Contract awaiting your approval". |
| 2 | Before counsel-a acts, admin-a tries the step: `decide "$ADMIN_A" $IE1 $SE1 APPROVED` | 403 `{"error":"Step not found or not assigned to you"}`. An admin can't decide someone else's step. |
| 3 | counsel-a: **My Queue**; `inst $IE1`. | E1's card is still there, reading "Escalates today" (after a day it reads "Escalated 1d ago"). The approval is PENDING with one PENDING step for Legal Counsel. |
| 4 | counsel-a's bell; Mailpit for legal@demo.com. | "Approval overdue — action required": `"QA overdue no target" is waiting on your approval and is overdue. Please review and decide.` In the bell and as an email. |
| 5 | admin-a's bell; Mailpit for admin@demo.com. | "Approval overdue — no escalation target": `"QA overdue no target" has waited past its deadline on step "Legal sign-off" (Legal Counsel), and the workflow names no one to escalate to. The approver can still decide; delegate the step or set an escalation target on the workflow.` Every active ADMIN other than the approver gets it (up to 10); legalops-a doesn't (not an ADMIN). |
| 6 | `audit APPROVAL_ESCALATED $IE1` | One event with no actor, resourceType approval_instance, metadata `{"stepId":"<SE1>","escalateTo":null,"adminsNotified":1}` (the number of other active admins). |
| 7 | counsel-a approves E1 from the card. | Accepted: E1 is **Approved**. |
| 8 | `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $E2 $W_ESCT; IE2=$INST; SE2=$STEP`; wait about a minute. | E2 leaves counsel-a's queue and appears in admin-a's ("LEGAL SIGN-OFF", "Escalates in 2d"). admin-a's bell and email: "Contract escalated to you for approval", `"QA overdue named target" approval was not acted upon and has been escalated to you.` `inst $IE2` → counsel-a's step ESCALATED, a new PENDING step for Admin User. `audit APPROVAL_ESCALATED $IE2` → `{"stepId":"<SE2>","escalateTo":"<ADMIN_A_ID>"}` with no adminsNotified. |
| 9 | `decide "$COUNSEL_A" $IE2 $SE2 APPROVED`, then admin-a approves from the card. | counsel-a: 403 `{"error":"Step not found or not assigned to you"}`. admin-a: accepted; E2 **Approved**. |
| 10 | A decision in time cancels the timer: `W_ESC5=$(wf "{\"name\":\"QA due in 3 min\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":0,\"name\":\"Legal sign-off\",\"approverId\":\"$COUNSEL_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":0.05}]}"); E3=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA in time" OTHER 4000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $E3 $W_ESC5; decide "$COUNSEL_A" $INST $STEP APPROVED`; wait 4 minutes. | No "Approval overdue" notification or email for E3, and no APPROVAL_ESCALATED event for it. |

**Also check**
- admin-b's bell has none of these. `GET /approvals/$IE1` as admin-b → 404 `{"error":"Approval instance not found"}`.
- To run a 48-hour timer now: set `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true` in `.env` (development only) and restart the API; open
  http://localhost:3001/admin/queues → the **notifications** queue → its delayed jobs → the `escalate` job with id
  `escalate-<stepId>` → promote it (verify the button name in Bull Board). The escalation runs at once.
- Escalation emails ignore the "Approval requested from me" setting; only **Off** stops them (E2E-NOTIF-01).
- Delete the QA overdue workflows afterwards.

**Known limits**
- A step escalated to a named user shows a new 48-hour deadline on its card, but it gets no new timer and never
  escalates again (reported). Delegated steps likewise.
- Approvals sent by the assistant get no timer at all (E2E-APPR-13).
- The builder can't set a deadline under 1 hour.
