### E2E-APPR-12 · Changing an approved contract's type, value, currency or document sends it back to Draft; its status can't be set by hand

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval`, `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide` · — · — · TC-WF-01, TC-WF-02, TC-WF-04
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra (step 5 starts a re-analysis, which needs the agents service to finish) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `C12=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA APPR-12 terms" MSA 40000)` (owner counsel-a). `approve_now $C12` → `HTTP 200`;
  `st $C12` → APPROVED.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Value: `curl -s -X PATCH $API/contracts/$C12 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"value":60000}' \| jq -r .status` | `DRAFT`. On the page (reload): pill **Draft**, **Send for Review** offered. |
| 2 | `approve_now $C12`; then PATCH `{"value":60000}` (the same value) and PATCH `{"title":"QA APPR-12 terms (renamed)"}`. | Both keep `APPROVED`. |
| 3 | Currency: PATCH `{"currency":"EUR"}`. | `DRAFT`. Then `approve_now $C12`. |
| 4 | A term change together with a status: PATCH `{"value":70000,"status":"EXECUTED"}`. | 409 `{"detail":"Changing the type, value or currency of an approved contract returns it to DRAFT for approval again. Change the status separately."}`; `st $C12` → APPROVED. |
| 5 | Type, from the page: as counsel-a open C12 → click the type chip "MSA" (tooltip "Click to correct the contract type") → pick "SOW". | Pill **Draft**. `audit CONTRACT_UPDATED $C12` → metadata `{"action":"retype","typeFrom":"MSA","typeTo":"SOW","statusFrom":"APPROVED","statusTo":"DRAFT"}`. A re-analysis starts (without the agents service it ends Failed; §2). |
| 6 | `approve_now $C12`. Document: counsel-a → header **Edit** → type a word into the document → wait for "Saved ✓" → **Done**. | Pill **Draft**. `audit CONTRACT_UPDATED $C12` → `{"action":"document_edited","versionNumber":2,"statusFrom":"APPROVED","statusTo":"DRAFT"}`. |
| 7 | `approve_now $C12`. Open C12 → **Edit** → **Done** without typing. | Still **Approved**; no new version: a save that changes nothing makes nothing (TC-WF-01). |
| 8 | New file: `printf 'QA v3 text\n' > /tmp/v3.txt; curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C12/versions -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@/tmp/v3.txt;type=text/plain" \| jq .versionNumber; st $C12` | A new version number; `DRAFT`. |
| 9 | By hand: PATCH `{"status":"APPROVED"}` on the Draft contract; then `{"status":"PENDING_APPROVAL"}` and `{"status":"REJECTED"}`. | 409 each: `{"detail":"APPROVED is set by the approval workflow, not by hand. Submit the contract for approval instead."}` (the status name varies). |
| 10 | `approve_now $C12`; as counsel-a, reload C12 → **Mark as Executed**. | The pill reads **Executed** (approved to executed without signatures, and without a sealed PDF). The header now offers **Archive**. |

**Also check**
- The Extraction Queue's corrections to value or currency reset an approved contract the same way (§4, TC-WF-04).
- A change while the approval is still pending doesn't restart it: the approvers decide on the changed contract.
- The CSV import refuses approval statuses row by row (§2, TC-WF-02).
- The owner (counsel-a) gets "<title> was updated" in the bell when someone else changes the contract, at most once an
  hour per contract (E2E-NOTIF-02).

**Known limits**
- The earlier approval record stays APPROVED in the API; only the contract's status goes back.

**Roles:** approver-a, contracts-a, counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key (steps 1–9); steps 10–13 need none · **Time:** ~25 min

| # | Do | Expect |

Every cell reads "—", and the rows link to a page that doesn't exist (reported). |

The reply says the action is prepared, not done. The pill still reads **Draft**. |
| 3 | **Apply**. | The card becomes "Applied · Submit this contract for approval (auto-selecting the matching workflow)" with **Undo**. The pill reads **Approval**. counsel-a's **My Queue** lists C13 (Standard approval). |
| 4 | Compare with **Send for Review**: Mailpit, counsel-a's bell, `audit APPROVAL_SUBMITTED $C13`, `audit AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED`. | No email to legal@demo.com, no bell notification, no APPROVAL_SUBMITTED event (an AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED event with toolName approval_route instead), and no AI summary (after 5 minutes the card says "No AI summary for this submission — review the contract directly."). Reported. |

| 6 | Ask again → **Apply**. counsel-a approves C13 from **My Queue**. contracts-a clicks **Undo**. | The undo is refused: "An approver has already acted on this request — cannot undo" (verify how the panel shows it). C13 stays **Approved**. |
| 7 | As counsel-a, open R6 and ask "Approve my pending approval step on this contract. Note: terms are standard." | The assistant looks up the approval first, then shows "About to run" approval_decide, with no "Undoable" badge and the text "Approve this approval step". It says this can't be undone. **Apply** → "Applied", with no **Undo**. R6 is **Approved**. `inst` → the comment the assistant passed. `audit APPROVAL_DECIDED` → metadata includes `"via":"agent"`. |

| 10 | Without a model: `T=$(curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' \| jq -r .id); C13b=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA APPR-13 api" OTHER 8000); curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads/$T/actions/apply -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"toolName\":\"approval_route\",\"args\":{\"contractId\":\"$C13b\"}}" \| jq '{ok, toolCallId, result}'` | `ok: true`, a `toolCallId`, and `result` `{ok:true, reversible:true, instanceId, stepId, stepIds, contractId, previousStatus:"DRAFT", workflowDefinitionId, firstApproverId:<COUNSEL_A_ID>, approverIds, currentStepOrder:0, autoApproved:false}`. |
| 11 | Undo it: `curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads/$T/actions/<toolCallId>/undo -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A"`; run it twice. | First: `{ok:true, toolCallId, rolledBackAt}`; `st $C13b` → DRAFT. Second: 409 `{"detail":"Already undone",…}`. |
| 12 | approval_decide through the same endpoint: as contracts-a, toolName approval_decide with counsel-a's instance and step ids and `"decision":"APPROVED"`; then the same as approver-a (in their own thread). | contracts-a: 403 `{"detail":"Missing permission: approve:workflow"}` (checked before the tool runs). approver-a: 403 `{"ok":false,"toolCallId":…,"error":{"detail":"Step not found or not assigned to you"}}`: the assistant can only decide the caller's own steps. |
| 13 | approval_list at the tool endpoint: `curl -s -X POST $TOOLS/approval_list -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'x-internal-service: agents' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"orgId\":\"$ORG_A\",\"userId\":\"$APPROVER_A_ID\",\"scope\":\"my-queue\"}" \| jq '{total, scope, first: (.items[0] \| {stepName, instanceId, title: .contract.title, status})}'`; then `"scope":"all"`; then `"userId":"$VIEWER_A_ID"`. | my-queue: approver-a's current steps, as on **My Queue**. `all` for approver-a: 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have configure:workflow permission"}`. viewer-a: 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:workflow permission"}`. |

**Also check**
- viewer-a asking "What's waiting on my approval?": approval_list isn't offered to viewer-a, and the assistant says it
  can't list approvals (verify the wording). No table appears.
- approval_route refuses what **Send for Review** refuses: a contract not in Draft, In Review or In Negotiation → 409
  "Cannot submit a contract with status … for approval"; one with an approval in flight → 409 "Contract already has an
  active approval workflow"; an inactive workflow id → 422 "That workflow is inactive or no longer exists. Omit it to use
  the workflow whose rules fit the contract."
- approval_route on an NDA of USD 5,000 approves it at once (`autoApproved: true`); **Undo** returns it to Draft.
- approval_decide with REJECTED and no comment → 400 `{"detail":"comment is required when rejecting"}`.
- After 15 minutes, **Undo** answers 410 "Undo window expired (15 minutes)".
- Route with the assistant, then within 15 minutes click **Send for Signature** (status Approval allows it), then
  **Undo**: the contract goes back to Draft although a signature request is out (verify; reported).

**Known limits**
- Approvals sent by the assistant send no notification or email, get no AI summary and no escalation timer, write no
  APPROVAL_SUBMITTED event and fire no `approval.submitted` webhook. The approver finds them only in **My Queue**.

| 10 | `audit SIGNATURE_SENT $S1` | Actor Legal Counsel; metadata `{signatureRequestId, signerCount:2, signers:[{name,email,role},…], signOrder:"ANY"}`. The contract's Activity tab lists "SIGNATURE SENT". |

Keep S1 for E2E-SIGN-02.

**Also check**
- Sending needs `sign:contract`: admin, counsel, legalops and contracts. procurement-a, finance-a, approver-a,
  viewer-a and rep-a see no **Send for Signature**; `sfs "$VIEWER_A" $S1 '[{"name":"x","email":"x@example.test"}]'` →
  403 `"detail":"Missing permission: sign:contract"`.
- The button shows on every status except Executed, Expired, Terminated and Archived: signing doesn't require an
  approval (a Draft can be sent). On an Executed contract there's no button; the API answers 409 `{"detail":"Contract already executed"}`.
- No document: `NV=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA no version","type":"OTHER"}' | jq -r .id)`
  → open it → **Send for Signature**: a yellow banner "Contract has no version to sign — upload or generate a version
  first." and **Send for signature** disabled. API: 400 `{"detail":"Contract has no version to sign"}`.
- Validation (API): an invalid email, no signers or 21 signers, `expiresInDays` 0 or 181, a message over 2,000
  characters → 422 `"detail":"Request body failed validation"`.
- A signer linked to a user must be that user: `sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S1 '[{"name":"X","email":"ceo@example.test","userId":"'$REP_A_ID'"}]'`
  → 400 `{"detail":"Signer ceo@example.test is linked to a user who is not an active member with that email"}` (TC-ACC-21).
- Other org: admin-b sending on `$S1` → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`; `GET $API/contracts/$S1/signature-requests`
  as admin-b → 200 `{"data":[]}`.
- A refusal shows in the dialog's red box (for example, send from two tabs after the contract became Executed:
  "Contract already executed").
- The API console (development) prints one line per signer:
  `[signing] ✉  signer1@example.test  →  http://localhost:5173/sign/<token>  (MSA "QA SIGN-01 any order", signer "Signer One" · expires <date>)`.

**Known limits**
- The dialog can't link a signer to an app user; internal signers are matched by email (E2E-SIGN-07).
- **Resend for Signature** creates a second request; the first stays open until voided (E2E-SIGN-05).
- The dialog offers 7 to 90 days; the API accepts 1 to 180.

### E2E-SIGN-02 · Each signer reviews and signs in the signer portal, and the last signature executes the contract

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `GET /sign/:token`, `POST /sign/:token/sign`, `GET /contracts/:id/signature-requests` · — · signing.worker · TC-SMK-05
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signers · **Needs:** Mailpit, a private browser window · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- S1 sent in E2E-SIGN-01. `T1=$(tok $S1 signer1@example.test); T2=$(tok $S1 signer2@example.test)`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | In a private window (not signed in), open Signer One's link from Mailpit. | "Loading document to sign…", then the portal. A dark strip: "Demo Org, Inc. · Signing portal", "Secure link", "Expires in 7d". A line: "Signing as Signer One · CFO · v1 · 0 / 2 signed" and **Print or save a copy** on the right. Title "QA SIGN-01 any order", "MSA · sent by Demo Org, Inc.". "Message from sender: Please sign by Friday." The document's text, read-only. A bottom bar: "Ready to sign? Review the document above, then click Sign." with **Decline** and **Sign**. Footer "Secured by draftLegal · Terms · Privacy". |
| 2 | **Print or save a copy**. | The browser's print dialog; the preview shows the document without the bars. Cancel it. |
| 3 | **Sign**. | Dialog "Sign this document": a box "QA SIGN-01 any order · v1"; "Type your full legal name to sign. Your signature, IP address, and timestamp will be captured + included in the signed audit trail."; "Your full legal name" (placeholder "Signer One"); a checkbox "I agree to conduct this transaction and sign electronically. I understand my electronic signature is legally binding, and that the document will be sealed with a tamper-evident digital signature."; **Cancel** and **Sign** (disabled). |
| 4 | Type the name only; then clear it and tick the box only. | **Sign** stays disabled until both are done. Esc, the ×, **Cancel** or a click outside closes the dialog. |
| 5 | Type "Signer One", tick the box, **Sign**. | The bar: "You've signed this document." and "Waiting on 1 more signature. Demo Org, Inc. will send the fully executed copy once everyone has signed." |
| 6 | counsel-a's view of S1 (the card refreshes every 15 s). | "Awaiting signatures · 1/2 signed". Signer One "Signed just now". Activity: "Signed · Signer One", "Viewed by signer · Signer One", "Sent for signature". Pill still **Signing**. On the **Signatures** page the row reads "Partly signed". |
| 7 | `sign $T1 "Signer One"` | 409 `{"detail":"Already signed"}`. |
| 8 | Open Signer Two's link in another private window → **Sign** → "Signer Two", tick → **Sign**. | "You've signed this document." and "That was the last signature. Demo Org, Inc. will send the fully executed copy." |
| 9 | counsel-a reloads S1. | Pill **Executed**. No **Send for Signature**; **Archive** is offered. The card: "Fully signed · 2/2 signed", "· Completed just now"; no **Send reminder** or **Void**. Activity ends with "Fully completed". |
| 10 | Reload a signer's link. | "Link unavailable" and "This signing request is no longer active", then "What to do next": "If you already signed, no further action is needed — the sender has your signature.", "Otherwise, reply to the email that carried this link and ask for a fresh one.", "Signing links are single-recipient. Forwarding one does not work." |
| 11 | `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' $API/sign/$T1`; `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' $API/sign/not-a-real-token`; `sign $T2 "again"` | 410 `{"detail":"This signing request is no longer active"}`; 404 `{"detail":"Invalid signing link"}`; 410 `{"detail":"Signing request is no longer active"}`. |
| 12 | `srq $S1 \| jq '{status, completedAt, signers: [.signers[] \| {name, status, signedName, signedAt, signedIp, signedUserAgent}], events: [.events[] \| {kind, ipAddress, userAgent, metadata}]}'` | status "COMPLETED" with completedAt. Each signer SIGNED with the typed name, the time, the IP (a loopback address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1 on a local stack) and the browser's user agent. Events, newest first: COMPLETED, SIGNED, VIEWED, SIGNED, VIEWED, SENT. The SIGNED events' metadata: `consentGiven: true`, `consentText: "Signer agreed to conduct business and sign electronically."`. |
| 13 | `audit SIGNATURE_COMPLETED $S1` | Two events: the completion `{signatureRequestId, signerCount:2}` and, a few seconds later, the seal `{"event":"document_sealed","sha256":"…","algorithm":"SHA-256","signatureRequestId":"…"}` (E2E-SIGN-09 checks the sealed PDF). |

**Also check**
- `POST /sign/:token/sign` with an empty `signedName` → 422 "Request body failed validation". The API doesn't require
  `consent`; the page does. A call with `"consent":false` is recorded with `consentGiven: false`.
- The typed name doesn't have to match the signer's name.
- A VIEWED event is recorded once per signer, on their first visit.
- With the agents service running, completion also starts obligation extraction (§6: the Obligations rail fills in).
- The webhooks `signature.completed` and `contract.executed` fire (E2E-NOTIF-06).
- A document with no readable text (for example D-SCAN.pdf when no OCR text came out): the portal shows "This request
  has no readable document attached" and "Nothing was included for you to review, so there is nothing to sign. Contact
  Demo Org, Inc. and ask them to re-send the request with the executed form of agreement attached."; the bar reads
  "Nothing to sign. No document was attached to this request."; **Sign** is disabled and **Decline** still works (verify
  with D-SCAN.pdf).
- A signer who reloads their page after signing, while others are still pending, is told "That was the last
  signature" (the count is off by one; reported).
- With a brand colour and logo set for the org (Admin → Organization, §1), the portal's top strip takes that colour and
  shows the logo; without them it is dark with a building icon.

**Known limits**
- The signer reads the version's extracted text, not the original PDF's layout. For a PDF upload the sealed file is the
  original PDF (E2E-SIGN-09).
- Nobody is emailed when a request completes: the signers get no executed copy (despite the page's wording) and the
  sender gets neither an email nor a bell notification (reported).

### E2E-SIGN-03 · In a sequential request, a later signer gets a link, and can act, only after the earlier signers have signed

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `POST /contracts/:id/send-for-signature`, `GET /sign/:token`, `POST /sign/:token/sign`, `POST /sign/:token/decline` · — · — · TC-SEC-11
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signers · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- `S3=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-03 in order" MSA 40000)` (a Draft: signing doesn't need approval).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | counsel-a: S3 → **Send for Signature** → **In sequence**. | A small order box appears at the start of each row, numbered 1 and 2. **Add signer** adds a row numbered 3; remove it. |
| 2 | Signer One (1), Signer Two (2) → **Send for signature**. | Pill **Signing**. |
| 3 | Mailpit. | Only signer1@example.test got an email. |
| 4 | S3's **Signatures** card. | "· Sequential signing"; the signer boxes show "· Order #1" and "· Order #2". |
| 5 | `T32=$(tok $S3 signer2@example.test)`; open `$WEB/sign/$T32` in a private window. | "Link unavailable" and "Earlier signers have not yet signed. You will be notified when it is your turn." |
| 6 | As signer 2 through the API: `curl -s -w '  HTTP %{http_code}\n' $API/sign/$T32`; `sign $T32 "Signer Two"`; `decline $T32 "early"` | All three: 403 `{"detail":"Earlier signers have not yet signed. You will be notified when it is your turn."}`. `srq $S3 \| jq '.status, [.events[].kind]'` → "PENDING" and no VIEWED event for signer 2. |
| 7 | Signer One signs from their email link. | "Waiting on 1 more signature…". |
| 8 | Mailpit; `srq $S3 \| jq '[.events[] \| {kind, next: .metadata.sequentialAdvance}]'` | signer2@example.test now has the signing email, with the original message. A SENT event with `next: true`. |
| 9 | Signer Two opens the link and signs. | S3 is **Executed**. |

**Also check**
- Signers with the same order number form a group: they are emailed together and sign in any order, and the next
  group is emailed when the whole group has signed.
- The **Signatures** page shows only the current signer under **Waiting on** ("Signer One") and "0 / 2 signed · in order".
- An internal later signer's sidebar **Signatures** badge counts the request only once it is their turn.
- Manual reminders go only to the current group (E2E-SIGN-05).

**Known limits**
- The sender isn't told as each signer signs; the card refreshes itself.
- The portal also has an in-page "Not your turn yet." banner, shown when a sign call is refused for turn order after
  the page loaded. Normal use doesn't produce it: a link opened too early shows "Link unavailable" instead (step 5).

### E2E-SIGN-04 · A signer declines with a reason: the request is voided, and the sender sees who declined and why

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `POST /sign/:token/decline`, `GET /signature-requests` · — · — · TC-WEB-04
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signers · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~8 min

**Preconditions**
- `S4=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-04 decline" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S4 '[{"name":"Signer One","email":"signer1@example.test"},{"name":"Signer Two","email":"signer2@example.test"}]'`

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Signer One opens their link → **Decline**. | Dialog "Decline to sign?": "Demo Org, Inc. is told immediately, and this signing link closes. You cannot undo it — they would have to send a new request." "Reason (optional, shared with the sender)" with the placeholder "e.g. the indemnity in clause 9 still needs to be resolved". **Keep reviewing** and **Decline to sign**. |
| 2 | **Keep reviewing**. | The dialog closes; nothing changed. |
| 3 | **Decline** → reason "Clause 9 indemnity" → **Decline to sign**. | "You declined to sign this document." and "Demo Org, Inc. has been notified. This link is now closed — if you meant to sign, ask them to send a new request." |
| 4 | counsel-a: S4's **Signatures** card. | "Voided · 0/2 signed" and, in red, "· Signer One declined: Clause 9 indemnity". Signer One "Declined". No **Send reminder** or **Void**. Activity: "Declined · Signer One". |
| 5 | **Signatures** page, S4's row. | Status "Voided". Waiting on: "Declined by Signer One" in red. |
| 6 | Signer Two opens their link; `sign "$(tok $S4 signer2@example.test)" "Signer Two"` | "Link unavailable", "This signing request is no longer active". The API: 410 `{"detail":"Signing request is no longer active"}`. |
| 7 | `audit SIGNATURE_VOIDED $S4` | Metadata `{signatureRequestId, declinedBy:"signer1@example.test", reason:"Clause 9 indemnity"}`; actor: the sender, Legal Counsel. |
| 8 | The contract's header. | The pill still reads **Signing**, with **Resend for Signature**. There's no way back to Draft or Approved by hand (reported). |

**Also check**
- A decline with no reason → the void reason reads "Signer One declined: (no reason given)".
- A signer who has signed can't then decline: in an "any order" request, sign as signer 1, then `decline` with the same
  token → 409 `{"detail":"Signer already responded"}`.
- A decline on an expired link → 410 `{"detail":"This signing link has expired"}` (E2E-SIGN-06).
- The sender gets no email or bell notification, although the page says they were "notified" (reported). The
  `signature.voided` webhook does fire (E2E-NOTIF-06).

**Known limits**
- One decline ends the request for every signer.

### E2E-SIGN-05 · The sender reminds pending signers and voids a request; a voided request can't be signed and emails no one else

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `POST /contracts/:id/signature-requests/:srId/remind`, `POST /contracts/:id/signature-requests/:srId/void` · — · notification.worker · TC-SEC-12
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b, external signers · **Needs:** Mailpit; Bull Board for step 4 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `S5=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-05 remind" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S5 '[{"name":"Signer One","email":"signer1@example.test"},{"name":"Signer Two","email":"signer2@example.test"}]' ANY 7`; `SR5=$(srq $S5 | jq -r .id)`.
- Signer One signs (their email link, or `sign "$(tok $S5 signer1@example.test)" "Signer One"`).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | counsel-a: S5's card → **Send reminder** (tooltip "Email a reminder to all still-pending signers"). | The button reads "Reminder sent". Mailpit: one new email, to signer2 only, subject "[Demo Org, Inc.] Signature requested: QA SIGN-05 remind", with the box "Message from Legal Counsel: Friendly reminder: a signature is still needed on this document." Activity: "Reminder sent". |
| 2 | A second reminder: `curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$S5/signature-requests/$SR5/remind -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` | 200 `{"ok":true,"signersNotified":1}`, but no second email arrives and no second "Reminder sent" event is logged: a request can be reminded by hand only once (reported; verify). |
| 3 | The scheduled reminders: `srq $S5 \| jq .expiresAt`. | The worker plans a "first" reminder 3 days before expiry and a "final" one 1 day before. |
| 4 | Run them now: with `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true` in `.env` (development only; restart the API), open http://localhost:3001/admin/queues → **notifications** → delayed jobs `sig-reminder-<SR5>-first` and `sig-reminder-<SR5>-final` → promote each (verify the button name). | Two emails to signer2: one with "Friendly reminder: a signature is still needed on this document.", one with "⚠ Final reminder — this signature link expires soon." `srq $S5 \| jq '[.events[] \| select(.kind=="REMINDED") \| .metadata]'` → `{kind:"first", signersNotified:1}` and `{kind:"final", …}`. |
| 5 | **Void** → click **Cancel** in the browser's confirm box "Void this signature request? This cannot be undone."; then **Void** → **OK**. | Cancel keeps it. OK: the card reads "Voided · 1/2 signed" and "· Voided by sender". `srq $S5 \| jq '.status, .voidedAt'` → "VOIDED" and a time. `audit SIGNATURE_VOIDED $S5` → actor Legal Counsel, `{signatureRequestId}`. |
| 6 | Signer Two's link; `sign "$(tok $S5 signer2@example.test)" "Signer Two"`; `decline` with the same token. | "Link unavailable", "This signing request is no longer active". Sign and decline: 410 `{"detail":"Signing request is no longer active"}`. |
| 7 | After the void: the card; remind through the API; void again through the API (`…/void` with `-d '{}'`). | No **Send reminder** or **Void** on the card. Remind: 409 `{"detail":"Request is VOIDED — cannot send reminder"}`. Void: 409 `{"detail":"Already terminated"}`. |
| 8 | A voided sequential request emails no next signer (X65): `S5b=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-05 void in order" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S5b '[{"name":"Signer One","email":"signer1@example.test","signOrder":1},{"name":"Signer Two","email":"signer2@example.test","signOrder":2}]' SEQUENTIAL`. Void it from its card. Then `sign "$(tok $S5b signer1@example.test)" "Signer One"`. | The sign call: 410 `{"detail":"Signing request is no longer active"}`. Mailpit: signer2 never gets a signing email for S5b. `srq $S5b \| jq '[.events[] \| {kind, next: .metadata.sequentialAdvance}]'` → VOIDED and the first SENT only; no SENT with `next: true`. |
| 9 | Optional race (TC-SEC-12 N6): a new two-signer sequential request, then `( sign <signer 1 token> R1 & curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/<id>/signature-requests/<srId>/void -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' & wait )`. | Whichever lands first, the request ends VOIDED, and no SENT with `next: true` is newer than the VOIDED event; signer 2 gets no email. The timing can't be forced: repeat a few times. |
| 10 | In Bull Board, promote one of the voided S5b's delayed reminders (`sig-reminder-<its request id>-first`). | The API log: "[signing-reminder] sr … is VOIDED (not PENDING) — skipping reminder". No email. |

**Also check**
- Reminding and voiding need `sign:contract`. viewer-a sees **Send reminder** and **Void** on the card anyway; clicking
  shows "You don't have permission to sign contracts." next to the button, and "Failed to void signature request. You
  don't have permission to sign contracts." (reported: offered to users who can't use them). API → 403
  `"detail":"Missing permission: sign:contract"`.
- Org B: admin-b reminding or voiding Org A's request → 404 `{"detail":"Signature request not found"}`.
- A void racing the last signature (TC-SEC-12 N5): whichever lands first wins. A VOIDED request never comes with an
  Executed contract or a sign call that answered 200.
- **Resend for Signature** on a Signing contract creates a second request; the first stays open and both are listed
  on the card, newest first. Void the old one by hand.

**Known limits**
- Voiding leaves the contract **Signing** (reported).
- A request that expires within 3 days gets no "first" reminder, and one that expires within a day gets none at all.

### E2E-SIGN-06 · An expired link can't be viewed, signed or declined, and the request is marked expired when it is next used

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `GET /sign/:token`, `POST /sign/:token/sign`, `POST /sign/:token/decline` · — · notification.worker · TC-SEC-12
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signer · **Needs:** the dev database (or wait 24 hours) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Three one-signer requests with 1-day expiry (the API allows 1 day; the dialog's shortest is 7):
  `for n in 6 6b 6c; do c=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-0$n expiry" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $c '[{"name":"Signer One","email":"signer1@example.test"}]' ANY 1 > /dev/null; echo "S$n=$c"; done`
  and set `S6`, `S6b`, `S6c` from the output.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open S6's link. | The strip reads "Expires in 1d". |
| 2 | Backdate all three (dev database only): `sql "UPDATE signature_requests SET \"expiresAt\" = now() - interval '1 hour' WHERE \"contractId\" IN ('$S6','$S6b','$S6c');"` | `UPDATE 3`. |
| 3 | counsel-a: S6's card (reload); the **Signatures** page. | The card still reads "Awaiting signatures" with "Expires today": the status changes only when the request is next used. The page shows "Awaiting" with a red "lapses today". |
| 4 | Reload S6's link. | "Link unavailable", "This signing link has expired". `srq $S6 \| jq .status` → "EXPIRED". |
| 5 | `sign "$(tok $S6 signer1@example.test)" "Signer One"` | 410 `{"detail":"Signing request is no longer active"}` (it is EXPIRED now). |
| 6 | Sign first on S6b: `sign "$(tok $S6b signer1@example.test)" "Signer One"` | 410 `{"detail":"This signing link has expired"}`. S6b: status EXPIRED, the signer still PENDING, the contract not Executed. |
| 7 | Decline first on S6c: `decline "$(tok $S6c signer1@example.test)" "late"` | 410 `{"detail":"This signing link has expired"}`. S6c: EXPIRED, not VOIDED; the signer still PENDING. |
| 8 | S6's card; the **Signatures** page → **Expired** tab. | "Expired · 0/1 signed", no buttons. The tab lists S6, S6b and S6c. |
| 9 | Remind and void S6 through the API. | Remind: 409 `{"detail":"Request is EXPIRED — cannot send reminder"}`. Void: 409 `{"detail":"Already terminated"}`. |

**Also check**
- If a scheduled reminder fires after the expiry, the worker marks the request EXPIRED and logs a "Voided" event with
  `autoExpired: true` (the card's Activity reads "Voided" for an expiry).
- An internal signer's **Sign →** link and `mySignPath` disappear once the request is past its expiry (TC-ACC-21 N4).

**Known limits**
- Expiry is applied lazily, when the link is used or a reminder fires; until then the card and page read as awaiting.
- The contract stays **Signing** after its request expires.

### E2E-SIGN-07 · Internal users sign through their own personal link, and see only their own

**Covers:** /signatures, /sign/:token · `GET /signature-requests`, `GET /contracts/:id/signature-requests` · — · — · TC-SEC-10, TC-ACC-11, TC-ACC-21
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `S7=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-07 internal" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S7 '[{"name":"Viewer A","email":"viewer@qa.test"},{"name":"Counterparty","email":"counterparty@example.test"}]'`
- `S7b=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA SIGN-07 rep signs" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S7b '[{"name":"Sam Sales","email":"SALES@DEMO.COM"}]'` (capitals on purpose).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Mailpit. | viewer@qa.test and sales@demo.com get the same signing email as an external signer. |
| 2 | viewer-a (may view contracts, may not send for signature): the sidebar **Signatures** badge, then the page. | Badge 1. The subtitle adds "1 is waiting on your signature." S7's row: Waiting on "You" (bold) "+1 more"; Action **Open →**. |
| 3 | viewer-a opens S7 → the rail's **Signatures**. | Both signers and their status. **Copy link** only on "Viewer A", not on "Counterparty". |
| 4 | **Copy link**, paste it into the address bar, sign. | The portal says "Signing as Viewer A". After signing, the badge goes back to 0. |
| 5 | `curl -s $API/contracts/$S7/signature-requests -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" \| jq '[.data[0].signers[] \| {email, hasToken: has("token")}]'`, and the same with `$COUNSEL_A`. | viewer-a: only viewer@qa.test has a token. counsel-a (may send for signature): both do. |
| 6 | Before rep-a signs: `curl -s "$API/signature-requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" \| jq '.data[] \| select(.contract.title=="QA SIGN-07 rep signs") \| {canOpenContract, mySignPath, signerFields: [.signers[] \| keys]}'` | `canOpenContract: false`, `mySignPath: "/sign/<token>"`, and no signer entry has a `token` or `userId` field. The address in capitals still matched. |
| 7 | rep-a (own scope; doesn't own S7b) → **Signatures**. | S7b's row: the title as plain text (not a link); Action **Sign →**; "1 is waiting on your signature." |
| 8 | **Sign →** → sign. | The portal says "Signing as Sam Sales". S7b becomes **Executed**. |
| 9 | rep-a opens `$WEB/contracts/$S7b`. | "Contract not found": rep-a signed without being able to open the contract. |

**Also check**
- rep-a sees only requests on contracts they own plus the ones they sign; `$API/contracts/$S7/signature-requests` as
  rep-a → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- An underscore in a member's address matches only an underscore, not any character (TC-ACC-21 N5).
- In a sequential request an internal later signer has no `mySignPath` (and no **Sign →**) before their turn.
- An API key with only `contracts:sign` → `GET /signature-requests` 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: view:contract"` (TC-ACC-11).

**Known limits**
- There is no sign button inside the app: internal signers use the same public page, through their link.
- A signer who can open the contract sees **Open →**, not **Sign →**; they sign from the email or **Copy link**.

### E2E-SIGN-08 · The Signatures page shows every request, who it waits on and for how long, with filters and search

**Covers:** /signatures · `GET /signature-requests` · — · — · TC-ACC-11
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-SIGN-01 to 07 done. The seed also added four requests, one per status, on the first seeded contracts, each with
  the signer "Alex Signer" (signer@counterparty.test, "Authorised Signatory").

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | counsel-a: left rail → **Queues** → **Signatures**. | Title **Signatures**, "Every contract sent for signature across your organization." Tabs **All**, **Awaiting**, **Completed**, **Voided**, **Expired**, each with a count that doesn't change as you switch tabs. A search box "Search contract or signer". Columns **Contract**, **Waiting on**, **Status**, **Sent**, **Action** (in capitals). |
| 2 | Read the rows. | Newest first. Contract: the title (a link) and "<TYPE> · <counterparty>". Waiting on: "x / y signed" (" · in order" for sequential), then the outstanding signer ("Name", "+N more", " · role" when one); a decline shows "Declined by <name>" in red. Status: **Awaiting**, **Partly signed**, **Completed**, **Voided** or **Expired**; an open request expiring within 7 days adds a red "lapses in Nd", "lapses today" or "lapsed Nd ago". Sent: "5m ago" and so on, plus "done …" in green once completed. Action: **Open →** (or **Sign →**, E2E-SIGN-07). |
| 3 | Click each tab. | Only that status. An empty tab: "No completed signature requests.", "No voided signature requests." and so on; the Awaiting tab's empty text reads "No pending signature requests." |
| 4 | Search "SIGN-04", then "signer2@example", then "zzzz". | A title match; a signer email match; then "No signature requests match "zzzz"." with "Open any contract and click **Send for Signature** to get started." |
| 5 | The seeded rows. | "Alex Signer · Authorised Signatory" under Waiting on for the seeded open request; seeded rows under Completed, Voided and Expired. |
| 6 | `curl -s "$API/signature-requests?status=COMPLETED&limit=2&offset=0" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{total, limit, offset, n: (.data \| length), statuses: ([.data[].status] \| unique), tokens: [.data[].signers[] \| select(has("token"))] \| length}'` | `total` = the number of completed requests, `limit` 2, `offset` 0, `n` 2 (or fewer), statuses `["COMPLETED"]`, tokens 0. `status=BOGUS` is ignored (every status comes back); `limit` is capped at 100. |
| 7 | viewer-a, rep-a and admin-b open **Signatures**. | viewer-a: all of Org A's requests. rep-a: requests on contracts rep-a owns and the ones rep-a signs. admin-b: only Org B's; a fresh Org B shows "No signature requests yet." |
| 8 | Stop the API and reload the page; then start it again. | "Failed to load signature requests." in a red box. |

**Also check**
- The sidebar **Signatures** badge counts the requests where the user is the signer being waited on now (by email).
- An API key without `view:contract` → 403.

**Known limits**
- The page loads the newest 50 requests; the per-status tab counts come from those 50 (**All** uses the true total).
  Verify with more than 50 requests.
- A request past its expiry reads as awaiting until it is next used (E2E-SIGN-06).

### E2E-SIGN-09 · After the last signature the contract gets a sealed PDF with a certificate page, and any change to the file shows

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `POST /sign/:token/sign`, `GET /contracts/:id/signature-requests` · — · signing.worker · TC-SMK-05
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signer · **Needs:** Adobe Acrobat Reader (or poppler's `pdfsig`); Gotenberg for text and Word contracts · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Upload D-MSA.pdf as counsel-a:
  `S9=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@$HOME/qa-docs/D-MSA.pdf;type=application/pdf" -F "title=QA SIGN-09 Northwind MSA" -F "type=MSA" | jq -r .id)`.
  Wait until its text is read (§2), then `sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $S9 '[{"name":"Signer One","email":"signer1@example.test","role":"CFO"}]'`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Signer One signs, typing "Signer One Legal". | S9 is **Executed**. |
| 2 | Wait 10–30 seconds. | API log: "[signing-worker] sealed sr=<request id> version=<version id> key=signed/<contract id>/<request id>.pdf". `audit SIGNATURE_COMPLETED $S9` has the `document_sealed` event with its `sha256`. |
| 3 | counsel-a opens S9 → the **Versions** tab (the tab bar shows once you leave the Document view; with two versions, the rail's **History** section has a **Negotiate** link that does this). | The newest is "Version 2", with the note "Signed by 1 signer — sealed with PAdES/X.509 (SHA-256 <first 12 hex characters>…)", its date and size. |
| 4 | **Actions** → **Download** (or the version's download icon). | A PDF opens in a new tab: D-MSA's own pages, then one more page. |
| 5 | Read the last page. | A green band "Signature Certificate" and "Demo Org, Inc. · <YYYY-MM-DD>". "Document", the title, "MSA · Signature request id: <id>". "Signers (1)", then a card: "Signer One · CFO", "signer1@example.test", "Signed as: Signer One Legal", "Signed: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> UTC", "IP: <address>". At the foot: "This certificate is generated automatically when all required signatures are collected. Each signer's typed name, IP address, and timestamp constitute the legal record of consent. The completed document is sealed with a PAdES/X.509 digital signature (SHA-256); any modification after signing invalidates it." and "Generated <time> · sealed with PAdES/X.509 (SHA-256)". |
| 6 | Look for the signer's browser on the certificate. | It isn't there (reported). It is recorded: `srq $S9 \| jq '.signers[0].signedUserAgent, [.events[] \| select(.kind=="SIGNED") \| .userAgent]'` prints it. |
| 7 | Save the file and compare hashes: `curl -s -o sealed.pdf "$(curl -s $API/contracts/$S9/download -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq -r .url)"; shasum -a 256 sealed.pdf; curl -s $API/contracts/$S9 -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '.versions[0].metadata._signature'` | The file's hash equals `_signature.sha256` and the audit event's `sha256`. `_signature`: `{"sha256":…,"algorithm":"SHA-256","format":"PAdES/X.509 (adbe.pkcs7.detached)","sealedAt":…,"signatureRequestId":…}`. |
| 8 | Open sealed.pdf in Adobe Acrobat Reader and open its signature panel. | One signature, signed by "draftLegal Signing Authority" (the development certificate's name), reason "Executed via draftLegal — signature request <id>". The local certificate is self-signed, so Acrobat reports the signer's identity as unknown or untrusted; it also reports that the document has not been modified since the signature was applied (verify Acrobat's exact wording). |
| 9 | `pdfsig sealed.pdf` | "Signature Type: adbe.pkcs7.detached", a SHA-256 hash, "Total document signed" and "Signature is Valid", with a warning that the certificate isn't trusted (verify the exact lines). |
| 10 | Tamper with a copy: `cp sealed.pdf tampered.pdf; printf 'X' \| dd of=tampered.pdf bs=1 seek=2000 conv=notrunc; pdfsig tampered.pdf; shasum -a 256 tampered.pdf` (and open it in Acrobat). | The signature no longer validates (pdfsig reports it invalid; Acrobat says the document was altered or corrupted after signing). The hash differs from the stored one. |
| 11 | S9's Document view. | It shows the sealed PDF (the current version), certificate page last. |

**Also check**
- The seal runs once per request: its job id is `seal-<request id>`, and a re-run finds the sealed version and logs
  "[signing-worker] seal already present sr=… version=…" without adding a version (verify by re-running the job from
  Bull Board's **signing** queue, if it offers that for a completed job).
- A text contract (such as S1 from E2E-SIGN-02) is sealed from its text: Gotenberg renders it to PDF, then the
  certificate page is added. With Gotenberg stopped (`docker stop clm_gotenberg`), the seal fails and retries 5 times
  over about 8 minutes ("[signing-worker] seal FAILED sr=… attempt=…"); start it again within that time and the seal
  succeeds. After the last retry the contract stays Executed with no sealed version; retry the failed job in Bull Board.
- Anyone who can open the contract can download the sealed PDF (`view:contract`; rep-a only on contracts rep-a owns).
- Outside development the certificate comes from `SIGNING_CERT_P12_BASE64` and `SIGNING_CERT_PASSPHRASE`. In
  development the API creates `.dev-signing-cert.p12` once (log "[signing-cert] generated a self-signed dev signing cert …").
- Eight or more signers: send an "any order" request to eight addresses and have all sign. The eighth signer's card is
  drawn over the top of the certificate page, and an empty page is added (reported).
- A version made while the request is out (for example an **Edit** save during signing) makes the seal fail on a
  duplicate version number (reported; verify: send, edit, sign, then read the signing-worker log).

**Known limits**
- The seal shows the file hasn't changed since sealing. The signers themselves are identified by their email link,
  typed name, IP and browser, not by a certificate of their own.
- Acrobat doesn't trust the development certificate.

### E2E-SIGN-10 · A contract uploaded as Word is sealed as a PDF rendered from its text (DD8)

**Covers:** /sign/:token · `POST /contracts/:id/send-for-signature`, `POST /sign/:token/sign` · — · signing.worker · TC-DOC-02
**Roles:** counsel-a, external signers · **Needs:** Gotenberg, Mailpit · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Upload D-NDA.docx as counsel-a:
  `S10=$(curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@$HOME/qa-docs/D-NDA.docx;type=application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" -F "title=QA SIGN-10 Brightwave NDA" -F "type=NDA" | jq -r .id)`.
  Wait until its text is read.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | counsel-a opens S10 and switches to the Original view. | "The original file isn't a PDF, so it can't be shown here. Download it from Actions." (TC-DOC-02). |
| 2 | **Send for Signature** → **In sequence**: Signer One (1), Signer Two (2) → **Send for signature**. Signer One signs; when signer 2's email arrives, Signer Two signs. | S10 is **Executed**. |
| 3 | Wait about 30 seconds; read the API log and the **Versions** tab. | "[signing-worker] sealed sr=…"; no "No PDF header found" error (the fault DD8 fixed). "Version 2": "Signed by 2 signers — sealed with PAdES/X.509 (SHA-256 …)". |
| 4 | **Actions** → **Download**. | A PDF: the NDA's text rendered as headings and numbered paragraphs (not Word's own layout), then the certificate page with "Signers (2)" and cards marked "Order #1" and "Order #2". |
| 5 | Check the seal as in E2E-SIGN-09 steps 7 to 10. | The same results. |
| 6 | `curl -s $API/contracts/$S10 -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '[.versions[] \| {versionNumber, mimeType, rendered: (.renderedPdfKey != null), s3Key}]'` | Version 2: application/pdf, s3Key `signed/<contract id>/<request id>.pdf`. Version 1 (the Word file) now also has a rendered PDF, so downloading version 1 gives that PDF; `…/download?versionId=<v1>&artifact=source` gives the .docx. |

**Also check**

### E2E-NOTIF-01 · Approval, escalation and signing emails reach Mailpit, as each person's email settings say

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval`, `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide`, `POST /contracts/:id/send-for-signature` · — · notification.worker · —
**Roles:** contracts-a, approver-a, viewer-a, admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Clear Mailpit's inbox (its **Delete all** button) so each email below is easy to spot.
- approver-a and viewer-a have the default settings: **Real-time**, and the first two toggles on.

Every email this section sends (earlier journeys produced most of them; this table is the checklist):

| Trigger | To | Subject | Body | Stopped by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A step is assigned (first step) | the approver | Contract awaiting your approval | `"<title>" has been submitted for approval (<step>).` | "Approval requested from me" off, or **Off** |
| The next step is assigned | the next approver | Contract awaiting your approval | `"<title>" requires your approval (<step>).` | the same |
| A step is delegated | the new approver | Contract approval delegated to you | `"<title>" approval has been delegated to you (<step>).` | **Off** only |
| Overdue, escalated to a named user | that user | Contract escalated to you for approval | `"<title>" approval was not acted upon and has been escalated to you.` | **Off** only |
| Overdue, no escalation target | the approver | Approval overdue — action required | `"<title>" is waiting on your approval and is overdue. Please review and decide.` | **Off** only |
| Overdue, no escalation target | each other active admin | Approval overdue — no escalation target | `"<title>" has waited past its deadline on step "<step>" (<approver>), …` | **Off** only |
| Sent for signature, or a sequential signer's turn | the signer | [Demo Org, Inc.] Signature requested: <title> | HTML and text, **Review & sign →** | nothing (not a notification) |
| Reminder (by hand, or 3 days before expiry) | the pending signers of the current group | the same | "Friendly reminder: a signature is still needed on this document." | nothing |
| Final reminder (1 day before expiry) | the same | the same | "⚠ Final reminder — this signature link expires soon." | nothing |
| Daily digest | the person | Your DraftLegal digest: N update(s) | E2E-NOTIF-03 | **Real-time** or **Off** |

Never emailed: an approval approved, rejected or auto-approved (bell only), and a signature signed, declined, voided or
completed (no notification at all).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `N1=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA NOTIF-01 one" NDA 20000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $N1` (QA NDAs, approver-a). | Mailpit: approver@qa.test, "Contract awaiting your approval". The same in approver-a's bell. |
| 2 | approver-a approves N1 from the card. | contracts@demo.com gets no email; contracts-a's bell has "Contract approved". |
| 3 | approver-a → **Settings** → **Notifications**. | Title "Notifications", "Pick what reaches you and how often." A section "Email me when…" ("All toggles persist immediately") with four toggles: "Approval requested from me" ("Get notified when a contract enters your approval queue."), "My approval request gets a decision" ("Know the moment one of your contracts is approved or rejected."), "Someone else changes a contract I own" ("Edits, new versions and status changes by colleagues. At most one an hour per contract."), "A contract I own is coming due" ("Weekly from 90 days before it expires, and before an auto-renewal notice deadline; obligations a week before they are due."). Defaults: on, on, off, on. Then "Delivery cadence": **Real-time** ("As things happen", selected), **Daily digest** ("One email at 9am, <timezone>"), **Off** ("Pause email"). |
| 4 | Untick "Approval requested from me". | A badge "Saving…", then "Saved". |
| 5 | `N2=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA NOTIF-01 two" NDA 20000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $N2` | No email to approver@qa.test; the bell has it. API log: "[notify] suppressed by preference for userId=<id> type=APPROVAL_REQUEST (approvalRequested is off)". |
| 6 | Delegation ignores that toggle: `N3=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA NOTIF-01 three" OTHER 5000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $N3 $W_QUICK; decide "$ADMIN_A" $INST $STEP DELEGATED "" $APPROVER_A_ID` | 200. An email "Contract approval delegated to you" reaches approver@qa.test. |
| 7 | approver-a: **Delivery cadence** → **Off**. Repeat step 6 with a new contract. | No email; the bell has it. API log: "… (digest is off)". |
| 8 | approver-a: back to **Real-time**, and tick "Approval requested from me". | "Saved". |
| 9 | Signing emails ignore these settings: viewer-a → **Off**; `N4=$(mk "$COUNSEL_A" "QA NOTIF-01 sign" MSA 40000); sfs "$COUNSEL_A" $N4 '[{"name":"Viewer A","email":"viewer@qa.test"}]'` | The signing email reaches viewer@qa.test anyway. Set viewer-a back to **Real-time**. |
| 10 | Decisions: with contracts-a's "My approval request gets a decision" on, have one of contracts-a's submissions approved and another rejected. | contracts@demo.com gets nothing; only the bell. The toggle has no effect (reported). |

**Also check**
- Without a mail server (remove `SMTP_HOST` from `.env`, restart the API): no emails; the bell still fills; the log says
  "[notify] no email provider configured — notification written to DB for userId=… type=…"; in development each
  signing link is printed on the API console ("[signing] ✉ …"). Put `SMTP_HOST` back afterwards.
- Notification emails are plain text; signing emails have an HTML and a text part. All come from qa@draftlegal.local.
- The last two toggles belong to §1 (contract changes) and §6 (due dates).

**Known limits**
- Notification emails have no link to the app.
- A failed email doesn't stop the bell notification; the API log says why the email didn't go.

### E2E-NOTIF-02 · The bell shows each notification, opens what it is about, and marks it read

**Covers:** /approvals · `GET /approvals/notifications`, `POST /approvals/notifications/mark-read` · — · notification.worker · TC-KEY-10
**Roles:** counsel-a, contracts-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- counsel-a has several unread notifications (earlier journeys). If not:
  `for n in 1 2; do submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA bell $n" SOW 5000)" > /dev/null; done`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | counsel-a: the bell at the top right of the header (its label is "Notifications"). | A small count on the bell ("9+" above nine). |
| 2 | Click it. | A panel "Notifications" with **Mark all read** and a ×. The 10 newest. Each row: an icon by type (a clock for an approval request, a tick for a decision, a warning for an escalation, an arrow for a delegation, a calendar for an obligation due, a repeat sign for a renewal, a file for a counterparty's new version, a bell otherwise), the title (bold while unread), the text on one line, "just now", "5m ago", "3h ago" or "2d ago", and a dot while unread. |
| 3 | Click an approval request row. | The panel closes, the app opens **Approvals**, and that row is now read (the count drops by one). |
| 4 | Click a "<title> was updated" row (from E2E-APPR-12, on counsel-a's contract). | The contract's page opens. |
| 5 | **Mark all read**. | The count disappears; the dots go; the **Mark all read** button is gone. |
| 6 | Leave the page open. From another user, send counsel-a a new approval. Wait up to 30 seconds. | The count comes back without a reload (the bell checks every 30 seconds). |
| 7 | `curl -s "$API/approvals/notifications?limit=2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{unreadCount, n: (.data \| length), nextCursor}'`; then again with `&cursor=<nextCursor>`. | Two items and a `nextCursor`; the second call returns the next two, older ones. |
| 8 | With at least two unread: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/approvals/notifications/mark-read -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"ids":["<one unread id>"]}'` | 204; counsel-a's `unreadCount` drops by one. |
| 9 | contracts-a sends the same call with another of counsel-a's unread ids and `$CONTRACTS_A`. | 204, but counsel-a's notification stays unread: the call only touches the caller's own. |
| 10 | counsel-a: the same call with `-d '{}'`. | 204; `unreadCount` is 0. |
| 11 | admin-b's bell. | None of Org A's notifications. |

**Also check**
- An API key → 403 `"detail":"This endpoint is for signed-in users, not API keys"` (TC-KEY-10).
- A user with no notifications sees the bell icon and "No notifications".
- Escalation and delegation rows open **Approvals**; counterparty-version and contract-updated rows open the contract.

**Known limits**
- The panel lists the 10 newest; older ones are reachable only through the API's cursor.
- Signature events create no notifications.

### E2E-NOTIF-03 · With the daily digest, approval emails wait and arrive together at 9am local time

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval` · — · notification.worker (holds the emails; scan.worker sends the digest) · —
**Roles:** approver-a, admin-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- To avoid waiting up to 15 minutes per run, add `DIGEST_PATTERN="* * * * *"` to `.env` and restart `pnpm dev`: the
  digest run then happens every minute. Remove it at the end.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | approver-a → **Settings** → **General** → **Timezone**: pick a zone where it is now between 09:00 and 23:59 (the list: UTC, America/Los Angeles, …, Asia/Tokyo, Australia/Sydney). | Saved on change. The hint: "Used for date display, currency formatting and digest delivery time." |
| 2 | **Settings** → **Notifications** → **Delivery cadence** → **Daily digest**. | "One email at 9am, <that zone>". The text above: "How often we should batch and send the notifications you've chosen. With the daily digest, escalations and approvals delegated to you still arrive right away." |
| 3 | Two approval requests to approver-a: `for n in 1 2; do submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA digest $n" NDA 20000)" > /dev/null; done` | The bell shows both at once. Mailpit: nothing yet. |
| 4 | Wait for the next run (a minute with the pattern above; otherwise up to 15). | One email to approver@qa.test: "Your DraftLegal digest: 2 updates". Body: "Hello <name>,", "Here is what happened in DraftLegal since your last digest:", two bullets "• Contract awaiting your approval", each followed by its text, "Open DraftLegal: http://localhost:5173", and "You get this once a day because Settings › Notifications is set to "Daily digest"." API log: "[scan-worker] notification-digest · …ms · users=1 sent=1 notifications=2 waiting=0 errors=0". |
| 5 | A third request to approver-a the same day. | Held: no email at the next runs; the log shows `waiting=1`. |
| 6 | admin-a delegates a W_QUICK step to approver-a (as in E2E-NOTIF-01 step 6). | Emailed at once, not held. |
| 7 | Let today's digest go again: `docker exec clm_redis redis-cli DEL "notification-digest:$APPROVER_A_ID:$(TZ=<that zone> date +%F)"` | At the next run: "Your DraftLegal digest: 1 update" with the third request. |
| 8 | Switch **Timezone** to a zone where it is before 09:00, and send another request. | No email at the next runs (`waiting=1`). |
| 9 | Switch to **Off** while that one is held. | At the next run it is dropped: no email (`sent=0`). |
| 10 | Restore **Real-time** and the timezone; remove `DIGEST_PATTERN` and restart. | Emails go out as they happen again. |

**Also check**
- Choosing **Daily digest** with no saved timezone saves the browser's timezone.
- Notifications about a contract (for example "<title> was updated") carry a link line
  (`http://localhost:5173/contracts/<id>`) in the digest; approval ones don't.
- A digest lists at most 50; the rest are counted: "…and N more in DraftLegal."

**Known limits**
- One digest per local day. Anything after it waits for the next day.
- Without a mail server nothing is held for the digest.

### E2E-NOTIF-04 · Slack requests are checked by their signature, `/contract` search answers, and approval buttons fall back safely (no Slack workspace needed)

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /slack/commands`, `POST /slack/interactions` · — · — · TC-SEC-08, TC-SEC-09
**Roles:** admin-a, contracts-a · **Needs:** Node 18+; `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` for steps 8–9 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- If Org A has Slack connected, note its settings and disconnect it (Admin → **Integrations** → **Slack** →
  **Disconnect**). Then connect a made-up workspace in "2 · Connect it here": **Team ID** `TQA5TEAM`, **Signing secret**
  `qa-slack-secret`, **Bot token** empty → **Connect Slack**. The tab then reads "Slack workspace connected",
  "Workspace (team ID) TQA5TEAM", "Signing secret configured", "Bot token (button-click identity) not set — buttons fall
  back to web links", "Workspace ownership unverified — reconnect with the bot token so no other org can claim this
  workspace".
- A pending approval: `$C1` on counsel-a (E2E-APPR-01): `qstep "$COUNSEL_A" "$C1"`.
- These helpers sign a request the way Slack does:

```bash
export API SLACK_SECRET=qa-slack-secret
# slack <commands|interactions> '<JSON object of string fields>' → posts it urlencoded, with Slack's v0 signature
slack() {
  node -e '
const c = require("crypto");
const body = new URLSearchParams(JSON.parse(process.argv[2])).toString();
const ts = String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + Number(process.env.SLACK_SKEW || 0));
const sig = "v0=" + c.createHmac("sha256", process.env.SLACK_SECRET).update("v0:" + ts + ":" + body).digest("hex");
fetch(process.env.API + "/slack/" + process.argv[1], { method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "x-slack-request-timestamp": ts, "x-slack-signature": sig }, body })
  .then(async r => console.log(r.status, await r.text()));' "$1" "$2"
}
# click <approval_approve|approval_reject> <instanceId> <stepId> → a press of the card's button
click() {
  slack interactions "$(jq -nc --arg p "$(jq -nc --arg a "$1" --arg i "$2" --arg s "$3" \
    '{type:"block_actions", team:{id:"TQA5TEAM"}, user:{id:"UQA0001"}, actions:[{action_id:$a, value:({instanceId:$i, stepId:$s} | tojson)}]}')" '{payload:$p}')"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `slack commands '{"team_id":"TQA5TEAM","user_id":"UQA0001","command":"/contract","text":"search Acme"}'` | 200. An ephemeral reply: `text` `<n> contract(s) matching “Acme”` and a block `🔍 *<n> contracts* matching *Acme*` (singular for one), then one line per contract, e.g. `• <http://localhost:5173/contracts/<id>\|Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement> — MSA · EXECUTED · Acme Corporation · USD 250,000`. At most 5 lines; with more: "…and N more — open the full list". |
| 2 | The same with `"text":"Acme"`; with `"text":""`; with `"text":"search zzqq"`. | "Acme" alone searches too. Empty: the help, `Usage: /contract search <query>`, with `*draftLegal commands*` and the two forms. No match: `No contracts matching “zzqq”.` and `🔍 No contracts matching *zzqq*. Try a counterparty name or contract title.` |
| 3 | `audit AGENT_ACTION` | An event with resourceType "integration", resourceId "slack", metadata `{"command":"/contract","query":"Acme","results":<n>,"slackUser":"UQA0001"}`. |
| 4 | Refusals: `SLACK_SECRET=wrong slack commands '{"team_id":"TQA5TEAM","text":"x"}'`; `slack commands '{"team_id":"TNOPE","text":"x"}'`; `SLACK_SKEW=-600 slack commands '{"team_id":"TQA5TEAM","text":"x"}'` (a 10-minute-old timestamp); `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/slack/commands -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"TQA5TEAM","text":"search x"}'` | Each: 401 `{"detail":"invalid Slack signature or unconnected workspace"}`. |
| 5 | Approve from "Slack" with no bot token: `click approval_approve $INST $STEP` | 200 `{"response_type":"ephemeral","replace_original":false,"text":"🔐 Deciding from Slack needs the bot token connected (Admin → Integrations → Slack). <http://localhost:5173/contracts/<C1>?tab=approval\|Decide in draftLegal> instead."}`. `inst $INST` → still PENDING. |
| 6 | A button with no reference: `slack interactions "$(jq -nc --arg p '{"type":"block_actions","team":{"id":"TQA5TEAM"},"user":{"id":"U1"},"actions":[{"action_id":"approval_approve","value":"{}"}]}' '{payload:$p}')"` | 200, ephemeral "⚠️ This approval button is missing its reference — decide in draftLegal instead." |
| 7 | Other interactions: action_id `approval_open`, or `"type":"view_submission"`; then `slack interactions '{"payload":"not-json"}'` | The first two: 200 `{"ok":true}` (ignored). The last: 400 `{"detail":"invalid payload"}`. |
| 8 | See the approval card without Slack. Set `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` in `.env`, restart the API, and run the receiver below in a spare terminal. Admin → **Integrations** → **Webhooks** → **New webhook**: **Name** "QA slack card", **URL** `http://127.0.0.1:8766/slack`, **Format** "Slack blocks" ("Pretty rendering for Slack-compatible receivers"), **Events** approval.submitted and approval.decided → **Create webhook**. Then `submit "$CONTRACTS_A" "$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA slack card" SOW 20000)"`. | The receiver prints `approval.submitted` and a Slack message: `"text":"📝 Approval requested: QA slack card"`, a header block "📝 Approval requested", a section `*<link\|QA slack card>*\nSOW · USD 20K · step: Legal review`, and an actions block with three buttons: "✅ Approve" (`action_id` approval_approve, style primary), "❌ Reject" (approval_reject, style danger) and "Open in draftLegal" (a URL ending `?tab=approval`). The Approve and Reject buttons' `value` is `{"instanceId":"…","stepId":"…"}`; those ids work with `click`. |
| 9 | Approve it in the app (counsel-a's **My Queue**). | The receiver prints `approval.decided` with `✅ *Approval approved* on <link\|<contract id>>`. |

The receiver for step 8 (also used by E2E-NOTIF-06):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('content-length', 0))).decode()
        print(self.headers.get('x-clm-event'), body, flush=True)
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers()
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 8766), H).serve_forever()
PY
```

**Also check**
- Two orgs claiming the same team id each get their own results (TC-SEC-08). A body over 256 KB → 413 (TC-SEC-09).
- The Slack tab is for admins only (§8).
- Clean up: **Disconnect** → "Disconnect Slack?" → **Disconnect Slack**; delete the webhook; remove
  `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS` and restart; restore any earlier Slack settings.

**Known limits**
- Without a bot token, the buttons can't decide: they send the clicker a link instead.

### E2E-NOTIF-05 · With a real Slack app, an approval request posts a card whose Approve and Reject buttons decide the step

**Covers:** /approvals · `POST /slack/interactions`, `POST /slack/commands` · — · — · TC-SEC-09
**Roles:** admin-a, contracts-a, slack-a (below) · **Needs:** a Slack workspace where you can install apps; a tunnel (`ngrok` or `cloudflared`) · **Time:** ~45 min

**Preconditions**
- A tunnel to the API: `ngrok http 3001`. Note its https address as `$TUNNEL`.
- An Org A user whose email is your Slack profile's email: Admin → **Users** → **Invite User** with that address and the
  Approver role, then accept the invite (§1). Call this user slack-a.
- A workflow "QA Slack" (**Manage Workflows** → **New Workflow**): one step "Slack approval", **Specific approver**
  slack-a.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Admin → **Integrations** → **Slack** → "1 · Create the Slack app": copy the manifest with its copy icon. | A JSON manifest with the `/contract` command, the interactivity URL and the scopes commands, incoming-webhook, users:read, users:read.email. A yellow note: "Slack must be able to reach these URLs — in local dev use a tunnel (ngrok / cloudflared) and adjust the manifest." |
| 2 | In the manifest, replace both `http://localhost:5173/api/v1/slack/…` URLs with `$TUNNEL/api/v1/slack/commands` and `$TUNNEL/api/v1/slack/interactions`. On api.slack.com/apps: **Create New App** → **From a manifest** → your workspace → paste → create → install it to the workspace, choosing a channel for its incoming webhook. | The app is installed. Note the **Signing Secret** (Basic Information), the **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-…`), the channel's webhook URL (`https://hooks.slack.com/…`) and the workspace's Team ID (starts with T). |
| 3 | "2 · Connect it here": **Team ID**, **Signing secret**, **Bot token** → **Connect Slack**. | "Slack workspace connected"; Bot token "configured"; Workspace ownership "verified by the bot token"; "Connected" with the time. |
| 4 | **Webhooks** → **New webhook**: Name "QA Slack channel", URL the hooks.slack.com address (the dialog says "Slack URL detected — events will be formatted as Slack messages."), Events approval.submitted, approval.decided, signature.sent, signature.completed, signature.voided, contract.executed → **Create webhook**. | Listed. |
| 5 | contracts-a submits a contract with "QA Slack". | In the channel: "📝 Approval requested", the title as a link, "<TYPE> · USD 8K · step: Slack approval" (the value varies), and buttons **✅ Approve**, **❌ Reject**, **Open in draftLegal**. |
| 6 | As slack-a in Slack, click **✅ Approve**. | The message is replaced by `✅ *Approved* by <slack-a's email> via Slack · view in draftLegal` (bold "Approved" in Slack). In the app: the contract is **Approved**; `inst` → the step APPROVED with no comment; `audit APPROVAL_DECIDED` → metadata `{"decision":"APPROVED","instanceId":"…","via":"slack"}`. The channel gets no "Approval approved" message: a Slack decision fires no `approval.decided` webhook (reported). |
| 7 | Another submission → **❌ Reject**. | `❌ *Rejected* by … via Slack`. The contract is **Draft**; the step's comment reads "Rejected via Slack by <email>". |
| 8 | A third submission; a Slack user who isn't slack-a clicks **✅ Approve**. | Only they see "⚠️ This approval step is not assigned to you (or was already decided)." (with no matching app user: "⚠️ Couldn't match your Slack account to a draftLegal user. Decide in draftLegal instead."). |
| 9 | A fourth: decide it in the app, then click its Slack button. | "⚠️ This approval step is not assigned to you (or was already decided)." The card doesn't update when the step is decided elsewhere. |
| 10 | Type `/contract search <a title word>` in a channel with the app. | An ephemeral list, as in E2E-NOTIF-04. |
| 11 | **Open in draftLegal** on a card. | The contract opens, on its Document view (the `?tab=approval` in the link is ignored). |
| 12 | Slack tab → **Disconnect** → "Disconnect Slack?" ("/contract stops responding in every channel, and Approve / Reject buttons in already-posted approval messages stop working — approvers will have to come back into draftLegal. …") → **Disconnect Slack**. Click a remaining button in Slack. | The tab shows the setup steps again. Slack shows an error for the click (the API answers 401). |

**Also check**
- A bot token from another workspace → 400 "That bot token belongs to Slack workspace <T…>, not <T…>." (TC-SEC-09).
- In the connected view, the underlined "Slack webhook" in "Approval requests post Approve / Reject buttons via your
  Slack webhook …" does nothing when clicked (reported).

**Known limits**
- One card per submission, for the first step's first approver only: parallel co-approvers and later steps get no card.
- A Slack decision is matched to a person by their Slack profile email; it needs the bot token.
