### E2E-NOTIF-06 · Teams channels (and any webhook) get approval and signing events as Adaptive Cards

**Covers:** /approvals, /sign/:token · `POST /contracts/:id/submit-approval`, `POST /approvals/:instanceId/decide`, `POST /contracts/:id/send-for-signature`, `POST /contracts/:id/signature-requests/:srId/void` · — · — · TC-WEB-04
**Roles:** admin-a, contracts-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** a Teams Workflows webhook URL, or `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` and the receiver from E2E-NOTIF-04 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Either a Teams channel with a Workflows webhook (the "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" template),
  or the local receiver running on port 8766 with `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` set and the API restarted.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Admin → **Integrations** → **Webhooks** → **New webhook**: Name "QA Teams"; URL the Teams address (one on `.logic.azure.com`, `.webhook.office.com` or `.powerplatform.com` is detected: "Teams workflow URL detected — events will be formatted as Adaptive Cards."), or `http://127.0.0.1:8766/teams` with **Format** "Teams card" ("Adaptive Cards for Teams Workflows webhooks"); Events approval.submitted, approval.decided, signature.sent, signature.completed, signature.voided, contract.executed → **Create webhook**. | Listed. |
| 2 | `T6=$(mk "$CONTRACTS_A" "QA teams card" SOW 20000); submit "$CONTRACTS_A" $T6` | A card "📝 Approval requested", "**QA teams card**", facts Type "SOW", Value "USD 20K", Step "Legal review", and a button **Review & decide** (to the contract). The receiver shows `{"type":"message","attachments":[{"contentType":"application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive","content":{"type":"AdaptiveCard","version":"1.4",…}}]}`. |
| 3 | counsel-a approves it. | "✅ Approval approved", fact Contract <id>, button **Open in draftLegal**. |
| 4 | counsel-a sends it for signature to signer1@example.test and signer2@example.test. | "✍️ Signature request sent" with fact Contract <id>. There is no Signers fact (reported: the card reads a field the event doesn't carry). |
| 5 | Both sign. | "✍️ All signatures collected" / "The contract is fully signed.", and "✅ Contract executed" with Contract and Executed facts. |
| 6 | Send another request on a new contract and **Void** it. | "🚫 Signature request voided" with Contract and Reason "Voided by sender" (after a decline: "<name> declined: <reason>"). |
| 7 | Admin → **Integrations** → **Webhooks** → click the webhook's row. | "Recent deliveries" lists each event with a green dot (status 200). |

**Also check**
- A **Generic JSON** webhook receives `{"event":"approval.submitted","timestamp":…,"data":{contractId, title, type, value, currency, instanceId, stepId, stepName, approverId}}`,
  and `approval.decided` with `data` `{instanceId, contractId, stepId, decision, instanceStatus, decidedBy}` (plus
  `"via":"agent"` when the assistant decided). The signing events and `contract.executed` likewise (TC-WEB-04; the
  webhook machinery itself is in §8).
- No `approval.submitted` for auto-approvals or approvals sent by the assistant; no `approval.decided` for Slack
  decisions (reported).
- Webhooks, like the Slack tab, are managed by admins only (`configure:organization`); other roles opening
  `$WEB/admin/integrations` see "Admin access required" (§8).

**Known limits**
- Teams cards can't approve or reject; they link to the app.
## 6. After signature: obligations, renewals, invoices, diligence, analytics and compliance

This section tests what Draft Legal does once a contract is signed. It covers the obligations the product extracts from a contract, lets people complete with evidence and reminds the owner about; the renewal calendar with its auto-renewal notice deadlines, advice and decisions; invoices matched to payment obligations, reconciled and disputed; diligence rooms that hold a target company's contracts apart from your own; the Analytics page and every CSV export in the product; and the regulatory compliance check with its PDF compliance package. It also covers the two daily scans in `scan.worker`, the admin routes that run them by hand, the three agent services behind these features (`obligations`, `renewals`, `compliance`) and the four assistant tools that read this data. Run 6.0 first: it defines the shell helpers and builds the fixtures. Then run the journeys in the order written. Within an area they build on each other (for example E2E-OBL-05 needs the obligations extracted in E2E-OBL-01), and the Preconditions name what each one needs from earlier. Journeys that call an AI model say so under **Needs**. Model output varies, so for those steps the expected result names what must be there, and marks wording or counts that may differ with "verify:".

### 6.0 Before you start

**Accounts and tokens.** Use the §0.5 variables: the tokens (`$ADMIN_A`, `$COUNSEL_A`, `$CONTRACTS_A`, `$REP_A`, `$FINANCE_A`, `$APPROVER_A`, `$VIEWER_A`, `$ADMIN_B`; re-run their `login` lines when calls start returning 401), `$ORG_A`, `$ORG_B`, `$ADMIN_A_ID`, `$COUNSEL_A_ID`, `$REP_A_ID` and `$INTERNAL_SECRET`. The web app is `$WEB`, Mailpit is http://localhost:8025 (§0.2). The agents service must be running with a model key for every journey marked **Needs: agents service**.

**Helpers.** Paste these into the shell you test from, at the start of this section. They replace any helper of the same name from an earlier section (`upload`, `qverify`, `sql`, `tj` and others there take different arguments).

```bash
# Dates relative to today, as YYYY-MM-DD: day +3, day -10 (macOS or GNU date)
day() { date -v"$1"d +%F 2>/dev/null || date -d "$1 days" +%F; }

# admin-b's user id (§0.5 sets the Org A ids); GET /users/me signs nobody in
export ADMIN_B_ID=$(curl -s "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" | jq -r .id)

# The agents service, and the API's internal tool routes the agents service calls (dev stack only)
export AGENTS=http://localhost:8002 INT=${API%/v1}/internal/ai
tj() { curl -s -X POST "$INT/tools/$1" -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H "x-internal-service: agents" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2"; }

# SQL against the dev database (the docker compose Postgres container)
sql() { docker exec -i clm_postgres psql -U clm -d clm_dev -At -c "$1"; }

# Upload a file as a new contract; prints its id.  upload <file> <mime type> <title> <counterparty> [token]
upload() { curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${5:-$COUNSEL_A}" \
  -F "file=@$1;type=$2" -F "title=$3" -F "counterpartyName=$4" | jq -r .id; }

# Wait until a contract's analysis ends; prints DONE or FAILED (polls every 10 s, up to 10 min)
waitdone() { for i in $(seq 1 60); do s=$(curl -s "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r .analysisStatus)
  case $s in DONE|FAILED) echo "$s"; return;; esac; sleep 10; done; echo "still $s"; }

# Import contracts from a CSV (no document, no analysis); exports <PREFIX>_<csv row> = id.  bulk <csv> <PREFIX> [token]
bulk() { eval "$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/bulk-import" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${3:-$COUNSEL_A}" \
  -F "file=@$1;type=text/csv" | jq -r --arg p "$2" \
  '.results[] | if .ok then "export \($p)_\(.row)=\(.id); echo \($p)_\(.row) \(.title)" else "echo row \(.row): \(.error)" end')"; }

# Correct a key term the way a reviewer does in the Extraction Queue.  qverify <contract id> '<json>' [token]
qverify() { curl -s -X POST "$API/review-queue/$1/verify" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${3:-$COUNSEL_A}" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2" | jq -c '{ok, field, detail}'; }

# A linked contract (amendment, exhibit_only, renewal, sow, order_form) expiring with its parent.  amend <parent> <type> <title>
amend() { curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$1/amendments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"relationshipType\":\"$2\",\"title\":\"$3\",\"expiryDate\":\"$(day +75)\"}" | jq -r .id; }

# A one-step approval workflow decided by counsel-a, and a helper that takes a DRAFT contract to EXECUTED
export W6=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/approvals/workflows" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"name\":\"QA W6\",\"steps\":[{\"order\":1,\"name\":\"Counsel sign-off\",\"approverId\":\"$COUNSEL_A_ID\",\"executionMode\":\"sequential\",\"requiredApprovals\":1,\"dueSoonHours\":48}]}" | jq -r .id)
execute() {
  set -- "$1" $(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$1/submit-approval" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"workflowDefinitionId\":\"$W6\"}" | jq -r '"\(.instanceId) \(.steps[0].id)"')
  curl -s -X POST "$API/approvals/$2/decide" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"stepId\":\"$3\",\"decision\":\"APPROVED\",\"comment\":\"QA\"}" > /dev/null
  curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"status":"EXECUTED"}' | jq -r .status
}
```

`execute <id>` prints `EXECUTED`. The same in the web app: on the contract page click **Send for Review**, pick workflow **QA W6**, click **Send**; as counsel-a open Sidebar → **Approvals** → **My Queue**, click **Approve** on the contract's card, then **Confirm Approval**; back on the contract page click **Mark as Executed**. Marking a contract executed this way does not extract its obligations (only a completed e-signature does); the journeys extract them by hand.

**Fixture files.** Make them in the folder you test from (the §0.7 documents' folder is simplest), on the day you test: the dates are relative to today. `F6-SUPPLY.txt` has dated obligations, an auto-renewal and a 90-day notice period:

```bash
cat > F6-SUPPLY.txt <<TXT
MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Master Supply Agreement is made on $(day -60) between QA Northwind Buyer Inc. ("Customer") and QA Harbor Components Ltd ("Supplier").

1. Term and renewal. This Agreement begins on $(day -60) and ends on $(day +110). It then renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term.
2. Onboarding fee. Customer shall pay Supplier an onboarding fee of USD 12,000 on or before $(day -3).
3. Security report. Supplier shall deliver a security audit report to Customer on or before $(day +3).
4. Insurance. Supplier shall deliver a renewed certificate of insurance to Customer on or before $(day +20).
5. Service levels. Supplier shall maintain 99.9% monthly availability and send Customer an availability report within ten (10) days after the end of each month.
6. Audit. Customer may audit Supplier's records once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
7. Limitation of liability. Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid in the twelve (12) months before the claim.
8. Governing law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
TXT
```

`F6-MANY.txt` has 30 separate dated obligations, `F6-LONG.txt` has one obligation at the start and one after 16,000 characters:

```bash
{ echo 'SERVICES SCHEDULE between QA Many Buyer Inc. ("Customer") and QA Many Vendor Ltd ("Supplier").'
  for i in $(seq -w 1 30); do echo "$i. The Supplier shall deliver deliverable QA-D$i to the Customer on or before $(day +$((200 + 10#$i)))."; done; } > F6-MANY.txt
{ echo "1. Fees. The Customer shall pay the QA-HEAD set-up fee of USD 100 on or before $(day +40)."
  for i in $(seq 1 300); do echo "Recital $i. This paragraph is background only and creates no obligation for either party."; done
  echo "99. Escrow. The Supplier shall deliver the QA-TAIL escrow statement to the Customer on or before $(day +50)."; } > F6-LONG.txt
grep -bo 'QA-TAIL' F6-LONG.txt   # the offset printed must be above 16000
```

`F6-DPA-WEAK.txt` is a data processing addendum with deliberate gaps (the strong one is in the repository, `apps/api/scripts/fixtures/ai-demo/dpa-tyrell.txt`):

```bash
cat > F6-DPA-WEAK.txt <<'TXT'
DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM

This Data Processing Addendum supplements the Services Agreement between QA Weak Processor Ltd ("Processor") and QA Controller GmbH ("Controller"), a company established in Germany.

1. Scope. Processor processes the personal data of Controller's employees and customers in the European Union (names, contact details, order history) solely to provide the hosted order-management service, for the term of the Services Agreement.
2. Instructions. Processor processes personal data only on Controller's documented instructions.
3. Confidentiality. Processor personnel with access to personal data are bound by written confidentiality obligations.
4. Security. Processor maintains encryption in transit and at rest, access controls and audit logging.
5. Sub-processors. Processor may engage any sub-processor at its discretion, without notice to Controller.
6. Breaches. Processor will notify Controller of a personal data breach.
7. Transfers. Transfers of personal data outside the EEA are made under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2021/914).
8. Governing law. This Addendum is governed by the laws of Germany.
TXT
```

For the diligence journeys, work in the folder that holds the §0.7 documents (for example `~/qa-docs`), copy them under distinctive names, and make two files the server must refuse:

```bash
cp D-MSA.pdf QA-DIL-Target-MSA.pdf; cp D-NDA.docx QA-DIL-Target-NDA.docx; cp D-SCAN.pdf QA-DIL-Target-Scan.pdf
cp D-FAKE.pdf fake.pdf            # a text file named .pdf (§0.7)
echo 'Legacy Word file' > legacy.txt && textutil -convert doc -output legacy.doc legacy.txt   # macOS; elsewhere save any file as Word 97-2003 .doc
```

**Who can do what here.** Every page in this section is open to every role; there is no route guard. What changes is what the API accepts. When the web app already knows the user's roles, it refuses a write before sending it and shows "You don't have permission to <action> contracts." where the screen shows errors; the API itself answers 403 with `"detail":"Missing permission: <action>:<resource>"`.

| What | Permission | Allowed | Refused |
|---|---|---|---|
| View every page, list, count, drawer, CSV export, evidence download, compliance report and compliance package | `view:contract` | all roles; rep-a sees only contracts rep-a owns (and rooms rep-a created) | — |
| Extract obligations, complete or reopen an obligation, run a compliance check, get renewal advice, log a renewal decision, add, reconcile, rematch or dispute an invoice, rename or archive a room | `edit:contract` | admin-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, legalops-a, procurement-a | rep-a, finance-a, approver-a, viewer-a |
| Create a diligence room, upload to it | `create:contract` | the five above, and rep-a (own rooms) | finance-a, approver-a, viewer-a |
| Delete a diligence room | `delete:contract` | admin-a, counsel-a, legalops-a | everyone else |
| Run the obligation or renewal scan by hand | `configure:user` | admin-a | everyone else |

**Reading the screens.** Rail section titles, table headers and some chips are set in capitals by the stylesheet; this section spells them as the code does (for example **Obligations**, not OBLIGATIONS). Day counts ("in 5d", "3d overdue") are worked out from local midnight, in the browser on pages and on the API server in alerts, so a count can be one day lower than expected when the API runs west of UTC. Money on pages is rounded to whole units.


### E2E-OBL-01 · Obligations are extracted from an executed contract and listed on its page

**Covers:** `/contracts/:id` (details rail → **Obligations**) · `POST /contracts/:id/extract-obligations` · `GET /contracts/:id/obligations` · agent service `obligations` · docs/38 TC-WEB-05, TC-WF-17
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- 6.0 helpers, `$W6` and `F6-SUPPLY.txt`.
- As counsel-a upload it: Sidebar → **Contracts** → **Upload PDF** → drop `F6-SUPPLY.txt` → **Title** "QA F6 Master Supply Agreement", **Counterparty Name** "QA Harbor Components Ltd" → **Upload contract** → **View Contract**. Or: `export F6=$(upload F6-SUPPLY.txt text/plain "QA F6 Master Supply Agreement" "QA Harbor Components Ltd")`. Note the id from the URL as `$F6`.
- `waitdone $F6` prints `DONE`.
- Fix the renewal terms so later journeys don't depend on the model: `qverify $F6 '{"field":"expiryDate","value":"'$(day +110)'"}'`, `qverify $F6 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'`, `qverify $F6 '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":90}'`, and the counterparty, which the analysis may have set to either party: `qverify $F6 '{"field":"counterpartyName","value":"QA Harbor Components Ltd"}'`. Each prints `{"ok":true,…}`.
- `execute $F6` prints `EXECUTED`. counsel-a owns the contract, so reminders go to legal@demo.com.
- For the refusal checks, a contract with no document: `printf 'title,status\nQA OBL no text,executed\n' > nt.csv; bulk nt.csv NT` (sets `$NT_2`).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$WEB/contracts/$F6`. Find the **Obligations** section in the details rail on the right (in a window narrower than 1280 px, click **Open details rail** first). | The section reads "No obligations extracted yet. Run a pass to pull every payment, SLA, renewal notice, audit right, and report deadline into a structured list the reminder cron can walk." with an **Extract obligations** button. |
| 2 | Click **Extract obligations**. | The button reads "Extracting…" for 5–40 s, then a list replaces the text and the section title shows a count. verify: about 5–8 rows. Each row shows the description, the type in capitals (PAYMENT, REPORT, SLA, AUDIT, …), "· customer" or "· provider", a section such as "§2", and the due reading: the onboarding fee (USD 12,000) "3d overdue" in red, the security report "due in 3d" in amber, the insurance certificate "due in 20d", rows with no date show their trigger in italics. A "high" chip marks open high-severity rows. The footer reads "Extracted <today's date>" and **re-run**. |
| 3 | If there are more than 6 rows, click **Show all N**, then **Show fewer**. | All rows show, then the first 6 again. Rows are ordered by due date, earliest first, undated last. |
| 4 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/$F6/obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{n: (.data\|length), summary, extractedAt, rows: [.data[] \| {type, dueDate: .dueDate[:10], status, owner, recurrence, severity, sectionRef}]}'` | `n` equals the rail's count. `summary` is one sentence (for example "7 obligations extracted covering payment, reporting, SLA and audit"). `extractedAt` is today. Every row has `status` "OPEN"; the fee has `dueDate` = `day -3`, `type` "payment", `owner` "customer"; the report `day +3`; the insurance `day +20`. |
| 5 | Click the onboarding-fee row. | The obligation drawer opens (its fields are checked in E2E-OBL-04). Close it with **Esc**. |
| 6 | `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=OBLIGATION_EXTRACTED&resourceId=$F6" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.events[0] \| {action, metadata, actor: .actor.email}'` | `metadata` `{"count":<n>,"trigger":"manual"}`, actor legal@demo.com. If a webhook subscribes to `obligation.extracted`, it receives `{contractId, count}` (TC-WEB-05 P1). |
| 7 | Click **re-run** in the section footer. | "re-running…", then the list again. Open rows are replaced by fresh ones (their ids change: repeat step 4 and compare), completed rows are kept (checked in E2E-OBL-03 step 9). |

**Also check**
- viewer-a on `$WEB/contracts/$F6` sees the list and **re-run**. On a contract with no obligations yet, **Extract obligations** is shown; clicking it shows "You don't have permission to edit contracts." under the button. API: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$F6/extract-obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A"` → 403, `"detail":"Missing permission: edit:contract"`. The same for rep-a, finance-a and approver-a.
- rep-a (doesn't own `$F6`): `GET $API/contracts/$F6/obligations` → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`. admin-b: the same 404, and `POST …/extract-obligations` → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- A contract that isn't executed: upload any text file as a new contract and open it. The section reads "Obligations are extracted once this contract is executed. Until then, focus on negotiation + risk review." and offers no button. (The API still extracts from a draft: see E2E-OBL-02.)
- An executed NDA (seeded "Globex — NDA"): the section reads "NDAs typically have just confidentiality + survival terms — nothing recurring to extract." with a **Extract anyway →** link. The same pattern for types SETTLEMENT ("Settlements are typically one-time — no ongoing obligations to track.") and AMENDMENT ("Amendments modify their parent contract; obligations live on the parent.").
- A contract with no document: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$NT_2/extract-obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` → 400 `{"detail":"No version to extract from"}`. A version with no text (an image-only upload whose text couldn't be read) → 400 `{"detail":"No plaintext on current version"}`.
- With the agents service stopped, the call answers 500 `"detail":"An unexpected error occurred. Reference the request id when reporting."`, and the rail shows "Request failed with status code 500" (known issues below). When the agents service answers with an error status (for example a wrong `INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET`), the API answers 502 `{"detail":"obligations extractor failed","upstream":"agents service error: …"}`.
- Optional, when the daily AI cost cap is set very low (Admin AI settings): 429 `"detail":"Daily AI cost cap reached ($x of $y). Try again tomorrow or raise the cap in Admin → AI Config."`.
- A room document's obligations are listed on its own contract page, but nowhere org-wide (E2E-DIL-03, TC-WF-17).

**Known limits**
- Obligations are extracted automatically only when an e-signature request completes (the signing flow). **Mark as Executed** does not extract; use **Extract obligations**.
- The model decides the rows, their types and severities; counts vary between runs.
- Known issue: the rail shows the browser's message ("Request failed with status code …") instead of the API's `detail` for server errors, and shows no error at all when **re-run** fails.
- Known issue (destructive, check last): when the model call itself fails, the agents service still answers 200 with `"obligations":[]` and an `error`, and the API has already deleted the contract's open obligations. To see it, make the model call fail (for example save an invalid key for the org's model provider in the admin AI settings) and click **re-run**: the response is 200 with `"ok":false` and an `"error":"extract_failed: …"`, and every open obligation of the contract is gone.

### E2E-OBL-02 · The obligations extractor reads only the first 16,000 characters and returns at most 25 obligations

**Covers:** agent service `obligations` (`POST $AGENTS/extract_obligations`) · `POST /contracts/:id/extract-obligations`
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `F6-MANY.txt` and `F6-LONG.txt` from 6.0. `$AGENTS` and `$INTERNAL_SECRET` set.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Without the secret: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/extract_obligations -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"plainText":"x"}'` | `{"error":"unauthorized"}` and `401`. |
| 2 | Empty text: `curl -s -X POST $AGENTS/extract_obligations -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"plainText":"   "}'` | `{"obligations":[],"summary":"Empty contract text — nothing to extract."}` (no model call). |
| 3 | 30 obligations: `jq -Rs '{plainText: ., contractType: "SOW"}' F6-MANY.txt \| curl -s -X POST $AGENTS/extract_obligations -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- \| jq '{n: (.obligations\|length), longestQuote: ([.obligations[].quote\|length]\|max), summary, model, provider}'` | `n` is at most 25 (verify: 25 when the model lists all 30). No quote is longer than 240 characters. `model` and `provider` name the model that ran. |
| 4 | Text past 16,000 characters: `jq -Rs '{plainText: ., contractType: "MSA"}' F6-LONG.txt \| curl -s -X POST $AGENTS/extract_obligations -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- \| jq '[.obligations[].description]'` | The QA-HEAD set-up fee is listed. Nothing mentions the QA-TAIL escrow statement: only the first 16,000 characters reach the model. |
| 5 | Through the API, which stores the rows: `export MANY=$(upload F6-MANY.txt text/plain "QA F6 Many Deliverables" "QA Many Vendor Ltd")` and `export LONG=$(upload F6-LONG.txt text/plain "QA F6 Long Schedule" "QA Long Vendor Ltd")`; `waitdone` each; then `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$MANY/extract-obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{ok, n: (.obligations\|length), summary, error}'` and the same for `$LONG` with `\| jq '[.obligations[].description]'`. | `$MANY`: `ok` true, `n` at most 25, `error` null. `$LONG`: the QA-HEAD fee only. Both contracts are drafts: the API extracts whatever the status. |

**Also check**
- Each stored row keeps what the service returned, lower-cased: `type` one of payment, sla, renewal, audit, report, termination, compliance, other; `owner` customer, provider, either or unknown; `recurrence` one-time, monthly, quarterly, annually, on-event or unknown; `severity` low, medium or high. A due date the model couldn't work out is `null`, with the event in `trigger`.
- The service caps at 25 even if the model returns more; the API caps stored rows at 100 (not reachable through this service).

### E2E-OBL-03 · An obligation is completed with a note and evidence, the evidence downloads, and it can be reopened

**Covers:** `/obligations` (**Complete**) · `/contracts/:id` (rail **complete**) · `POST /obligations/:id/complete` · `GET /obligations/:id` · `GET /obligations/:id/evidence` · `POST /obligations/:id/reopen` · docs/38 TC-ACC-05, TC-ACC-07
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, viewer-a, finance-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key (step 9 only) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-OBL-01 done: `$F6` has open obligations, including the insurance certificate (due in 20 days) and the monthly availability report.
- `D-INVOICE.pdf` (§0). For the refusals: `echo '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>' > drawing.svg`, `: > empty.pdf`, and a 26 MB file: `mkfile -n 26m big.pdf` (macOS) or `truncate -s 26M big.pdf`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Obligations**. Type "insurance" in the search box ("Search description or contract"). Click **Complete** on the insurance row. | A dialog "Mark obligation complete" with the obligation's description, a **Completion note** (optional) box with the hint "What was done? Reference numbers, payment date, etc.", an **Evidence file** (optional, 25MB max) area with **Attach evidence (PDF, image, CSV…)**, and **Cancel** / **Mark complete**. |
| 2 | Type the note "Certificate received from the broker, ref QA-INS-1". Click **Attach evidence (PDF, image, CSV…)** and pick `D-INVOICE.pdf`. | The area shows the file name and its size (for example "84.2 KB") with a remove button (**Remove file**). |
| 3 | Click **Mark complete**. | The button reads "Saving…", the dialog closes, and the row leaves the Open tab. The **Open** card goes down by 1 and **Completed (30d)** up by 1. |
| 4 | Click the **Completed** tab and click the insurance row. | The drawer shows the pill "Completed" and a green box "Completed <Mon d, yyyy> by Legal Counsel", the note, and the file name **D-INVOICE.pdf** as a button. Its footer shows **Reopen** (no **Mark complete**). |
| 5 | Click **D-INVOICE.pdf** in the drawer. Then `curl -s "$API/obligations/<insurance id>/evidence" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{filename, mimeType, url: (.url\|.[0:40])}'` (the id is in the page URL as `?obligation=<id>`). | A new tab downloads D-INVOICE.pdf. The API gives `filename` "D-INVOICE.pdf", `mimeType` "application/pdf" (the type detected from the bytes) and a presigned storage URL. |
| 6 | Click **Reopen** in the drawer. | A spinner, then the pill reads "Open" and the completed box is gone; the row is back on the Open tab. `GET …/evidence` now answers 404 `{"detail":"No evidence on this obligation"}`. |
| 7 | In the same drawer click **Mark complete**, leave the note and file empty, click **Mark complete** in the dialog. | Completed again. `curl -s "$API/obligations/<insurance id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{status, completionNote, evidenceFilename, by: .completedBy.email}'` → `"COMPLETED"`, `null`, `null`, `"legal@demo.com"`. |
| 8 | Open `$WEB/contracts/$F6`. In the **Obligations** section hover the monthly availability-report row, click **complete**, type a note, click **Mark complete**. | The row turns green, its description is struck through, and it shows "done" instead of **complete**. |
| 9 | Click **re-run** in the section footer. | The two completed rows are still there, marked "done". Known issue: the fresh extraction adds new open copies of them (a second insurance-certificate row and a second availability-report row, not done). |
| 10 | `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=OBLIGATION_COMPLETED&resourceId=$F6" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[] \| .metadata]'` | Newest first: the report `{…,"hasEvidence":false,"hasNote":true}`; the second insurance completion `{…,"hasEvidence":false,"hasNote":false}`; the reopen `{"obligationId":…,"action":"reopen"}`; the first completion `{"obligationId":…,"type":…,"hasEvidence":true,"hasNote":true}`. |

**Also check**
- By API, with JSON instead of a file: `curl -s -X POST "$API/obligations/<an open id>/complete" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"note":"QA API"}' \| jq '{status, completionNote}'` → `"COMPLETED"`, `"QA API"`. The same call again → 409 `{"detail":"Already completed"}`. Reopening an open obligation → 409 `{"detail":"Obligation is not completed"}`.
- Evidence refused by type: attach `drawing.svg` → the dialog shows "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, DOC, XLSX, TXT, CSV, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, TIFF, HEIC." and the obligation stays open (TC-ACC-05 N4, N5; P3, P4 for a PNG named `.pdf` and a TIFF, which are accepted and stored as their real type).
- Empty file: `empty.pdf` → "The uploaded file is empty." (400).
- Too big: picking `big.pdf` shows "File too large — 25MB max (this is 26.0 MB)." and nothing is sent. By API: `curl -s -X POST "$API/obligations/<id>/complete" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F file=@big.pdf` → 413 `{"detail":"Evidence file too large (25MB max)"}`.
- viewer-a, finance-a, approver-a and rep-a see **Complete** on every open row of the Obligations page; confirming shows "You don't have permission to edit contracts." in the dialog. Their drawer shows neither **Mark complete** nor **Reopen**. API: 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- rep-a by id on counsel-a's obligation: `GET /obligations/<id>` and `GET /obligations/<id>/evidence` → 404 `{"detail":"Obligation not found"}` (TC-ACC-07 N3). admin-b: `GET`, `POST …/complete` and `POST …/reopen` → 404 `{"detail":"Obligation not found"}`.
- If a webhook subscribes to `obligation.completed`, it receives `{obligationId, contractId, type, completedAt, hasEvidence}` (TC-WEB-05).

**Known limits**
- A reopen is recorded under the action `OBLIGATION_COMPLETED` with `"action":"reopen"` in its metadata; there is no separate reopen action.
- Reopening unlinks the evidence from the obligation; the file stays in storage but isn't shown again.
- The download link is valid for 10 minutes.
- Known issue: **Complete** on the Obligations page is shown to roles that can't complete, while the drawer hides it from them.
- Known issue: re-running extraction re-creates obligations that were already completed as new open rows (step 9).

### E2E-OBL-04 · The Obligations page shows every status in the right tab, with true counts, search, the drawer and CSV export

**Covers:** `/obligations` · `GET /obligations` · `GET /obligations/stats` · `GET /obligations/:id` · `GET /obligations/export`
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-OBL-01 to -03 done: `$F6` has open rows (the fee 3 days overdue, the report due in 3 days) and completed rows; `$MANY` has 25 open rows due 201–225 days ahead.
- No control in the product sets an obligation to Overdue or Waived: those states come from imported or seeded data (for example `pnpm demo:seed`). Make one of each on `$MANY` with SQL:
  ```bash
  export OVD=$(sql "SELECT id FROM obligations WHERE \"contractId\"='$MANY' ORDER BY \"dueDate\" LIMIT 1")
  export WVD=$(sql "SELECT id FROM obligations WHERE \"contractId\"='$MANY' ORDER BY \"dueDate\" LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1")
  sql "UPDATE obligations SET status='OVERDUE', \"dueDate\"=now()-interval '12 days' WHERE id='$OVD'"
  sql "UPDATE obligations SET status='WAIVED', \"dueDate\"=now()-interval '40 days', \"completionNote\"='QA waived by agreement' WHERE id='$WVD'"
  ```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Post-signature** → **Obligations**. | Heading "Obligations", the line "Every commitment extracted from your executed contracts — payments, SLAs, renewals, audits, and reports.", **Export CSV** at the top right. Four cards: **Open**, **Due in 30d**, **Overdue**, **Completed (30d)**. Tabs **All**, **Open**, **Due soon**, **Overdue**, **Completed**, each but All with a count badge when above 0. The page opens on **Open**, oldest due date first, undated rows last. Above the table: "<N> obligations". |
| 2 | Compare with `curl -s "$API/obligations/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` and `curl -s "$API/obligations?status=OVERDUE&limit=100" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq .total`. | **Open** = `open` (status Open, any date). **Due in 30d** = `dueSoon` (Open, due from now to 30 days ahead). **Overdue** = `overdue` (Open and past its date) + the stored-Overdue total (1 here, `$OVD`). **Completed (30d)** = `completedRecent`. Each tab badge equals its card. |
| 3 | Look at the `$F6` onboarding-fee row. | Columns **Description**, **Contract**, **Due**, **Status**. The description line has a type icon; below it a severity dot and word (e.g. "High"), "· PAYMENT", "· customer" and "§2". **Contract** shows "QA F6 Master Supply Agreement" over "QA Harbor Components Ltd" (a link to the contract). **Due** reads "3d overdue" in red. **Status** is the pill "Open" with a red dot (an open obligation past its date reads as risk). A **Complete** button ends the row. A monthly row shows "↻ monthly" in its meta line; an undated row reads "No due date". |
| 4 | Click **Due soon**. | Open rows due within 30 days, including overdue ones: the fee (3d overdue) and the report ("Due in 3d") are listed. Known issue: the header count includes the overdue rows while the tab badge and the **Due in 30d** card leave them out. |
| 5 | Click **Overdue**. | The fee (pill "Open", red dot, "3d overdue") and `$OVD` (pill "Overdue", "12d overdue"), oldest due first. The header count equals the **Overdue** card. |
| 6 | Click **Completed**. | The rows completed in E2E-OBL-03, pill "Completed", **Due** showing the plain date, no **Complete** button. Known issue: this tab lists every completed obligation ever, while its badge and the **Completed (30d)** card count the last 30 days only. |
| 7 | Click **All** and find `$WVD` (search "QA-D"). | Pill "Waived" (grey dot); **Due** shows its date in grey, not "40d overdue"; no **Complete** button. |
| 8 | Search: type "QA F6" (a contract title), then "onboarding" (a description word), then "zzqx". | First the `$F6` rows, then the fee only, then the empty state `No obligations match "zzqx".`. The search matches the description or the contract title, not the counterparty. |
| 9 | Clear the search, click the fee row (not its link or button). | The URL gains `?obligation=<id>`. The drawer: eyebrow "Obligation · payment", the description as its title, pill "Open" with a red dot, "3 days overdue" in red, and the severity, for example "High Severity" (the stylesheet capitalises each word). A list: **Who** "The customer" (or "The provider", "Either party", "Not stated"), **Due** "<Mon d, yyyy>", **Repeats** "Once". "From the contract, §2" over the quoted clause in italics. A box with the contract title, "QA Harbor Components Ltd · Owner: Legal Counsel" and the link **Open the contract at §2**. Footer **Mark complete**. |
| 10 | Click **Open the contract at §2**. Go back. Open an undated row's drawer. | The contract page opens with `?section=2`; if its table of contents has "2", that entry flashes for 5 s. The undated drawer shows **Due** "When: <trigger>" (or "No date stated") and **Repeats** "monthly". |
| 11 | Close the drawer with **Close** (the X), with **Esc**, and by clicking outside it. Then reload the page with `?obligation=<id>` in the URL, and once with `?obligation=nope`. | Each closes the drawer and removes `?obligation=` from the URL. The reload opens the drawer on that obligation directly. `nope` shows "This obligation couldn't be loaded. It may have been removed." |
| 12 | On each tab click **Export CSV** and open the file. | A download named `obligations-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv` with the columns Type, Description, Owner, Severity, Recurrence, Section, Due Date, Status, Contract, Counterparty, Contract Type, Completed At, Completed By, Completion Note, Has Evidence, and the tab's rows. The insurance completion from E2E-OBL-03 has Completed By `legal@demo.com`; a completion with a file has Has Evidence `yes`. Known issues: with text in the search box, the file still holds the whole tab; on **Overdue** the file lacks `$OVD` (stored Overdue). |
| 13 | Filters only the API offers: `curl -s "$API/obligations?type=payment&severity=high&limit=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{total, n: (.data\|length), limit, offset}'`; then `?contractId=$F6`, `?status=WAIVED`, `?dueWithin=7`, `?sort=severity&order=desc`, `?limit=5&offset=5`. | Each narrows as named; `dueWithin=7` keeps rows due by today + 7 days, whatever their status (overdue and completed ones included); rows carry `contract {id, title, status, type, counterpartyName}` and `completedBy`. |
| 14 | Look at the sidebar's **Obligations** badge. | It shows the stats `overdue` number (Open and past due), which leaves out `$OVD`: known issue, it can be lower than the page's **Overdue** card. |

**Also check**
- Invalid queries: `?severity=critical`, `?bucket=late`, `?limit=101` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid query","issues":[…]}`. `GET /obligations/export?format=xlsx` → 400 `{"detail":"Only csv is supported"}`.
- viewer-a sees the same page and can export; see E2E-OBL-03 for its **Complete** button.
- Empty states, as admin-b (Org B has no obligations): **All** "No obligations extracted yet.", **Open** "Nothing outstanding — every extracted commitment is discharged.", **Due soon** "Nothing due in the next 30 days.", **Overdue** "Nothing overdue — well done.", **Completed** "No obligations completed in the last 30 days.", each with "Obligations are auto-extracted when a contract is signed; you can also run extraction manually from any contract page." admin-b's `GET /obligations?contractId=$F6` → 200 with `data: []` (TC-WF-17 N6).
- With the API stopped (after the retries): "Failed to load obligations."
- The page refreshes its list and counts every 60 s: complete an obligation by API and watch the page change without a reload.
- Deleted contract: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/contracts/$LONG" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` → 204. Known issue: its QA-HEAD obligation is still on the page, in the counts and in the CSV, and its contract link opens "Contract not found" (the daily scan does skip it).
- A diligence room's obligations never appear here (E2E-DIL-03); rep-a sees only obligations on contracts rep-a owns (E2E-ANL-02).

**Known limits**
- Each tab shows at most 100 rows; the header count is the full total and there is no paging.
- Sorting is fixed to due date, earliest first.
- The drawer counts overdue days from the exact time, the list from calendar days, so they can differ by one.

### E2E-OBL-05 · The contract owner gets a reminder a week before an obligation falls due, from the daily scan or a manual run

**Covers:** `scan.worker` (obligation reminders) · `POST /cron/obligations` · Mailpit · header **Notifications** · docs/38 TC-WEB-05, TC-WF-17
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$F6`'s onboarding fee (due 3 days ago) and security report (due in 3 days) are still Open (E2E-OBL-01; the re-runs gave them new ids, which doesn't matter). No scan has run since.
- counsel-a owns `$F6`. In counsel-a's Settings → Notifications, "A contract I own is coming due" is on and delivery is real-time (the defaults).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run the scan by hand, as admin-a: `curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' \| jq` | `{"ok":true,"result":{"scannedContracts":…,"obligationsSeen":…,"notified":…,"skippedAcked":0,"skippedCooldown":…,"skippedNoOwner":0,"errors":[]},"ranAt":"…"}`. `notified` is at least 2. |
| 2 | Open Mailpit (wait up to 30 s). | Two emails to legal@demo.com. Subject "Overdue 3d · QA F6 Master Supply Agreement", body "<SEVERITY> · payment · <the fee's description>" (for example "HIGH · payment · …"). Subject "Due in 3d · QA F6 Master Supply Agreement", body "<SEVERITY> · report · …". No email for the insurance certificate (20 days out) or for undated rows. |
| 3 | As counsel-a click the bell (**Notifications**) in the header. | The badge counts the unread items. The panel "Notifications" lists the same two titles with their bodies and "just now" (or "<n>m ago"). Clicking one opens `$WEB/contracts/$F6` and marks it read; **Mark all read** clears the badge. |
| 4 | `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=OBLIGATION_OVERDUE&resourceId=$F6" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[] \| {metadata, actor}]'` | One event: `metadata` `{"obligationId":…,"type":"payment","severity":…,"daysOverdue":3,"dueDate":"<day -3>"}`, `actor` null (the system). A webhook subscribed to `obligation.overdue` gets one delivery (TC-WEB-05 P2). |
| 5 | `curl -s "$API/obligations?contractId=$F6&limit=100" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '[.data[] \| {description: .description[:40], notifiedAt}]'` | The fee and the report have `notifiedAt` set; the others `null`. |
| 6 | Repeat step 1 at once. | No new emails. The two obligations are counted in `skippedCooldown` (72-hour cooldown), and there is still one `OBLIGATION_OVERDUE` event. |
| 7 | Repeat with `-d '{"force":true}'`. | Two new emails with the same subjects. Still one `OBLIGATION_OVERDUE` event (and one webhook). |
| 8 | Repeat with `-d '{"leadDays":30,"force":true}'`. | Also "Due in 20d · QA F6 Master Supply Agreement" for each open insurance-certificate row (the copy E2E-OBL-03 step 9 created), and for any other open obligation due within 30 days. |
| 9 | As counsel-a: Settings → Notifications → turn off "A contract I own is coming due". Run step 7 again. Turn it back on. | New notifications in the bell, but no new email in Mailpit; the API log reads "[notify] suppressed by preference for userId=… type=OBLIGATION_DUE (contractExpiringSoon is off)". With the digest set to "Daily digest" instead, the email waits for the 9 a.m. digest (the notifications section covers the digest). |
| 10 | The schedule: look at the API's startup log (the `pnpm dev` terminal). To see a scheduled run now, add the line `OBLIGATION_SCAN_PATTERN="*/2 * * * *"` to `.env`, restart `pnpm dev`, and wait up to 2 minutes. Then remove the line and restart again. | Startup prints "[scan-worker] registered repeatable jobs · obligations=0 9 * * * renewals=15 9 * * * digests=*/15 * * * *" (09:00 and 09:15 UTC daily). With the override, within 2 minutes: "[scan-worker] obligation-scan-daily · <n>ms · scanned=<n> notified=<n> skippedAcked=0 skippedCooldown=<n> errors=0". verify: after the restart without the override, the 2-minute run stops (see Known limits). |

**Also check**
- Only admins may run it: step 1 with `$COUNSEL_A`, `$CONTRACTS_A` or `$VIEWER_A` → 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: configure:user"`. The web app has no button for it.
- Body checks: `{"leadDays":0}`, `{"leadDays":366}` or `{"leadDays":"7"}` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request","issues":[…]}`.
- `{"scope":"all"}` from admin-a still scans Org A only. The external scheduler calls it as the internal service: `curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/obligations" -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H "x-internal-service: agents" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"scope":"all"}'` walks every org; with `-H "x-org-id: $ORG_B"` and no scope, Org B only.
- Completed, Waived and stored-Overdue obligations never get reminders. Nor does an obligation more than 7 days past its date (`$OVD`, 12 days), a diligence room's (TC-WF-17 N2) or a deleted contract's (TC-WF-17 P4).
- If the contract's owner no longer exists, the reminder goes to the org's oldest active user (only reachable by editing data).

**Known limits**
- Reminders run from 7 days before the due date to 7 days after it, at most once every 72 hours per obligation: with the daily run, about 7, 4 and 1 days before, then 2 and 5 days after.
- `skippedAcked` is always 0: nothing counts into it.
- Known issue (verify): a deactivated owner still gets the reminder. Deactivate contracts-a, give a contract contracts-a owns an obligation due in 3 days, run step 1: Mailpit shows the email to contracts@demo.com.
- Known issue (verify): changing `OBLIGATION_SCAN_PATTERN` (or `RENEWAL_SCAN_PATTERN`) leaves the old schedule registered in Redis, so both run. If the 2-minute run continues after step 10, clear the scans queue's repeat keys in Redis and restart the API.

### E2E-OBL-06 · The Assistant lists a contract's obligations with obligations_list

**Covers:** `obligations_list` · `/agent`
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b (as the identity passed to the tool) · **Needs:** agents service + model key (step 1) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-OBL-01 to -03 done. `$NT_2` (the contract with no document) from E2E-OBL-01.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Ask: "What obligations do we have under the QA F6 Master Supply Agreement, and which of them are overdue?" | Tool chips appear above the answer: `contract_search` (to find the contract), then `obligations_list` with the contract's title in its summary. The answer lists the obligations with their due dates and says the USD 12,000 onboarding fee (due <day -3>) is overdue. verify: completed rows are left out or marked completed. The right pane opens a table **Obligations** ("<n> tracked") with columns Obligation, Type, Due, Severity and **Export CSV**. |
| 2 | Same data without the model: `tj obligations_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$F6'"}' \| jq '{total, statuses: [.items[].status], first: (.items[0] \| {type, dueDate, contractTitle, counterpartyName}), diagnostic}'` | `total` = the rail's count, completed rows included; items oldest due first; `contractTitle` "QA F6 Master Supply Agreement"; `diagnostic` null. |
| 3 | Add `"dueWithin":7` to the body. | Items due by today + 7 days, plus recurring ones. Known issue: completed and overdue rows are included too; the tool has no status filter. |
| 4 | A contract never extracted: `"contractId":"'$NT_2'"`. | `items` [] and `diagnostic` `{"kind":"no_obligations_extracted","message":"1 contract have not had obligations extracted yet. Run \"Extract obligations\" on the relevant contract pages first.","contractsAwaitingExtraction":[{"id":…,"title":"QA OBL no text"}]}` (the grammar is as the code writes it). |

**Also check**
- Own scope: step 2 with `"userId":"'$REP_A_ID'"` → `items` [] (rep-a doesn't own `$F6`) and no diagnostic about it.
- Another org's user naming Org A: `"userId":"'$ADMIN_B_ID'"` → 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:contract permission"}`; in chat the chip turns red with "obligations list failed".
- Wrong secret: `curl -s -X POST "$INT/tools/obligations_list" -H "x-internal-secret: nope" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'` → 401 `{"detail":"Internal endpoint — bad secret"}`.
- Descriptions and quotes follow the org's PII mode (redacted in redact mode), as other contract text sent to the model.

**Known limits**
- Without a contract id the tool reads obligations from at most 500 of the org's contracts, in no set order; in a very large org some are left out without notice.


### E2E-REN-01 · The Renewals page lists executed contracts by month, the lapsed ones first, with auto-renewal and the notice deadline

**Covers:** `/renewals` · `GET /renewals` · `GET /renewals/stats` · docs/38 TC-WF-10
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- Take the counts before the fixture: `curl -s "$API/renewals/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" > ren-before.json`.
- The fixture below, imported by counsel-a (so counsel-a owns it), with renewal terms set as reviewer corrections. The notice deadline is the expiry date minus the notice period, for auto-renewing contracts only: `$R_5` (140 days out, 120 days' notice) must give notice within 20 days; `$R_6` (100 days out) passed its deadline 20 days ago.

```bash
cat > qa-ren.csv <<CSV
title,type,status,counterpartyname,value,currency,expirydate
QA REN Lapsed 10,MSA,executed,QA Renew Alpha,10000,USD,$(day -10)
QA REN This week,MSA,executed,QA Renew Bravo,20000,USD,$(day +5)
QA REN Month,LICENSE,executed,QA Renew Charlie,30000,USD,$(day +25)
QA REN Notice at risk,MSA,executed,QA Renew Delta,40000,USD,$(day +140)
QA REN Notice passed,MSA,executed,QA Renew Echo,50000,USD,$(day +100)
QA REN Notice unknown,MSA,executed,QA Renew Foxtrot,60000,USD,$(day +140)
QA REN No auto-renew,MSA,executed,QA Renew Golf,70000,EUR,$(day +60)
QA REN Far out,MSA,executed,QA Renew Hotel,80000,USD,$(day +400)
QA REN Draft,MSA,draft,QA Renew India,90000,USD,$(day +30)
QA REN Lapsed 45,MSA,executed,QA Renew Juliet,1000,USD,$(day -45)
CSV
bulk qa-ren.csv R      # sets R_2 … R_11, in the order above
qverify $R_5 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'; qverify $R_5 '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":120}'
qverify $R_6 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'; qverify $R_6 '{"field":"noticePeriod","value":"120 days"}'
qverify $R_7 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'; qverify $R_7 '{"field":"noticePeriod","value":"30-60 days"}'
qverify $R_8 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"no"}';  qverify $R_8 '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":120}'
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Post-signature** → **Renewals**. | Heading "Renewals", the line "Every executed contract heading toward its expiry — grouped by month so you can see what decisions are needed when.", **Export CSV** at the top right. Four cards: **This week**, **Next 30 days**, **Next 90 days**, **Decisions needed** (subtitle "next 90d · USD <amount> ACV", or "next 90d" when there's no value). Tabs **Next year** (selected), **This week**, **Next 30d**, **Next 60d**, **Next 90d**, **Overdue**, each but Next year with a count badge when above 0. Below them the decision filter, a search box "Search title or counterparty", and **Notice at risk <n>** when any row is at risk. |
| 2 | `curl -s "$API/renewals/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` and compare with `ren-before.json`. | `overdue` +1, `thisWeek` +1, `next30` +2, `next60` +3, `next90` +3, `undecided` +3, `totalAcvNext90` +120000. The cards show `thisWeek`, `next30`, `next90` and `undecided`; the tab badges `thisWeek`, `next30`, `next60`, `next90`, `overdue`. |
| 3 | Scroll the month groups. | One card per month of expiry, earliest month first, so the group holding "QA REN Lapsed 10" (expired 10 days ago) comes first: lapsed contracts lead. Each header reads "<Month YYYY>", "<n> renewal(s)" and "USD <amount>K ACV" (the sum of the values in that month). |
| 4 | Read the fixture's rows. | "QA REN Lapsed 10": "<Mon d, yyyy> · 10d ago" in red. "QA REN This week": "· in 5d" in amber, bold. "QA REN Month": "· in 25d" in amber. "QA REN No auto-renew": "· in 60d" in grey and no notice line. "QA REN Notice passed": under its date, in red with a warning icon, "Notice deadline passed · <date 20 days ago>". "QA REN Notice at risk": "Notice by <date 20 days ahead> · 20d left" in red with the icon. "QA REN Notice unknown": "Auto-renews · notice period unknown" in grey. Each row: the title (a link), the type in capitals (LICENSE, MSA), a line "<counterparty> · <currency> <value> · <owner>" (for example "QA Renew Alpha · USD 10K · Legal Counsel"; "QA REN No auto-renew" shows "EUR 70K"), then **Decide** and **Open →**. |
| 5 | Hover each notice line. | "QA REN Notice at risk" and "Notice passed": "Auto-renews. 120 days' notice to terminate, so notice must be served by <date>." "Notice unknown": "This contract auto-renews, but no notice-to-terminate period was extracted, so the deadline to stop it is unknown." |
| 6 | Look for "QA REN Far out", "QA REN Draft", "QA REN Lapsed 45". | Not listed: 400 days is past the one-year window, a draft isn't executed, and 45 days ago is past the 30-day look-back. |
| 7 | `curl -s "$API/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{total, window, rows: [.data[] \| select(.title\|startswith("QA REN")) \| {title, expiry: .expiryDate[:10], notice}]}'` | Seven rows, soonest expiry first. `notice`: at risk `{"autoRenew":true,"days":120,"deadline":"<day +20>T00:00:00.000Z","setBy":null}`; passed `{true,120,"<day -20>T…",null}`; unknown `{"autoRenew":true,"days":null,"deadline":null,"setBy":null}`; no auto-renew `{"autoRenew":false,"days":120,"deadline":null,"setBy":null}`; the others `autoRenew` false. `window` runs from 30 days ago to 365 days ahead. The same rows are grouped under `months`. |
| 8 | Click each tab. | **This week**: "QA REN This week". **Next 30d**: + "QA REN Month". **Next 60d** and **Next 90d**: + "QA REN No auto-renew". **Overdue**: "QA REN Lapsed 10" (expired within the last 30 days). Other Org A contracts may appear too. |
| 9 | Back on **Next year**, click **Notice at risk**. Then click it again. | Pressed, the list keeps only at-risk rows ("QA REN Notice at risk", "QA REN Notice passed", and any others whose deadline has passed or is within 30 days); each month's ACV is re-added from the rows shown. Released, all rows return. On a tab with no at-risk rows the button isn't shown. |
| 10 | Type "Echo" in the search box, then "zzqx". | First only "QA REN Notice passed" (its counterparty is QA Renew Echo), with its month's ACV re-added; then `No renewals match "zzqx".` with "Renewals appear here once a contract is executed and the expiry date is set." |
| 11 | The decision filter (**Filter by renewal decision**): pick **Decided**, then **No decision yet**, then **All decisions**. | **Decided** lists only contracts with a decision logged (none of the fixture yet, E2E-REN-02 adds one); **No decision yet** the rest; **All decisions** everything. |
| 12 | The sidebar's **Renewals** badge. | Equals `undecided` from step 2. |
| 13 | API parameters: `?bucket=next_30`, `?status=pending`, `?lookaheadDays=500`. | The same filters as the tabs and the decision filter; `lookaheadDays=500` adds "QA REN Far out". |

**Also check**
- `?bucket=later` or `?lookaheadDays=0` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid query","issues":[…]}`.
- viewer-a sees the same page (every role may view); rep-a only its own contracts (E2E-ANL-02).
- admin-b (Org B has no renewals): the empty state "No upcoming renewals in this window." with "Renewals appear here once a contract is executed and the expiry date is set." With the API stopped: "Failed to load renewals."
- The page refreshes every 60 s.
- **Open →** and the title open `/contracts/<id>`. **Decide** opens `/contracts/<id>#renewal`: known issue, the page doesn't scroll to the **Renewal** rail section; find it in the details rail.
- Executed amendments and exhibits are never rows of their own (E2E-REN-03); diligence-room contracts never appear (E2E-DIL-03, TC-WF-16).

**Known limits**
- ACV totals add values in different currencies as one number and label them with the month's first currency (here "QA REN No auto-renew"'s EUR 70,000 is added into USD totals, and into the **Decisions needed** subtitle).
- The look-back is 30 days: a contract that lapsed earlier drops off the page.
- Known issue: `GET /renewals/stats` (the cards, tab badges and sidebar badge) also counts executed amendments and exhibits that the list leaves out (E2E-REN-03 step 8).

### E2E-REN-02 · The daily renewal scan alerts the owner on expiry or on the notice deadline, once a week, until a decision is logged

**Covers:** `scan.worker` (renewal scan) · `POST /cron/renewals` · `POST /contracts/:id/renewal-decision` · Mailpit · header **Notifications** · docs/38 TC-WF-10, TC-RENEW-02
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-REN-01's fixture, and no renewal scan since it was imported (a contract is alerted at most once a week). `$F6` (expiring in 110 days, auto-renewing, 90 days' notice) from E2E-OBL-01.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: `curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' \| jq` | `{"ok":true,"result":{"scannedContracts":…,"candidates":…,"notified":…,"skippedCooldown":…,"skippedNoOwner":0,"errors":[]},"ranAt":"…"}`, `notified` at least 7. |
| 2 | Mailpit (emails to legal@demo.com, the owner) and counsel-a's bell. | One alert each (subject = title): "Expired 10d ago · QA REN Lapsed 10", body "QA Renew Alpha · USD 10000 — review renewal options now."; "Expires in 5d · QA REN This week" ("QA Renew Bravo · USD 20000 — review renewal options now."); "Expires in 25d · QA REN Month"; "Expires in 60d · QA REN No auto-renew" ("QA Renew Golf · EUR 70000 — review renewal options now."); "Notice deadline passed · QA REN Notice passed", body "QA Renew Echo · USD 50000 — auto-renews: the 120-day notice deadline (<day -20>) has passed. Check whether it can still be stopped."; "Notice deadline in 20d · QA REN Notice at risk", body "QA Renew Delta · USD 40000 — auto-renews unless 120 days' notice is served by <day +20>."; "Notice deadline in 20d · QA F6 Master Supply Agreement", body "QA Harbor Components Ltd — auto-renews unless 90 days' notice is served by <day +20>." (with " · USD <value>" after the name if the analysis found one). |
| 3 | Look for the others. | No alert for "QA REN Notice unknown" (no deadline to work out; expiry 140 days away), "QA REN Far out", "QA REN Draft" or "QA REN Lapsed 45". Clicking an alert in the bell opens the contract. |
| 4 | Repeat step 1 at once. | No new alerts; the fixture's contracts are counted in `skippedCooldown` (7-day cooldown). |
| 5 | Log a decision: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$R_3/renewal-decision" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"decision":"renew"}'` → then step 1 with `-d '{"force":true}'`. | The decision answers `{"ok":true,"decision":"renew"}`. The forced run alerts the others again but not "QA REN This week": a contract with a decision (other than "unknown") is skipped even with `force`. On the Renewals page its row now shows the pill "Renew" instead of **Decide**, and **Decisions needed** and the sidebar badge go down by 1. |
| 6 | Step 1 with `-d '{"leadDays":30,"force":true}'`. | "QA REN No auto-renew" (60 days out, no deadline) is not alerted; the notice-deadline alerts still are (they have their own 30-day lead). |
| 7 | The schedule: as in E2E-OBL-05 step 10, with the line `RENEWAL_SCAN_PATTERN="*/2 * * * *"` in `.env`. | "[scan-worker] renewal-scan-daily · <n>ms · scanned=<n> notified=<n> skippedCooldown=<n> errors=0" (daily at 09:15 UTC without the override). |

**Also check**
- Step 1 as counsel-a, contracts-a or viewer-a → 403 `"detail":"Missing permission: configure:user"` (TC-WF-10 N6). No button in the web app.
- `{"leadDays":0}` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request",…}`. `{"scope":"all"}` from an admin scans only the admin's org; the internal-service call walks every org, as in E2E-OBL-05.
- An executed amendment or exhibit is never alerted on its own (E2E-REN-03 step 6, TC-RENEW-02). A diligence room's contracts aren't scanned (TC-WF-16 N5).
- A contract whose owner no longer exists is counted in `skippedNoOwner`; renewal alerts have no fallback recipient (only reachable by editing data).
- `"decision":"unknown"` counts as no decision: the contract is alerted again after the cooldown.

**Known limits**
- Expiry alerts start 90 days before the expiry (the `leadDays`); notice alerts start 30 days before the notice deadline, for notice periods up to 366 days. After it lapses, a contract is still alerted for 30 days.
- One alert per contract per 7 days, then none once a decision is logged.
- The notification preference "A contract I own is coming due" governs these emails too.

### E2E-REN-03 · A signed amendment's notice period moves the deadline and is named in notice.setBy; an amendment is never a renewal of its own

**Covers:** `/renewals` · `GET /renewals` (`notice.setBy`) · `GET /renewals/stats` · `POST /cron/renewals` · `renewal_advice` · docs/38 TC-RENEW-01, TC-RENEW-02, TC-FAMILY-01
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a · **Needs:** Mailpit · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- 6.0 helpers (`amend`, `execute`). A stats snapshot: `curl -s "$API/renewals/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" > ren3-before.json`.
- The base licence, auto-renewing with 30 days' notice, expiring in 75 days:
  ```bash
  printf 'title,type,status,counterpartyname,expirydate\nQA REN2 Licence,LICENSE,executed,QA Northwind Data,%s\n' "$(day +75)" > qa-ren2.csv
  bulk qa-ren2.csv RB      # sets RB_2
  qverify $RB_2 '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'; qverify $RB_2 '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":30}'
  ```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s "$API/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq --arg id "$RB_2" '.data[] \| select(.id==$id) \| .notice'` and the Renewals page. | `{"autoRenew":true,"days":30,"deadline":"<day +45>T00:00:00.000Z","setBy":null}`. The row reads "Notice by <date 45 days ahead>" in grey. |
| 2 | A draft amendment with 60 days' notice: `export RA=$(amend $RB_2 amendment "QA REN2 Licence — Amendment No. 1")`, then `qverify $RA '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":60}'`. Repeat step 1. | Unchanged: an unsigned amendment changes nothing (TC-RENEW-01 N5). |
| 3 | Sign it: `execute $RA` (prints EXECUTED). Repeat step 1. | `{"autoRenew":true,"days":60,"deadline":"<day +15>T00:00:00.000Z","setBy":"QA REN2 Licence — Amendment No. 1"}`. The row reads "Notice by <date 15 days ahead> · 15d left" in red with the icon, its tooltip "Auto-renews. 60 days' notice to terminate, so notice must be served by <date>.", and it is counted in **Notice at risk**. |
| 4 | An exhibit claiming 180 days: `export RX=$(amend $RB_2 exhibit_only "QA REN2 Licence — Exhibit A")`, `qverify $RX '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":180}'`, `execute $RX`. Repeat step 1. | Still 60 days and `setBy` Amendment No. 1: an exhibit changes no terms. |
| 5 | Look for the amendment and the exhibit as rows (both executed, both expiring in 75 days): on the page, and `curl -s "$API/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq --arg a "$RA" --arg x "$RX" '[.data[] \| select(.id==$a or .id==$x)] \| length'`. | Neither is a row; the count is `0`. An amendment or exhibit renews with its contract. |
| 6 | The scan: `curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"force":true}'`, then counsel-a's bell and Mailpit. | "Notice deadline in 15d · QA REN2 Licence", body "QA Northwind Data — auto-renews unless 60 days' notice is served by <day +15>." No alert names "Amendment No. 1" or "Exhibit A". (The forced run re-alerts E2E-REN-02's contracts too; ignore those.) |
| 7 | The assistant tool, without the model: `tj renewal_advice '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$RB_2'"}' \| jq '.items[0] \| {contractTitle, autoRenews, noticeDays, noticePeriodSetBy, noticeDeadline, noticeDeadlinePassed}'`; then the portfolio, `'{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","leadDays":90,"limit":50}'` piped to `jq --arg a "$RA" --arg x "$RX" '[.items[] \| select(.contractId==$a or .contractId==$x)] \| length'`. | `{"contractTitle":"QA REN2 Licence","autoRenews":true,"noticeDays":60,"noticePeriodSetBy":"QA REN2 Licence — Amendment No. 1","noticeDeadline":"<day +15>","noticeDeadlinePassed":false}`; then `0`. |
| 8 | `curl -s "$API/renewals/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` against `ren3-before.json`. | Known issue: `next90` and `undecided` went up by 3 (the licence, the amendment and the exhibit) while the list gained 1 row; the cards, tab badges and sidebar badge over-count. |
| 9 | A second amendment that ends auto-renewal: `export RC=$(amend $RB_2 amendment "QA REN2 Licence — Amendment No. 2")`, `qverify $RC '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"no"}'`, `execute $RC`. Repeat step 1. | `{"autoRenew":false,"days":60,"deadline":null,"setBy":"QA REN2 Licence — Amendment No. 1"}`: the latest signed amendment wins on auto-renewal, No. 1 still set the period. The row has no notice line. |

**Also check**
- The contract page of `$RB_2` lists its amendments in the family view (contracts section); the assistant's `contract_get` shows them with a `familyNote` (TC-FAMILY-01).
- A **renewal**-type child (relationship "Renewal") also changes the terms like an amendment; a SOW or order form under a parent keeps its own term and is listed on its own.

**Known limits**
- The Renewals page doesn't show which amendment set the notice period (`setBy` is in the API only; FIX_TRACKER GG4 "Not done").
- An amendment that changes the expiry date isn't applied: the deadline still counts back from the contract's own expiry (TC-RENEW-01 N4).
- A rep who owns the base contract but not an amendment made by someone else doesn't see that amendment, so its deadline is worked out from the base period (by design of own scope, TC-FAMILY-01 N2).
- Known issue: `GET /renewals/stats` and `GET /renewals/export` still count and list amendments and exhibits (step 8, E2E-REN-05).

### E2E-REN-04 · Renewal advice and a renewal decision are recorded from the contract page and shown on the Renewals page

**Covers:** `/contracts/:id` (details rail → **Renewal**) · `/renewals` · `POST /contracts/:id/renewal-advice` · `POST /contracts/:id/renewal-decision` · agent service `renewals`
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `$F6` (executed, text, expiring in 110 days) from E2E-OBL-01; `$R_4` ("QA REN Month", no document) from E2E-REN-01.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$WEB/contracts/$F6`; find the **Renewal** section in the details rail. | It shows because the expiry is within 180 days: "Expires in 110d · <date>" (grey; amber from 90 days, red from 30), the text "Get a recommendation — renew, renegotiate, let expire, or pause — grounded in the contract text + tracked obligations.", **Get renewal advice**, and under "Log decision" the buttons **Renew**, **Renegotiate**, **Let expire**, **Pause**. |
| 2 | Click **Get renewal advice**. | "Analysing contract…" for 10–40 s, then: a pill with the recommendation and confidence (for example "RENEGOTIATE · medium conf"), a rationale paragraph, "Negotiation points" (up to 5, each a topic, a severity chip, our position and the reasoning in italics), "Risk flags" (up to 5, with a warning icon), a timeline in italics, and the footer "Advised <date>" with **re-run**. verify: the recommendation and points vary; the confidence is at most medium (see Known limits). |
| 3 | The same through the API: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$F6/renewal-advice" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{ok, error, rec: .advice.recommendation, conf: .advice.confidence, points: (.advice.negotiationPoints\|length), flags: (.advice.riskFlags\|length), model: .advice.model}'` | `ok` true, `error` null, `rec` one of renew, renegotiate, let_expire, pause; `conf` high, medium or low; at most 5 points and 5 flags; `model` names the model. The rail shows the new advice after a reload (the API call replaced the stored advice). |
| 4 | Sidebar → **Renewals**, find "QA F6 Master Supply Agreement". Hover the chip. | The assistant chip "AI: Renegotiate" (or "AI: Renew", "AI: Let expire", "AI: Pause"); the hover shows the rationale. **Decide** is still there: advice isn't a decision. |
| 5 | Back on `$F6`, under "Log decision" click **Renegotiate**. | The button takes the recommendation colours and "Recorded: Renegotiate" appears below. On the Renewals page the row shows the pill "Renegotiate" in place of the AI chip and **Decide**. With the filter on **Decided** it is listed; on **No decision yet** it isn't. |
| 6 | API decisions: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$F6/renewal-decision" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"decision":"let_expire","note":"QA"}'`; then `-d '{"decision":"unknown"}'`; then `-d '{"decision":"maybe"}'`. | `{"ok":true,"decision":"let_expire"}`: the page pill reads "Let expire" (red dot). Then `{"ok":true,"decision":"unknown"}`: on the Renewals page the row is back to **Decide**, and after a reload the rail reads "Recorded: unknown" with no button highlighted (the web app has no button to clear a decision). Then 400 `{"detail":"invalid decision"}`. |
| 7 | The agent service directly: without the secret `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/renewal_advice -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"plainText":"x"}'`; with it and empty text, `-H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -d '{"plainText":""}'`. | `{"error":"unauthorized"}` 401. Then `{"recommendation":"pause","confidence":"low","rationale":"Empty contract text — nothing to analyse.","negotiationPoints":[],"riskFlags":["no_text_available"],"timeline":""}`. |

**Also check**
- A contract with no document: open `$R_4` ("QA REN Month", 25 days out), click **Get renewal advice**. Known issue: nothing visible happens (the button comes back, no message); the API answers 400 `{"detail":"No version to analyse"}`. A version without text → 400 `{"detail":"No plaintext on current version"}`.
- viewer-a, finance-a, approver-a on `$F6` see the same section and buttons. Known issue: **Get renewal advice** and the decision buttons do nothing visible for them (the request is refused as "You don't have permission to edit contracts." but the section shows no error). API: 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- rep-a (doesn't own `$F6`) → both routes 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`; admin-b → 404.
- The section is hidden when the expiry is more than 180 days ahead or more than 30 days past, unless advice was saved before; with no expiry date it never shows.
- Cost cap reached → 429 with the cost-cap message (as E2E-OBL-01); the agents service answering an error status → 502 `{"detail":"renewal advisor failed","upstream":"…"}`; the agents service stopped → 500.
- Known issue: when the model's answer can't be read, the advice is still saved, as "PAUSE · low conf" with the rationale "LLM output could not be parsed.", and the Renewals page shows "AI: Pause". The API response has `"ok":false` and an `error`.
- Known issue: logging a decision writes no audit event: `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?resourceId=$F6" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[].action]'` has nothing for it.

**Known limits**
- Known issue: the advisor is never given the contract's obligations (the API reads an old metadata field that extraction now removes), so its confidence can't reach "high" and the section's promise "grounded in … tracked obligations" isn't met.
- The model reads the first 14,000 characters of the contract.

If the tool's coverage is partial, the answer says the list is partial. verify: wording. |

- `"limit":51` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request",…}` (TC-AI-10 N4).
