### E2E-INV-01 · An invoice entered by hand matches a payment obligation by vendor, date and currency, with the amount checked against the contract total

**Covers:** `/invoices` · `POST /invoices` · `GET /invoices` · `GET /invoices/:id` · docs/38 TC-ACC-18, TC-WF-17
**Roles:** counsel-a, finance-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- `curl -s "$API/invoices/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" > inv-before.json`.
- Two executed contracts with a total value, and an open payment obligation on each. Obligations are normally extracted by the model; the SQL makes them exact so the scores below are fixed.

```bash
cat > qa-inv.csv <<CSV
title,type,status,counterpartyname,value,currency,expirydate
QA INV Ledgerline — Logistics MSA,MSA,executed,QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd,12000,USD,$(day +300)
QA INV Orchid — Supply Agreement,VENDOR,executed,QA Orchid Paper Co,5000,EUR,$(day +300)
CSV
bulk qa-inv.csv K      # K_2 = Ledgerline, K_3 = Orchid
sql "INSERT INTO obligations (id, \"orgId\", \"contractId\", type, description, quote, \"dueDate\", recurrence, status, \"createdAt\", \"updatedAt\") VALUES
 ('qa_inv_ob1', '$ORG_A', '$K_2', 'payment', 'QA INV Ledgerline onboarding fee', 'QA', '$(day -10)', 'one-time', 'OPEN', now(), now()),
 ('qa_inv_ob2', '$ORG_A', '$K_3', 'payment', 'QA INV Orchid quarterly service fee', 'QA', NULL, 'quarterly', 'OPEN', now(), now())"
```

How a match is scored, against every open payment obligation on a live contract of the org (not a diligence room's), best score wins, 40 or more to link: vendor name equal to the contract's counterparty 40 (one contains the other 27, a shared word of 3+ letters 13); the obligation's due date within 7 days of the invoice date 25 (30 days 15, 60 days 7; an undated recurring obligation 10); same currency as the contract 10; description words shared with the obligation 15 (3+ words) or 7; amount against the contract's total value: within 2% 15, 10% 10, 50% 5, more than 5 times off −15.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Post-signature** → **Invoices**. | Heading "Invoices", the line "Match incoming vendor invoices to the payment obligations on your executed contracts.", **Add invoice**. Cards **Pending**, **Matched**, **Reconciled**, **Disputed**, **Open total** ("pending + matched"). Tabs **All**, **Pending**, **Matched**, **Reconciled**, **Disputed** with count badges. A search box "Search vendor or invoice #". |
| 2 | Click **Add invoice**. | A dialog "Add invoice", "Auto-matches against open payment obligations on your contracts.", with **Vendor name** (hint "Match works best when this matches the contract counterparty."), **Amount**, **Currency** (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD), **Invoice date** (today), **Due date** (optional), **Invoice number** (optional), **Description** (optional), and **Cancel** / **Add + match**. **Add + match** stays disabled until there is a vendor, an amount above 0 and a date. |
| 3 | Enter I-A from the table below and click **Add + match**. | "Saving…", then a dialog "Match found": "We linked this invoice to **QA INV Ledgerline — Logistics MSA** at **90%** confidence.", a card "QA INV Ledgerline onboarding fee", and **Done**. |
| 4 | Click **Done** and find the row. | Vendor "QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd", below it "#QA-INV-A · issued <Mon d, yyyy>", then the match line: the contract title (a link), the obligation's description and a "90%" chip. **Amount** "$12,000", **Due** "5d overdue" in red, **Status** "Matched", actions **Reconcile**, **Rematch**, **Dispute**. |
| 5 | Enter the other invoices of the table, one by one. | The result column of the table. When nothing reaches 40, no dialog appears (the dialog just closes) and the row reads "No match — rematch or link manually" with status "Pending" and the actions **Rematch** and **Dispute**. |
| 6 | `curl -s "$API/invoices?q=QA-INV&limit=100" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '[.data[] \| {n: .invoiceNumber, status, score: .matchScore, contract: .contract.title, obligation: .matchedObligation.description}]'` | One entry per invoice, newest invoice date first, with the statuses, scores (0.9, 0.62, …), contracts and obligations of the table. `GET /invoices/<I-A id>` adds `matchedObligation.status` "OPEN" and the contract's `type`. |
| 7 | Create I-A2 by API to read the reasons: `curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"vendorName":"QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd","invoiceNumber":"QA-INV-A2","amount":12000,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"'$(day -8)'","description":"Ledgerline onboarding fee invoice"}' \| jq '{status: .invoice.status, score: .invoice.matchScore, matchReason}'` | 201. `status` "MATCHED", `score` 0.97 (JSON may print 0.9700000000000001), `matchReason` "exact counterparty match · dueDate within 7d of invoiceDate · currency matches · weak description match · amount matches contract value". |

| Invoice | Vendor name | Amount | Currency | Invoice date | Due date | Invoice number | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I-A | QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd | 12000 | USD | `day -8` | `day -5` | QA-INV-A | Matched to QA INV Ledgerline — Logistics MSA, 90% (40 + 25 + 10 + 15) |
| I-B | QA Ledgerline | 11500 | USD | `day -30` | `day +10` | QA-INV-B | Matched, 62% (27 partial vendor + 15 date within 30 days + 10 + 10 amount within 10%); Due "Due in 10d" |
| I-C | QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd | 100000 | USD | `day -100` | `day -20` | QA-INV-C | No match, Pending: 40 + 10 − 15 (amount more than 5 times the contract's 12,000) = 35; Due "20d overdue" |
| I-C2 | QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd | 12000 | USD | `day -100` | `day +40` | QA-INV-C2 | Matched, 65%: as I-C but the amount matches the total (+15): the amount check decides; Due shows the date |
| I-D | QA Orchid Paper Co | 5000 | EUR | `day -5` | — | QA-INV-D | Matched to QA INV Orchid — Supply Agreement, 75% (40 + 10 undated quarterly obligation + 10 same currency + 15); Due "—" |
| I-D2 | QA Orchid Paper Co | 5000 | USD | `day -5` | `day +5` | QA-INV-D2 | Matched to the Orchid agreement, 65%: the currency differs from the contract's EUR; Due "Due in 5d" |
| I-F | QA Unrelated Stationers | 12000 | USD | `day -10` | — | QA-INV-F | Known issue: matched to the Ledgerline MSA at 50% with no vendor signal at all (date 25 + currency 10 + amount 15) |

**Also check**
- Refusals by API (as counsel-a): `"amount":0` or `"currency":"US"` or `"contractId":""` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid invoice","issues":[…]}`; `"invoiceDate":"yesterday"` → 400 `{"detail":"invalid invoiceDate"}`; `"contractId"` of an Org B contract or of a deleted contract → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` and nothing is created (TC-ACC-18 N1, N5, N6).
- finance-a, viewer-a, approver-a and rep-a see **Add invoice**; **Add + match** shows "You don't have permission to edit contracts." in the dialog. API: 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- admin-b: `GET /invoices/<I-A id>` → 404 `{"detail":"Invoice not found"}`, and Org B's list doesn't show Org A's invoices.
- Own scope: rep-a's list holds only invoices on contracts rep-a owns and unlinked ones rep-a entered; auto-matching for an own-scope editor stays on that user's contracts (TC-ACC-18 P3, P4, N2–N4).
- A diligence room's payment obligation is never matched (TC-WF-17 N3).
- If a webhook subscribes to `invoice.created`, it receives `{invoiceId, contractId, vendorName, amount, currency, status}` (TC-WEB-04).
- Read vendor, number, date and amount off `D-INVOICE.pdf` and add it by hand. It matches only if its vendor is (part of) the counterparty of a contract with an open payment obligation; otherwise it is Pending.

**Known limits**
- There is no invoice upload or extraction: invoices are typed in or posted to the API. A file such as `D-INVOICE.pdf` can be attached as evidence when completing a payment obligation (E2E-OBL-03).
- Obligations carry no amount; the amount is checked against the whole contract's value.
- The matcher looks at no more than 500 open payment obligations. With the full demo data loaded (`pnpm demo:seed`), another contract's obligation may win a row; read `matchReason`.
- Amounts show without cents, and "Due in <n>d" / "<n>d overdue" round to the nearest day (±1 across the day).

### E2E-INV-02 · Invoices move through Pending, Matched and Reconciled; reconciling closes the obligation, and the totals follow

**Covers:** `/invoices` · `POST /invoices/:id/reconcile` · `POST /invoices/:id/rematch` · `GET /invoices/stats` · `GET /invoices` · `GET /invoices/:id` · docs/38 TC-ACC-18
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, finance-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-INV-01 done (I-A to I-F, and I-A2).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s "$API/invoices/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` against `inv-before.json`, and the page's cards. | `pending` +1 (I-C), `matched` +7 (A, A2, B, C2, D, D2, F), `reconciled` +0, `disputed` +0, `openTotal` +169,500 (the EUR amount added as if USD). Each card and tab badge equals its figure; **Open total** is rounded (for example "$170K" above $10,000, "$1.64M" above a million). |
| 2 | Click each tab; then search "Ledgerline", "QA-INV-D", "zzqx". | **Pending**: I-C. **Matched**: the seven, newest invoice date first. Search: I-A, I-A2, I-B, I-C, I-C2 (the vendor name); then I-D and I-D2 (the invoice number); then `No invoices match "zzqx".` with "Add an invoice to auto-match it against the payment obligations on your contracts." and **Add invoice**. The search also matches the description. |
| 3 | On I-A click **Reconcile**. | The status becomes "Reconciled", the actions go, **Due** shows the plain date. **Matched** −1, **Reconciled** +1, **Open total** −12,000. |
| 4 | Sidebar → **Obligations**, search "QA INV Ledgerline". Then `curl -s "$API/obligations/qa_inv_ob1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{status, completionNote, by: .completedBy.email}'` and `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=OBLIGATION_COMPLETED&resourceId=$K_2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[].metadata]'`. | The obligation is Completed. `"COMPLETED"`, `"Reconciled via invoice <I-A id>"`, `"legal@demo.com"`. One event `{"obligationId":"qa_inv_ob1","source":"invoice_reconcile","invoiceId":"<I-A id>"}`. |
| 5 | Reconcile I-B and I-A2 (both also matched to `qa_inv_ob1`). | Both Reconciled. The obligation is unchanged (its note still names I-A) and there is still one audit event: a reconcile that closes nothing records nothing (TC-ACC-18 N8). |
| 6 | By API: reconcile I-A again; rematch I-A. | 409 `{"detail":"Already reconciled"}`; 409 `{"detail":"Cannot rematch a reconciled invoice"}`. |
| 7 | On I-F click **Rematch**. | The matcher runs again: `qa_inv_ob1` is closed, so nothing reaches 40. I-F becomes "Pending" with "No match — rematch or link manually"; its Ledgerline link is gone. By API `POST /invoices/<I-F id>/rematch` returns `{"invoice":{…,"status":"PENDING","contractId":null},"matchReason":null}`. |
| 8 | Link by hand (API only) and rematch: `curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"contractId":"'$K_3'","vendorName":"QA Manual Link Test","invoiceNumber":"QA-INV-E","amount":999,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"'$(day -2)'"}' \| jq '{status: .invoice.status, contract: .invoice.contract.title, matchReason}'`; then **Rematch** on its row. | 201, `"PENDING"`, `"QA INV Orchid — Supply Agreement"`, `null`: the manual link is kept, with no obligation. The row shows "No match — rematch or link manually" and a **Contract** link. Known issue: after **Rematch** the **Contract** link is gone; `GET /invoices/<I-E id>` shows `contractId` null. |
| 9 | Compare the cards with `GET /invoices/stats` again. | `pending` +3 (I-C, I-E, I-F), `matched` +3 (I-C2, I-D, I-D2), `reconciled` +3 (I-A, I-A2, I-B), `disputed` 0 against `inv-before.json`; `openTotal` +134,999. |
| 10 | API list parameters: `?status=RECONCILED`, `?vendor=orchid`, `?contractId=$K_2`, `?limit=2&offset=2`, `?status=PAID`. | The reconciled ones; I-D and I-D2; I-A, I-A2, I-B, I-C2; the second page of two; 400 `{"detail":"Invalid query","issues":[…]}`. |

**Also check**
- finance-a (role description "Financial visibility — view contracts; view obligations; approve") sees every action. Known issue: **Reconcile** and **Rematch** do nothing visible for finance-a, viewer-a, approver-a or rep-a (the request is refused, and the page shows no error). API: 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- admin-b: reconcile or rematch an Org A invoice → 404 `{"detail":"Invoice not found"}`.
- Paths the page doesn't offer (API only, on a throwaway invoice such as `{"vendorName":"QA Throwaway","amount":1,"invoiceDate":"'$(day -1)'"}`): reconcile a Pending invoice → 200, Reconciled, no obligation closed. Known issue: a Disputed invoice can be reconciled by API too.
- A reconciled invoice's obligation belongs to the invoice's own contract only: a mismatched link closes nothing (TC-ACC-18 N7).
- If a webhook subscribes to `invoice.reconciled`, it receives `{invoiceId, contractId, obligationId, reconciledAt}` (TC-WEB-04).

**Known limits**
- **Open total** and the counts are over the whole org (or rep-a's scope), not the current tab or search.
- **Open total** adds all currencies as one number and shows it in dollars.
- The page lists at most 100 invoices per tab, with the full count above the table.

### E2E-INV-03 · A dispute is filed with a reason, and a disputed invoice leaves the working queue

**Covers:** `/invoices` (**Dispute**) · `POST /invoices/:id/dispute` · `GET /invoices/stats`
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-INV-02 done: I-C2 and I-D2 are Matched, I-A is Reconciled.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | On I-C2 click **Dispute**. | A dialog "Dispute invoice" with "QA Ledgerline Freight Ltd · $12,000 · #QA-INV-C2", a **Reason** box marked required (placeholder "e.g. Amount exceeds the committed rate card by $4,200; PO number does not match."), the hint "Recorded on the invoice and shown to whoever picks it up next.", and **Cancel** / **Dispute invoice**. |
| 2 | Type "abc". Then replace it with "Duplicate of QA-INV-A — same shipment." and click **Dispute invoice**. | With 3 characters the button stays disabled; with 4 or more it is enabled. The dialog closes. I-C2's status is "Disputed" (red dot), the reason shows in red under the match line (at most two lines; hover shows it all), the actions are gone and **Due** shows the plain date. **Matched** −1, **Disputed** +1, **Open total** −12,000. The **Disputed** tab lists it. |
| 3 | `curl -s "$API/invoices/<I-C2 id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{status, disputeReason}'` | `"DISPUTED"`, `"Duplicate of QA-INV-A — same shipment."`. |
| 4 | On I-D2 click **Dispute**, type a reason, then click **Cancel**. Open it again and close it with the X and by clicking outside. | Nothing changes; I-D2 stays Matched. |
| 5 | By API: dispute I-A (reconciled), then I-C2 again. | 404 `{"detail":"Invoice not found or not in a disputable state"}` both times. |
| 6 | By API, with no reason: `curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices/<I-D2 id>/dispute" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'`. | `{"ok":true}`: I-D2 is Disputed with no reason shown (the page asks for one, the API doesn't). |

**Also check**
- viewer-a: **Dispute invoice** → "Could not record the dispute. Try again." (known issue: the permission reason is hidden). API 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`.
- admin-b by API → 404 `{"detail":"Invoice not found or not in a disputable state"}`.
- The page has no control to lift a dispute. Known issue: `POST /invoices/<I-D2 id>/rematch` (API) turns it back to Matched and keeps the old `disputeReason`.
- Known issue: a dispute writes no audit event and sends no webhook.
- The assistant sees the dispute reason, redacted to the org's PII mode (E2E-INV-04).

### E2E-INV-04 · The Assistant reports what a vendor billed with invoice_list

**Covers:** `invoice_list` · `/agent` · docs/38 TC-INVL-01
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b (as the identity passed to the tool) · **Needs:** agents service + model key (step 1) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-INV-01 to -03 done. The Ledgerline invoices now are: I-C (Pending, 100,000), I-C2 (Disputed, 12,000), I-B (Reconciled, 11,500), I-A and I-A2 (Reconciled, 12,000 each).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Ask: "What has QA Ledgerline Freight billed us so far, and is any of it disputed?" | An `invoice_list` chip (vendor "QA Ledgerline Freight" in its summary). The answer lists the invoices oldest first with number, date, amount and status, gives the total billed (USD 147,500), and says QA-INV-C2 is disputed: "Duplicate of QA-INV-A — same shipment." verify: wording. |
| 2 | Without the model: `tj invoice_list '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","counterpartyName":"QA Ledgerline"}' \| jq '{numbers: [.items[].invoiceNumber], total, billedTotal, byStatus, note}'` | `numbers` ["QA-INV-C","QA-INV-C2","QA-INV-B","QA-INV-A","QA-INV-A2"] (oldest invoice date first, then in the order entered), `total` 5, `billedTotal` {"USD":147500}, `byStatus` {"PENDING":1,"DISPUTED":1,"RECONCILED":3}, `note` absent. |
| 3 | By contract: `"contractId":"'$K_2'"` instead of the name. Then add `"status":"DISPUTED"`. | The invoices linked to the Ledgerline MSA: QA-INV-C2, QA-INV-B, QA-INV-A, QA-INV-A2 (I-C was never linked); then only "QA-INV-C2". |
| 4 | Nothing on file: `"counterpartyName":"Qwxzy Vorptrak"`. | `items` [], `total` 0, `note` "No invoices on file for this. Say so; do not estimate what was billed." |

**Also check**
- Own scope: step 2 with `"userId":"'$REP_A_ID'"` → no items (rep-a owns neither contract) and the same `note`.
- Another org's user naming Org A: `"userId":"'$ADMIN_B_ID'"` → 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:contract permission"}`; in chat the chip shows "permission denied" (TC-INVL-01 N3).
- Descriptions and dispute reasons are redacted to the org's PII mode (TC-INVL-01 P2, N4).
- `"status":"PAID"` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request",…}`.

### E2E-DIL-01 · A diligence room is created and filled in batches of at most 50 files

**Covers:** `/diligence` · `/diligence/:id` · `POST /diligence` · `GET /diligence` · `GET /diligence/:id` · `POST /diligence/:id/upload` · `GET /diligence/:id/documents` · docs/38 TC-ACC-05, TC-ACC-07, TC-ACC-10, TC-WF-15
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key (document analysis) · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- The room files from 6.0 (`QA-DIL-Target-MSA.pdf`, `QA-DIL-Target-NDA.docx`, `QA-DIL-Target-Scan.pdf`, `legacy.doc`, `fake.pdf`).
- For E2E-DIL-03, note the figures now: `curl -s "$API/analytics/summary" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq .totalContracts > dil-total-before.txt`.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: Sidebar → **Insights** → **Diligence**. | Heading "Diligence Rooms", the line "Bulk-upload contracts for cross-document analysis — M&A due diligence, vendor consolidation, portfolio reviews.", **New room**. With no rooms: "No diligence rooms yet.", "Create a room to bulk-upload up to 50 contracts and run cross-document analysis." and **Create first room**. |
| 2 | Click **New room**. Type a name, then press **Esc**, then click outside the dialog. | A dialog "New diligence room", "Group a batch of contracts for cross-document analysis.", **Name** (placeholder "Acme M&A — Vendor Contracts"), **Description** (optional), **Cancel** / **Create room**. With text typed, **Esc** and the outside click don't close it; an empty dialog closes on either. **Create room** is disabled while the name is empty. |
| 3 | Name "QA DIL Target Co — Vendor Contracts", description "QA diligence of Target Co's supplier contracts", **Create room**. | "Creating…", the dialog closes and the room's card is first (rooms are ordered by last update): the name, the description, "0 docs", "Updated <date>". `curl -s "$API/diligence" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '.data[0] \| {id, name, status, documentCount, progress}'` → `status` "ACTIVE", `documentCount` 0, `progress` {"done":0,"failed":0,"processing":0}. `export ROOM=<id>`. |
| 4 | Open the room (click its name or the arrow **Open room**). | `/diligence/<id>`: **All rooms** back link, the name as heading, the description, **Export CSV** disabled, cards **Documents** 0, **Extracted** 0, **Processing** 0. A drop zone "Drop contracts here or click to browse", "PDF or DOCX · up to 50 files per upload", **Browse files**. Below: "No documents in this room yet. Upload some to start." |
| 5 | Click **Browse files** and select the five files together. | The button reads "Uploading 5…". Then, in red under the drop zone: "Skipped 2 files: legacy.doc — Legacy .doc files are not supported. Open the file in Word, save it as .docx, and upload again. fake.pdf — Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT." The other three are in the room: a table "Cross-document extraction", "3 docs", rows "QA DIL Target MSA", "QA DIL Target NDA", "QA DIL Target Scan" (titles from the file names), each with a status pill and spinner ("Parsing", "Analyzing", …) while it runs. **Documents** 3, **Processing** up to 3. The drop zone shrinks to "Drop more contracts here — PDF or DOCX, up to 50 per upload" and **Browse files**. |
| 6 | Wait (1–3 minutes a document; the page refreshes every 5 s). | **Extracted** rises as each finishes; rows fill in counterparty, value, term and a risk meter. verify: the scanned PDF may end "Failed": then a **Failed** card, the banner "1 document failed to extract. Nothing below them is a model reading — open them to inspect." with **Show the 1 failed**, and the row washed red. |
| 7 | `curl -s "$API/diligence/$ROOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{documentCount, progress}'` and `curl -s "$API/diligence/$ROOM/documents" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '[.data[] \| {title, type, status, analysisStatus}]'` | `documentCount` 3 with `progress` matching the cards. Three documents in upload order, `status` "DRAFT", `type` "OTHER" until analysis sets one. |
| 8 | Back on **Diligence**, look at the card; click "3 docs". | The card shows "3 docs" and, as they apply, "<n> ready", "<n> processing", "<n> failed", "<n> queued". Clicking expands a list of up to 5 documents, each "<title>" over "<type> · <status> · <analysis state>" (the state only when not done), each opening the contract; with more than 5, "+ <n> more — open room →". |
| 9 | In the room, drag a text file onto the drop zone (copy `F6-SUPPLY.txt` to `QA-DIL-Target-Terms.txt` first). | It is added ("QA DIL Target Terms"): the server takes TXT, though **Browse files** offers only .pdf, .docx and .doc. |
| 10 | The per-upload cap: `for i in $(seq 1 51); do cp QA-DIL-Target-NDA.docx cap-$i.docx; done`, then **Browse files** and select all 51. | "Cap is 50 files per upload — please split into multiple batches." and nothing is sent. |
| 11 | The same by API: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/diligence/$ROOM/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" $(for i in $(seq 1 51); do printf -- '-F file=@cap-%s.docx ' $i; done)` | 413 `{"detail":"Too many files in one upload — cap is 50. Split into multiple requests."}`; the room still holds 4 documents. (Optional, costs 50 analyses: 50 files → 201 with `"count":50`.) |
| 12 | `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?resourceType=diligence_room&resourceId=$ROOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[] \| {action, metadata}]'` | `CONTRACT_UPLOADED` events with `{"fileCount":3,"skippedCount":2,"source":"diligence_upload"}` (and one for the drag-and-drop), and `CONTRACT_CREATED` with `{"source":"diligence_create","name":"QA DIL Target Co — Vendor Contracts"}`. |

**Also check**
- Only `fake.pdf`: the error "fake.pdf: Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT." and nothing added (API 415 with a `skipped` list; TC-ACC-05 N3). An empty file is skipped with "The uploaded file is empty.". No files by API → 400 `{"detail":"No files uploaded"}`.
- rep-a may create a room and upload (create permission, own scope); rep-a's **Diligence** lists only rooms rep-a created, and counsel-a's room by id → 404 `{"detail":"Diligence room not found"}` for the room, its documents, results and export (TC-ACC-07 N4, TC-ACC-10 P2, N4).
- viewer-a, finance-a and approver-a: **Create room** → "You don't have permission to create contracts." in the dialog; API 403 `"Missing permission: create:contract"`; the same for an upload.
- admin-b: `GET /diligence/$ROOM` and `POST …/upload` → 404 `{"detail":"Diligence room not found"}`.
- Error states: the list "Failed to load diligence rooms."; `$WEB/diligence/nope` → "Room not found." with **Back to all rooms**.
- An amendment created from a room document stays in the room (TC-WF-15 P6).

**Known limits**
- The cap is 50 files per upload, not per room; the empty page's "up to 50 contracts" means one batch. The room page lists up to 1,000 documents.
- Known issue: **Browse files** offers `.doc`, which the server always refuses, and doesn't offer `.txt`, which it accepts.

### E2E-DIL-02 · The room's comparison table and CSV export show each document's extracted terms

**Covers:** `/diligence/:id` · `GET /diligence/:id/results` · `GET /diligence/:id/export`
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** analysis finished (E2E-DIL-01) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-DIL-01 done; at least one document shows **Extracted**.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Read the table. | Columns **Title**, **Counterparty**, **Value**, **Term**, **Risk**, and an **Open →** link per row. Under a title: its type in capitals (not shown for OTHER), a status pill while not done (washed red when Failed), and "<nn>% confidence" with a hollow diamond when the model's confidence is under 70% (hover: "Model confidence <nn>% — verify against the document"). **Counterparty** or "—"; **Value** such as "USD 250K" or "—"; **Term** the effective date over "→ <expiry>"; **Risk** a meter with its score, or "—" (hover: "Extraction failed — never scored" on a failed row, "Not scored" otherwise). |
| 2 | If a row failed: **Show the <n> failed**, then **Show all documents**. | Only the failed rows, the header reading "<n> failed of <m>"; then all rows. With a filter on and nothing failed: "No failed documents — every extraction in this room succeeded." |
| 3 | `curl -s "$API/diligence/$ROOM/results" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{total, room, rows: [.data[] \| {title, analysisStatus, riskScore, autoRenew, terminationNotice, governingLaw, paymentTerms}]}'` | One row per document, `room` {id, name}. `governingLaw` and `autoRenew` are filled when the analysis found them. Known issue: `terminationNotice` and `paymentTerms` are null for analysed documents (the analysis stores `noticePeriodDays` and `paymentTermsDays`, which these columns don't read). |
| 4 | Click **Export CSV**. | A download named `diligence-QA_DIL_Target_Co_Vendor_Contracts.csv` with the columns Title, Type, Status, Counterparty, Value, Currency, Effective Date, Expiry Date, Jurisdiction, Risk Score, Auto Renew, Termination Notice, Governing Law, Payment Terms, Analysis Status, Summary, one line per document, failed and running ones included. Known issue: **Risk Score** is the page's score times 100 (a meter reading 42 exports as 4200). |
| 5 | Click **Open →** on a row. | The document's contract page opens and works as any contract's (rail, review, obligations on request). |

**Also check**
- `curl -s "$API/diligence/$ROOM/export?format=xlsx" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` → 400 `{"detail":"Only csv is supported (Excel coming in V1.1)"}`. The API's own file name is "<room name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv"; the page saves it as `diligence-<room name>.csv`.
- With the API stopped, **Export CSV** shows "Could not export this room — try again." for 5 seconds.
- rep-a and admin-b → 404 `{"detail":"Diligence room not found"}` for `/results` and `/export`.

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|

| 2 | Sidebar → **Renewals**, and `curl -s "$API/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq --arg d "$DOC" '[.data[] \| select(.id==$d)] \| length'`; `GET /renewals/stats` against `dil-ren.json`. | Not on the page, `0` in the API, stats unchanged, though it is executed and expires in 45 days (TC-WF-16 N3, N4). |
| 3 | `curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/renewals" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"force":true}'`, then Mailpit. | No alert for "QA DIL Target MSA" (TC-WF-16 N5). |
| 4 | Extract its obligations: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$DOC/extract-obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{ok, n: (.obligations\|length)}'`; then `curl -s "$API/obligations?contractId=$DOC" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq .total`, `curl -s "$API/contracts/$DOC/obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '.data\|length'`, and the Obligations page (search "QA DIL Target"). | `ok` true with some obligations. Naming the contract shows them (`total` and the rail's list, TC-WF-17 P1); the Obligations page, its counts and its CSV don't (TC-WF-17 N1). |

| 6 | Sidebar → **Assistant** → **New conversation**: "Find the QA DIL Target MSA." | The assistant doesn't list or cite the room document (TC-WF-15 N6). |

### E2E-DIL-04 · A room is renamed, archived and deleted (API only), taking its documents with it

**Covers:** `PATCH /diligence/:id` · `DELETE /diligence/:id` · `GET /diligence/:id` · `/diligence`
**Roles:** counsel-a, contracts-a, rep-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-DIL-01 to -03 done (`$ROOM`, `$DOC`). The web app has no control to rename, archive or delete a room; these are API calls.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Rename: `curl -s -X PATCH "$API/diligence/$ROOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"QA DIL Target Co — Final"}'` | `{"ok":true}`. The room page's heading shows the new name within 5 s, the **Diligence** list within 30 s. |
| 2 | Archive: `-d '{"status":"ARCHIVED"}'`. | `{"ok":true}`. The card and the room page show the pill "Archived". Known issue: the room still accepts uploads. |
| 3 | Reactivate: `-d '{"status":"ACTIVE"}'`. | The pill is gone. |
| 4 | Refusals: `-d '{"status":"CLOSED"}'` and `-d '{"name":""}'` as counsel-a; the rename as rep-a and as viewer-a. | 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request","issues":[…]}` twice; 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"` twice. |
| 5 | Delete as contracts-a, then as rep-a: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/diligence/$ROOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A"`. | 403 `"Missing permission: delete:contract"` both times (contracts-a has no delete permission; rep-a neither, even for its own rooms). |
| 6 | Delete as counsel-a. | `204`. The room disappears from **Diligence**; its page shows "Room not found."; `GET /diligence/$ROOM` → 404 `{"detail":"Diligence room not found"}`. |
| 7 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/$DOC" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq .detail` and `sql "SELECT count(*) FROM contracts WHERE \"diligenceRoomId\"='$ROOM' AND \"deletedAt\" IS NULL"`. | `"Contract not found"` and `0`: the room's documents were deleted with it. A second DELETE → 404 `{"detail":"Diligence room not found"}`. |

**Known limits**
- Known issue: renaming, archiving and deleting a room write no audit event.
- Deletion is a soft delete: rows stay in the database with `deletedAt` set.


### E2E-ANL-01 · Every card and chart on the Analytics page counts what its label says

**Covers:** `/analytics` · `GET /analytics/summary` · `GET /analytics/distributions` · `GET /analytics/timeseries` · `GET /analytics/top-counterparties` · docs/38 TC-WF-16
**Roles:** admin-a, viewer-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- `$W6` from 6.0. Nobody else changes Org A's contracts during this journey (it compares figures before and after).
- A snapshot helper, and the "before" snapshot:

```bash
anl() { T=${2:-$ADMIN_A}; {
  curl -s "$API/analytics/summary" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" | jq -c '{totalContracts, executedContracts, pendingApprovals, expiringSoon, highRiskOpen, executedTotalValue, executedTotalCurrency}'
  curl -s "$API/analytics/distributions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" | jq -c '{byStatus: (.byStatus|sort_by(.key)), byType: (.byType|sort_by(.key)), byRisk}'
  curl -s "$API/analytics/timeseries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" | jq -c '.series[-1]'
  curl -s "$API/analytics/top-counterparties?limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" | jq -c '[.data[] | select(.counterparty|startswith("QA ANL"))]'
} > "anl-$1.txt"; }
anl before
```

- The fixture, as admin-a: two executed MSAs for one counterparty (one expiring within 90 days) and a draft NDA made high-risk and sent for approval.

```bash
cat > qa-anl.csv <<CSV
title,type,status,counterpartyname,value,currency,expirydate
QA ANL Exec One,MSA,executed,QA ANL Counterparty,9000000,USD,$(day +30)
QA ANL Exec Two,MSA,executed,QA ANL Counterparty,50000,USD,$(day +200)
QA ANL Draft,NDA,draft,QA ANL Other,,USD,
CSV
bulk qa-anl.csv A "$ADMIN_A"      # A_2, A_3, A_4
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$A_4" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"riskScore":75}' | jq -c '{riskScore}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$A_4/submit-approval" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"workflowDefinitionId\":\"$W6\"}" | jq -c '{status}'
anl after; diff anl-before.txt anl-after.txt
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Read the diff. | `totalContracts` +3, `executedContracts` +2, `pendingApprovals` +1, `expiringSoon` +1, `highRiskOpen` +1, `executedTotalValue` +9050000. `byStatus`: EXECUTED +2, PENDING_APPROVAL +1. `byType`: MSA +2, NDA +1. `byRisk`: high +1, none +2. The last month of the series: `created` +3, `executed` +2. Top counterparties: `[{"counterparty":"QA ANL Counterparty","counterpartyId":null,"count":2,"value":9050000,"currency":"USD"}]`. (The PATCH printed `{"riskScore":75}`, the submission `{"status":"PENDING"}`.) |
| 2 | As admin-a: Sidebar → **Insights** → **Analytics**. | Heading "Analytics", "Portfolio KPIs, cycle time, and contract distribution at a glance." Under "Portfolio — as of now" five cards, each the API's `summary` figure: **Total contracts**; **Executed** with "USD <x>M total"; **Pending approvals** with "Org-wide, every approver"; **Expiring (90d)** with "Executed, expiry inside 90d"; **High risk + open** with "Score > 60, not executed". Each reflects step 1's change. |
| 3 | "Throughput — decided in the window" and its **Window:** select (**Last 30 days**, **Last 90 days** selected, **Last 180 days**, **Last year**). | **Cycle time**: the average days from creation to execution of contracts executed in the window (for example "12.4d", "<1d" under a day, "—" when none), subtitle "Median <x> · created → executed". **Approval acceptance**: "<n>%", "Approved ÷ (Approved + Rejected)". **On-time execution**: "<n>%", "% executed within 14d of creation". The two QA ANL executed contracts were created and executed in the same second, so they pull cycle time toward "<1d" and count as on time. |
| 4 | Change the window to **Last 30 days**, then **Last year**. | Only the three throughput figures can change; the cards above and the charts below don't (they are the whole portfolio now). The request is `GET /analytics/summary?days=30`. |
| 5 | "Distribution — whole portfolio": **Monthly contract volume** ("Last 12 months · ▸ marks the month in progress"). Hover the last point. | Twelve months, the last label ending "▸". Two lines: **Created** (dashed, round points) and **Executed** (solid, square points); the legend shows the same shapes. The tooltip of the last month shows Created and Executed, each 3 and 2 higher than before the fixture. |
| 6 | **Status distribution** ("<n> states · <m> contracts"). | One bar per status label, largest first, the count printed at the bar's end, coloured like the status pills. "Executed" is 2 higher, "Awaiting approval" 1 higher; statuses sharing a label ("In review") are one bar. `<m>` equals **Total contracts**. |
| 7 | **Risk distribution** ("<n> scored contracts"). | Bars "<30 (low)", "30–59 (medium)", "60–79 (high)", "80+ (critical)"; "60–79 (high)" is 1 higher. The footer reads "<n> more (<p>% of the portfolio) carry no risk score and are not plotted.", its count 2 higher. |
| 8 | **Contract types** ("<n> types", or "Top 10 of <n>"). | Types in words ("MSA", "NDA", "Vendor agreement", "License"…), largest first; MSA +2, NDA +1. With more than 10 types, the footer names the rest: "<k> smaller types are not shown: <Type> (<count>), …". |
| 9 | **Top counterparties by executed value**. Hover a **Total ACV** cell. | Columns **Counterparty**, **Contracts**, **Total ACV**, and a **View →** link. "QA ANL Counterparty · 2 · USD 9.05M", its **View** cell "—" (an imported name, not a counterparty record). The hover shows the exact figure ("USD 9,050,000"). A seeded counterparty such as "Acme Corporation" has **View →**. |
| 10 | Click each card, then a **View →**. | **Total contracts** → `/contracts`. **Executed** → `/contracts?status=EXECUTED` (the list filtered to Executed). **Pending approvals** → `/approvals`. **Expiring (90d)** → `/renewals?bucket=next_90`: known issue, the page opens on **Next year**. **High risk + open** → `/contracts?riskBand=high` (scores of 67 and up, any status: a neighbourhood of the card's set, as its subtitle warns). **View →** → `/contracts?counterpartyId=<id>&filterLabel=<name>`, the list filtered to that counterparty. |

**Also check**
- API bounds: `GET /analytics/summary?days=6` or `?days=3651` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid query","issues":[…]}`. `GET /analytics/top-counterparties?limit=3` returns up to 5 rows and `?limit=100` up to 50. `GET /analytics/timeseries` returns 12 entries `{month "YYYY-MM", label "<Mon YY>", created, executed}`.
- viewer-a sees the same figures (org scope). rep-a's are its own (E2E-ANL-02).
- Diligence-room documents move no figure (E2E-DIL-03, TC-WF-16); nor do deleted contracts.
- As admin-b (a new org): every card 0, the throughput figures "—", the charts "Nothing to plot yet." and the table "No executed contracts yet." Known issue: **Monthly contract volume** still draws twelve zero points; its own empty text "No contracts created in the last 12 months." never shows.

**Known limits**
- What each number counts: **Total contracts**: every contract of the org, whatever its status, not deleted and not in a diligence room. **Executed**: those with status Executed; the subtitle adds their values across currencies and labels the sum with the most common currency. **Pending approvals**: approvals pending, in progress or escalated, for every approver. **Expiring (90d)**: executed contracts expiring from today to 90 days ahead. **High risk + open**: stored risk score above 60 and status not Executed, Expired, Terminated or Archived. **Cycle time** and **On-time execution** use the contract's last update as its execution time, so a later edit of an executed contract lengthens it. **Monthly contract volume** counts contracts by the month they were created; its "Executed" line is those of them that are executed now.
- Known issue: the risk bands here (30, 60, 80) aren't the app's (34, 67), and scores stored on the old 0–1 scale (the seeded demo contracts, such as "Umbrella Corp — Vendor Agreement" at 0.65, shown as 65 on its page) all land in "<30 (low)" and never count as high risk.
- Known issue (verify): with the API running west of UTC, the month labels of **Monthly contract volume** are one month behind (a label is made from a UTC date and printed in the server's time zone).

**Covers:** `/analytics` · `/obligations` · `/renewals` · `/invoices` · `/diligence` · `GET /analytics/summary` · `GET /analytics/distributions` · `GET /analytics/top-counterparties` · `GET /obligations/stats` · `GET /renewals/stats` · `GET /invoices/stats` · `GET /diligence` · docs/38 TC-ACC-07, TC-ACC-10


Compare **Total contracts** with `sql "SELECT count(*) FROM contracts WHERE \"ownerId\"='$REP_A_ID' AND \"deletedAt\" IS NULL AND \"diligenceRoomId\" IS NULL"`. | Equal: only rep-a's contracts are counted (TC-ACC-10 P4). **Expiring (90d)** includes "QA ANL Rep Exec". The top-counterparties table shows "QA ANL Counterparty · 1 · USD 5K"; admin-a's shows it with 3 and "USD 9.05M" (9,055,000 shown with two decimals). The charts count only rep-a's contracts. |

| 7 | The sidebar badges on **Obligations** and **Renewals**. | They count rep-a's contracts only. |

**Also check**
- rep-a opening counsel-a's contract, obligation, invoice or room by id → 404 ("Contract not found", "Obligation not found", "Invoice not found", "Diligence room not found"; TC-ACC-07).
- rep-a may create and fill a room but not rename or delete it: `PATCH` → 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`, `DELETE` → 403 `"Missing permission: delete:contract"`.
- rep-a can't complete obligations, reconcile invoices, run compliance checks or log renewal decisions, even on its own contracts (no `edit:contract`): see the permission table in 6.0.

### E2E-CMP-01 · A compliance check reports each framework's required clauses as present, partial, missing or risky

**Covers:** `/contracts/:id` (details rail → **Compliance**) · `POST /contracts/:id/compliance-check` · `GET /contracts/:id/compliance` · agent service `compliance`
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- `F6-DPA-WEAK.txt` from 6.0, and the repository's strong processing addendum. Upload both as counsel-a and wait for their analysis (a compliance check runs on any status):

```bash
export WEAK=$(upload F6-DPA-WEAK.txt text/plain "QA CMP Weak DPA" "QA Weak Processor Ltd"); waitdone $WEAK
export TYRELL=$(upload <repo>/apps/api/scripts/fixtures/ai-demo/dpa-tyrell.txt text/plain "QA CMP Tyrell DPA" "Tyrell Corporation"); waitdone $TYRELL
cid() { curl -s -G "$API/contracts" --data-urlencode "search=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=20" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r --arg t "$1" '.data[] | select(.title==$t) | .id'; }
export CALDERA=$(cid "Caldera Health Networks — SOW #07 (HIPAA EHR Integration)")   # seeded by pnpm dev:setup
```

The four frameworks and the requirement ids the checker uses: GDPR (`gdpr_processing_scope`, `gdpr_documented_instructions`, `gdpr_confidentiality`, `gdpr_security_measures`, `gdpr_subprocessor_consent`, `gdpr_data_subject_rights`, `gdpr_breach_notification`, `gdpr_deletion_return`, `gdpr_audit_rights`, `gdpr_international_transfers`); HIPAA (`hipaa_permitted_uses`, `hipaa_safeguards`, `hipaa_breach_notification`, `hipaa_subcontractor_flowdown`, `hipaa_minimum_necessary`, `hipaa_individual_rights`, `hipaa_termination_return`, `hipaa_hhs_access`); SOX (`sox_audit_rights`, `sox_records_retention`, `sox_internal_controls`, `sox_financial_accuracy`, `sox_whistleblower_nonretaliation`); CCPA, which covers CPRA (`ccpa_no_sale`, `ccpa_purpose_limitation`, `ccpa_consumer_rights`, `ccpa_subcontractor_flowdown`, `ccpa_compliance_certification`). Each check is **present**, **partial** (the clause exists but is weaker than required), **missing**, or **risky** (the wording works against the requirement).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/$WEAK/compliance" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A"` | `{"report":null}`: no check has run. |
| 2 | As counsel-a open `$WEB/contracts/$WEAK` and find the **Compliance** section in the details rail. | "No compliance check run yet. Scan this contract against GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, and CCPA — every finding grounded in a verbatim clause quote with a concrete fix." and **Run compliance check**. |
| 3 | Click **Run compliance check**. | "Checking…" for 20–60 s. Then the section shows a summary paragraph; if any finding is critical, a red line "<n> critical finding(s) — review before signature"; and one row per framework: the name, a status chip ("compliant", "gaps", "non-compliant" or "n/a", in capitals) and, for an applicable framework, "<score>/100". The section title's count is the number of applicable frameworks that aren't compliant. verify: GDPR is "gaps" or "non-compliant" with a score under 100; HIPAA, SOX and CCPA are "n/a" (the model decides applicability). The footer reads "Checked <date>" and **re-run**. |
| 4 | Click the GDPR row. | It expands to the requirements that aren't present, each "<requirement> · <status> §<section>", a "HIGH" or "CRITICAL" chip on high or critical gaps, the finding, the quoted clause in quotation marks (for partial and risky ones), and "→ <recommendation>"; the last line "+ <n> requirements satisfied". verify: sub-processors **risky** (clause 5 lets the processor add any sub-processor without notice); breach notification **partial** (no time limit); return or deletion of data and audit rights **missing**; the rest present. |
| 5 | Click the HIPAA row. | An italic line saying why HIPAA doesn't apply (verify: no protected health information), or "Not applicable to this contract." when the model gave no reason. |
| 6 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/$WEAK/compliance" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '{overall: .report.overall, requested: .report.frameworksRequested, checkedAt: .report.checkedAt, gdpr: [.report.frameworks[] \| select(.framework=="GDPR") \| .checks[] \| {id, status, severity, quote: (.quote != null)}]}'` | `overall` `{status, summary, criticalCount}`, `requested` ["GDPR","HIPAA","SOX","CCPA"], `checkedAt` now. Every check id comes from the list above; `status` one of present, partial, missing, risky; `severity` low, medium, high or critical; missing checks have no quote. At most 20 checks per framework. |
| 7 | The strong addendum: open `$TYRELL`, **Run compliance check**, expand GDPR. | verify: GDPR "compliant" (or "gaps" with one or two items) and a high score; the expanded list shows the checks, all or nearly all present. |
| 8 | A healthcare contract: open `$CALDERA`, **Run compliance check**. | verify: HIPAA is applicable, with a score and checks (the SOW concerns protected health information); GDPR likely "n/a". |
| 9 | One framework by API: `curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$WEAK/compliance-check" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"frameworks":["GDPR"]}' \| jq '{ok, fws: [.report.frameworks[].framework], requested: .report.frameworksRequested}'`. Reload the contract page. | `{"ok":true,"fws":["GDPR"],"requested":["GDPR"]}`. The stored report is replaced: the rail now lists GDPR only. |
| 10 | `curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=COMPLIANCE_CHECKED&resourceId=$WEAK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.events[].metadata]'` | One event per run, newest first, for example `{"frameworks":["GDPR"],"status":"gaps","criticalCount":0,"trigger":"manual"}`. |
| 11 | The agent service directly: without the secret `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST $AGENTS/check_compliance -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"plainText":"x"}'`; with it, `-d '{"plainText":""}'`; then `jq -Rs '{plainText: ., frameworks: ["PCI"]}' F6-DPA-WEAK.txt \| curl -s -X POST $AGENTS/check_compliance -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- \| jq '[.frameworks[].framework]'`. | `{"error":"unauthorized"}` 401. Then `{"frameworks":[],"overall":{"status":"not_applicable","summary":"Empty contract text — nothing to check.","criticalCount":0}}`. Then all four frameworks: an unknown name falls back to every framework (the API refuses it first, see below). |

**Also check**
- Refusals: `-d '{"frameworks":["PCI"]}'` or `-d '{"frameworks":"GDPR"}'` → 400 `{"detail":"frameworks must be a subset of: GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, CCPA"}`. Known issue: `-d '{"frameworks":[]}'` → 502 `{"detail":"compliance agent failed","upstream":"no valid frameworks requested"}` instead of a 400.
- A contract with no document (`$NT_2`) → 400 `{"detail":"No version to check"}`; a version without text → 400 `{"detail":"No plaintext on current version"}`.
- viewer-a, finance-a, approver-a, rep-a: **Run compliance check** (and **re-run**) → "You don't have permission to edit contracts." under the button. API: 403 `"Missing permission: edit:contract"`. They can read the report (`GET …/compliance`).
- rep-a on counsel-a's contract → both routes 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`; admin-b → 404.
- When the model call fails, the API answers 502 `{"detail":"compliance agent failed","upstream":"compliance_failed: …"}` and keeps the previous report. With the agents service stopped: 500. Cost cap: 429 with the cost-cap message.

**Known limits**
- The verdicts are the model's, against a fixed list of requirements; run to run, a status or score can differ.
- The model reads the first 60,000 characters.
- The check doesn't run by itself; nothing re-runs it when the contract changes.
- Known issue: the compliance package's audit trail doesn't list compliance checks (E2E-CMP-02).

### E2E-CMP-02 · The compliance package PDF carries the cover, the signatures, an audit trail checked against the hash chain, and the contract document

**Covers:** `/contracts/:id` (**Actions** → **Compliance package (PDF)**) · `GET /contracts/:id/compliance-export` · docs/38 TC-OPS-02
**Roles:** counsel-a, viewer-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** nothing extra (step 7 needs `psql` access through `sql`) · **Time:** ~25 min

**Preconditions**
- `$F6` (executed; uploaded, corrected, approved, obligations extracted, completed and reminded in earlier journeys).
- Two seeded executed contracts: "Globex — NDA" has a completed signature request (signer Alex Signer; the seed gives it to the second demo contract it creates, so if yours differs use any contract signed through the signing flow); "Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement" (the AI demo seed) has a PDF as its document. `export GLOBEX=$(cid "Globex — NDA") ACME=$(cid "Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement")` (`cid` from E2E-CMP-01).
- To read a PDF's text in the shell: `pdftotext` (poppler); or open the file in any PDF viewer.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a open `$WEB/contracts/$F6`, click **Actions** at the top right, then **Compliance package (PDF)**. | A download `compliance-QA_F6_Master_Supply_Agreement-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`. |
| 2 | Page 1. | A green band, "COMPLIANCE PACKAGE", the title, "MSA · EXECUTED" (the type the analysis gave), then **Contract ID**, **Counterparty** "QA Harbor Components Ltd", **Effective date**, **Expiry date** (<day +110>), **Value** ("USD <n>" or "—"), **Jurisdiction**, **Owner** "Legal Counsel (legal@demo.com)", **Current version** "v1", **Organization** "Demo Org, Inc.", **Generated at** (an ISO time). Footer "Demo Org, Inc. · CLM Compliance Export · Page 1". |
| 3 | The next page. | No "SIGNATURE EVIDENCE" page: `$F6` was marked executed, never e-signed. "AUDIT TRAIL" with the line "<N> events recorded · each checked against the organization's hash chain: intact", and a table **When (UTC)**, **Action**, **Actor**, **Hash**, oldest first. Rows such as "Document uploaded", "Viewed", "Contract updated" (the corrections), "Approval submitted", "Approval decided", "Status changed" (to Executed), "Obligations extracted", "Obligation completed", "Obligation went overdue" (actor "system"); each hash "<10 characters>… ok". The footer's page number counts on. |
| 4 | Download the package of `$GLOBEX` (the same menu). | Page 2 "SIGNATURE EVIDENCE": "Request <last 12 characters of its id>", "Sent <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC · Completed <…> UTC", and a box for the signer: "Alex Signer", "Authorised Signatory", "signer@counterparty.test", "Signed <…> UTC", "Typed name: Alex Signer" (no IP line: the seed stored none). |
| 5 | Download the package of `$ACME`. | After the audit trail, the contract's own PDF pages follow (its latest version is a PDF). The title reads "Acme Corporation  Master Services Agreement": characters outside plain ASCII (the dash) are dropped. |
| 6 | By API: `curl -s -D - -o pkg.pdf "$API/contracts/$F6/compliance-export" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" \| grep -i -E '^content-(type\|disposition)'` and `pdftotext pkg.pdf - \| head -40`. | `content-type: application/pdf`; `content-disposition: attachment; filename="compliance-QA_F6_Master_Supply_Agreement-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf"`. The text of steps 2–3. viewer-a may download it. |
| 7 | The chain check (destructive: restore it at the end). Pick one of `$F6`'s events and alter it: `EV=$(sql "SELECT id FROM audit_events WHERE \"resourceId\"='$F6' AND action='OBLIGATION_EXTRACTED' ORDER BY \"createdAt\" LIMIT 1"); sql "SELECT coalesce(\"userAgent\",'NULL') FROM audit_events WHERE id='$EV'"; sql "UPDATE audit_events SET \"userAgent\"='qa-tamper' WHERE id='$EV'"`. Download the package again. | The audit line, in red: "<N> events recorded · CHAIN CHECK FAILED at <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC (the event was altered after it was recorded)". That row's hash reads "<10 characters>… FAILED" in red; the other rows still "ok". Admin → **Organization** → **Audit Log** → **Verify integrity** reports the break too (TC-OPS-02). |
| 8 | Restore it: `sql "UPDATE audit_events SET \"userAgent\"=NULL WHERE id='$EV'"` (or the value step 7 printed), and download again. | "… each checked against the organization's hash chain: intact" again. |

**Also check**
- On a contract that isn't executed, **Actions** has no **Compliance package (PDF)**. The API still returns a package for it (its subtitle then reads, for example, "MSA · DRAFT").
- rep-a on counsel-a's contract → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`; admin-b → 404; an unknown id → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`.
- If the stored PDF can't be read, the package ends with a page "SIGNED CONTRACT (UNAVAILABLE)" and "Source PDF could not be loaded: <reason>".
- Known issue: when the download fails, the menu shows nothing (the error only goes to the browser console).

**Known limits**
- The trail lists at most 500 events, oldest first, and only contract lifecycle actions (created, updated, deleted, viewed, uploaded, status changed, versions, approvals, signatures, obligations, comments, share links, redline analysis). Known issue: compliance checks and renewal decisions aren't among them.
- The appended document is the latest version's file when it is a PDF, signed or not; after an editor save (a version without a file) nothing is appended.
- Events recorded before hashing began are counted as "(<n> older events predate hashing)" and marked "— (no hash)"; a fresh stack has none.

### E2E-CMP-03 · The Assistant answers "is this contract GDPR compliant?" from the stored report with compliance_get

**Covers:** `compliance_get` · `/agent` · `GET /contracts/:id/compliance`
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b (as the identity passed to the tool) · **Needs:** agents service + model key (steps 1–2) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-CMP-01 done (`$WEAK` has a GDPR-only report, `$TYRELL` a full one). `$GLOBEX` has never been checked.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a: **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Ask: "Is the QA CMP Tyrell DPA GDPR compliant? What, if anything, is missing?" | A `contract_search` chip, then `compliance_get`. The answer states GDPR's status and score from the stored report and lists any gaps with their recommendations, quoting the clauses; it doesn't re-run the check. verify: wording. |
| 2 | Ask: "Is the Globex — NDA GDPR compliant?" | A `compliance_get` chip. The answer says no compliance check has been run on it and that one can be run from the Compliance section of the contract page; it doesn't guess. |
| 3 | Without the model: `tj compliance_get '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$WEAK'"}' \| jq '{title, type, fws: [.report.frameworks[] \| {framework, status, score}], overall: .report.overall.status, note}'` | `title` "QA CMP Weak DPA", the frameworks and statuses of `GET /contracts/$WEAK/compliance`, `note` absent. |
| 4 | The same for `$GLOBEX`. | `report` null and `note` "No compliance check has been run on this contract yet. The user can run one from the Compliance section on the contract page (or POST /contracts/:id/compliance-check)." |

**Also check**
- An unknown or other-org contract id → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found in this org"}`; in chat the chip shows "contract not found".
- rep-a (`"userId":"'$REP_A_ID'"`) on counsel-a's contract → 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found in this org"}`. `"userId":"'$ADMIN_B_ID'"` with Org A → 403 `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have view:contract permission"}`.
- Missing `contractId` → 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request",…}`.
## 7. The AI assistant and AI administration

This section tests the AI assistant everywhere it appears: the **Ask** side panel on every signed-in page, the full-page
**Assistant** at `/agent`, and the AI actions inside the contract editor. It drives every one of the assistant's 31
tools (the brief counted 32; the tool registry `apps/agents/app/tools/__init__.py` and `agent-tools.txt` list 31), the
rules that keep its answers honest, amended terms and the renewal-prep brief, skills, per-contract Q&A, and the admin
controls: model routing, bring-your-own keys, usage, the daily cost cap, the AI audit log and the personal-data mode.
Run it in this order: **7.0** first (it uploads fixtures whose analysis takes a few minutes), then **E2E-AIADM-01**
(proves a model answers on the default settings), then **E2E-AI-01 to E2E-AI-16**, then **E2E-SKL-01 to 03**, and last
**E2E-AIADM-02 to 06**, which change keys, the cost cap and the privacy mode and put them back when they finish.
Model answers vary from run to run. The checks look at which tools ran (the trace), what the tools returned, fixed
product wording, and numbers you can read off the data, never at the model's exact words. When a model-dependent check
fails, repeat the prompt once in a new thread before filing it, and file the prompt, the trace and the answer together.

### 7.0 Before you start (commands, sample files and fixtures for this section)

**Needs:** the §0 stack with the agents service at `http://localhost:8002` and at least one model key
(`GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) in both `apps/api/.env` and the agents service's env;
Elasticsearch running and indexed (for `portfolio_search`); an embedding key (OpenAI, Google or Voyage) for E2E-AI-15;
`jq`. Mailpit only for E2E-AI-08.

**What the §0 seed gives this section** (all in Org A, all owned by admin-a unless said otherwise):
- Contracts with full document text (from `apps/api/scripts/seed-ai-demo.ts`): **Acme Corporation — Master Services
  Agreement** (MSA, Executed, USD 250,000, Delaware law; §3.2 auto-renews for 1-year terms unless 90 days' notice of
  non-renewal; §3.3 termination for convenience on 90 days' notice; §9.2 each party's aggregate liability capped at
  $500,000, not applying to §8 indemnification, §5 confidentiality breaches, or gross negligence / wilful misconduct;
  §2.3 payment within 30 days; §10 $5,000,000 professional liability insurance; §11.2 JAMS arbitration in Wilmington),
  **Globex — Mutual NDA**, **Umbrella Corporation — SLA** (99.9% uptime), and six SOWs (Stark, Vertex Cloud, Caldera
  Health, Ironbridge, Lumen Bio, Helix Systems).
- Contracts with a short summary only (from `lib/demo-workspace.ts`): Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement, Globex —
  NDA, Initech — Software License Agreement (Approved), Umbrella Corp — Vendor Agreement (Under negotiation, USD
  120,000), Stark Industries — SOW #12, Wayne Enterprises — Partnership Agreement (Pending approval, USD 500,000), Pied
  Piper — SLA, Dunder Mifflin — Employment Agreement, Veridian Dynamics — Research NDA (Expired), **Massive Dynamic —
  Cloud Services MSA** (Draft, USD 300,000).
- 20 published templates (e.g. **Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement**), the universal playbook, 9 built-in skills, and one
  approval workflow, **Standard approval**, whose single step **Legal review** goes to the LEGAL_COUNSEL user
  (counsel-a).
- No matters, intake requests, custom fields, obligations or invoices. The journeys below create what they need.

**Shell setup** (run once, after §0's `login` helpers have set the tokens):

```bash
export AGENTS=http://localhost:8002
export INT=${API%/v1}/internal/ai            # the internal tool routes the agents service calls
id_of() { curl -s "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" | jq -r .id; }
export ADMIN_A_ID=$(id_of $ADMIN_A) COUNSEL_A_ID=$(id_of $COUNSEL_A) REP_A_ID=$(id_of $REP_A) VIEWER_A_ID=$(id_of $VIEWER_A)
day() { date -v"$1"d +%F 2>/dev/null || date -d "$1 days" +%F; }        # day +75 → the date 75 days from today
cid() { curl -s "$API/contracts?limit=100&search=$(jq -rn --arg q "$1" '$q|@uri')" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \
        | jq -r --arg t "$1" '.data[] | select(.title==$t) | .id' | head -1; }
export C_ACME=$(cid "Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement") C_MASSIVE=$(cid "Massive Dynamic — Cloud Services MSA")
export C_UMBRELLA_VA=$(cid "Umbrella Corp — Vendor Agreement") C_GLOBEX=$(cid "Globex — Mutual NDA")
echo $C_ACME $C_MASSIVE $C_UMBRELLA_VA $C_GLOBEX            # four ids, none empty
```

Command **ASK** — one assistant turn over the API, as the web pages send it. It prints each tool call as
`[tool <name> <args>]`, each result as `[result <name> ok=…] <first 200 characters>`, each write proposal as
`[card <name> reversible=…] <summary>`, the answer, and the final `[done <provider>/<model> tier=… source=…]` line.
Turns sent this way are not saved as threads (only the web pages save threads).

```bash
ask() {  # ask <token> "<message>" [<session id: reuse it for a follow-up turn>]
  curl -sN -X POST "$API/agent/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
    -d "$(jq -nc --arg m "$2" --arg s "${3:-qa7-$RANDOM$RANDOM}" '{message:$m, sessionId:$s, agentMode:true}')" \
  | sed -n 's/^data: \({.*\)$/\1/p' \
  | jq -rj 'if .type=="token" then .delta
      elif .type=="tool_call_start" then "\n[tool " + .name + " " + (.args|tojson) + "]\n"
      elif .type=="tool_call_result" then "[result " + .name + " ok=" + (.ok|tostring) + "] " + (.result[0:200]) + "\n"
      elif .type=="tool_call_awaiting_confirmation" then "\n[card " + .name + " reversible=" + (.reversible|tostring) + "] " + (.preview.summary // "") + "\n"
      elif .type=="error" then "\n[error] " + .error + "\n"
      elif .type=="done" then "\n[done " + (.provider // "") + "/" + (.model // "") + " tier=" + (.tier // "") + " source=" + (.source // "") + "]\n"
      else empty end'; echo; }
```

Command **TJ** — call one internal tool route exactly as the agents service does. What it prints is what the model is
given (before the model's untrusted-data framing):

```bash
tj() { curl -s -X POST "$INT/tools/$1" -H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET" -H "x-internal-service: agents" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$2"; }
```

Fixture helpers (upload, analysis status, field verification, approval through **Standard approval**, status change,
invoices):

```bash
upload() {  # upload <token> <file> "<title>" "<counterparty>" [<parent id, uploads it as an amendment>]  → prints the new id
  curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -F "file=@$2;type=text/plain" -F "title=$3" -F "counterpartyName=$4" \
    ${5:+-F "parentContractId=$5"} ${5:+-F "relationshipType=amendment"} | jq -r .id; }
analysis() { curl -s "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r .analysisStatus; }
qverify()  { curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/review-queue/$1/verify" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2"; }
submit()   { curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$1/submit-approval" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' \
             | jq -r '"\(.instanceId) \(.steps[0].id // .status // .error)"'; }
decide()   { curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/approvals/$1/decide" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
             -d "{\"stepId\":\"$2\",\"decision\":\"$3\",\"comment\":\"QA7\"}"; }
approve()  { set -- $(submit "$1"); [ "$2" = "AUTO_APPROVED" ] || decide "$1" "$2" APPROVED; }   # prints 200 (nothing when auto-approved)
patchc()   { curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2" | jq -c '{status, detail}'; }
inv()      { curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$1" | jq -c '{number: .invoice.invoiceNumber, id: .invoice.id}'; }
```

`D7-LICENCE.txt` and `D7-AMEND1.txt` are generated with today's dates by the fixture F7-L commands below.

**Fixtures.** Run these now. Analysis takes 1–3 minutes per upload; the journeys need it finished.

F7-V, F7-I, F7-P — three uploads by counsel-a (so counsel-a owns them):
```bash
export C_VAL=$(upload $COUNSEL_A D7-VALIDATE.txt "QA7 Northwind — Services Agreement" "Northwind Traders Ltd")
export C_INJ=$(upload $COUNSEL_A D7-INJECT.txt "QA7 Brightline — Consulting Agreement" "Brightline Advisory LLC")
export C_PII=$(upload $COUNSEL_A D7-PII.txt "QA7 Northwind Payroll — Services Agreement" "Northwind Payroll Ltd")
```

F7-L — a licence family for amendments, renewals, invoices and the renewal brief (adapted from docs/38 TC-PREP-01
command R). The licence is US$0.25 per compute unit, 30 days' payment, 30 days' notice of non-renewal, renewal increases
capped at 5%, initial term ending 75 days from today (T+75). Amendment No. 1, effective 60 days ago, makes the fee
US$0.20 and the notice 60 days, so the notice deadline is T+15. Three invoices are billed on the licence; the middle one
is an overcharge of US$0.05 × 25,000 = US$1,250.00.
```bash
cat > D7-LICENCE.txt <<TXT
PLATFORM LICENSE AGREEMENT

This Platform License Agreement is made on $(day -300) between Demo Org, Inc. ("Customer") and QA Lakehouse Co ("Provider").

1. Licence. Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive subscription to the Provider data platform.
2. Fees. Customer will pay US\$0.25 per compute unit consumed, invoiced monthly in arrears and payable within thirty (30) days of invoice.
3. Term and renewal. The initial term ends on $(day +75). This Agreement then renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term.
4. Renewal pricing. On each renewal, fees may increase by no more than five percent (5%).
5. Limitation of liability. Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid in the twelve (12) months before the claim.
6. Governing law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
TXT
cat > D7-AMEND1.txt <<TXT
AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE PLATFORM LICENSE AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 1 is effective $(day -60). It amends the Platform License Agreement between Demo Org, Inc. and QA Lakehouse Co.

1. Section 2 (Fees) is amended: from the effective date of this Amendment, the fee is US\$0.20 per compute unit consumed.
2. Section 3 (Term and renewal) is amended: notice of non-renewal must be given at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term.
3. All other terms of the Agreement are unchanged.
TXT
export L_BASE=$(upload $COUNSEL_A D7-LICENCE.txt "QA Lakehouse — Platform License Agreement" "QA Lakehouse Co")
export L_AMD1=$(upload $COUNSEL_A D7-AMEND1.txt "QA Lakehouse — Platform License Agreement — Amendment No. 1" "QA Lakehouse Co" $L_BASE)
analysis $L_BASE; analysis $L_AMD1                          # repeat until both print DONE: the analysis writes key terms and would overwrite the next lines
qverify $L_BASE '{"field":"expiryDate","value":"'$(day +75)'"}'
qverify $L_BASE '{"field":"autoRenew","value":"yes"}'; qverify $L_BASE '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":30}'
qverify $L_AMD1 '{"field":"effectiveDate","value":"'$(day -60)'"}'; qverify $L_AMD1 '{"field":"noticePeriodDays","value":60}'
for c in $L_BASE $L_AMD1; do approve $c; patchc $c '{"status":"EXECUTED"}'; done
inv '{"contractId":"'$L_BASE'","vendorName":"QA Lakehouse Co","invoiceNumber":"QLH-101","amount":6250,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"'$(day -90)'","description":"25,000 compute units @ US$0.25"}'
inv '{"contractId":"'$L_BASE'","vendorName":"QA Lakehouse Co","invoiceNumber":"QLH-102","amount":6250,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"'$(day -30)'","description":"25,000 compute units @ US$0.25"}'
inv '{"contractId":"'$L_BASE'","vendorName":"QA Lakehouse Co","invoiceNumber":"QLH-103","amount":5000,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"'$(day -5)'","description":"25,000 compute units @ US$0.20"}'
```
Expected: every `qverify` prints `200`; each `approve` prints `200` (or nothing, if the workflow auto-approved it); each
`patchc` prints `{"status":"EXECUTED","detail":null}`; each `inv` prints its invoice number and an id.

**How to read the assistant's trace.** Above each answer, every tool call is a one-line chip:
- Icon: spinning (running; after 3 s a counter such as `4.2s` appears), tick (found something), slashed circle (found
  nothing), pause (a write proposal waiting for you), warning triangle (failed).
- Then the tool name, then what it was asked for: the entity it resolved (a contract title), or the first 6 characters
  of an id and `…`, or the search terms (`"query"`, `type=…`, `status=…`, `counterparty=…`, `expires <from>…<to>`,
  `value ≥ …`, `by value`, `limit=…`).
- Then what came back: `12 of 189 matched`, `3 results`, `2 matches`, `no results`, `no matches`, the failure in red
  (`contract not found`, `permission denied`, `unknown tool`), or a size such as `1532ch` when the result has no list.
- Click the chip to expand **Args** and **Result** (**Result (truncated)** when the stream cut it).
- Two tools have their own renderer instead of a chip: `contract_cite` shows a **Citations** box, `redline_propose` a
  **Redline proposal** card.

### E2E-AIADM-01 · An admin sees how the org's AI calls are routed, and the assistant answers with the model routing chooses

**Covers:** /agent · `GET /admin/ai/settings` · `PUT /admin/ai/settings` · `GET /agent/models` · `POST /agent/chat` · agents service: chat · docs/38 TC-AI-01
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Org A's AI settings untouched (every tier on Platform default). Note which provider key(s) the stack has.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: left rail → **Admin** → **Organization** → tab **AI Config**. | Heading **AI Config**, "Control how this organization's AI calls are routed, billed, and audited." Six sections in this order: **Model routing**, **Personal data sent to AI**, **API keys (BYOK)**, **Cost cap**, **Usage**, **Audit log**. |
| 2 | Read **Model routing**. | Text "Leave a tier on Platform default to let us pick the best available model, or pin it to a specific provider + model for reproducibility." Six rows with their descriptions: **Reasoning**, **Default**, **Fast**, **Embeddings**, **Rerank**, **Vision / OCR**. Each dropdown shows `Platform default — <provider/model>` (the tier's first candidate). The Default dropdown lists `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`, `openai/gpt-4.1`, `google/gemini-2.5-flash`. An info box: "Platform defaults resolve in order of the tier's candidate list; the first provider with a configured key wins. …". The button reads **Saved** and is disabled. |
| 3 | `curl -s $API/admin/ai/settings -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '{defaultModel, dailyCostCapUsd, capPolicy, tiers: (.platformRouting\|keys)}'` | `defaultModel` null, `dailyCostCapUsd` null, `capPolicy` "block", tiers `default, embed, fast, reasoning, rerank, vision_ocr`. |
| 4 | Left rail → **Assistant** → **New conversation**. Send "How many contracts do we have?" | An answer streams in. Under it: `Machine-authored · <model> · N tool call(s) · <seconds>s`. `<model>` is the first model of the Default list whose provider has a key (with only a Google key: `gemini-2.5-flash`). |
| 5 | Same question over the API: `ask $ADMIN_A "How many contracts do we have?"` | A `[tool contract_search …]` line, the answer, and `[done <provider>/<model> tier=default source=platform]` with the same model as step 4. |
| 6 | Back in AI Config, set **Default** to the model of step 4 (e.g. `google/gemini-2.5-flash`). Before saving, change it again, then click **Discard**. | While the draft differs, **Discard** appears and the main button reads **Save changes**. **Discard** puts the dropdown back. |
| 7 | Set **Default** to that model again and click **Save changes**. | Toast "Model routing saved". Under the dropdown: "Override active — always uses google/gemini-2.5-flash". The button returns to **Saved**. |
| 8 | On `/agent`, **New conversation**, ask the question again. | The footer names the pinned model. The step-3 curl now shows `"defaultModel":"google/gemini-2.5-flash"`. |
| 9 | Scroll to **Audit log** in AI Config. | Newest row: "Admin User changed default model from null to google/gemini-2.5-flash", your email and IP; click it to see **Metadata** `{"changed":{"defaultModel":{"from":null,"to":"google/gemini-2.5-flash"}}}` and the User-Agent. |
| 10 | Set **Default** back to "Platform default — …" and **Save changes**. | Toast "Model routing saved"; the "Override active" line disappears; a second audit row "… changed default model from google/gemini-2.5-flash to null". |
| 11 | `curl -s $API/agent/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '.models[0]'` | 200 for any signed-in user. Each entry has `provider`, `model_id`, `display_name`, `context_window`. |

**Also check**
- Permissions: only ADMIN has `configure:organization`. As counsel-a (or any other role) the left rail has no **Admin**
  group. `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' $API/admin/ai/settings -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` → `403`,
  `"detail":"Missing permission: configure:organization"`; the same for `PUT /admin/ai/settings`.
- Opening `$WEB/admin/org` as counsel-a still shows the page (there is no page guard); on **AI Config** the sections
  load nothing (their calls return 403) and nothing can be saved. Verify: no error message explains why.
- `PUT /admin/ai/settings` with `{"capPolicy":"maybe"}` → 400 `"detail":"Invalid body"`; with
  `{"dailyCostCapUsd":-1}` → 400.
- `GET /agent/models` with the agents service stopped → 502 `{"detail":"Agent service unavailable"}`.
- Only if the stack has keys for two providers: pin **Default** to the second provider's model (the one that did not
  answer in step 4) and ask again. Expected: the footer names the pinned model. Verify: reading
  `apps/agents/app/routes/chat.py`, every chat turn arrives with `provider` defaulted to `anthropic` (or the first
  provider with an env key), and the orchestrator passes it on as a provider override, which replaces a pinned model of
  another provider (and its BYOK key) with that provider's platform model. File it if the footer shows the other model.

**Known limits**
- Pinning a tier to a provider that has no key at all does not fail: the agents service falls back to the platform's
  first available model. The footer shows which model really answered.
- There is no UI for a per-request model pin. `POST /agent/chat` accepts `provider` + `modelId` (see E2E-AI-16).
