### E2E-AI-12 · "Prepare me for the <counterparty> renewal" writes the whole seven-part brief from the data, with the overcharge and no ids

**Covers:** /agent · `POST /agent/chat` · counterparty_memory · renewal_advice · contract_get · obligations_list · invoice_list · playbook_check · contract_search · agents service: chat · docs/38 TC-PREP-01
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~20 min (each brief takes 30–90 s)

**Preconditions**
- 7.0's F7-L, with Amendment No. 2 deleted (E2E-AI-11 step 10). T = today.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `ask $COUNSEL_A "Prepare me for the QA Lakehouse Co renewal." \| tee qa7-brief.txt` (or send it on `/agent`, where the same calls show as chips). | Three rounds of tool calls before any answer text: `counterparty_memory` and `renewal_advice`; then `contract_get`, `obligations_list`, `invoice_list`, `playbook_check` and `renewal_advice` for the chosen contract; then `contract_search` for executed contracts of the same type without a counterparty filter (and `contract_get` again if needed). No text such as "I'll now retrieve…" appears between the tool lines. |
| 2 | Read the brief's first line. | It names the agreement by title and says why it was chosen, e.g. "Renewal brief for the QA Lakehouse — Platform License Agreement: its notice deadline is the next one ahead." It may name other agreements on file, by title. |
| 3 | Read the headings. | In this order: Timeline, Commercial terms, Obligations, Invoices vs pricing, Risks, Benchmark, What to renegotiate. |
| 4 | Timeline and Commercial terms. | Expiry T+75; renews automatically; notice deadline T+15, set by Amendment No. 1's 60 days; about 15 days left to give notice. Fee US$0.20 per compute unit (amended from US$0.25), renewal increases capped at 5%, payment in 30 days. Not 30 days' notice, not a T+45 deadline, not US$0.25 as the current fee. |
| 5 | Invoices vs pricing. | Each invoice is checked against the price in force on its date: QLH-101 at US$0.25 is right (it predates the amendment); QLH-102 is an overcharge, listed with its number, the rate billed (US$0.25), the agreed rate (US$0.20) and the difference: US$0.05 × 25,000 = US$1,250.00; QLH-103 is right. Total overbilled: US$1,250.00. |
| 6 | Obligations, Risks, Benchmark. | Each has content from its tool, or one line saying nothing is on file, and only when that section's tool is in the trace (`obligations_list`, `playbook_check`, `contract_search`). On a fresh seed the benchmark may say there is no other executed licence to compare with. |
| 7 | What to renegotiate. | In this order, skipping what doesn't apply, each with its reason: a credit for the US$1,250.00 overcharge; the renewal price (the 5% cap, or a price hold for volume); terms the benchmark shows are worse than usual; the notice deadline T+15 as the date to decide by. Follow-up buttons end the answer (e.g. draft the notice, open the contract). |
| 8 | `grep -oE '\bc[a-z0-9]{24}\b' qa7-brief.txt` | No output: no contract id anywhere in the brief. |
| 9 | Look for totals. | The only sums are the overcharge (rate difference × quantity) and the total overbilled; no annual spend or other new total. |
| 10 | Run step 1 twice more (each `ask` uses a new session). | Each run passes steps 2–9. Record any run that fails and which check. |
| 11 | `ask $COUNSEL_A "Prepare me for the Acme Corporation renewal." \| tee qa7-brief-acme.txt` | The trace includes `invoice_list` before the brief; Invoices vs pricing says in one line that no invoices are on file. The brief never says "no data on file" for a section whose tool is missing from the trace. |

**Also check**
- Permissions: the brief uses only read tools. For a role that is not offered `playbook_check` (SALES_REP, PROCUREMENT,
  FINANCE, APPROVER), verify that Risks says the playbook check is not available to them rather than "no risks". rep-a
  (own scope) sees none of this fixture and gets no brief for QA Lakehouse Co.

**Known limits** (FIX_TRACKER GG5 — prompt rules, no server-side check)
- In the tracker's runs one brief in 11 still stopped after the first round of tools (it listed the counterparty's
  contracts and stopped). File it with the trace if it happens more often.
- A contract id still slipped into 3 of the last 6 briefs checked; step 8 catches it.
- Nothing checks on the server that the prep's tools ran before the answer, so a brief can in principle claim missing
  data it never looked for; step 11 checks for it.

### E2E-AI-13 · Each role gets only the tools it may use, sees only what it may see, and can't reach another user's or org's threads

**Covers:** the Assistant side panel · /agent · `POST /agent/chat` · `POST /agent/threads/:id/actions/apply` · `GET /agent/threads/:id` · `POST /agent/threads` · `POST /agent/threads/:id/turns` · `GET /agent/threads` · `GET /skills` · contract_create_from_template · redline_propose · playbook_check · approval_list · template_list · request_list · contract_search · contract_get · counterparty_list · comment_add · user_search · agents service: chat
**Roles:** viewer-a, rep-a, finance-a, approver-a, procurement-a, admin-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key; Org B · **Time:** ~25 min

**What each role is offered.** `POST /agent/chat` needs `view:contract` (every role has it). Before the turn, the API
withholds tools the caller could never use; the model is never told about them.

| Role | Tools not offered | Read tools refused on use (chip `permission denied`) | Write Apply that fails ("Missing permission: …") |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADMIN, LEGAL_OPS | none | none | none |
| LEGAL_COUNSEL | none | `approval_list` for the whole org (needs `configure:workflow`) | none |
| CONTRACT_MANAGER | none | `approval_list` for the whole org | `approval_decide` |
| SALES_REP (own scope) | `redline_propose`, `playbook_check`, `approval_list` | `org_memory` withholds the playbook | `comment_add`, `contract_update`, `approval_route`, `redline_apply`, `approval_decide` |
| PROCUREMENT | `playbook_check`, `approval_list` | `org_memory` withholds the playbook | `approval_decide` |
| FINANCE, APPROVER | `contract_create_from_template`, `redline_propose`, `playbook_check` | `template_list`, `request_list`; `org_memory` withholds playbook and clause library | `comment_add`, `contract_update`, `approval_route`, `redline_apply`, `request_create` |
| VIEWER | `contract_create_from_template`, `redline_propose`, `approval_list` | `request_list` | `comment_add`, `contract_update`, `approval_route`, `redline_apply`, `request_create`, `approval_decide` |
| API key without the admin scope | also `user_search` | — | — |

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As viewer-a, `/agent`: "Draft an NDA with Initech Solutions." | No `contract_create_from_template` chip and no card. The answer says it cannot create the draft for you (wording varies). `curl -s "$API/contracts?limit=100&search=Initech" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '[.data[].title]'` shows no new contract. |
| 2 | viewer-a: "Add a comment to Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement saying QA7 viewer test." Click **Apply** on the card. | The card appears (the proposal is allowed); Apply gives "Failed · Add a comment … · Missing permission: edit:contract". No comment is written. |
| 3 | viewer-a: "Propose a redline for the liability clause of Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement." | No `redline_propose` chip and no proposal card; the answer says it can't do that. |
| 4 | viewer-a: "What's in my approval queue?" | No `approval_list` chip; the answer says approvals aren't available to them. |
| 5 | viewer-a: "What intake requests are open?" | A `request_list` chip, `permission denied`; the answer says they don't have access, not that there are none. |
| 6 | As rep-a: "How many contracts do we have?" | The count is rep-a's own: equal to `curl -s "$API/contracts?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" \| jq .total` (0 on a fresh seed), never the org's total. |
| 7 | rep-a: "Summarise Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement." | Nothing found (`contract_search` `no results`, or `contract_get` `contract not found`); the answer says it can't find it and quotes nothing from it. |
| 8 | rep-a: "Who are our biggest counterparties by value?" | Counterparty names may be listed, but every count and value covers rep-a's own contracts only (0 on a fresh seed). |
| 9 | As finance-a: "What templates can I draft from?" | A `template_list` chip, `permission denied` (Result detail "The user in this conversation does not have view:template permission"); the answer says they can't see templates. |
| 10 | As procurement-a on the Acme contract page: "Compare this contract to our playbook." | No `playbook_check` chip; the answer says it can't run a playbook check for them. |
| 11 | As admin-b (Org B), `/agent`: "List all our contracts." then "Summarise Acme Corporation — Master Services Agreement." | Only Org B's contracts; the Acme contract is not found. |
| 12 | Take an Org A thread id (`$T` from E2E-AI-07). As admin-b: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' $API/agent/threads/$T -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B"`; the same with `POST $API/agent/threads/$T/turns` (body `{"userMessage":"x","assistant":{"content":"y"}}`) and `POST $API/agent/threads/$T/actions/apply` (body `{"toolName":"comment_add","args":{"contractId":"x","body":"y"}}`). | `404` `{"detail":"Thread not found"}` each time. |
| 13 | As admin-b: `ask $ADMIN_B "What did I ask you earlier in this conversation?" $T` | The answer says there is no earlier conversation: history is kept per org, user and session, so reusing another user's session id reads nothing. |
| 14 | As admin-a: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' $API/agent/threads/$T -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` (counsel-a's thread, same org). | `404` `{"detail":"Thread not found"}`. |
| 15 | As admin-b: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST $API/agent/threads -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"id\":\"$T\"}"` | Not the Org A thread: verify the status is 409 (`"A record with these details already exists"`) and that nothing of Org A's thread is returned. |

**Also check**
- With an API key made in the Integrations section (scope `contracts:read`): `GET $API/agent/threads` → `403`
  `{"detail":"This endpoint is for signed-in users, not API keys", …}`; `GET $API/skills` → `403`
  `{"detail":"This endpoint is not available to API keys without the admin scope", …}`. Verify what `POST
  $API/agent/chat` answers for such a key (it is allowed by `view:contract`; `user_search` is withheld).
- `tj redline_propose '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$VIEWER_A_ID'","contractId":"'$C_ACME'","sectionRef":"9"}'` →
  `403` `{"detail":"The user in this conversation does not have edit:contract permission"}` (the server refuses even if
  the tool were offered).

### E2E-AI-14 · The editor's AI (Draft new, the selection popover, the toolbar, Doc AI, ghost text and margin badges) suggests and changes nothing until you accept

**Covers:** /contracts · /contracts/:id · /templates · `POST /agent/draft` · `POST /agent/assist-stream` · `POST /agent/assist` · `POST /agent/complete` · `POST /agent/classify-clause` · `POST /agent/compare` · docs/38 TC-PII-09, TC-PII-10

- E2E-AI-09's `QA7 Redline — Services Agreement` (`$C_RED`, Draft). Signed in as counsel-a.

| 6 | Click ✨ with nothing selected. | No popover: the Ask panel opens with the cursor in its composer. |
| 7 | In edit mode, place the cursor at the end of a paragraph, type "The Supplier shall deliver the goods " (ending with a space) and wait about a second. | Grey suggested text appears after the cursor. **Tab** inserts it; Esc or any other key removes it. |
| 8 | Look at the left margin of paragraphs of 80 or more characters (view or edit mode). | Small badges **MARKET**, **AGGR.**, **WEAK** or **OFF** (at most 12 in a document). Hovering shows the meaning ("In line with common market practice", "Heavily favors one side — review before sending", "Materially weaker than market — consider tightening", "Not in the standard playbook — custom language") and a one-line reason. |
| 9 | Click a badge that is not **MARKET**. | A popover with a headline ("Aggressive — review before send", "Weaker than market" or "Off the standard playbook"), the reason, and **Rewrite to market**, **Accept as-is**, **Dismiss**. **Rewrite to market** opens the Selection popover on that paragraph; the other two close it. A **MARKET** badge's popover ("In line with market practice") has no **Rewrite to market**. |
| 10 | Left rail → **Templates** → **New Template**. Type a sentence into the section editor, select it, and click the toolbar's **✏️ Rewrite** ("AI: ✏️ Rewrite (select text first)"). | "Thinking…", then a banner **AI Suggestion**: the original struck through (−), the proposal (+), an explanation, and **Apply** / **Dismiss**. **Apply** replaces the selected range; **Dismiss** leaves the text. The other toolbar actions are 🧹 Simplify, 🔍 Expand, ⚖️ Check Compliance, 🔄 Suggest Alternative. |
| 11 | Click **✏️ Rewrite** with nothing selected. | A hint "Select text first" under the toolbar. |
| 12 | Click **Doc AI ▾** → "✨ Fix Layout" ("Clean up PDF extraction artifacts"). | "Fixing…", then the content is replaced and a banner reads "Doc AI updated the document — click Save Draft to keep the changes." |
| 13 | **Doc AI ▾** → "📝 Rewrite Document" ("AI rewrites full document"). | A dialog "Rewrite entire document?" — "The AI will rewrite the full document content. Your current text will be replaced. This cannot be undone unless you have a saved version." — with **Cancel** and **Rewrite** ("Rewriting…" on the button while it runs). Cancel changes nothing. Leave the template unsaved. |
| 14 | `/agent/compare` has no page (the Playbook page's **Test Clause** uses `POST /playbook/test`). Call it: `CAT=$(curl -s "$API/playbook/positions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq -r '.grouped[0].category.id')`, then `curl -s -X POST $API/agent/compare -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"clauseText\":\"Each party's liability is capped at the fees paid in the prior 12 months.\",\"clauseCategoryId\":\"$CAT\"}" \| jq '{bestMatch, score, explanation}'` | 200 with the position that fits best, a score and an explanation (and `deviations`). |

**Also check**
- `POST /agent/draft`:
  - as viewer-a with `"saveAs":{"title":"x"}` → `403` `"detail":"Missing permission: create:contract"`;
  - as viewer-a without `saveAs` → 200 with a draft preview, nothing saved;
  - `{"userMessage":"  "}` → `400` `{"detail":"userMessage is required"}`;
  - `saveAs.contractId` of another org's contract → `404` `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`;
  - a type with no template → `422` `{"error":"NO_TEMPLATE_MATCH","detail":"No template matches this contract type. Create a template for this type first, then retry."}`, shown in the Draft Details form.
- **Draft new** is shown only to roles with `create:contract`.
- `POST /agent/assist-stream` with `{"selectedText":""}` → `400` `{"detail":"selectedText is required"}`. `POST
  /agent/assist` with `"action":"shout"` → `422` "Request body failed validation"; a selection whose SSN is split by
  bold markup → `422` with the detail "The selection has a redacted value split by formatting (bold or a link inside it),
  so it can't go to the AI. Remove that formatting and try again." (TC-PII-09 N1).
- `POST /agent/complete` with `{"contextBefore":"short"}` → `{"completion":"","reason":"too_short"}`; `POST
  /agent/classify-clause` with a clause under 30 characters → `{"category":"skip","position":"skip","reasoning":""}`.
- With the agents service stopped: the popover shows "Stream failed (502)" with **Try again**; the toolbar shows the
  API's reason ("Agent service unavailable") for 4 seconds ("AI request failed — please try again." when there is none);
  ghost text and badges simply don't appear (`{"completion":"","error":"upstream_unavailable"}`, `{"category":"skip",…,"error":"upstream_unavailable"}`).
- `POST /agent/compare`: without `clauseCategoryId` → `400` `{"detail":"clauseText and clauseCategoryId are required"}`;
  a category with no positions → `404` `{"detail":"No playbook positions found for this category"}`; as rep-a →
  `403` "Missing permission: view:playbook".
- Personal data in the selection goes out as tokens and comes back as the real value (docs/38 TC-PII-09 P2–P4).

**Known limits**
- `/agent/complete`, `/agent/classify-clause` and `/agent/compare` don't tell the agents service which org is asking, so
  they run on the platform key and default models, not the org's own key or model routing, and their use is not
  recorded in **Usage**.

### E2E-AI-15 · Asking a question about one contract (Q&A) answers from its clauses, with sources, and degrades honestly

**Covers:** `POST /contracts/:id/ask` · agents service: agent · docs/38 TC-PII-09 (P6, N5)
**Roles:** counsel-a, rep-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key; an embedding key · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- The Acme contract's clauses are embedded (the §0 seed embeds them when an embedding key is set; otherwise re-run
  analysis on it with **Re-run AI analysis**, E2E-AI-07 step 19). There is no page for this route; all steps are API calls.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_ACME/ask -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question":"What is the liability cap and what does it not cover?"}' \| jq '{answer, mode, citations: (.citations\|length), sources: [.sources[]?.clauseType], message}'` | 200. `answer` names $500,000 and the three carve-outs, citing the clauses it used; `mode` "prompt" (clauses cited as `[Clause N]`) or "anthropic_native" (Anthropic's citations); `sources` lists the matched clauses (up to 8); no `message`. |
| 2 | Same with `"limit":3`. | At most 3 `sources`. |
| 3 | `-d '{"question":"   "}'` | `400` `{"detail":"question is required"}`. |
| 4 | As rep-a (own scope, not the owner), and as admin-b (Org B). | `404` `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` both times. |
| 5 | Ask about the "QA7 No document" contract from E2E-AI-04 (no clauses). | 200 `{"answer":null,"sources":[],"message":"No relevant clauses found — try re-uploading to extract text"}`. |
| 6 | On `$C_PII`: `-d '{"question":"Which clause gives the contractor social security number?"}'` | The `answer` quotes `219-09-9999` where it gives the number, never a `[PII:…]` token: the clauses went to the model as tokens and the API put the values back. |
| 7 | Stop the agents service and repeat step 1. Start it again. | 200 `{"answer":null,"sources":[…],"message":"Agent unavailable — showing relevant clauses"}`: the matched clauses are still returned. |

**Also check**
- The same agents-service route (`/agent/ask`) answers `POST /search/ask`, and `/agent/portfolio-query` answers `POST
  /search/portfolio-query` (both tested in the search part of this document; docs/38 TC-AI-03).
- With no embedding key the clause lookup itself fails; verify the route answers 500 rather than a message.

### E2E-AI-16 · The chat and thread APIs stream typed events, keep a conversation's memory, validate input, and keep the legacy path honest

**Covers:** `POST /agent/chat` · `GET /agent/models` · `POST /agent/threads` · `POST /agent/threads/:id/turns` · `GET /agent/threads` · `GET /agent/threads/:id` · `DELETE /agent/threads/:id` · agents service: chat · docs/38 TC-AI-01 (P5)
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -sN -X POST $API/agent/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"message":"How many NDAs do we have?","agentMode":true,"sessionId":"qa7-session-0001"}'` | `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Lines `data: {…}`; every frame carries `session_id` "qa7-session-0001", `provider` and `model_id` (null); `type` is `tool_call_start` (`id`, `name`, `args`), `tool_call_result` (`result`, `truncated`, `ok`), `tool_progress` (`elapsedSec`, only for tools slower than 3 s), `token` (`delta`), and last `done` (`provider`, `model`, `tier`, `source`), then `data: [DONE]`. |
| 2 | `ask $COUNSEL_A "Name them." qa7-session-0001` | No new search, or a search consistent with step 1: the earlier result is remembered for this session (kept 24 hours). |
| 3 | `curl -sN … -d '{"message":"What is an NDA?"}'` (no `agentMode`). | The legacy path: frames with only `delta` (the reply in word-sized pieces), no `type` and no tool calls, then `[DONE]`. |
| 4 | Legacy path: `-d '{"message":"Draft an NDA for Acme"}'`. | When the draft agent finds a template: a reply beginning "✅ I've drafted your NDA using **<template>** (completeness: N%)." and ending "You can review and edit it in the Contract Editor." (otherwise "I couldn't find a suitable template for your request. …"). Verify: no contract is created (`GET /contracts?search=Acme` unchanged). The web pages never use this path (they send `agentMode: true`). |
| 5 | `curl -s $API/agent/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq -r '.models[] \| "\(.provider)/\(.model_id)"'`. Pick a model whose provider has a key and send `-d '{"message":"Say hello in five words","agentMode":true,"provider":"<provider>","modelId":"<model_id>"}'`. | The final `done` frame names that model: an explicit pin wins over the org's routing. |
| 6 | `-d '{"message":""}'`; then `-d '{"message":"hi","provider":"mistral"}'`; then `-d '{"message":"hi","agentMode":true,"provider":"<keyed provider>","modelId":"no-such-model"}'`. | `422` "Request body failed validation"; `422` again (only `anthropic`, `openai`, `google` are accepted); `400` with a `detail` containing "Unknown provider/model". |
| 7 | `curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' \| jq '{id, title}'` | A new thread, `"title":"New chat"`. |
| 8 | Twice: `-d '{"id":"qa7-thread-0001","title":"QA7 API thread"}'`. | Both calls return the same row (the call is idempotent on `id`). |
| 9 | `-d '{"title":""}'` and `-d '{"id":"short"}'`. | `400` `{"detail":"Invalid body", "issues": …}` both times. |
| 10 | `curl -s -X POST $API/agent/threads/qa7-thread-0001/turns -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"userMessage":"hello","assistant":{"content":"hi","model":"test-model"},"toolCalls":[{"toolName":"contract_search","args":{},"status":"success","result":"{}"}]}'` | `{"userMessageId":…,"assistantMessageId":…,"toolCallIds":[…one id…]}`. The thread keeps its title "QA7 API thread" (a title is filled from the first message only while it is "New chat"). |
| 11 | Post a turn to step 7's "New chat" thread with `"userMessage"` of 70 characters. | Its title becomes the first 57 characters plus "…". |
| 12 | Turns with no `userMessage`, or with a tool call `"status":"maybe"`. | `400` `{"detail":"Invalid body", …}`. |
| 13 | `curl -s "$API/agent/threads?limit=2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '.threads[] \| {id, title, messageCount, toolCallCount}'`; then `GET $API/agent/threads/qa7-thread-0001`. | The two most recently updated threads, with counts. The single thread has its `messages` (user "hello", assistant "hi" with `model` "test-model") and `toolCalls`. |
| 14 | `curl -s -X DELETE $API/agent/threads/qa7-thread-0001 -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A"` | `{"id":"qa7-thread-0001","archived":true}`; the thread leaves the list. |
| 15 | The agents service directly: `curl -s $AGENTS/health`; `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' $AGENTS/agent/models`; the same with `-H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET"`. | `{"status":"ok","replayMode":…}`; `401` `{"error":"unauthorized"}` without the secret; the model list with it. Only the API should call the service (it adds the caller's identity and permissions). |

**Also check**
- Permissions: `POST /agent/chat` needs `view:contract` (every role); the thread routes need a signed-in user (API keys
  get `403` "This endpoint is for signed-in users, not API keys") and only ever touch the caller's own threads.
- `ask` output on any turn ends with `[done <provider>/<model> tier=<tier> source=platform|byok]`: `source` says whose key
  paid (E2E-AIADM-02).
- `GET /agent/threads?scopeType=contract` without `scopeId` is not filtered (both are needed).

**Known limits**
- The legacy (non-agent) path has no tools, and its "draft" reply claims a draft that is never saved.

**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

| # | Do | Expect |

Built-ins ship with the product; org skills are created by admins and shared with everyone.", a **New org skill** button, a search box "Search by slug, name, description" and a scope filter **All scopes** (options dashboard, current_contract, current_request, selection, portfolio, any). |

Past invocations keep their snapshot."; **Cancel** and **Save changes**. |
| 5 | Click **Cancel** (do not save a built-in: E2E-SKL-03 explains why). Open the drawer again and click the dimmed area beside it. | Both close the drawer without saving. |
| 6 | Open `$WEB/settings/skills`. | The same page (an alias with no menu link). |
| 7 | `curl -s $API/skills -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq '[.skills[] \| {slug, ownerType, contextScope, version}]'` | The nine built-ins (plus any org skill), `ownerType` "built_in"; no `systemPrompt` in the list. `?scope=dashboard` → the two dashboard skills; `?scope=bogus` → `422`. |
| 8 | `S_RC=$(curl -s $API/skills -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq -r '.skills[] \| select(.slug=="@review-contract") \| .id'); curl -s $API/skills/$S_RC -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" \| jq -r .systemPrompt`, then the same with `$ADMIN_A`. | counsel-a gets `[hidden — admin-only]`; admin-a gets the full prompt. |
| 9 | As counsel-a: look at the left rail, then open `$WEB/admin/skills` and **Edit** `@review-contract`. | No **Admin** group in the rail, but the page opens (reading skills is open to every user). The drawer shows a lock line "You don't have permission to view this prompt (admin role required)." and a disabled prompt box reading `[hidden — admin-only]`. |
| 10 | Still counsel-a: **Save changes**; then **New org skill** → fill any valid values → **Create**. | Save fails with the line "Request failed with status code 403". Create fails with "Missing permission: configure:organization". |

**Also check**
- `GET /skills/<another org's skill id>` → `404` `{"detail":"Skill not found"}`.
- A limited API key (no admin scope) → `403` "This endpoint is not available to API keys without the admin scope".

**Known limits**
- The pages have no guard: a non-admin sees **New org skill** and **Edit**, and learns only on saving that they can't.
- The edit drawer's error shows the raw HTTP message instead of the API's reason.

| 9 | "@qa7-portfolio-brief who are our biggest counterparties by value?" | No `counterparty_list` chip (the skill allows only `contract_search`); the answer ranks from `contract_search` or says it can't with this skill. |

The answer behaves as in step 8 (this page shows no slug chip above the message). |
| 12 | "@no-such-skill hello" (panel). | Treated as plain text: no skill chip, the default assistant answers. |

| 14 | As admin-b: `curl -s $API/skills -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" \| jq '[.skills[].slug]'`; then create `@qa7-portfolio-brief` in Org B with the step-4 values through `POST $API/skills`. | Org B's list has the nine built-ins but not Org A's skill. After a reload the skill is gone from the page, the chip strip and both `@` menus; "@qa7-portfolio-brief …" is plain chat. |

**Known limits**
- **Model tier**, follow-ups and required roles are saved but not used when a skill runs: it runs on the org's default
  routing, shows no follow-up suggestions, and anyone can invoke it.
- An allowed-tools list naming no real tool makes the skill run with every tool (the orchestrator falls back to the full
  list); verify with `allowedTools: ["not_a_tool"]`.
- **Save changes** always bumps the version, even when nothing that is versioned changed (the drawer sends every field).
- A new skill is mention-only until edited (the create drawer has no Triggers). A "selection"-scope skill is never
  offered in the panel's `@` menu. The **button** trigger is not used anywhere.

### E2E-SKL-03 · Built-in skills do what their description says; "Draft from template" only searches; built-ins are shared by every org

**Covers:** /admin/skills · the Assistant side panel · /agent · `GET /skills` · `PATCH /skills/:id` · `POST /agent/chat` · contract_get · contract_summarize · playbook_check · contract_search · clause_search · agents service: chat
**Roles:** counsel-a, admin-a, admin-b · **Needs:** agents service + model key; Org B · **Time:** ~15 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As counsel-a on the Acme contract page, click the skill chip **Review contract**, add "review it", send. | Chip `@review-contract` above your message. The trace starts with `contract_get`, then `playbook_check`. Five short sections: SUMMARY, KEY TERMS, TOP RISKS (three, each with a quote and a § reference), PLAYBOOK (the failing clauses, worst first, or a statement that the playbook has no position for them — never "compliant" by default), SUGGESTED REDLINES (one line each, offering to draft them). No card; nothing applied. |
| 2 | Same page: "@review-nda check this". | It says the contract is not an NDA and stops. |
| 3 | On **Globex — Mutual NDA**: chip **Review NDA**, send "review". | Five numbered checks (MUTUALITY, TERM & SURVIVAL, CARVE-OUTS, IP ASSIGNMENT, JURISDICTION), each with ✓ / △ / ✗ and a quoted clause, then a VERDICT line ("Sign as-is", "Sign with minor redlines" or "Do not sign without Legal"). |
| 4 | On **Massive Dynamic — Cloud Services MSA**: chip **Prep for approval**, send "prep it". | Headings DEAL AT A GLANCE, WHAT WE GET, WHAT WE GIVE UP, RISK CALLOUTS, PRECEDENTS, RECOMMENDED APPROVERS; it ends with one question like "Route to Legal for approval?". Trace: `contract_get` (the skill allows only `contract_get`, `contract_summarize`, `clause_search`). |
| 5 | On `/dashboard`: chip **Draft from template**, add "an NDA with Initech Solutions", send. | The assistant asks for details one at a time or describes what it would fill in. The trace has at most `contract_search` / `clause_search`; there is no `contract_create_from_template` chip and no card. No contract is created. |
| 6 | **New thread**, no skill: "Draft an NDA with Initech Solutions." | The drafting card appears (E2E-AI-09). Click **Cancel**. |
| 7 | Chip **Draft from scratch**, "a data-sharing agreement with Umbrella Corporation". | It proposes a skeleton and library clauses and reminds you a scratch draft should go to Legal; no draft is created (search-only, like step 5). |
| 8 | In the panel type `@` on `/dashboard`, then `@exp` on the Acme contract page; then type `@exp` on `/agent`. | Panel on the dashboard: `@compliance-sweep` is offered (portfolio skills show there) though it is not a chip. Panel on the contract page: no `@explain-clause` (a selection-scope skill is never offered in the panel). `/agent` offers every skill, so `@explain-clause` appears there. |
| 9 | Built-ins are global. As admin-b: `curl -s -X PATCH $API/skills/<id of @review-nda> -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"description":"QA7 edited by Org B"}' \| jq .description` (get the id with step 8 of E2E-SKL-01, slug `@review-nda`). As admin-a reload **Admin** → **Skills**. | `"QA7 edited by Org B"`. Org A's list now shows that description under `@review-nda`: an admin of any org can change a built-in for every org. |
| 10 | Put it back: the same PATCH with `{"description":"NDA-tuned 5-check review: mutuality, term, carve-outs, IP, jurisdiction."}`. | The original description. |

**Known limits**
- The **Draft from template** and **Draft from scratch** chips cannot draft: their skills allow only search tools. To
  draft from chat, ask without a skill (E2E-AI-09) or use **Contracts** → **Draft new** (E2E-AI-14).
- The chip strip shows at most four chips; `@renewal-check` has no chip (mention only).
- Editing a built-in's prompt changes it for every org and survives until the seed script refreshes it.

### E2E-AIADM-02 · An admin adds, tests, rotates and removes the org's own provider keys; only the first 8 characters are ever shown

**Covers:** /admin/org (AI Config) · `GET /admin/ai/keys` · `PUT /admin/ai/keys/:provider` · `POST /admin/ai/keys/:provider/test` · `DELETE /admin/ai/keys/:provider` · `GET /admin/ai/audit` · `POST /agent/chat` · agents service: chat
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key; a valid key for the provider that answers (the stack's own key will do) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- No BYOK key set. Note the provider that answers chat (E2E-AIADM-01 step 5); the steps use Google as the example.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-a: **Admin** → **Organization** → **AI Config** → **API keys (BYOK)**. | "Use your own provider accounts. When a key is set for a provider, this org's calls to that provider bill your account and skip the platform cost cap." Rows **OpenAI**, **Anthropic**, **Google**, **Voyage**, **Cohere**, **Mistral**, each with a **Not set** pill, "No key configured · falls back to platform default or skips if unavailable" and **Add key**. A note: "Rotating a key invalidates its prior verification — we clear the tested-at timestamp and prompt you to test again. …". |
| 2 | **Google** → **Add key**. | An editor "Google API key": a password field ("AIza…"), the note "The key is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never leaves this server in plaintext. We store only the first 8 characters for display.", **Cancel** and **Save & test** (disabled until 8 characters). |
| 3 | Type `short` and press Enter. | Toast "Key looks too short" — "Double-check you pasted the full API key." Nothing is saved. |
| 4 | Paste the valid key and click **Save & test**. | "Saving…", then toast "Google key verified" — "Next calls from your org will use this key." The row: pill **Verified**, "<first 8 characters>•••••• · tested just now", buttons **Test**, **Rotate**, **Remove**. |
| 5 | `curl -s $API/admin/ai/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.data[] \| select(.provider=="google")'` | `configured` true, `keyPrefix` = the key's first 8 characters, `testStatus` "success", `lastTestedAt` set. No field holds the key. The other providers: `configured` false. |
| 6 | `ask $ADMIN_A "How many contracts do we have?"` | The last line reads `[done google/<model> tier=default source=byok]`: the org's key paid for the call. |
| 7 | Click **Test**. | Toast "Key works ✓"; "tested just now". |
| 8 | **Rotate**: the editor reads "New Google key (replaces current)". Paste `AIzaQA7-invalid-key-000000000000000000000` → **Save & test**. | Toast "Google key saved but failed verification" with the provider's message ("Google 400: …"). Pill **Failed**; the prefix is now `AIzaQA7-`. |
| 9 | Send any question in the Ask panel. | The turn fails (the org's key is tried first, even after a failed test): see E2E-AIADM-06 step 1. |
| 10 | **Rotate** back to the valid key → **Save & test**. | **Verified** again; chat works. |
| 11 | Click **Remove**, then **Cancel** in the dialog; click **Remove** again, then **Remove key**. | Dialog "Remove this BYOK key?": "Calls to Google fall back to the platform key. If your org has no platform key for this provider, every feature routed to it starts failing — extraction, review and the assistant included. The key cannot be recovered; you would need to paste it again." Cancel keeps the key. **Remove key**: toast "Google key removed", pill **Not set**. |
| 12 | `ask $ADMIN_A "How many contracts do we have?"` | `source=platform` again. |
| 13 | **Voyage** → **Add key** → `pa-qa7-0000000000000000` → **Save** (this provider has no live test, so the button is **Save**). | Toast "Voyage key saved" — "We'll validate it on first real use." Pill **Saved**; no **Test** button. |
| 14 | `curl -s -X POST $API/admin/ai/keys/voyage/test -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"`. Reload the page. Then remove the Voyage key. | `{"ok":true,…}` without contacting Voyage, and the pill now reads **Verified** (see Known limits). Removal as in step 11. |
| 15 | Scroll to **Audit log**. | Newest first: "Admin User removed the voyage API key (was pa-qa7-0)", "… tested voyage key — verified", "… added a voyage API key (prefix pa-qa7-0)", "… removed the google API key (was …)", "… rotated google key (AIzaQA7- → …)", "… tested google key — failed", and so on. No row shows more than the 8-character prefix. |

**Also check**
- `PUT $API/admin/ai/keys/foo` → `400` `{"detail":"Unknown provider \"foo\""}`; `PUT …/google` with `{"apiKey":"short"}` → `400`
  `{"detail":"Invalid body", …}`; `POST …/google/test` with no key stored → `404`
  `{"detail":"No BYOK key configured for this provider"}`; `DELETE …/google` with none stored → 200
  `{"provider":"google","configured":false}` and no audit row.
- Every key route as counsel-a → `403` "Missing permission: configure:organization".

**Known limits**
- A key that failed its test is still used for every call to that provider until it is rotated or removed.
- For Voyage, Cohere and Mistral the test route answers `ok: true` without calling the provider, so the API marks the key
  "Verified" even though the page promised to "validate it on first real use".
- A BYOK chat turn is still recorded as platform spend and counts against the daily cap (E2E-AIADM-04, FIX_TRACKER X54).

### E2E-AIADM-03 · The AI audit log records every AI settings and key change, filterable, and never a key

**Covers:** /admin/org (AI Config, Audit Log tab) · `GET /admin/ai/audit`
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- E2E-AIADM-01 and 02 done (routing and key events exist).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | AI Config → **Audit log**. | "Every change to model routing, BYOK keys, and the cost cap. Append-only — entries can never be edited or removed. Plaintext keys are never logged." A filter with **All changes**, **Settings updated**, **Key created**, **Key rotated**, **Key deleted**, **Key tested**. Rows newest first: a sentence ("Admin User changed default model from null to google/gemini-2.5-flash"), a relative time (hover for the exact time), and "<email> · <IP>". |
| 2 | Click a row. | **Metadata** as JSON (e.g. `{"provider":"google","keyPrefix":{"from":"…","to":"…"}}`) and "User-Agent: …". |
| 3 | Choose **Key tested**. | Only test rows ("… tested google key — verified" / "— failed"). |
| 4 | Choose a type with no events (e.g. **Key deleted** on a new org). | `No "key deleted" events yet` and "Events will appear here as soon as an admin modifies AI settings or BYOK keys." |
| 5 | `curl -s "$API/admin/ai/audit?limit=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '.events[] \| {action, resourceType, resourceId, actor: .actor.email}'` | Up to 5 events, `action` one of `AI_SETTINGS_UPDATED`, `AI_KEY_CREATED`, `AI_KEY_UPDATED`, `AI_KEY_DELETED`, `AI_KEY_TESTED`; `resourceType` `ai_settings`, `ai_key` or `organization` (privacy-mode changes). |
| 6 | `?action=AI_KEY_TESTED`; then `?action=CONTRACT_CREATED`; then `?from=<today>&to=<tomorrow>`; then `?limit=500`. | Only key tests; `{"events":[]}` (non-AI actions are never returned here); only today's events; at most 200 events. |
| 7 | **Admin** → **Organization** → tab **Audit Log**, Action `AI_KEY_CREATED` → **Filter**. | The same events in the org-wide log, which also verifies the chain; it also holds `AGENT_TOOL_APPLIED`, `AGENT_TOOL_UNDONE`, `PII_REDACTED` and `PII_BOUNDARY_REDACTED`. |

**Also check**
- `GET /admin/ai/audit` as counsel-a → `403` "Missing permission: configure:organization".
- With 50 or more AI events the section ends with "Showing the 50 most recent AI changes. Every event, with a check of
  the chain, is on the Audit Log tab."
- A privacy-mode change reads "Admin User changed piiRedactionMode from <old> to <new>" (the setting's raw name; `null`
  the first time).

### E2E-AIADM-04 · Usage shows the last 30 days of AI spend, and the daily cost cap blocks or only warns as set

**Covers:** /admin/org (AI Config) · `GET /admin/ai/usage` · `GET /admin/ai/cap-status` · `PUT /admin/ai/settings` · `POST /agent/chat` · `POST /contracts/:id/ask` · agents service: chat
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~15 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | AI Config → **Usage**. | "Platform-paid AI spend over the last 30 days. BYOK traffic isn't tracked here — that bills your provider account directly." and "since <date 30 days ago>". After this section's chats: tiles **Total spend** ("$x.xx", "30d window"), **Calls** ("avg $0.0000 / call"), **Tokens** ("Xk in · Yk out"); bars **By provider** and **By tier** ("$x.xx · n"). A note about Langfuse. A new org shows "No platform-paid calls yet". |
| 2 | `curl -s $API/admin/ai/usage -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \| jq '{windowDays, estimated, totals, providers: [.byProvider[].provider]}'` | `windowDays` 30, `estimated` true, totals, and `providers` including `requested-default` (how chat turns are recorded). |
| 3 | AI Config → **Cost cap**. | "Daily USD ceiling for platform-paid calls. BYOK calls (…) bypass this cap — you bill your own provider directly." A band "$<used> / $50.00", "<p>% of today's cap used · $<left> remaining", today's date and "resets at 00:00 UTC"; **Daily cap (USD)** (placeholder 50.00; "Leave blank to inherit the platform default ($50/day). Max $100,000."); **Enforcement policy** with **Block** / **Warn**; the caption "Platform calls will return a CostCapExceededError once today's spend exceeds the cap." |
| 4 | `curl -s $API/admin/ai/cap-status -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` | `{"usedUsd":…,"capUsd":50,"remainingUsd":…,"pctUsed":…,"policy":"block","date":"<today>"}`. |
| 5 | Type `-1` in **Daily cap (USD)**. | "Enter a non-negative number up to 100,000."; **Save changes** disabled. **Discard** puts the old value back. |
| 6 | Set it to `0`, keep **Block**, **Save changes**. | Toast "Cost cap updated". The band shows "$<used> / $0.00". The audit log: "Admin User changed daily cap from null to 0". |
| 7 | As counsel-a, ask anything in the Ask panel; then on `/agent`. | Panel: "Sorry, the AI assistant ran into a problem. Try again, or refresh if it persists." `/agent`: the same text, "Stream failed (429)" and **Try again**. |
| 8 | `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST $API/agent/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"message":"hi","agentMode":true}'` | `429` `{"error":"cost_cap_exceeded","detail":"Daily AI spend cap reached for this organization. Contact your admin to raise the cap or wait for the daily reset (UTC midnight).","usedUsd":…,"capUsd":0}`. |
| 9 | `curl -s -X POST $API/contracts/$C_ACME/ask -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question":"What is the liability cap?"}' \| jq '{answer, message}'` | Verify: `{"answer":null,"message":"Agent unavailable — showing relevant clauses"}`: the model call is refused at the cap. |
| 10 | Choose **Warn**, **Save changes**. | Caption "Platform calls will keep working; a warning is logged and surfaces in the audit trail." Chat works again. The API log has a line `[costCap] org=… OVER (warn-only): …`. |
| 11 | Clear **Daily cap (USD)**, choose **Block**, **Save changes**. | "$<used> / $50.00" again. |

**Also check**
- `PUT /admin/ai/settings` `{"dailyCostCapUsd":100001}` → `400` "Invalid body". Both usage routes as counsel-a → `403`
  "Missing permission: configure:organization".
- The band's colour follows the share used: under 50% green, 50–80% amber, over 80% red.

**Known limits**
- Chat usage is estimated from the message and the streamed reply only, recorded as provider/model `requested-default`,
  so Usage under-reports chat and the cap barely sees it (FIX_TRACKER X54, blocked on a product decision). A BYOK chat
  turn is still recorded and counted against the cap, although the page says BYOK is neither tracked nor capped.
- A cap of 0 blocks all platform-paid AI; the band then reads "0.0% of today's cap used".
- **Warn** writes only a server log line; no audit-trail entry is written, whatever the caption says.
- The page doesn't say the figures are estimates, and the per-day series the API returns (`byDay`) isn't shown.

### E2E-AIADM-05 · The personal-data mode decides what reaches the model: markers (redact), stable placeholders (tokenize) or the raw text (off)

**Covers:** /admin/org (AI Config) · the Assistant side panel · `POST /agent/chat` · contract_get · agents service: chat · docs/38 TC-PII-01 to TC-PII-10
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, legalops-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key · **Time:** ~25 min

**What the mode covers.** In contract text going to a model: US Social Security numbers (SSN), ITINs, card numbers
(Luhn-valid, only when a payment word such as "card" or "credit" is in the document), IBANs (valid check digits, only
with a banking word), passport numbers and dates of birth (only after their keyword), IPv4 addresses, and API keys with
common prefixes. **Not** covered: email addresses and phone numbers in contract text (they are often the notice
details), names, postal addresses, and anything you type into the chat yourself.

**Preconditions**
- 7.0's `$C_PII` analysed. Org A on **Redact** (the default when the setting has never been changed).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | AI Config → **Personal data sent to AI**. | "Before any text reaches an AI model, personal data such as SSNs, tax IDs, card and bank numbers, passport numbers and dates of birth is handled this way. Values are put back in the drafts you keep. Every change is recorded in the audit log." Three choices: **Redact** ("Replace personal data with a marker such as [REDACTED:SSN]. The default."), **Tokenize** ("Replace each value with a stable placeholder, so the AI can tell values apart without seeing them."), **Off** ("Send text as it is. Only for a model you host or have agreed terms with."). **Redact** is selected. |
| 2 | `tj contract_get '{"orgId":"'$ORG_A'","userId":"'$COUNSEL_A_ID'","contractId":"'$C_PII'"}' \| jq -r .plainText` | `[REDACTED:SSN]`, `Date of birth: [REDACTED:DOB]`, `Passport No. [REDACTED:PASSPORT]`, `credit card [REDACTED:CC]`, `IBAN [REDACTED:IBAN]`, `at [REDACTED:IP]`, `key [REDACTED:API_KEY]`. Unchanged: `legal@northwind.example`, `+1 415 555 0142`, `Jane Doe, 1 Main Street, Springfield`. `jq ._piiPolicy` on the same call → `{"mode":"redact","total":<7 or more>}`. |
| 3 | As counsel-a on that contract, panel: "What is the contractor's Social Security Number, and where do notices go?" | The `contract_get` chip's Result shows the same markers. The answer says the number is redacted and gives the email and phone as written. |
| 4 | As admin-a: **Admin** → **Organization** → **Audit Log**, Action `PII_REDACTED` → **Filter**. | Rows for this contract with metadata `surface` "contract_get.plainText", `mode` "redact", `counts` `{"SSN":1,"DOB":1,"PASSPORT":1,"CC":1,"IBAN":1,"IP":1,"API_KEY":1}`. |
| 5 | AI Config → click **Tokenize**. | Toast "Privacy mode saved" — "Tokenize"; **Tokenize** is selected. The AI Config audit log: "Admin User changed piiRedactionMode from null to tokenize". |
| 6 | Run step 2 twice. | Placeholders `[PII:SSN:<8 hex>]`, `[PII:DOB:…]`, `[PII:CC:…]` and so on, identical in both runs; `_piiPolicy.mode` "tokenize". The keyword stays ("Date of birth: [PII:DOB:…]"). |
| 7 | Ask step 3 again in a new thread. | The answer can show a `[PII:SSN:…]` placeholder where the number would be; the real number is never shown. |
| 8 | Click **Off**. Run step 2; ask step 3 again. | The raw values (`219-09-9999`, `4111 1111 1111 1111`, …); `_piiPolicy` null; no new `PII_REDACTED` row. The answer can state the SSN. |
| 9 | Click **Redact** again. | Back to markers (step 2). |
| 10 | As legalops-a (who may change other organization settings), open `$WEB/admin/org` directly (the left rail has no Admin group for them), tab **AI Config**, and click **Tokenize**. As viewer-a, send `curl -s -X PATCH $API/organization -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"settings":{"piiRedactionMode":"off"}}'`. | legalops-a: toast "Save failed" — "Changing piiRedactionMode requires configure:organization". viewer-a: `403` "Missing permission: configure:integration". The mode stays Redact. |

**Also check**
- `PATCH /organization` as admin-a with `{"settings":{"piiRedactionMode":"partial"}}` → `400`
  `{"detail":"piiRedactionMode must be one of: redact, tokenize, off"}`.
- Pseudonyms differ between orgs for the same value (docs/38 TC-PII-02 N2), and are keyed (not a plain hash, N1).
- Where a model's output is stored or written into a contract (the upload pipeline, extraction, chat redlines, the
  approval summary, the editor's AI, Q&A), values go out as round-trip tokens `[PII:KIND:<16 hex>]` and come back as the
  real values: docs/38 TC-PII-01 and TC-PII-06 to TC-PII-10. A redline or editor suggestion that lost a token is refused
  rather than written ("The suggestion lost a redacted value from your text. Try again.").
- Anything a call site missed is caught once more before it leaves the API and logged as `PII_BOUNDARY_REDACTED` (docs/38
  TC-PII-01).

**Known limits**
- What you type into the chat goes to the model as typed, in every mode.
- In tokenize mode the chat answer is not turned back into values: placeholders can appear in the answer.
- Email addresses, phone numbers, names and postal addresses in contract text are never masked.
- A card number is caught only when the document has a payment word somewhere, an IBAN only with a banking word, a
  passport number or date of birth only after its keyword.

### E2E-AIADM-06 · With no model key, a bad key, or the agents service down, the assistant says so instead of hanging

**Covers:** the Assistant side panel · /agent · /admin/org (AI Config) · `POST /agent/chat` · `GET /agent/models` · `PUT /admin/ai/keys/:provider` · `POST /admin/ai/keys/:provider/test` · `DELETE /admin/ai/keys/:provider` · agents service: chat · agents service: agent
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key; permission to restart the local services · **Time:** ~20 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Give the org a bad key for the provider that answers (E2E-AIADM-02 step 8: **Rotate** to `AIzaQA7-invalid-key-000000000000000000000`). As counsel-a ask in the Ask panel, then on `/agent`. | The turn ends with an error. Panel: "The AI assistant isn't configured for your workspace yet. An admin needs to add an OpenAI or Anthropic API key in Organization → AI Config." (when the provider's error mentions the key; otherwise "Sorry, the AI assistant ran into a problem. Try again, or refresh if it persists."). `/agent`: the same text, the raw error (e.g. "… API key not valid …") and **Try again**. The failed turn is kept in the `/agent` conversation. `ask` prints `[error] …`. |
| 2 | Rotate back to the valid key, then click **Try again**. | The same question is sent again and answered. |
| 3 | Stop the agents service. Ask in the panel and on `/agent`. | Panel: "Sorry, the AI assistant ran into a problem. Try again, or refresh if it persists." `/agent`: the same, with "Stream failed (500)" (verify the status) and **Try again**. `GET /agent/models` → `502` `{"detail":"Agent service unavailable"}`. Contract Q&A returns clauses with "Agent unavailable — showing relevant clauses" (E2E-AI-15 step 7). Start the service again. |
| 4 | Stop the API and the agents service. Remove the model key variables from `apps/api/.env` and from the agents service's env. Start both. | The API log shows `[aiRouter] ⚠ No platform key for critical tier(s): default, fast. The app boots and all non-AI features (auth, browse, upload, manage contracts) work normally, but AI features return 503 until you set one of GOOGLE_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY in apps/api/.env and restart. …`. Sign-in, the Contracts list and contract pages work. |
| 5 | Ask in the panel and on `/agent`. `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST $API/agent/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"message":"hi","agentMode":true}'` | Panel and `/agent`: "The AI assistant is temporarily unavailable — please try again in a moment." (`/agent` adds "Stream failed (502)"). The API returns `502` `{"detail":"Internal Server Error"}`: the agents service refuses a chat when it has no key of its own. |
| 6 | Still without platform keys: as admin-a add a valid BYOK key (E2E-AIADM-02 step 4). Ask again. | Verify: the key tests **Verified** (the test calls the provider directly), but chat still fails as in step 5, because the agents service checks for its own key before it looks up the org's. File it if so. Remove the BYOK key. |
| 7 | Put the keys back in both env files and restart both services. Ask again. | Answered normally. |

**Also check**
- An empty model reply ends the turn with "The model returned an empty response — no answer was produced. This is usually
  transient; try asking again or rephrasing." (seen on `/agent` as the raw error). It can't be forced on demand.
- The daily cost cap refusal is E2E-AIADM-04 step 7–8.

**Known limits**
- The friendly "isn't configured" message appears only when the provider's error names the key. A stack with no platform
  key shows "temporarily unavailable", which suggests waiting rather than adding a key.
- A cost-cap refusal in the panel shows only the generic "Sorry, …" text; the reason ("Daily AI spend cap reached …")
  is visible only through the API.
## 8. Integrations, the API, platform security, the marketing site and production checks

This section covers four areas. **INT** is Admin → Integrations and the public REST API: API keys (scopes, the one-time reveal, revocation, expiry), calling the API with a key, webhooks and the worker that delivers them (`webhook.worker`), the payload and signature a receiver gets, failures, retries and the Health tab, Slack and Teams. **SEC** is security that cuts across the product: one organization can never reach another's data, own-scope users see only their own records, sessions expire and rotate, a deactivated user loses access, uploads are judged by their bytes, response headers and CORS, what a production API refuses that a development one allows, and the secrets and internal endpoints that must stay closed. (Personal-data masking before model calls is tested in §7.) **WEB** is the public marketing site, page by page, with its contact form, links, sitemap and claims tripwire. **PROD** is what to check on the hosted demo after each deploy, read-only or low-impact, plus the CI smoke scripts. Run it in this order: the INT journeys on the local stack first (they create the keys, webhooks and the local receiver that later journeys reuse), then SEC (it needs Org B), then WEB against the marketing dev server, then PROD: E2E-PROD-01 on the local stack before a release, E2E-PROD-02 to E2E-PROD-05 against production after each deploy.

### Before you start: setup used by this section

**Variables.** The tokens, ids and helpers of §0.5 (`$ADMIN_A`, `$COUNSEL_A`, `$CONTRACTS_A`, `$REP_A`, `$VIEWER_A`, `$LEGALOPS_A`, `$ADMIN_B`, `$ORG_A`, `$ORG_B`, `$ADMIN_A_ID`, `$COUNSEL_A_ID`, `$VIEWER_A_ID`, `$SEED`, `$QA`, `login`, `$INTERNAL_SECRET`). Access tokens live 15 minutes; run the `login` lines again when calls start answering 401 "Token invalid or expired". A curl `login` signs that user out of any browser tab at its next refresh (§0.5): use one user in the browser and another with curl, or sign in again afterwards. One more id, used by several journeys:

```bash
# The seeded Org A contract "Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement"
export C_A=$(curl -s "$API/contracts?search=Acme" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(.title=="Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement") | .id')
```

**Command R — a local webhook receiver (one line).** It listens on `http://localhost:8766`, prints every delivery (time, path, the `x-clm-event`, `x-clm-delivery-id` and `user-agent` headers, and the raw body), checks the `x-clm-signature` header when you give it the webhook's secret in `WHSEC`, and answers with the status in `STATUS` (default 200). Needs only Node, which the stack already uses. Stop it with Ctrl-C and start it again to change `WHSEC` or `STATUS`.

```bash
WHSEC='' STATUS=200 node -e 'const c=require("crypto");require("http").createServer((q,s)=>{let b="";q.on("data",d=>b+=d);q.on("end",()=>{const want="sha256="+c.createHmac("sha256",process.env.WHSEC||"").update(b).digest("hex");console.log(`\n${new Date().toISOString()} ${q.method} ${q.url}\nx-clm-event: ${q.headers["x-clm-event"]}  x-clm-delivery-id: ${q.headers["x-clm-delivery-id"]}  user-agent: ${q.headers["user-agent"]}\nsignature: ${process.env.WHSEC?(q.headers["x-clm-signature"]===want?"OK":"MISMATCH"):"(set WHSEC to check)"}\n${b}`);s.writeHead(Number(process.env.STATUS||200)).end("ok")})}).listen(8766,()=>console.log("receiver on http://localhost:8766"))'
```

**Letting the API deliver to your machine.** Webhook URLs that point at private addresses (localhost, 10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.169.254 …) are refused in every environment. For the INT journeys that use command R, add `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` to the repo-root `.env` and restart the API (stop `pnpm dev` and start it again; a variable set in the shell also works: `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true pnpm --filter api dev`). Remove it and restart when the INT journeys are done; E2E-INT-06 "Also check" confirms the guard is back. If you'd rather keep the guard on, a public request catcher you control (for example a fresh `https://webhook.site/<id>`) works too, but then demo data leaves your machine.

**The API runs the background workers in-process** in development (`webhook.worker` included), so deliveries happen seconds after the event. Run exactly one API process against your Redis (§0); a second one steals queued deliveries.

**Automated checks for this section** (run them first; a failure points at the same area):

```bash
pnpm --filter api exec vitest run src/lib/marketing-claims.test.ts src/lib/webhook-events-coverage.test.ts \
  src/lib/ssrf-guard.test.ts src/lib/file-type.test.ts src/lib/runtime-mode.test.ts src/lib/secrets.test.ts
# With the test database, Redis and MinIO from docs/38 §0.6:
#   src/routes/api-keys.integration.test.ts src/routes/api-key-create.integration.test.ts
#   src/routes/webhook-emit.integration.test.ts src/workers/webhook-redirect.integration.test.ts
#   src/routes/slack-team.integration.test.ts src/routes/marketing.integration.test.ts
#   src/routes/tenant-isolation-crawl.integration.test.ts src/routes/cross-org.integration.test.ts
#   src/routes/own-scope-rest.integration.test.ts src/routes/strict-mode.integration.test.ts
#   src/routes/internal-checks.integration.test.ts
```

### E2E-INT-01 · Only an admin can open Admin → Integrations; every other role is told to ask the admin

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-key-scopes` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `GET /admin/integrations/events` · `GET /admin/integrations/slack` · `GET /admin/integrations/health` · TC-KEY-01 (N7–N9), TC-WEB-03 (N4)
**Roles:** admin-a, legalops-a, counsel-a, contracts-a, rep-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in to `$WEB` as admin-a. A second browser or a private window for the other roles.
- Org A has no API keys or webhooks yet (a fresh `pnpm dev:setup` has none). If it has some, the counts below differ; everything else holds.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Left sidebar → **Admin** → **Integrations**. | URL `/admin/integrations`. Heading **Integrations** with the subtitle "API keys for external systems to call CLM, and webhooks for CLM to push events to you." Four tabs: **API Keys** (selected), **Webhooks**, **Slack**, **Health**. |
| 2 | Look at the **API Keys** tab. | "0 keys", a **New API key** button, and the empty state "No API keys yet." / "Create one to let an external system call `/api/v1/*` with Bearer auth." |
| 3 | Click **Webhooks**. | "0 webhooks", a **New webhook** button, and "No webhooks configured." / "Add a webhook to receive HMAC-signed POSTs when events fire (contract executed, signature completed, etc.)." |
| 4 | Click **Slack**. | Three cards: "1 · Create the Slack app", "2 · Connect it here", "3 · Notifications channel" (E2E-INT-09 goes through them). |
| 5 | Click **Health**. | Four cards: **Webhooks** "0/0 healthy" / "all good"; **Deliveries (24h)** "0" / "no failures"; **Success rate (7d)** "—" / "no deliveries yet"; **API keys** "0" / "never used". Below them "No webhooks configured." / "Add one on the Webhooks tab — health appears here once deliveries start flowing." and the note "Auto-refreshes every 30s. “Failing” = 3+ consecutive failures; “Degraded” = failures within the last 7 days." |
| 6 | Reload the page. | It opens on **API Keys** again: the selected tab is not kept in the URL. |
| 7 | In the second browser sign in as legalops-a. Look at the sidebar, then open `$WEB/admin/integrations` by URL with DevTools → Network open. | The sidebar has no **Admin** section. The page shows the heading **Integrations** and the notice **Admin access required**: "Integrations (API keys, webhooks) are managed by your organization admin. Contact your admin to enable an API key or webhook for your team." No tabs, and no request to `/api/v1/admin/integrations/…`. |
| 8 | Repeat step 7 as counsel-a, contracts-a, rep-a and viewer-a. | The same notice for each role. |
| 9 | API as legalops-a: command A with `T=$LEGALOPS_A`. | Every line reads `403 Missing permission: configure:organization`. (LEGAL_OPS holds `configure:integration`, which none of these routes accept.) |
| 10 | Command A with `T=$VIEWER_A`, then with `T=$ADMIN_A`. | viewer-a: the same six 403s. admin-a: `200` on all six lines. |
| 11 | No token: `curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks"` | 401 with `detail` "Missing or invalid Authorization header". |

Command A (the routes behind the four tabs; set `T` first; prints route, status and `detail` on one line):
```bash
for p in api-keys api-key-scopes webhooks events slack health; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/int01.json -w '%{http_code}' "$API/admin/integrations/$p" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T")
  printf '%-16s %s %s\n' "$p" "$code" "$(jq -r '.detail // empty' /tmp/int01.json)"; done
```

**Also check**
- Only ADMIN holds `configure:organization` (as its all-permissions grant). Every other built-in role gets the notice in step 7 and the 403s in step 9.
- An Org B admin opening the page sees only Org B's keys, webhooks and Slack settings (E2E-SEC-01).

**Known limits**
- The tab is not part of the URL, so a reload or a shared link always opens **API Keys**.
- If the key list request fails (for example the API is down), the API Keys tab shows "No API keys yet." instead of an error.
- The page shows no inbound email address. The per-contract address `contracts+<contract id>@<INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN>` appears only in share emails (as their Reply-To, with "You can also simply reply to this email with your marked-up copy attached…"), when `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN` is set: §4.

### E2E-INT-02 · An admin creates API keys with chosen scopes and an expiry, and sees each full key only once

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-key-scopes` · `POST /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · TC-KEY-01, TC-KEY-08
**Roles:** admin-a, viewer-a, legalops-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Signed in to `$WEB` as admin-a, on Admin → Integrations → **API Keys**.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Click **New API key**. | A dialog **New API key** with **Name** (placeholder "Salesforce sync"), **Scopes** with the hint "What this key may do. Choose at least one.", and **Expires**. Buttons **Cancel** and **Create key**; **Create key** is disabled. |
| 2 | Look at the Scopes box, then open **Expires**. | Exactly 11 checkboxes: `contracts:read`, `contracts:write`, `contracts:delete`, `contracts:sign`, `contracts:export`, `requests:read`, `requests:write`, `templates:read`, `templates:write`, `reports:read`, `admin`. Expires offers **Never** (selected), **30 days**, **90 days**, **1 year**. |
| 3 | Type a name and tick nothing. Then tick a scope and replace the name with three spaces. | **Create key** stays disabled both times; DevTools → Network shows no POST. |
| 4 | Name `QA reader`, tick `contracts:read`, Expires **30 days**, click **Create key**. | The dialog closes and a modal **API key created** opens: "This is the only time you'll see the full key. Copy it now — we don't store it." The key starts with `clm_live_`. Below it: "Use it as `Authorization: Bearer clm_live_…`" (the key's first 20 characters). Click **Copy**: the button reads **Copied**. Save the key as `$KEY_READ`. |
| 5 | Click **Done**. | The modal closes (it has no × and ignores clicks outside). The table has one row: Name `QA reader`; Prefix = the key's first 12 characters followed by "…"; Scopes `contracts:read`; Created by **Admin User**; Last used `never`; Status **Active**; a **Revoke** link. The heading reads "1 key". |
| 6 | Create three more the same way, saving each key: `QA writer` (`contracts:write`, Never) as `$KEY_WRITE`; `QA requests` (`requests:write` and `templates:read`, 90 days) as `$KEY_REQ`; `QA admin` (`admin`, Never) as `$KEY_ADMIN`. | Four rows, newest first, heading "4 keys". A key with two scopes shows them comma-separated. |
| 7 | `curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/api-key-scopes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` | 200 `{"scopes":[…]}` with the same 11 strings as step 2. |
| 8 | Create one by API (command A) and save its `key` as `$KEY_EXPORT`. | 201 with `id`, `name` "QA export only", `prefix`, `scopes` `["contracts:export"]`, `expiresAt` about 90 days ahead, `createdAt`, and `key` (the only response that ever carries it). |
| 9 | List by API (command B). | 200. Five items, each with `createdBy` = `{id, name: "Admin User", email: "admin@demo.com"}`. No item has a `key` or `keyHash` field. |
| 10 | Reload the page. | The table shows prefixes only; nothing on the page shows a full key again. |
| 11 | Admin → **Organization** → **Audit Log** tab. Type `API_KEY_CREATED` in **Action**, click **Filter**. | One `API_KEY_CREATED` entry per key, on `api_key · <key id>`, by Admin User; its metadata holds `name`, `scopes` and `expiresAt`. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA export only","scopes":["contracts:export"],"expiresInDays":90}' | jq
```

Command B:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" \
  | jq '.data[] | {name, prefix, scopes, expiresAt, revokedAt, lastUsedAt, createdBy}'
```

**Also check**
- Bad requests are refused with 400 `{"detail":"Invalid request","issues":[…]}` and create nothing (vary command A's body):
  - no `scopes` field, or `"scopes":[]` → the issue message is "Choose at least one scope — a key with no scopes cannot call any endpoint.";
  - `"scopes":["contracts:read","obligations:read"]` → the issue message starts "scopes must be a subset of: contracts:read, contracts:write, …";
  - `"expiresInDays":0` or `3651` → refused (1 to 3650 days are allowed);
  - a name longer than 100 characters → refused. In the dialog the red box shows only "Invalid request".
- viewer-a or legalops-a sending command A → 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization".
- **Cancel** or the × in the dialog's corner closes it and creates nothing.
- A token whose user can no longer make keys (demoted or deactivated within the token's 15 minutes) → 403 `detail` "Only an active member who can manage API keys can create one"; the agents service's internal headers get the same 403 (TC-KEY-08).
- An API key can't create keys, even an `admin` one (E2E-INT-04).

**Known limits**
- The key table has no expiry column. An expiry shows only as **Expired** once it has passed, and on the Health tab as "n expiring within 30d".
- Revoked keys stay listed; there is no delete, rename or regenerate. The list shows the newest 100 keys.
- Clicking outside the **New API key** dialog closes it and loses what was typed.
- Two scopes grant nothing usable: see E2E-INT-03.

### E2E-INT-03 · A system calling the REST API with a key gets what its scopes allow and a clear refusal for the rest

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Last used) · API routes called with keys: `GET /contracts`, `GET /contracts/:id`, `POST /contracts`, `PATCH /contracts/:id`, `DELETE /contracts/:id`, `GET /contracts/export`, `GET /templates`, `GET /clauses`, `POST /requests` · TC-KEY-02, TC-KEY-12, TC-KEY-13
**Roles:** admin-a (keys), admin-b · **Needs:** Org B · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- The keys from E2E-INT-02: `$KEY_READ`, `$KEY_WRITE`, `$KEY_REQ`, `$KEY_ADMIN`, `$KEY_EXPORT`. `$C_A` from the setup.
- An Org B contract: `C_B=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"ORG B SECRET MSA","type":"MSA"}' | jq -r .id)`

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_READ"` | `200`. |
| 2 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_READ" -o /tmp/c.json -w '%{http_code}\n'; jq -r .title /tmp/c.json` | `200`, then "Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement". |
| 3 | The same code-only call for `$API/templates` and `$API/clauses` with `$KEY_READ`. | `200` both: `contracts:read` includes templates and clauses. |
| 4 | Command A, line 1 (PATCH with the read key). | 403 `detail` "Missing permission: edit:contract". `$C_A`'s title is unchanged. |
| 5 | Command A, line 2 (create with the write key). Save `id` as `$C_KEY`. | 201. `ownerId` equals `$ADMIN_A_ID`: a key acts as the user who made it. Contracts in the web app lists "QA key contract". |
| 6 | Command A, line 3 (rename with the write key). | 200 with `title` "QA key contract (renamed)"; the Contracts list shows it after a reload. |
| 7 | Command A, line 4 (delete with the write key). | 403 `detail` "Missing permission: delete:contract"; the contract is still listed. |
| 8 | Command A, line 5 (raise a request with `$KEY_REQ`), then `GET $API/templates` and `GET $API/contracts` with `$KEY_REQ`. | 201 with an `id`; the request shows under Requests. Templates `200`; contracts 403 "Missing permission: view:contract". |
| 9 | `curl -s "$API/contracts/export" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_EXPORT"` | 403 `detail` "Missing permission: view:contract": the export routes need `view:contract`, and no route checks what `contracts:export` grants. |
| 10 | Another org's record: `curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_B" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_READ"` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`. |
| 11 | No or bad credentials: `curl -s "$API/contracts"`; then add `-H "Authorization: Bearer clm_live_notarealkey"`; then `-H "Authorization: Bearer not-a-token"`. | 401 "Missing or invalid Authorization header"; 401 `{"title":"Unauthorized","detail":"API key invalid or revoked","status":401}`; 401 "Token invalid or expired". |
| 12 | Reload Admin → Integrations → API Keys. | **Last used** shows a date and time for `QA reader`, `QA writer`, `QA requests` and `QA export only`; `QA admin` still reads `never`. |
| 13 | Open the **Health** tab. | The **API keys** card shows the number of unrevoked keys; its line reads "1 expiring within 30d" (`QA reader`), or "last used just now" when no key expires within 30 days. |

Command A (one request per line):
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$C_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_READ" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"should not change"}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_WRITE" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA key contract","type":"NDA"}' | jq '{id, title, ownerId}'
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$C_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_WRITE" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA key contract (renamed)"}' | jq '{title}'
curl -s -X DELETE "$API/contracts/$C_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_WRITE"
curl -s -X POST "$API/requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_REQ" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA key request","type":"NDA","description":"Mutual NDA with Acme"}' | jq '{id, title}'
```

**Also check** — what each scope lets a key do (refusals are 403 `detail` "Missing permission: <action>:<resource>"):

| Scope | The key may | Works, for example | Refused, for example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contracts:read` | view contracts, templates, clauses | `GET /contracts`, `GET /contracts/:id`, `GET /contracts/export`, `GET /obligations`, `GET /renewals`, `GET /invoices`, `GET /analytics/summary`, `POST /search` | `PATCH /contracts/:id` (edit:contract) |
| `contracts:write` | view, create and edit contracts | `POST /contracts`, `POST /contracts/upload`, `PATCH /contracts/:id`, `POST /matters` | `DELETE /contracts/:id` (delete:contract) |
| `contracts:delete` | delete contracts only | `DELETE /contracts/:id` | `GET /contracts` (view:contract) |
| `contracts:sign` | send, remind and void signature requests | `POST /contracts/:id/send-for-signature` | `GET /contracts` |
| `contracts:export` | nothing a route checks | — | `GET /contracts/export` (view:contract) |
| `requests:read` | view requests | `GET /requests` | `POST /requests` (create:request) |
| `requests:write` | view, create and edit requests | `POST /requests`, `PATCH /requests/:id` | `GET /contracts` |
| `templates:read` | view templates | `GET /templates`, `POST /templates/:id/preview` | `POST /templates` (create:template) |
| `templates:write` | view, create and edit templates | `POST /templates`, `PATCH /templates/:id` | `DELETE /templates/:id` (delete:template) |
| `reports:read` | nothing a route checks | — | `GET /analytics/summary` (view:contract) |
| `admin` | everything in its org except what E2E-INT-04 lists | `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks`, `GET /users`, `POST /admin/users/:id/deactivate` | key management, giving access, a person's own things |

- A contract, matter or converted request a key creates is owned by the key's maker (or the requester, for a converted request), and the record's creator field and audit entry name the key: TC-KEY-12, TC-KEY-13. A binder split requested by a key: TC-KEY-14.
- A key made before scopes were required (no scopes) shows "none — can’t call any endpoint" in red in the Scopes column and gets 403 "Missing permission: view:contract" (TC-KEY-02 N6, needs SQL).
- A contract created with a key fires `contract.created` to subscribed webhooks like any other (E2E-INT-07).

**Known limits**
- `contracts:export` and `reports:read` are offered in the dialog, but no route checks `export:contract` or `view:report`, so a key holding only those gets 403 everywhere. Exports need `contracts:read`.
- Last used is updated in the background and may lag the call by a moment.
