### E2E-INT-04 · No key can manage keys, give anyone access or act as a person, whatever its scope

**Covers:** `GET /admin/integrations/api-key-scopes` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `POST /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/api-keys/:id` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · TC-KEY-05, TC-KEY-09, TC-KEY-10, TC-KEY-11
**Roles:** admin-a (keys) · **Needs:** nothing extra (step 7: agents service + model key) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$KEY_ADMIN` and `$KEY_READ` from E2E-INT-02; `$VIEWER_A_ID` from the setup; `$READER_ID` = the id of `QA reader` (E2E-INT-02 command B).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Key management with the admin key: command A, lines 1–4. | Each prints 403 with `"detail":"This endpoint is for signed-in users, not API keys"`. The API Keys tab shows no key "Minted by key", and `QA reader` is still **Active**. |
| 2 | Giving access with the admin key: command A, lines 5–8 (invite an ADMIN, bulk-import an ADMIN, make viewer-a an ADMIN, reactivate viewer-a). | Each 403 with the same `detail`. Admin → Users shows no `qa-key-invite@…` or `qa-key-bulk@…`, and viewer-a still has the VIEWER role. |
| 3 | A person's own things with the admin key: command A, lines 9–15 (profile read and rename, password change, notifications, mark read, chat threads list and create). | Each 403 with the same `detail`. No user is renamed "Key"; no thread "Key thread" appears in anyone's Assistant history. |
| 4 | What the admin key may do: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"`, then the same for `$API/users` and `$API/organization`. | `200` each: an `admin` key manages webhooks and reads the org's shared data. |
| 5 | The org's shared data with a narrow key: command B with `T=$KEY_READ`. | Every line reads `403 This endpoint is not available to API keys without the admin scope`. |
| 6 | Command B with `T=$KEY_ADMIN`, then with `T=$VIEWER_A`. | `200` on each line except `skills/qa-no-such-skill` (`404`, "Skill not found", which means it got past the guard) and `agent/models` (`200`, or `502` "Agent service unavailable" when the agents service is down). A signed-in viewer gets the same codes. |
| 7 | Needs agents service + model key. Command C with `T=$KEY_READ`, then with `T=$KEY_ADMIN`. | With `$KEY_READ` the stream has no `tool_call_start` named `user_search` and the answer lists no member emails. With `$KEY_ADMIN` it may call `user_search` (TC-KEY-11). |

Command A (one request per line):
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/admin/integrations/api-key-scopes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Minted by key","scopes":["admin"]}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys/$READER_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/admin/users/invite" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"qa-key-invite@example.test","name":"Key Invite","roles":["ADMIN"]}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/admin/users/bulk-import" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '[{"email":"qa-key-bulk@example.test","name":"Key Bulk","roles":["ADMIN"]}]'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X PATCH "$API/admin/users/$VIEWER_A_ID/roles" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"roles":["ADMIN"]}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/admin/users/$VIEWER_A_ID/reactivate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X PATCH "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Key"}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/users/me/password" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"oldPassword":"whatever-123","newPassword":"whatever-456"}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/approvals/notifications" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/approvals/notifications/mark-read" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/agent/threads" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/agent/threads" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_ADMIN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"Key thread"}'
```

Command B (the org's shared data; set `T`; prints path, status and `detail` on one line):
```bash
for p in users team/workload organization organization/industry-packs admin/users/roles skills skills/qa-no-such-skill dashboard agent/models; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/int04.json -w '%{http_code}' "$API/$p" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T")
  printf '%-28s %s %s\n' "$p" "$code" "$(jq -r '.detail? // empty' /tmp/int04.json 2>/dev/null)"; done
```

Command C (one agent-mode chat turn; prints the tool calls):
```bash
curl -sN -X POST "$API/agent/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"List every member of our organization with their email address and role.","agentMode":true}' | grep tool_call_start
```

**Also check**
- An `admin` key may deactivate a user (for offboarding scripts) but never reactivate one: invite a throwaway VIEWER "QA Offboard" as admin-a (Admin → Users → **Invite User**), then `POST $API/admin/users/<its id>/deactivate` with `$KEY_ADMIN` → 200 `{"message":"User deactivated"}`; `POST …/reactivate` with the key → 403 as above; admin-a can reactivate it in Admin → Users (TC-KEY-05).
- A scope-less legacy key gets 403 on command B's paths too (TC-KEY-09 N3).

**Known limits**
- Webhooks, Slack settings and share links an `admin` key configured keep working after that key is revoked (accepted in X46).

### E2E-INT-05 · A revoked or expired key stops working at once, and both acts are on the audit record

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/api-keys/:id` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `GET /admin/integrations/health` · TC-KEY-02 (N7), TC-KEY-03, TC-KEY-04, TC-KEY-06
**Roles:** admin-a, admin-b · **Needs:** Org B; database access for step 8 · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Keys from E2E-INT-02. `QA reader` has been used (E2E-INT-03). `$READER_ID` and `$WRITER_ID` = the ids of `QA reader` and `QA writer` (E2E-INT-02 command B).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | API Keys tab → **Revoke** on `QA writer`, then **Cancel**. | The dialog closes; `QA writer` stays **Active**; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_WRITE"` prints `200`. |
| 2 | **Revoke** on `QA reader`. | Dialog **Revoke this API key?**: "QA reader clm_live_xxx… stops working immediately, and every system authenticating with it starts getting 401s. Revocation is permanent — issue a new key to restore access. This key was last used <date and time>." Buttons **Cancel** and **Revoke key**. |
| 3 | Click **Revoke key**. | The dialog closes. The row stays, with Status **Revoked** and no **Revoke** link. |
| 4 | `curl -s "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_READ"` | 401 `{"title":"Unauthorized","detail":"API key invalid or revoked","status":401}`. |
| 5 | Revoke it again by API: `curl -s -X DELETE "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys/$READER_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` | 404 `{"detail":"API key not found"}`. |
| 6 | Admin → **Organization** → **Audit Log**: **Action** `API_KEY_REVOKED` → **Filter**. | One `API_KEY_REVOKED` on `api_key · <QA reader id>` by Admin User. |
| 7 | Command A (the same filter through the API). | 200; the list holds exactly one `API_KEY_CREATED` and one `API_KEY_REVOKED`. |
| 8 | Expiry: create `QA lapsed` (`contracts:read`, 30 days) and save its key and id. Expire it in the dev database: `docker exec -it clm_postgres psql -U clm -d clm_dev -c "UPDATE api_keys SET \"expiresAt\" = now() - interval '1 minute' WHERE id = '<QA lapsed id>';"` Reload the tab and call `GET $API/contracts` with the key. | Status **Expired** (in red). The call answers 401 `detail` "API key expired". |
| 9 | Another org's admin: `curl -s -X DELETE "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys/$WRITER_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B"`; then `curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B"` | 404 `{"detail":"API key not found"}`; `QA writer` is still **Active** in Org A. Org B's list holds none of Org A's keys. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/audit?action=API_KEY_CREATED,API_KEY_REVOKED&resourceType=api_key&resourceId=$READER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '[.events[] | {action, resourceId}]'
```

**Also check**
- Revoking needs `configure:organization`: viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization"; any API key → 403 "This endpoint is for signed-in users, not API keys".
- Esc closes the confirm dialog like **Cancel**. With the API stopped, **Revoke key** leaves the dialog open with "Could not revoke this key. Try again.", and **Create key** in the New API key dialog shows "Failed to create.".
- A key stops working when the user who made it is deactivated, and it is marked **Revoked** with every key made through it (E2E-SEC-04, TC-KEY-04). A key whose maker is demoted from ADMIN answers 401 "API key invalid or revoked" but is not marked Revoked, and works again if the maker is made ADMIN again (TC-KEY-06, accepted behaviour).

**Known limits**
- Revocation can't be undone; issue a new key.
- The Health tab's **API keys** count includes keys that have expired but were never revoked.

### E2E-INT-06 · A webhook pointed at a local receiver gets a signed test event, and its delivery log shows it

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Webhooks tab) · `GET /admin/integrations/events` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/test` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries` · webhook.worker · TC-WEB-03, TC-SEC-07
**Roles:** admin-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** command R and `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` (setup) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Command R running (without `WHSEC` for now). The API restarted with `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true`.
- Signed in as admin-a on Admin → Integrations → **Webhooks**.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Command A (the events a webhook can subscribe to). | `15`, then: `contract.created`, `contract.uploaded`, `contract.updated`, `contract.executed`, `signature.sent`, `signature.completed`, `signature.voided`, `approval.submitted`, `approval.decided`, `obligation.extracted`, `obligation.completed`, `obligation.overdue`, `invoice.created`, `invoice.reconciled`, `amendment.created`. No `contract.expired`. |
| 2 | Click **New webhook**. | Dialog **New webhook**: **Name** (placeholder "Slack notifications"); **URL** (placeholder "https://your.app/clm-webhook  or  https://hooks.slack.com/services/…"); **Format** with **Generic JSON** "Standard envelope: { event, timestamp, data }" (selected), **Slack blocks** "Pretty rendering for Slack-compatible receivers" and **Teams card** "Adaptive Cards for Teams Workflows webhooks"; **Events** with the same 15 checkboxes. **Create webhook** is disabled. |
| 3 | Type Name `QA local hook` and URL `http://localhost:8766/hook`, no event. Then tick `contract.created` and `contract.updated` and change the URL to `localhost:8766/hook`. | **Create webhook** stays disabled until there is a name, a URL starting `http://` or `https://`, and at least one event. |
| 4 | Put the URL back to `http://localhost:8766/hook` → **Create webhook**. | The dialog closes. A card **QA local hook**, its URL under the name, and "2 events · never fired"; on the right **Test**, **Disable** and a trash icon. The heading reads "1 webhook". |
| 5 | Click the card's name to expand it. Then command B (the webhook's full signing secret) and restart command R with `WHSEC='<that value>'`. | The card shows "Subscribed events" with the chips `contract.created` and `contract.updated`, "Recent deliveries (0)" and "No deliveries yet — fire a test event to verify connectivity.". Command B prints a value starting `whsec_`. |
| 6 | Click **Test** on the card. | Within seconds command R prints a POST to `/hook` with `x-clm-event: webhook.test`, an `x-clm-delivery-id`, `user-agent: CLM-Webhooks/1.0`, `signature: OK`, and the body `{"event":"webhook.test","timestamp":"<ISO time>","data":{"message":"This is a test event from draftLegal","firedAt":"<ISO time>","orgId":"<Org A's id>"}}`. The page shows no confirmation. |
| 7 | Watch the expanded card (it refreshes every 5 s while open). | "Recent deliveries (1)": a green dot, `webhook.test`, the time, and "200 · 1 attempt". At the bottom "Signing secret: whsec_XXXXXXXXXX… (use to verify X-CLM-Signature)" (16 characters). Clicking the name again folds the card. |
| 8 | Reload the page. | The card line reads "2 events · last fired <date and time>". |
| 9 | Command C (the delivery log by API). | 200 `{"data":[…]}` with one item: `event` "webhook.test", `attempts` 1, `succeeded` true, `responseStatus` 200, `errorMessage` null, `createdAt`, `deliveredAt`. |
| 10 | Check the signature by hand: copy the body command R printed and run command D. | The same `sha256=…` value as the `x-clm-signature` header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact raw body, keyed with the whole `whsec_…` string. |
| 11 | Create a second webhook through the API, subscribed to every event: command E. Keep `$WH_ALL`. | 201; its `events` hold all 15. The tab lists **QA all events** with "15 events · never fired". Its deliveries print `signature: MISMATCH` in command R, which checks one secret at a time (restart R with its secret to check it). |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/events" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '.events | length, .'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA local hook") | .secret'
```
Command C:
```bash
WH_LOCAL=$(curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA local hook") | .id')
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_LOCAL/deliveries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq
```
Command D (paste the body exactly as printed between the single quotes):
```bash
WHSEC='<the secret>'
node -e 'console.log("sha256="+require("crypto").createHmac("sha256",process.argv[1]).update(process.argv[2]).digest("hex"))' "$WHSEC" '<raw body>'
```
Command E:
```bash
WH_ALL=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/events" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -c '{name:"QA all events", url:"http://localhost:8766/hook", events:.events}')" | jq -r .id); echo "$WH_ALL"
```

**Also check**
- Create refusals by API (400; nothing created): `"events":[]`, a missing name, `"url":"ftp://example.com/x"` or `"type":"email"` → `{"detail":"Invalid request","issues":[…]}`; `"events":["contract.expired"]` → `{"detail":"Unknown events: contract.expired"}`. In the dialog the red box shows the `detail` only.
- `POST …/webhooks/<id>/test` answers `{"ok":true,"message":"Test delivery queued"}`; an unknown or deleted id → 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}`.
- viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization" on every webhook route. An `admin` API key may create and test webhooks (TC-KEY-05 P1).
- The address guard, when you remove `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS` and restart at the end of the INT journeys: creating a webhook to `http://localhost:8766/hook`, `http://127.0.0.1/x`, `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or `http://[::1]/x` → 400 "Invalid request" with the issue "Webhook URL must be a public http(s) endpoint" (the dialog shows only "Invalid request"). **Test** on a localhost webhook that already exists (QA flaky hook) then logs a failed delivery with status "—" and the error "Webhook URL host is not allowed". A public name that resolves to a private address fails at delivery with "Webhook URL resolves to a private or internal address"; redirects are not followed: "Redirect (307) not followed: set the webhook to its final URL" (TC-SEC-07).

**Known limits**
- The page shows only the first 16 characters of the signing secret; the full secret is only in the API (the create response and the list). There is no way to rotate it except deleting and re-creating the webhook.
- The signature covers the body only; there is no timestamp header, so a receiver that wants to refuse replays must check the body's `timestamp` itself.
- **Test** gives no confirmation; the result appears in the expanded card or after a reload. On a disabled webhook, **Test** sends nothing and logs nothing.

### E2E-INT-07 · Real product events reach only the webhooks subscribed to them; Disable, edit and delete work

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Webhooks tab) · `PATCH /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries` · webhook.worker · TC-WEB-04, TC-WEB-05
**Roles:** admin-a, contracts-a, counsel-a, admin-b · **Needs:** command R and the flag; Org B; agents service + model key for step 9 · **Time:** ~30 min

**Preconditions**
- **QA local hook** and **QA all events** (`$WH_ALL`) from E2E-INT-06; command R running.
- A third webhook subscribed to `invoice.created` only: **New webhook**, Name `QA invoices only`, URL `http://localhost:8766/invoices` (its own path, so you can tell its deliveries apart), event `invoice.created` → **Create webhook**.
- A new contract for the events: `C_H=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA hook contract","type":"NDA","counterpartyName":"Hook Co"}' | jq -r .id)` (this is step 1).

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Create `$C_H` (command in Preconditions). | Command R prints `contract.created` twice (QA local hook and QA all events), `data` `{contractId, title: "QA hook contract", type: "NDA", status, counterpartyName: "Hook Co"}`. Nothing on `/invoices`. |
| 2 | Upload `D-NDA.docx`: Contracts → **Upload PDF** → drop it → **Upload contract**. | `contract.uploaded` once (only QA all events subscribes): `{contractId, title, filename, mimeType, fileSize}`, `mimeType` the DOCX type. |
| 3 | Command A, line 1 (rename `$C_H`). | `contract.updated` twice: `{contractId, title: "QA hook contract (renamed)", status, changes: ["title"], source: "user"}`. |
| 4 | Command A, line 2 (add an SOW under `$C_H`). | 201. `amendment.created` on QA all events: `{contractId (the new SOW), parentContractId: $C_H, relationshipType: "sow", title: "QA SOW 1", type}`. |
| 5 | Command A, line 3 (log an invoice); keep `.invoice.id` as `$INV_H`. | `invoice.created` on QA all events and on `/invoices`: `{invoiceId, contractId, vendorName: "Hook Co", amount: 1200, currency: "USD", status}`. |
| 6 | Command A, line 4 (reconcile it). | `invoice.reconciled` on QA all events: `{invoiceId, contractId, obligationId, reconciledAt}` (`obligationId` null when the invoice matched no obligation). |
| 7 | Approvals (§5): on a DRAFT contract click **Send for Review** and send it; then as counsel-a approve it in **Approvals**. | `approval.submitted`: `{contractId, title, type, value, currency, instanceId, stepId, stepName, approverId}`. Then `approval.decided`: `{instanceId, contractId, stepId, decision: "APPROVED", instanceStatus, decidedBy}`. Approved through the Assistant's confirm card, it also carries `via: "agent"` (TC-WEB-05). |
| 8 | Signatures (§5): send a contract for signature and have every signer sign; void a second request; have the signer of a third decline with a reason. | `signature.sent` `{contractId, signatureRequestId, signerCount, signOrder, expiresAt}`; when all have signed, `signature.completed` `{contractId, signatureRequestId, signerCount, completedAt}` and `contract.executed` `{contractId, executedAt}`; the void gives `signature.voided` with `reason` "Voided by sender"; the decline gives `signature.voided` with `reason` "<signer name> declined: <reason>". |
| 9 | Needs agents service + model key. Obligations (§6): extract obligations from a contract whose text has one date already past; complete one; then run the scan with command A, line 5. | `obligation.extracted` `{contractId, count}`; `obligation.completed` `{obligationId, contractId, type, completedAt, hasEvidence}`; `obligation.overdue` once for the past-due one `{contractId, obligationId, description, dueDate, daysOverdue}`. A second scan sends no second `obligation.overdue`. |
| 10 | Expand **QA invoices only**. | "Recent deliveries (1)": only `invoice.created`. A webhook gets only the events it subscribed to. |
| 11 | As admin-b rename an Org B contract (`PATCH $API/contracts/$C_B` with `$ADMIN_B`). | Nothing reaches command R: Org A's webhooks never get Org B's events. |
| 12 | Click **Disable** on **QA all events**, then run command A, line 1 again with another title. | The card gets a **Disabled** chip and its button reads **Enable**. Only QA local hook delivers this `contract.updated`; QA all events gets no delivery and no row in its log. Click **Enable**: the chip goes and the next event arrives again. |
| 13 | Edit through the API (the page has no edit form): command B. | `{"ok":true}`. After a reload the card reads **QA all events (renamed)** and "1 event". A new `contract.created` (create another contract as in step 1) now reaches only QA local hook. |
| 14 | Trash icon on **QA local hook**; click **Cancel**; then the trash icon again. | Dialog **Delete this webhook?**: "QA local hook stops receiving events at http://localhost:8766/hook. Anything downstream that relies on contract.created, contract.updated goes quiet with no error on their side. To pause instead, use Disable." Buttons **Cancel** and **Delete webhook**. **Cancel** (or Esc) closes it and keeps the webhook. |
| 15 | Click **Delete webhook**; then command C. | The card disappears and the heading count drops. Command C: the delivery log → 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}`; deleting again → 404, the same. The next contract event doesn't reach `/hook` from it. |

Command A (one request per line):
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/contracts/$C_H" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA hook contract (renamed)"}' | jq .title
curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_H/amendments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTRACTS_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"relationshipType":"sow","title":"QA SOW 1"}' | jq '{id, parentContractId}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"vendorName":"Hook Co","amount":1200,"currency":"USD","invoiceDate":"2026-09-01","contractId":"'"$C_H"'"}' | jq '{id: .invoice.id}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/invoices/$INV_H/reconcile" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq .status
curl -s -X POST "$API/cron/obligations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_ALL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA all events (renamed)","events":["contract.updated"]}'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_LOCAL/deliveries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_LOCAL" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"
```

**Also check**
- `PATCH` refusals (the webhook is unchanged after each): `{"events":["contract.updated","contract.expired"]}` → 400 `{"detail":"Unknown events: contract.expired"}`; `{"events":[]}` or `{"url":"not a url"}` → 400 "Invalid request"; a deleted id or another org's id → 404 "Webhook not found".
- **Disable** / **Enable** send `PATCH {"enabled":false}` / `{"enabled":true}`. `PATCH` accepts `name`, `url`, `events` and `enabled`, not the format (`type`).
- The delete dialog names at most three events and "+n more": try it on a webhook with all 15.
- Delete hides and disables the webhook; its delivery rows stay in the database.
- Error states: stop the API, then confirm a delete → the dialog stays open with "Could not delete this webhook. Try again."; submit **New webhook** → the red box "Failed to create webhook.". Start the API again.
- An event whose webhook is disabled or deleted after it was queued is skipped by the worker, with no delivery row (the API log says "no longer eligible — skipping").

**Known limits**
- The page can enable, disable and delete a webhook, but not rename it or change its URL, events or format: use `PATCH`, or delete and re-create for a new format.
- `contract.expired` isn't offered: nothing in the product moves a contract to EXPIRED.
- Events fire after the change is saved; a failed delivery never undoes the change.

### E2E-INT-08 · A failing receiver is retried, shows as Failing on the Health tab, and Retry re-sends the failed event

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Webhooks and Health tabs) · `GET /admin/integrations/health` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries/:deliveryId/retry` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries` · webhook.worker
**Roles:** admin-a, viewer-a · **Needs:** command R and the flag · **Time:** ~20 min (about 3 of them waiting)

**Preconditions**
- Command R restarted with `STATUS=500`. It answers every webhook with 500, so click **Disable** on **QA all events (renamed)** (still subscribed to `contract.updated`) for this journey, and **Enable** it at the end.
- A webhook **QA flaky hook**, URL `http://localhost:8766/flaky`, event `contract.updated` only (create it on the Webhooks tab). `$WH_FLAKY` = its id (command A, line 1).
- `$C_H` from E2E-INT-07. Admin-a on the **Health** tab.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Look at QA flaky hook's row on **Health**. | Status **Healthy**; Webhook column the name and URL; Last delivery "never"; 24h "0 ok"; 7d "0 ok"; Last error "—"; no **Retry**. |
| 2 | Rename `$C_H` (E2E-INT-07 command A, line 1, with a new title). | Command R prints a `contract.updated` POST to `/flaky` and answers 500. |
| 3 | **Webhooks** tab → expand QA flaky hook. | "Recent deliveries (1)": a red dot, `contract.updated`, "500 · 1 attempt", and the error "Non-2xx response: 500". The card has the chip "1 failure". |
| 4 | Wait about 3 minutes, watching command R. | Four more POSTs, roughly 10, 20, 40 and 80 seconds apart: 5 attempts in all, each with its own `x-clm-delivery-id`. The log shows 5 rows, each "500 · 1 attempt"; the chip reads "5 failures". |
| 5 | **Health** tab (it refreshes every 30 s; reload to see it at once). | QA flaky hook: **Failing** with "5 consecutive failures" under it; Last delivery "<n>m ago" and "failed"; 24h "0 ok · 5 failed"; 7d "0 ok · 5 failed"; Last error "Non-2xx response: 500" over "contract.updated · <n>m ago"; a **Retry** button. The **Webhooks** card reads "<healthy>/<total> healthy", its line includes "1 failing", and it turns red; **Deliveries (24h)** says "5 failed" (or more); **Success rate (7d)** is below 100%. |
| 6 | Command A, line 2 (the health API). | 200. QA flaky hook's entry: `health` "failing", `consecutiveFailures` 5, `deliveries` `{"ok24h":0,"fail24h":5,"ok7d":0,"fail7d":5}`, `lastFailure` `{deliveryId, event: "contract.updated", errorMessage: "Non-2xx response: 500", responseStatus: 500, at}`. `summary` has `failing` ≥ 1, `deliveries24h`, `failed24h`, `successRate7d`; `apiKeys` has `active`, `expiringSoon`, `lastUsedAt`. |
| 7 | Restart command R with `STATUS=200`. On **Health** click **Retry** on QA flaky hook. | The icon spins; about 2 s later the table refreshes. Command R prints `contract.updated` again: the same `data` as step 2, a new `x-clm-delivery-id`. The row turns **Degraded** (failures within 7 days); the consecutive-failures line is gone; Last delivery "just now" and "success"; 24h "1 ok · 5 failed". |
| 8 | Retry refusals: command A, lines 3–4; then click **Disable** on the card and run line 5. | A delivery that succeeded → 400 `{"detail":"Delivery already succeeded"}`. An unknown delivery → 404 `{"detail":"Delivery not found"}`. On the disabled webhook → 400 `{"detail":"Webhook is disabled — enable it before retrying"}`; Health shows **Disabled**, with no **Retry**, and the Webhooks card's "n disabled" count goes up by one. Click **Enable** afterwards. |
| 9 | Stop command R, rename `$C_H` again, and within a minute start command R again with `STATUS=200`. | The first attempt fails with status "—" and Node's connection error as the message (verify: "fetch failed"); a later automatic attempt succeeds. The card's failure chip disappears (the last delivery succeeded) and the consecutive failures reset to 0. |

Command A (the delivery ids come from `GET $API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_FLAKY/deliveries`, `data[].id` with `succeeded` true or false):
```bash
WH_FLAKY=$(curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[] | select(.name=="QA flaky hook") | .id')
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '{summary, apiKeys, flaky: (.webhooks[] | select(.name=="QA flaky hook"))}'
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_FLAKY/deliveries/<a succeeded delivery id>/retry" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_FLAKY/deliveries/no-such-delivery/retry" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_FLAKY/deliveries/<a failed delivery id>/retry" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"
```

**Also check**
- Health states: **Healthy** = enabled, no failure in 7 days; **Degraded** = a failure in the last 7 days, or 1–2 consecutive failures; **Failing** = 3 or more consecutive failures; **Disabled** = switched off. The Webhooks card turns amber for degraded, red for failing.
- The Success rate card: green at 95% and above, amber from 80%, red below; "—" / "no deliveries yet" with no deliveries in 7 days.
- A receiver that never answers fails after 15 seconds (verify: the error reads "This operation was aborted").
- viewer-a → 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization" on the health and retry routes.

**Known limits**
- Each attempt is its own delivery row, so "· n attempts" always reads 1 and one failed event shows as 5 rows. The `x-clm-delivery-id` header changes with every attempt, so a receiver can't use it to recognise a repeat.
- **Retry** is offered only for each webhook's most recent failed delivery (older ones need the API with their id), and it stays offered after a later delivery succeeded; retrying then sends the old event again.
- After the fifth failed attempt nothing retries on its own; the Health tab is where it shows.
- The receiver's response body is not shown anywhere (with the address guard on it isn't stored either).

### E2E-INT-09 · Slack: connect the workspace, post events to a channel, test the slash command, disconnect

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Slack and Webhooks tabs) · `GET /admin/integrations/slack` · `PUT /admin/integrations/slack` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/slack` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/test` · webhook.worker · TC-ACC-01, TC-ACC-02, TC-SEC-08, TC-SEC-09
**Roles:** admin-a, rep-a, legalops-a · **Needs:** command R and the flag (steps 8–9); a real Slack workspace is optional (steps 10–11) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Org A has no Slack connection (the Slack tab shows the three setup cards). If it has one, note its Team ID, disconnect it, and reconnect it at the end.
- Admin-a on Admin → Integrations → **Slack**.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Read card "1 · Create the Slack app". | "Go to api.slack.com/apps → “Create New App” → “From a manifest”, pick your workspace, and paste this manifest…". A dark box holds the manifest: app and bot name `draftLegal`, slash command `/contract` with `url` = your browser's address + `/api/v1/slack/commands` (locally `http://localhost:5173/api/v1/slack/commands`), interactivity `request_url` ending `/api/v1/slack/interactions`, bot scopes `commands`, `incoming-webhook`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`. Below it the amber note "Slack must be able to reach these URLs — in local dev use a tunnel (ngrok / cloudflared) and adjust the manifest." |
| 2 | Click the copy icon at the top right of the manifest ("Copy manifest"). | The icon turns into a tick for about 1.5 s; the clipboard holds the manifest JSON. |
| 3 | Card "2 · Connect it here": type a **Team ID** only. | **Connect Slack** stays disabled until both **Team ID** and **Signing secret** are filled. **Signing secret** and **Bot token (optional)** hide what you type. |
| 4 | **Team ID** `TQA8SLACK`, **Signing secret** `qa-slack-secret-8`, no bot token → **Connect Slack**. | The form is replaced by **Slack workspace connected**: Workspace (team ID) `TQA8SLACK`; Signing secret "configured"; Bot token (button-click identity) "not set — buttons fall back to web links"; Workspace ownership "unverified — reconnect with the bot token so no other org can claim this workspace"; Connected <date and time>; two bullets; **Disconnect**. |
| 5 | `curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/slack" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A"` | `{"connected":true,"teamId":"TQA8SLACK","configuredAt":"…","hasSigningSecret":true,"hasBotToken":false,"teamVerified":false}`. No secret. |
| 6 | Command A with `$REP_A`, then with `$ADMIN_A`. | `0` both times: the organization settings every member reads never hold the secret; their `settings.slack` is only `{connected, teamId, configuredAt, hasSigningSecret, hasBotToken}` (TC-ACC-01). |
| 7 | Test the connection with a signed slash command: `export API SECRET=qa-slack-secret-8 TEAM=TQA8SLACK TEXT='search Acme'`, run command B; then `TEXT=''`; then `TEXT='search zzzz-nothing'`. | 200 with `text` "<n> contract(s) matching “Acme”" and blocks listing up to 5 Org A contracts, each linking to `http://localhost:5173/contracts/<id>`. Empty `TEXT`: the help, `text` "Usage: /contract search <query>". The last: `text` "No contracts matching “zzzz-nothing”.". Admin → Organization → Audit Log, Action `AGENT_ACTION`: an entry on `integration · slack` with metadata `command` "/contract", `query` and `results`. |
| 8 | Slack messages without Slack: **Webhooks** → **New webhook**, Name `QA slack format`, URL `http://localhost:8766/slack`, **Format** **Slack blocks**, events `approval.submitted` and `contract.executed` → **Create webhook** → **Test**. | Command R prints `{"text":"🔔 Test event from CLM","blocks":[{"type":"header","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"🔔 Test event from CLM"}},{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"Your webhook is wired correctly. You should see real events here as contracts move through their lifecycle."}}]}`, still with an `x-clm-signature`. |
| 9 | Send a contract for review (§5) and watch command R. | An `approval.submitted` message: `text` "📝 Approval requested: <title>", header "📝 Approval requested", a section with the linked title and "<type> · <value> · step: <step name>", and buttons "✅ Approve" (`approval_approve`), "❌ Reject" (`approval_reject`) and "Open in draftLegal" (link `…/contracts/<id>?tab=approval`). |
| 10 | Optional, real Slack: in your Slack app's settings add an incoming webhook for the channel you want and copy its URL (`https://hooks.slack.com/services/…`). **New webhook** → paste it. | Under the URL: "Slack URL detected — events will be formatted as Slack messages."; the **Format** choice disappears. Create it with `approval.submitted` and click **Test**: the channel shows "🔔 Test event from CLM". Approve/Reject clicks need Slack to reach the interactivity URL (a tunnel locally): §5. |
| 11 | Optional, real Slack: disconnect (step 13), then connect with the real Team ID, signing secret and the app's `xoxb-` bot token. | Workspace ownership "verified by the bot token"; `GET …/slack` has `"teamVerified":true`. With a tunnel, `/contract search <word>` typed in Slack answers in the channel. |
| 12 | In the connected card, click the underlined words "Slack webhook" in the second bullet. | Nothing happens: it looks like a link but isn't. Open the **Webhooks** tab yourself. |
| 13 | **Disconnect**. | Dialog **Disconnect Slack?**: "/contract stops responding in every channel, and Approve / Reject buttons in already-posted approval messages stop working — approvers will have to come back into draftLegal. Your signing secret and bot token are deleted; reconnecting means pasting them again from the Slack app config." Buttons **Cancel** and **Disconnect Slack**. Confirm: the setup cards return; `GET …/slack` → `{"connected":false}`; command B → 401 `{"detail":"invalid Slack signature or unconnected workspace"}`. |

Command A (count the secret in the organization settings; set the token):
```bash
curl -s "$API/organization" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" | grep -c 'qa-slack-secret-8'
```
Command B (a correctly signed `/contract` request, Slack's v0 signature; `export API SECRET TEAM TEXT` first):
```bash
node -e '
const c = require("crypto");
const body = new URLSearchParams({ team_id: process.env.TEAM, user_id: "UQA0001", command: "/contract", text: process.env.TEXT }).toString();
const ts = String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000));
const sig = "v0=" + c.createHmac("sha256", process.env.SECRET).update("v0:" + ts + ":" + body).digest("hex");
fetch(process.env.API + "/slack/commands", { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "x-slack-request-timestamp": ts, "x-slack-signature": sig }, body })
  .then(async r => console.log(r.status, await r.text()));'
```
Command C (connect through the API; vary `botToken`):
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X PUT "$API/admin/integrations/slack" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"teamId":"TQA8SLACK","signingSecret":"qa-slack-secret-8","botToken":"abc"}'
```

**Also check**
- Connect refusals (command C, or the red box under the form; nothing is saved): `"botToken":"abc"` → 400 `{"detail":"Bot token must start with xoxb-"}`; `"xoxb-qa-not-a-real-token"` (needs internet) → 400 "Slack rejected the bot token (invalid_auth)."; a real token of another workspace → 400 "That bot token belongs to Slack workspace T…, not TQA8SLACK."; a missing Team ID or secret → 400 "Invalid request".
- `TEXT='Acme'` (no "search") searches too; a wrong `SECRET`, an unknown `TEAM` or a body that isn't urlencoded → 401 "invalid Slack signature or unconnected workspace"; a body over 256 KB → 413 (TC-SEC-09).
- Two orgs naming the same team id each get their own results, and Org B connecting doesn't disconnect Org A (TC-SEC-08). Saving organization settings can't overwrite or blank the Slack configuration (TC-ACC-02).
- rep-a and legalops-a → 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization" on `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /admin/integrations/slack`.
- `PUT` while connected replaces the configuration (the page offers the form only after **Disconnect**).
- Error states, with the API stopped: **Connect Slack** shows the red box "Failed to save."; **Disconnect Slack** leaves the dialog open with "Could not disconnect. Try again.".

**Known limits**
- There is no channel picker and no test button on the Slack tab: the channel is chosen in Slack when you create the incoming webhook, and the test is that webhook's **Test** button.
- The manifest's URLs are the browser's own address; Slack can't reach a local stack without a tunnel, and the manifest must be edited by hand for it.
- The underlined "Slack webhook" in the connected card does nothing.
- Connecting and disconnecting Slack is not written to the audit log (slash-command searches are, as `AGENT_ACTION`).
- The slash command and the Approve/Reject buttons in depth: §5 (`POST /slack/commands`, `POST /slack/interactions`).

### E2E-INT-10 · Teams: events arrive as Adaptive Cards through a Teams workflow webhook

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` (Webhooks tab) · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/test` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id` · webhook.worker
**Roles:** admin-a · **Needs:** command R and the flag; a Microsoft Teams tenant is optional (step 6) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- Command R running; admin-a on the **Webhooks** tab.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | **New webhook**; paste the made-up Teams workflow URL `https://prod-00.westus.logic.azure.com:443/workflows/qa/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?sig=qa`. | Under the URL: "Teams workflow URL detected — events will be formatted as Adaptive Cards."; the **Format** choice disappears. |
| 2 | Name `QA teams detect`, tick `approval.submitted` → **Create webhook**. Run command A. Then delete it (trash icon → **Delete webhook**) without testing, so nothing goes to Microsoft. | Command A lists it with `"type":"teams"`. |
| 3 | The API detects it too: command B, then `DELETE $API/admin/integrations/webhooks/<its id>`. | 201 with `"type":"teams"` although no `type` was sent (hosts ending `.logic.azure.com`, `.webhook.office.com` or `.powerplatform.com`); the delete answers 204. |
| 4 | Locally: **New webhook** `QA teams format`, URL `http://localhost:8766/teams`, **Format** **Teams card**, events `approval.submitted`, `approval.decided`, `signature.sent`, `contract.updated` → **Create webhook** → **Test**. | Command R prints `{"type":"message","attachments":[{"contentType":"application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive","content":{"$schema":"http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json","type":"AdaptiveCard","version":"1.4","body":[{"type":"TextBlock","size":"Medium","weight":"Bolder","text":"🔔 Test event from draftLegal","wrap":true},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Your Teams webhook is wired correctly. You should see real events here as contracts move through their lifecycle.","wrap":true,"spacing":"Small"}]}}]}` with a signature. |
| 5 | Send a contract for review (§5), approve it, rename a contract, and send one for signature. | `approval.submitted`: "📝 Approval requested", the title in bold, facts Type / Value / Step, and one action **Review & decide** opening `…/contracts/<id>?tab=approval`. `approval.decided`: "✅ Approval approved" (or "❌ Approval rejected"), fact Contract, action **Open in draftLegal**. `contract.updated` has no card of its own: "🔔 contract.updated" with up to six facts and **Open in draftLegal**. `signature.sent`: "✍️ Signature request sent" with the fact Contract only (see Known limits). |
| 6 | Optional, with Teams: in a Teams channel add the Workflows template that posts a card when a webhook request is received; copy its URL; create a webhook with it (Teams is detected) and click **Test**. | The channel shows the card "🔔 Test event from draftLegal". |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq '.data[] | {name, type, url}'
```
Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"QA teams api","url":"https://prod-00.westus.logic.azure.com:443/workflows/qa/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?sig=qa","events":["approval.submitted"]}' | jq '{id, type}'
```

**Also check**
- The dialog's detection needs a host with a part before `logic.azure.com`, `webhook.office.com` or `powerplatform.com`; for a URL it doesn't recognise, **Format** stays visible and the default is **Generic JSON** unless you pick **Teams card**.
- With a Slack URL pasted, the Slack format wins whatever format was picked before.

**Known limits**
- Teams cards have no Approve / Reject buttons (that would need an Azure bot); approvers use **Review & decide**.
- There is no Teams connection page: Teams is a webhook format only.
- The `signature.sent` card never shows the number of signers: it reads a `signers` field, while the event sends `signerCount`.
- A webhook's format can't be changed after creation; delete and re-create it.

### E2E-SEC-01 · Org B can't see or change anything of Org A's, in the UI or through the API

**Covers:** `/contracts/:id` and the Contracts search (as admin-b) · `/admin/integrations` (as admin-b) · `/agent` · Admin → Organization → Audit Log · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `PATCH /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/test` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries` · `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id/deliveries/:deliveryId/retry` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/webhooks/:id` · `GET /admin/integrations/health` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `DELETE /admin/integrations/api-keys/:id` · `GET /admin/integrations/slack` · plus the contract, search, share-link, thread, audit, user, approval and organization routes in command B · TC-ACC-01, TC-ACC-15, TC-ACC-24, TC-KEY-03 (N3–N5), TC-SEC-08, TC-WEB-04 (N2)
**Roles:** admin-a (fixtures), admin-b · **Needs:** Org B; agents service + model key for step 5 · **Time:** ~30 min

**Preconditions**
- Org B exists (§0) and has a contract `$C_B` (E2E-INT-03). `$ADMIN_B` is fresh.
- Org A fixtures from earlier journeys and command A: `$C_A`; a portal link `$LINK_A` on it; QA flaky hook (`$WH_A`) with a failed delivery `$DLV_A` (E2E-INT-08); the `QA writer` key id (`$KEY_A_ID`); an Assistant thread `$THREAD_A`; an audit event `$AUDIT_A`; `$COUNSEL_A_ID`; an approval `$APPROVAL_A` if one exists (E2E-INT-07 step 7).
- admin-b signed in to `$WEB` in a second browser.

Command A (as admin-a):
```bash
LINK_A=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_A/share" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"label":"QA SEC-01"}' | jq -r .shareLink.id)
WH_A=$WH_FLAKY
DLV_A=$(curl -s "$API/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/deliveries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.succeeded==false)][0].id')
KEY_A_ID=$WRITER_ID
THREAD_A=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/agent/threads" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA SEC-01 thread"}' | jq -r .id)
AUDIT_A=$(curl -s "$API/admin/audit?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.events[0].id')
APPROVAL_A=$(curl -s "$API/approvals/all" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r '.data[0].instanceId // empty')
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As admin-b open `$WEB/contracts/$C_A`. | "Contract not found" and **Back to Contracts**; nothing of the Acme contract. |
| 2 | As admin-b: Contracts → type `Acme` in "Search by title, counterparty, or content…". | No Org A contract (with none of Org B's matching: "No contracts match your filters"). |
| 3 | As admin-b: Admin → **Integrations**, each tab. | Only Org B's keys and webhooks (none of the QA ones), Org B's own Slack state, and health for Org B only. |
| 4 | As admin-b: Admin → **Organization** → **Audit Log**. | Only Org B's events; nothing about Acme, QA keys or QA webhooks. |
| 5 | Needs agents service + model key. As admin-b: **Assistant** → "What is the liability cap in the Acme Corp — Master Services Agreement?" | The answer says it can't find that contract (or asks which one); it never quotes Org A's terms (the seeded cap is "$500,000") or names other Org A contracts. |
| 6 | Command B: every call is admin-b's token against Org A's ids. | Each line's status and message as in the table below. |
| 7 | Afterwards, as admin-a. | `$C_A` keeps its title; `GET $API/contracts/$C_A/share` still lists `$LINK_A`; QA flaky hook is unchanged; `QA writer` is **Active**; counsel-a can sign in; `GET $API/agent/threads/$THREAD_A` still returns the thread. |
| 8 | As admin-b rename `$C_B` (`PATCH $API/contracts/$C_B` with `{"title":"ORG B renamed"}`). Then, as admin-a, expand Org A's webhooks on the Webhooks tab. | No Org A webhook gets a delivery for it (no new row in any log; nothing at command R if it still runs): Org A's webhooks get only Org A's events. |
| 9 | An Org A key on Org B data: `curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_B" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_WRITE"` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`. |
| 10 | As admin-b invite an address that has an account in Org A: `POST $API/admin/users/invite` with `{"email":"legal@demo.com","name":"X","roles":["VIEWER"]}`. | 409 "A user with this email already has an account in another workspace. Ask them to use a different email or contact support to merge accounts." No organization is named. |

What command B must print, line by line:

| Line | Call as admin-b | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /contracts/$C_A` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` |
| 2 | `PATCH /contracts/$C_A` `{"title":"hijack"}` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` |
| 3 | `DELETE /contracts/$C_A` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` |
| 4 | `GET /contracts/$C_A/download` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` |
| 5 | `GET /contracts/$C_A/attachments/0/download` | 404 `{"detail":"Contract not found"}` |
| 6 | `GET /contracts/$C_A/comments` | 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}` |
| 7 | `POST /search` `{"q":"Acme"}` | 200; `data` has no Org A contract |
| 8 | `GET /search/facets` | 200; `total` is Org B's own count |
| 9 | `GET /contracts/$C_A/share` | 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}` |
| 10 | `POST /contracts/$C_A/share` `{}` | 404 `{"error":"Contract not found"}` |
| 11 | `DELETE /contracts/$C_A/share/$LINK_A` | 404 `{"error":"Share link not found"}` |
| 12 | `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` | 200; no Org A webhook |
| 13 | `PATCH /admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A` `{"url":"https://example.com/stolen"}` | 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}` |
| 14 | `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/test` | 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}` |
| 15 | `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/deliveries` | 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}` |
| 16 | `POST /admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/deliveries/$DLV_A/retry` | 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}` |
| 17 | `DELETE /admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A` | 404 `{"detail":"Webhook not found"}` |
| 18 | `GET /admin/integrations/health` | 200; only Org B's webhooks and key counts |
| 19 | `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` | 200; no Org A key |
| 20 | `DELETE /admin/integrations/api-keys/$KEY_A_ID` | 404 `{"detail":"API key not found"}` |
| 21 | `GET /admin/integrations/slack` | 200; Org B's own state (`{"connected":false}` unless Org B connected Slack) |
| 22 | `GET /agent/threads/$THREAD_A` | 404 `{"detail":"Thread not found"}` |
| 23 | `POST /agent/threads` `{"id":"$THREAD_A"}` | 409 "A record with these details already exists" (see Known limits); Org A's thread unchanged |
| 24 | `GET /admin/audit/$AUDIT_A` | 404 `{"detail":"Audit event not found"}` |
| 25 | `GET /admin/audit?action=API_KEY_CREATED` | 200; none of Org A's key events |
| 26 | `GET /users` | 200; only Org B's members |
| 27 | `GET /admin/users/$COUNSEL_A_ID` | 404 `{"detail":"User not found"}` |
| 28 | `POST /admin/users/$COUNSEL_A_ID/deactivate` | 404 `{"detail":"User not found"}` |
| 29 | `GET /approvals/$APPROVAL_A` (when set) | 404 `{"error":"Approval instance not found"}` |
| 30 | `GET /organization` | 200; Org B's own name and settings |

Command B (bash or zsh; `b METHOD PATH [JSON]` prints the body, then the status):
```bash
b() { if [ -n "$3" ]; then curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X "$1" "$API$2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$3"; else curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X "$1" "$API$2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_B"; fi; }
b GET    "/contracts/$C_A"
b PATCH  "/contracts/$C_A" '{"title":"hijack"}'
b DELETE "/contracts/$C_A"
b GET    "/contracts/$C_A/download"
b GET    "/contracts/$C_A/attachments/0/download"
b GET    "/contracts/$C_A/comments"
b POST   "/search" '{"q":"Acme"}'
b GET    "/search/facets"
b GET    "/contracts/$C_A/share"
b POST   "/contracts/$C_A/share" '{}'
b DELETE "/contracts/$C_A/share/$LINK_A"
b GET    "/admin/integrations/webhooks"
b PATCH  "/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A" '{"url":"https://example.com/stolen"}'
b POST   "/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/test"
b GET    "/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/deliveries"
b POST   "/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A/deliveries/$DLV_A/retry"
b DELETE "/admin/integrations/webhooks/$WH_A"
b GET    "/admin/integrations/health"
b GET    "/admin/integrations/api-keys"
b DELETE "/admin/integrations/api-keys/$KEY_A_ID"
b GET    "/admin/integrations/slack"
b GET    "/agent/threads/$THREAD_A"
b POST   "/agent/threads" "{\"id\":\"$THREAD_A\"}"
b GET    "/admin/audit/$AUDIT_A"
b GET    "/admin/audit?action=API_KEY_CREATED"
b GET    "/users"
b GET    "/admin/users/$COUNSEL_A_ID"
b POST   "/admin/users/$COUNSEL_A_ID/deactivate"
[ -n "$APPROVAL_A" ] && b GET "/approvals/$APPROVAL_A"
b GET    "/organization"
```

**Also check**
- Matter links, matter views and counts never cross organizations (TC-ACC-24); chat history belongs to the org, user and session that wrote it (TC-ACC-15).
- Two orgs claiming the same Slack team id each get only their own contracts from `/contract search` (TC-SEC-08).
- An Org A API key revoked by Org B's admin: 404 (E2E-INT-05 step 9).

**Known limits**
- A portal link is a credential in itself: whoever holds its URL can open that one contract, whatever their organization (§4). That's by design, not an org boundary.
- Line 23: creating a thread with another org's thread id answers 409, which tells the caller that id exists somewhere; ids are random, and nothing is read or changed.
- These are spot checks. The automated crawl (`tenant-isolation-crawl.integration.test.ts`) calls every route with another org's ids, with and without the database-level isolation.

### E2E-SEC-02 · A sales rep (own scope) sees and counts only their own contracts and requests

**Covers:** `/contracts`, `/contracts/:id`, `/counterparties/:id`, `/dashboard`, `/obligations`, `/renewals`, `/invoices`, `/diligence`, `/analytics`, `/agent`, `/admin/integrations` (as rep-a) · `GET /contracts/:id`, `GET /contracts/export`, `POST /search`, `GET /search/facets`, `POST /search/portfolio-query`, `POST /contracts/:id/amendments` · TC-ACC-07 to TC-ACC-13, TC-ACC-20 to TC-ACC-23
**Roles:** rep-a, counsel-a, admin-a · **Needs:** nothing extra (step 12: agents service + model key) · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Two contracts with the same counterparty, one per owner (command A). If Counterparties has no "Zephyr QA", add it as counsel-a (**Add Counterparty**).
- rep-a signed in to `$WEB` in one browser, admin-a in another.

Command A:
```bash
C_REP=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"Rep Alpha MSA","type":"MSA","counterpartyName":"Zephyr QA"}' | jq -r .id)
C_OTHER=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"Kestrel Bravo Terms","type":"MSA","counterpartyName":"Zephyr QA"}' | jq -r .id)
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | As rep-a: **Contracts**. As admin-a: **Contracts**. | rep-a sees "Rep Alpha MSA" and not "Kestrel Bravo Terms"; admin-a sees both. |
| 2 | As rep-a open `$WEB/contracts/$C_OTHER`. | "Contract not found" and **Back to Contracts**. |
| 3 | Command B with `T=$REP_A`, then with `T=$ADMIN_A`. | rep-a: `404` on every line (body `{"detail":"Contract not found"}`: 404, not 403, so the rep can't tell the contract exists). admin-a: `200` on every line, except `/download`, which may answer 404 "No file stored for this version" for a contract made without a file. |
| 4 | As rep-a: Contracts search box → `Kestrel`. | "No contracts match your filters". |
| 5 | Command C (rep-a's CSV export, search and facets). | The export contains no "Kestrel Bravo Terms" (`0`); the search returns an empty `data`; the facets' `total` is the number of contracts rep-a owns. |
| 6 | `curl -s -X POST "$API/search/portfolio-query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"all Zephyr QA contracts"}'` | 403 `detail` "Portfolio queries need access to all contracts. Use search to find your own." |
| 7 | As rep-a: **Counterparties** → **Zephyr QA**. | Only "Rep Alpha MSA" is listed (admin-a's page lists both). |
| 8 | **Dashboard** as rep-a, then as admin-a. | rep-a's **Active Contracts** and **Open Requests** count only rep-a's records, lower than admin-a's. |
| 9 | As rep-a: **Obligations**, **Renewals**, **Invoices**, **Diligence**, **Analytics**. | Only rows and counts from rep-a's own contracts (and rooms rep-a created); TC-ACC-10 has the exact figures to compare. |
| 10 | `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_OTHER/amendments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"QA amendment"}'`; then the same on `$C_REP`. | 404 "Contract not found"; then 201 on rep-a's own contract. |
| 11 | As rep-a open `$WEB/admin/integrations`. | **Admin access required** (E2E-INT-01). |
| 12 | Needs agents service + model key. As rep-a: **Assistant** → "List our MSAs with Zephyr QA." | Only "Rep Alpha MSA" (TC-ACC-13). |

Command B (the contract and its sub-routes; set `T`):
```bash
for p in "" /versions /comments /signature-requests /download /family /precedents; do printf '%-22s ' "${p:-/}"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/contracts/$C_OTHER$p" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T"; done
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s "$API/contracts/export" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" | grep -c "Kestrel Bravo Terms"
curl -s -X POST "$API/search" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"q":"Kestrel"}' | jq '.data | length'
curl -s "$API/search/facets" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A" | jq .total
```

**Also check**
- Signature-request lists (TC-ACC-11), the approval count and team workload (TC-ACC-20), signing links for signers who can't open the contract (TC-ACC-21), converted requests (TC-ACC-22), the collaboration server (TC-ACC-23), and the Assistant's tools under own scope (TC-ACC-12, TC-ACC-16).
- counsel-a (org scope) sees both contracts everywhere.

**Known limits**
- Own scope comes only with the built-in SALES_REP role; custom roles can't be created (the Roles page is read-only, §1).

### E2E-SEC-03 · Sessions expire and rotate: stale or signed-out tokens are refused, and the app recovers cleanly

**Covers:** `/login`, any signed-in page · `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `POST /auth/logout` (§1's routes, used here) · TC-SES-01 to TC-SES-05, TC-SEC-12, TC-SEC-13
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~25 min (includes waiting for tokens to expire)

**Preconditions**
- So you don't wait 15 minutes, restart the API with a short access-token lifetime: `JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES_IN=3m pnpm --filter api dev` (keep the unit: a bare number is read as milliseconds). Put it back to the default afterwards.
- Chrome, one tab on `$WEB`, DevTools → Network with **Preserve log** and the filter `api/v1`. Paste these console helpers (again after every reload):
```js
const claims = t => JSON.parse(atob(t.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/')))
const auth = () => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('clm-auth')).state
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Sign in at `$WEB/login` as counsel-a. Run `claims(auth().accessToken)`; note `auth().refreshToken` as R1 and `auth().accessToken` as `$OLD`. | `/dashboard` opens. The claims show `type: "access"`, a `sid`, and `exp - iat` = 180 (900 with the default 15m). The `POST /api/v1/auth/login` response has `"expiresIn":180`. |
| 2 | Keep the tab in front and wait 3½ minutes. | About 30 s after expiry the app's polling gets 401s, makes one `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (200), and repeats the failed calls with the new token. You stay on the page, signed in. |
| 3 | `curl -s "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD"` | 401 `detail` "Token invalid or expired". |
| 4 | `curl -s -X POST "$API/auth/refresh" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"refreshToken":"<R1>"}'` | 401 `{"detail":"Refresh token revoked"}`: step 2's refresh rotated it. |
| 5 | Sign counsel-a in with curl (`login legal@demo.com $SEED`), go back to the browser and wait for its next refresh (up to 3½ minutes). | The browser's `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` answers 401 "Refresh token revoked" and the tab goes to `/login?next=<the page you were on>`: one session per user. |
| 6 | Sign in again. | You land on the page named in `next`. |
| 7 | Note `auth().refreshToken`, then the user menu (your initials and name, top right) → **Sign out**. Send the noted token to `POST $API/auth/refresh`. | The app shows `/login` (without `next`). The refresh answers 401 "Refresh token revoked". |
| 8 | Open `$WEB/login?next=//evil.example` and sign in; sign out; then `$WEB/login?next=https://evil.example`. | Both land on `/dashboard`: `next` only accepts a path on this site. |
| 9 | Change one character in the last part of `$OLD` and call `GET $API/users/me` with it; then call it with a refresh token as the Bearer. | 401 "Token invalid or expired" both times. |

**Also check**
- Two tabs of the same user share one session without signing each other out (TC-SES-02); only a refused refresh signs a tab out, and only that tab (TC-SES-03); a refresh rotates atomically (TC-SES-04); sign-out ends the server session even after an idle pause (TC-SES-05).
- Signing links and portal links expire on their own clock (§4, §5; TC-SEC-12). Collaboration connections are refused after token expiry and closed when access changes (TC-SEC-13).

**Known limits**
- Access tokens aren't revoked on the server: one keeps working until it expires (15 minutes by default), even after **Sign out** or a deactivation (E2E-SEC-04). Refresh tokens are revoked at once.
- There is no "sign out everywhere"; a new sign-in or a deactivation ends the other session at its next refresh.

### E2E-SEC-04 · A deactivated user loses access, and their API keys die with them

**Covers:** `/admin/users` (§1), `/login`, `/admin/integrations` · `POST /admin/users/:id/deactivate`, `POST /admin/users/:id/reactivate`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh` · `POST /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · TC-KEY-04, TC-KEY-08
**Roles:** admin-a, a disposable admin "QA Key Maker" · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- Command A creates the disposable admin, signs it in with curl and makes a key with that session. It prints "Invite accepted. You can now log in." and the key.
- Then sign in to `$WEB` as `qa-keymaker@example.test` in a private window and open the Dashboard (the curl token stays valid: access tokens outlive a new sign-in).

Command A:
```bash
KM=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/users/invite" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"qa-keymaker@example.test","name":"QA Key Maker","roles":["ADMIN"]}')
KM_ID=$(echo "$KM" | jq -r .id)
curl -s -X POST "$API/auth/accept-invite" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"token\":\"$(echo "$KM" | jq -r .inviteToken)\",\"password\":\"QaKeyMaker-2026!\"}" | jq -r .message
KEYMAKER=$(login qa-keymaker@example.test 'QaKeyMaker-2026!')
KM_KEY=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEYMAKER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"KM key","scopes":["contracts:read"]}' | jq -r .key); echo "$KM_KEY"
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KM_KEY"` | `200`. |
| 2 | As admin-a: Admin → **Users** → the row menu of QA Key Maker ("Actions for QA Key Maker") → **Deactivate…** → dialog **Deactivate this user?** → **Deactivate user**. | The row's status reads **Deactivated**. |
| 3 | Admin → **Integrations** → **API Keys**. | "KM key", Created by QA Key Maker, is **Revoked**. |
| 4 | Admin → **Organization** → **Audit Log**: Action `USER_DEACTIVATED` → **Filter**; expand the newest. | `USER_DEACTIVATED` on `user · <KM_ID>` by Admin User, with metadata `apiKeysRevoked: 1`. |
| 5 | `curl -s "$API/contracts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KM_KEY"` | 401 "API key invalid or revoked". |
| 6 | With the deactivated user's curl token (inside its lifetime): `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/users/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEYMAKER"`; then command B. | `/users/me` still answers `200` until the token expires (see Known limits). Command B: 403 `detail` "Only an active member who can manage API keys can create one"; no key is created. |
| 7 | The private window: wait until its access token expires (15 minutes, or 3 with E2E-SEC-03's setting). | Its `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` answers 401 "Refresh token revoked" and the tab goes to `/login?next=…`. |
| 8 | Try to sign in as QA Key Maker in the browser; then with command C. | The login page shows "Invalid email or password". The API answers 403 `{"detail":"Account deactivated. Contact your admin."}` (see Known limits). |
| 9 | As admin-a: ⋮ on QA Key Maker → **Reactivate**. Repeat step 5, then sign in as QA Key Maker. | The user is Active and can sign in again; "KM key" stays **Revoked** and still gets 401. |
| 10 | Guard rails, as admin-a: deactivate yourself (`POST $API/admin/users/$ADMIN_A_ID/deactivate`); deactivate QA Key Maker twice; deactivate admin-b (its id: `GET $API/users` with `$ADMIN_B`, the entry for admin@orgb.test). | 400 "Cannot deactivate yourself"; the second time 400 "User is already deactivated"; 404 "User not found", and admin-b can still sign in. |

Command B:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "$API/admin/integrations/api-keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEYMAKER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"KM late key","scopes":["contracts:read"]}'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"qa-keymaker@example.test","password":"QaKeyMaker-2026!"}'
```

**Also check**
- Keys made through the deactivated user's keys (possible before X46) are revoked with them and stay revoked after a reactivation (TC-KEY-04, needs SQL).
- An `admin` API key may deactivate a user but not reactivate one (E2E-INT-04).
- viewer-a deactivating anyone → 403 "Missing permission: configure:user".
- Clean up: deactivate QA Key Maker again when done.

**Known limits**
- Access tokens are stateless: a deactivated user's open session works until its access token expires (15 minutes by default), then it is signed out. Only key creation re-checks the user at once.
- The login page shows "Invalid email or password" for every refusal: a deactivated account, an invitation not accepted yet (the API says "Please accept your invitation first."), and rate limiting. The real reason is only in the API's answer.

### E2E-SEC-05 · Uploads are judged by their bytes: disguised, empty and legacy files are refused

**Covers:** `/contracts` (**Upload PDF** → **Upload Contracts**) · `POST /contracts/upload`, `POST /contracts/:id/versions`, `POST /contracts/:id/attach`, `GET /contracts/:id/versions` · TC-ACC-04, TC-ACC-05, TC-ACC-06, TC-DOC-08
**Roles:** counsel-a · **Needs:** nothing extra · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- Command A makes the test files in `~/qa-sec05`; copy `D-MSA.pdf` (§0) there too. Run the curl commands from that folder.
- Signed in to `$WEB` as counsel-a; `$COUNSEL_A` fresh; `$C_A` from the setup.

Command A:
```bash
mkdir -p ~/qa-sec05 && cd ~/qa-sec05
printf '<html><body><script>alert(document.domain)</script></body></html>' > fake.pdf
printf '\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nnot-really-an-image' > image.pdf
printf '\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0\xa1\xb1\x1a\xe1legacy-word' > old.docx
printf 'MZ\x90\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00program' > program.docx
: > empty.pdf
echo 'just a zip' > inner.txt && zip -q notdocx.docx inner.txt
printf 'Plain text services agreement.\nFees: 100 USD.\n' > notes.txt
```
Command B (upload `F` declared as `TYPE` as a new contract):
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@$F;type=$TYPE"
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | UI: **Contracts** → **Upload PDF** → the dialog **Upload Contracts** ("PDF, DOCX, or TXT · up to 50 MB each · multiple files supported") → drop `fake.pdf` → **Upload contract**. | The file's row turns red with "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT."; no new contract in the list. |
| 2 | Command B with `F=image.pdf TYPE=application/pdf`. | 415 `{"detail":"This file type is not accepted here. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT."}` |
| 3 | `F=old.docx TYPE=application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` | 415 "Legacy .doc files are not supported. Open the file in Word, save it as .docx, and upload again." |
| 4 | `F=program.docx` (same TYPE), then `F=notdocx.docx`. | 415 "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT." both times. |
| 5 | `F=empty.pdf TYPE=application/pdf` | 400 "The uploaded file is empty." |
| 6 | `F=D-MSA.pdf TYPE=text/html` (a real PDF declared as HTML); read the new contract's versions: `GET $API/contracts/<new id>/versions`, field `data[0].mimeType`. | 201, and `mimeType` is `application/pdf`: the detected type is stored, not the declared one. |
| 7 | `F=notes.txt TYPE=text/plain` | 201; its version's `mimeType` is `text/plain`. |
| 8 | A disguised file as a new version: command C, line 1. | 415 "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, TXT."; `$C_A`'s version count is unchanged. |
| 9 | A disguised file as an attachment: command C, line 2. | 415 "Unsupported or mismatched file type. Allowed: PDF, DOCX, DOC, XLSX, TXT, CSV." (attachments accept more types, and a legacy `.doc` is allowed there, stored as `application/msword`). |

Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_A/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@fake.pdf;type=application/pdf" -F "changeNote=SEC-05"
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_A/attach" -H "Authorization: Bearer $COUNSEL_A" -F "file=@fake.pdf;type=application/pdf" -F "label=SEC-05"
```

**Also check**
- Request attachments, diligence-room uploads and obligation evidence use the same check (TC-ACC-05); the counterparty portal and inbound email refuse disguised files, and downloads are served only as an allowed type, anything else as `application/octet-stream` (TC-ACC-06).
- A DOCX that inflates past 100 MB is refused without being expanded: 413 "This DOCX expands to more than 100 MB when opened, or is damaged, so it can't be processed." (TC-DOC-08).
- The dialog's own filter accepts any file named `.pdf`, `.docx` or `.txt`: the server is the real check.

**Known limits**
- Files over 50 MB are refused; legacy `.doc` can't be a contract, only an attachment.

### E2E-SEC-06 · The API and the hosted sites send security headers, refuse foreign origins, and rate-limit

**Covers:** `GET /marketing/contact/health` (as a probe) · the API's `/health/live` · `POST /auth/login` · `POST /slack/commands` · TC-SEC-09 (N5)
**Roles:** anonymous · **Needs:** nothing extra (step 8: internet) · **Time:** ~10 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -sI http://localhost:3001/health/live` | 200 with `cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin`, `cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin`, `origin-agent-cluster: ?1`, `referrer-policy: no-referrer`, `strict-transport-security: max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `x-dns-prefetch-control: off`, `x-download-options: noopen`, `x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN`, `x-permitted-cross-domain-policies: none`, `x-xss-protection: 0`, an `x-request-id`, and `x-ratelimit-limit: 10000` with `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset`. No `content-security-policy` and no `x-powered-by`. |
| 2 | `curl -sI http://localhost:3001/health/live -H 'x-request-id: qa-trace-1'` | `x-request-id: qa-trace-1` comes back: the id a bug report can quote. |
| 3 | An allowed origin: `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "$API/marketing/contact/health" -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5174'` | `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5174`, `access-control-allow-credentials: true`, `access-control-expose-headers: content-disposition,x-redline-stats`. |
| 4 | A foreign origin: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/marketing/contact/health" -H 'Origin: https://evil.example'` | 403 with `detail` "Origin https://evil.example not allowed". |
| 5 | A preflight from the app's origin: `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X OPTIONS "$API/contracts" -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: PATCH' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type'` | 204 with `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173` and `access-control-allow-methods` including `PATCH`. |
| 6 | The per-email sign-in limit, with an email that has no account: command A. | Attempts 1–10: 401 "Invalid email or password". The 11th: 429 `{"detail":"Too many login attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."}`. Never use a real user's email: it would lock them out for 15 minutes. |
| 7 | An oversized Slack request: command B. | 413: the Slack routes take at most 256 KB. |
| 8 | The hosted sites (read-only): `curl -sI https://app.draft-legal.com/` and `curl -sI https://draft-legal.com/` | App: `x-frame-options: DENY`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` on the page. Site: `x-content-type-options: nosniff` and `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, no `x-frame-options`. verify: whether Firebase Hosting adds `strict-transport-security`. |

Command A:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 11); do curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nobody-qa@example.test","password":"wrong-password"}'; done
```
Command B:
```bash
python3 -c "print('text=' + 'a'*300000)" | curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/slack/commands" -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @-
```

**Also check**
- The local web and marketing dev servers send none of the hosting headers; check them on the hosted sites (step 8, E2E-PROD-03).
- Sign-in is also limited to 200 attempts per 15 minutes per address ("Too many login attempts from your network. Try again in 15 minutes."); registration to 5 per hour per address ("Too many registration attempts. Try again in an hour."): don't use up §0's Org B registration.
- The whole API is limited to 10,000 requests a minute per address in development and 1,000 in production (E2E-SEC-07 step 2, E2E-PROD-03 step 4); the contact form to 5 an hour (E2E-WEB-04).

**Known limits**
- No Content-Security-Policy is sent by the API, the app or the marketing site.
- The marketing site can be framed by another site (no `x-frame-options`).
