### E2E-SEC-07 · Production refuses what development allows: weak secrets, development-only flags and the looser rate limit

**Covers:** the API's boot checks (FIX_TRACKER Y5) · `/health`, `/health/live`, Bull Board (`/admin/queues`) · TC-SEC-01, TC-SEC-02, TC-SEC-03, TC-SEC-05
**Roles:** operator (no app user) · **Needs:** the local infrastructure; a terminal in `apps/api` · **Time:** ~20 min

**Preconditions**
- These steps start a second, throw-away API on port 3091 in production mode, with the workers and the collaboration server off so it takes no jobs from your dev API. Stop it (Ctrl-C) after each step.
- Three strong values: `export S1=$(node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('base64url'))")`, and the same for `S2` and `S3`.
- Command A is the base run; a variable given on the command line wins over the `.env` file, so each step changes only what it names. `<fix>` below stands for `Generate one: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('base64url'))"`.

Command A:
```bash
NODE_ENV=production PORT=3091 WORKERS_ENABLED=false COLLAB_DISABLED=1 BULL_BOARD_OPEN= INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL= \
JWT_SECRET="$S1" PORTAL_JWT_SECRET="$S2" INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET="$S3" \
pnpm exec tsx --env-file=../../.env src/index.ts
```

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Run command A. In another terminal: `curl -s http://localhost:3091/health` | The API logs "API listening on http://0.0.0.0:3091". `/health` has `"versions":{"node":"…","env":"production","commit":"unknown"}`. |
| 2 | `curl -sI http://localhost:3091/health/live` and `curl -sI http://localhost:3001/health/live`; compare `x-ratelimit-limit`. | `1000` on 3091 (strict), `10000` on 3001 (development). |
| 3 | `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3091/admin/queues/api/queues`; then again with `-H "x-internal-secret: $S3"`. | `{"error":"Unauthorized"} 401`; then 200 with the six queues `documents`, `notifications`, `agents`, `scans`, `webhooks`, `signing`. |
| 4 | Stop it. Command A with `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true` (instead of the empty value). | The process exits before listening: `Error: [runtime-mode] BULL_BOARD_OPEN (opens the Bull Board queue UI without the internal secret) is for a developer's own stack, and NODE_ENV=production is strict. Unset it, or run with NODE_ENV=development.` |
| 5 | Command A with `INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL=1`. | It exits: `… INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL (accepts inbound email from any sender into any contract) is for a developer's own stack, and NODE_ENV=production is strict. …` |
| 6 | Command A with `NODE_ENV=staging BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true`; then `NODE_ENV=` (empty) with the same flag. | The same refusal, naming `NODE_ENV=staging`, then `NODE_ENV=unset`: anything but `development` or `test` is strict. |
| 7 | Command A with `INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET=change-me-internal-secret-min-32-chars` (the `.env.example` value). | It exits: `Error: [secrets] INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET is set to a known-insecure placeholder. Refusing to boot with NODE_ENV=production. <fix> and set it on the API, the worker and the agents service.` |
| 8 | Command A with `JWT_SECRET="${S1:0:31}"` (31 characters). | It exits: `Error: [secrets] JWT_SECRET is too short (31 chars); require >= 32 with NODE_ENV=production. <fix>` |
| 9 | Command A with `PORTAL_JWT_SECRET=` (empty). | It exits: `Error: [secrets] PORTAL_JWT_SECRET is not set. Refusing to boot with NODE_ENV=production on an insecure default. <fix> and set PORTAL_JWT_SECRET.` |
| 10 | Command A with `INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET=` (empty). | It boots, with the warning `[secrets] INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET is not set: the agents service can't call the API. <fix> and set it on the API, the worker and the agents service.`; every internal call is then refused (TC-SEC-01 N5). |
| 11 | Step 7's placeholder with `NODE_ENV=development`, and `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true`. | It boots with the warning `[secrets] INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET is a placeholder — fine for dev, but production will refuse to boot with it.`, and Bull Board answers 200 without the header: development allows both. |

**Also check** — what strict mode changes:

| | Development (`NODE_ENV=development`) | Strict (production, staging, a preview, unset) |
|---|---|---|
| Placeholder or short JWT, portal or internal secret | a warning; boots | refuses to boot |
| `JWT_SECRET` or `PORTAL_JWT_SECRET` unset | a local secret is generated and kept | refuses to boot |
| `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true` | Bull Board opens without the secret | refuses to boot |
| `INBOUND_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL=1` | inbound mail from any sender is accepted | refuses to boot |
| Rate limit, whole API | 10,000 a minute per address | 1,000 |
| Seed admin password | `password123` | `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (12+ characters, never containing password123) or a random one printed once (TC-SEC-03) |
| Signing certificate | a self-signed one is generated | `SIGNING_CERT_P12_BASE64` and `SIGNING_CERT_PASSPHRASE` required ("[signing-cert] SIGNING_CERT_P12_BASE64 + SIGNING_CERT_PASSPHRASE are required outside development and tests…") |
| Links printed to the console (signing, share, invite) | whole | masked (`/portal/[REDACTED]`, TC-OPS-04) |
| Log format | readable | JSON lines |
| Inbound email from an unknown sender | 403 naming the development flag | 403 "Sender <email> is not authorised on this contract." |

- The same in every mode: the webhook address guard (off only with `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true`, allowed in any mode for self-hosted installs that deliver to their own network) and Bull Board needing the internal secret.
- The agents service refuses a weak secret on Cloud Run, and the self-host edge drops the internal headers (TC-SEC-02).

**Known limits**
- The throw-away API shares your dev database and Redis; always keep `WORKERS_ENABLED=false` on it.
- The signing-certificate refusal needs a seal, which runs in the worker (off here); `strict-mode.integration.test.ts` covers it.

### E2E-SEC-08 · Secrets and internal endpoints stay closed

**Covers:** `/admin/integrations` · `GET /admin/integrations/webhooks` · `GET /admin/integrations/api-keys` · `GET /admin/integrations/slack` · the internal routes (`/api/internal/ai/*`, Bull Board, the chunk callback), `POST /inbound/email`, `PATCH /approvals/:instanceId/summary`, `GET /metrics` · TC-ACC-01, TC-SEC-04, TC-SEC-05, TC-SEC-06, TC-OPS-03, TC-OPS-04
**Roles:** admin-a, counsel-a, rep-a · **Needs:** database access (step 1); `$INTERNAL_SECRET` (§0) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Keys are stored hashed: `docker exec -it clm_postgres psql -U clm -d clm_dev -c "SELECT name, prefix, length(\"keyHash\") AS hash_len FROM api_keys ORDER BY \"createdAt\" DESC LIMIT 5;"` | Each key has its 12-character prefix and a 64-character hash (SHA-256); no column holds a full key. |
| 2 | Webhook secrets: `GET $API/admin/integrations/webhooks` with `$COUNSEL_A`, then with `$ADMIN_A`. | counsel-a: 403 "Missing permission: configure:organization". admin-a: every webhook with its full `secret`. The page shows only 16 characters of it. |
| 3 | Slack secrets, with Slack connected (E2E-INT-09 step 4): `curl -s "$API/organization" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REP_A"`, then with `$ADMIN_A`. | `settings.slack` is `{"connected":true,"teamId":…,"configuredAt":…,"hasSigningSecret":true,"hasBotToken":false}` for both; no secret anywhere (TC-ACC-01). |
| 4 | The agents service's internal API without the secret: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/internal/ai/tools/contract_search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'`; again with `-H 'x-internal-secret: wrong'`. | 401 `{"detail":"Internal endpoint — bad secret"}` both times. |
| 5 | Posing as the agents service on a normal route: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/contracts" -H 'x-internal-service: agents' -H 'x-internal-secret: wrong'` | 401 "Missing or invalid Authorization header": a wrong secret gets no bypass. |
| 6 | Bull Board: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3001/admin/queues/api/queues`; then with `-H "x-internal-secret: $INTERNAL_SECRET"`. | 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` (unless your `.env` sets `BULL_BOARD_OPEN=true`); then 200 with the six queues. Encoded paths such as `/%61dmin/queues/api/queues` are refused too (TC-SEC-05). |
| 7 | The chunk-and-index callback without the secret: command A. | 401 `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}`. |
| 8 | Inbound email with no `INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET` configured: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/inbound/email" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"to":"contracts+'"$C_A"'@inbound.example.com","from":"qa@example.com"}'` | 503 `{"error":"Inbound email handler not configured"}` (§4 tests it with the secret set). |
| 9 | An approval's AI summary written by a user (needs `$APPROVAL_A`, E2E-SEC-01): `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X PATCH "$API/approvals/$APPROVAL_A/summary" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"aiSummary":"forged"}'` | 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}`: only the agents service may write it, not even an admin (TC-SEC-04). |
| 10 | Metrics: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$API/metrics"` | 404 `{"detail":"Not found"}` while `METRICS_TOKEN` isn't set; with it set, 401 `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}` without `Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>` (TC-OPS-03). |

Command A:
```bash
V=$(curl -s "$API/contracts/$C_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_A" | jq -r .currentVersionId)
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/contracts/$C_A/versions/$V/chunk"
```

**Also check**
- Logs and error reports never carry signing, portal or invite tokens, bearer tokens or credential query parameters (TC-OPS-04).
- AI provider keys an admin stores show only their prefix, and personal data is masked before every model call (§7).

**Known limits**
- The full webhook signing secret is readable by every admin and every `admin`-scope key; there is no rotation.
- Production Gotenberg (the PDF renderer) answers without authentication on Cloud Run; making it private is deferred (docs/38 "Not covered here", X11).

### E2E-WEB-04 · A contact-form enquiry is validated, saved, emailed to the sales inbox and rate-limited

**Covers:** marketing `/contact` · `POST /marketing/contact` · `GET /marketing/contact/health` · TC-WEB-02, TC-SITE-02 (P1)
**Roles:** anonymous visitor · **Needs:** Mailpit; `MARKETING_CONTACT_EMAIL=sales@example.test` in the repo-root `.env` (it isn't in `.env.example`) and the API restarted with SMTP to Mailpit (§0); database access (step 6) · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- `$MKT` served by the dev server: its `/api` proxy goes to your local API, so the form posts locally.
- The API accepts 5 submissions per hour per client address, valid or not. The steps below use them in order; to rerun, wait an hour. (The dev server's proxy may reach the API from `127.0.0.1` while curl uses `::1`; then each has its own count.)

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s "$API/marketing/contact/health"`, then `curl -s "$MKT/api/v1/marketing/contact/health"`. | `{"ok":true}` both times; the second went through the dev server's proxy. |
| 2 | Open `$MKT/contact`. | Tab "Contact \| Draft Legal". Eyebrow "Contact", heading "Tell us about your contracts.", a line with the link **start free** (→ `https://app.draft-legal.com/register`). Three contacts: **Email** `aniket.tatipamula@gmail.com` (a mailto link); **Book a 30-min demo** with "Email us to pick a time"; **Open source questions** with "GitHub Discussions" (→ the repo's `/discussions`). The form: **Your name** (placeholder "Maya Chen"), **Work email** ("maya@vertex.cloud"), **Company** ("Vertex Cloud"), **What brings you here?**, **Send message**, and "We use this only to respond to you. No marketing emails without consent." No sticky bar here. |
| 3 | Click **Send message** with the form empty; then with a name and `not-an-email`. | The browser's own required-field and email-format prompts; nothing is sent. |
| 4 | DevTools → Network. **Your name** `QA Form`, **Work email** `qa-form@example.test`, **Company** `QA Co`, **What brings you here?** `Trying the contact form locally, please ignore.` → **Send message**. | The button reads "Sending…", then the form becomes a tick with "Thanks — we've got your message." and "We'll reply by email. In the meantime, the full product is on GitHub if you want to look around." The request was `POST http://localhost:5174/api/v1/marketing/contact` → 201 `{"ok":true,"id":"…","createdAt":"…"}`; nothing went to `draftlegal-prod-13353.web.app`. |
| 5 | Mailpit. | One email to `sales@example.test`, subject "New contact: QA Form (QA Co)", body "QA Form <qa-form@example.test>, QA Co", "Source: contact", the message, and "(submission <id>)". |
| 6 | Where it's stored: `docker exec -it clm_postgres psql -U clm -d clm_dev -c "SELECT id, name, email, company, source, ip FROM marketing_contacts ORDER BY \"createdAt\" DESC LIMIT 3;"` | A row with the submitted values and `source` "contact". The API log has "[marketing] new contact submission". The app has no screen for enquiries. |
| 7 | Open `$MKT/contact?source=security_pack`. Fill name and email, type `hi` in **What brings you here?** → **Send message**. | Above the fields, the chip "Source: security pack". The request answers 400 and a red box says "Invalid form data" (the body names the field: `{"error":"Invalid form data","details":{"message":["message is too short"]}}`). |
| 8 | Write a longer message (5+ characters) and send. | The success state. Mailpit's email says "Source: security_pack"; the row's `source` is `security_pack`. |
| 9 | The old email-capture body: command A, line 1. | 400 `{"error":"Invalid form data","details":{"name":["Required"],"message":["Required"]}}`; no row, no email. |
| 10 | Command A, line 2, repeated until it answers 429. | 201 until the address's fifth submission this hour, then 429; no row or email for the refused ones. From the form, a 429 shows "Too many submissions from this network. Try again in an hour, or email aniket.tatipamula@gmail.com directly." |
| 11 | DevTools → Network → **Offline** (or block `*marketing/contact*`); submit the form. | A red box (`data-testid="contact-form-error"`): "Could not reach our server. Check your connection or email aniket.tatipamula@gmail.com directly." Never the success state. |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/marketing/contact" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"lead@example.test","source":"template_nda"}'
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/marketing/contact" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"QA Tester","email":"qa@example.test","company":"QA Co","message":"Interested in a demo, please.","source":"contact"}'
```

**Also check**
- Without `MARKETING_CONTACT_EMAIL` an enquiry is still saved (201), nobody is emailed, and the API logs "[marketing] contact saved but nobody notified — set MARKETING_CONTACT_EMAIL and an email provider".
- A server error shows "Something went wrong on our side. Please try again, or email aniket.tatipamula@gmail.com directly.".
- Other `source` values the site sends, each shown as a chip: `commercial_license` (Open Source page), `compare_correction` and `migrate_<slug>` (comparison pages), `industry_<slug>` (industry pages).
- `VITE_API_ORIGIN` overrides where the form posts, and a production build posts to `https://draftlegal-prod-13353.web.app/api/v1/marketing/contact` (TC-WEB-02 P6, N6). Never submit the live site's form without the owner's OK: it files a real enquiry.
- API validation: an invalid email → `details.email` ["valid work email is required"]; a message over 5,000 characters, a name over 200 → 400.

**Known limits**
- There is no screen in the app to read enquiries: they are in the `marketing_contacts` table and the notification email.
- A short or missing message is reported only as "Invalid form data"; the form doesn't say which field.
- The stored `ip` is read from the `X-Forwarded-For` header as the client sent it, so it can be faked (the rate limit uses the address resolved through the trusted proxy, which a client can't choose).

### E2E-PROD-01 · The CI smoke scripts pass against a local stack

**Covers:** `scripts/smoke-prod.mjs`, `scripts/smoke-ui.mjs` · `/login`, `/dashboard`, `/contracts`, `/contracts/:id` · the API routes the API smoke calls (sign-in, dashboard, lists, chat, upload, comments, `/health`) · TC-SMK-01 to TC-SMK-07 (the manual smoke)
**Roles:** admin-a · **Needs:** agents service + model key; Playwright's Chromium · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
- The whole local stack running (web, API, agents service with a model key).
- Chromium for Playwright, once: `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`.
- Both scripts sign in as admin@demo.com, which signs that user out of any browser tab (§0); use another user in the browser meanwhile.
- admin-a has passed the setup wizard once (§0.4, **Skip setup**); otherwise the wizard covers the pages the UI smoke opens.
- They change data (see Known limits): run them on your own stack only.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Command A (the API smoke). | "Smoke test against http://localhost:5173", then sections "▶ 1. Authentication" to "▶ 9. Service health probes", one ✓, ✗ or – line per check. It ends "Smoke results: N pass / 0 fail / M skipped" and exits 0 (`echo $?`). |
| 2 | Read these lines. | ▶ 1: "POST /auth/login returns 200 + accessToken" and "user payload returned (orgId=…, roles=ADMIN)". ▶ 3 "List endpoints": contracts, counterparties, templates, clauses, matters. ▶ 4 "Search": "– GET /search route · 404 (route may not be mounted with this name)" (always; see Known limits). ▶ 5: "chat streamed tokens"; the line "chat used Google Gemini (expected)" appears only with a Google key. ▶ 7: either a pending contract's analysis reaches DONE, or "– pipeline trigger · no PENDING contract found — all already processed". ▶ 7.9: 19 reads. ▶ 8: "front-end HTML served (200, root div present)" and "Firebase Hosting /api/** proxy → Cloud Run api-service OK" (locally the Vite proxy). ▶ 9: "api-service /health · db=…ms redis=…ms". |
| 3 | Command B (the UI smoke; add `HEADLESS=false` to watch it). | "UI smoke against http://localhost:5173"; ▶ 1 "login form rendered (email + password inputs visible)" and "login submit · landed on /dashboard"; ▶ 2 "dashboard has numeric content (KPI tiles populated)"; ▶ 3 "contracts list shows seeded rows"; ▶ 4 "(clicked anchor: /contracts/<id>)", "navigated to /contracts/:id", "contract detail page renders panels · found: …"; ▶ 5 "Assistant streamed a visible response"; ▶ 6 "no uncaught console errors". It ends "UI smoke: N pass / 0 fail" and "Screenshots in: …/scripts/screenshots/smoke-ui". |
| 4 | Open `scripts/screenshots/smoke-ui/06-assistant-empty.png` and `07-assistant-after-send.png`. | Both show the app's "This page doesn't exist" page for `/assistant` (the Assistant page is `/agent`), with the side Assistant rail open on the right; the message went to the rail's box. Read the rail in `07-…`: ▶ 5 passes whether or not a reply arrived (see Known limits). |
| 5 | Command A with a wrong `ADMIN_PASSWORD`; then command B with it. | API smoke: "✗ POST /auth/login · status=401 …", "Cannot continue without a valid token. Aborting.", exit code 1. UI smoke: "✗ login submit · still on /login after submit", exit code 1. |

Command A:
```bash
API_URL=http://localhost:5173 API_DIRECT=http://localhost:3001 ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@demo.com ADMIN_PASSWORD='<password>' node scripts/smoke-prod.mjs
```
Command B:
```bash
APP_URL=http://localhost:5173 ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@demo.com ADMIN_PASSWORD='<password>' node scripts/smoke-ui.mjs
```

**Also check**
- Always set `API_DIRECT` locally: without it the last check calls the production API's `/health`.
- In CI (E2E-PROD-02) the same scripts run against `https://draftlegal-prod-13353.web.app` as "API smoke (~60s, 49 checks)" and "UI smoke (~25s, real Chromium)", signed in as the smoke admin from the repository's secrets. A failed UI smoke uploads the screenshots as the artifact `ui-smoke-screenshots-<run id>`.

**Known limits**
- The API smoke writes: it adds a comment "Smoke test comment <number>" to the first listed contract (it stays), uploads a contract "Smoke <time>", renames it "Smoke renamed <number>" and deletes it (a soft delete), may start the analysis of a pending contract, and runs two Assistant chat turns (model cost).
- Its "Search" check calls `GET /search`, which doesn't exist (search is `POST /search`), so it is always skipped. The "PDF generation reachable" check its header lists doesn't exist either.
- The UI smoke's Assistant check opens `/assistant`, which the app doesn't have, types into the last text box it finds (the side rail's, at its 1440 px width), and passes whenever the page has more than 200 characters of text: it can't fail on a missing reply.
- The API smoke's "agent tool callback" check reports a failure if the model's answer merely contains the word "database".
- Its section 7.10 prints as "▶ 7.1. Comments add → list round-trip" (a number, not a label).
- Both scripts default to production URLs and `password123`; always pass the variables.

### E2E-PROD-02 · After a deploy, the run records what was serving, deploys, passes both smokes and skips the rollback

**Covers:** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (jobs "Deploy gotenberg + agents + api + web", "Production smoke (API + UI)", "Auto-rollback (smoke failed)"; the step "Record what is serving now") · `scripts/deploy.sh` · TC-DEPLOY-01, TC-DEPLOY-02, TC-DEPLOY-03
**Roles:** an operator with read access to the repository's Actions runs (step 7: Cloud Run Viewer on the production project) · **Needs:** `gh` signed in, or the GitHub web UI · **Time:** ~15 min per deploy

**Preconditions**
- A push to `main` started **Deploy to production** (or someone ran it by hand). Read-only: nothing here changes production.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | GitHub → **Actions** → **Deploy to production** (or `gh run list --workflow deploy.yml --limit 5`); open the newest run. | Three jobs: "Deploy gotenberg + agents + api + web", "Production smoke (API + UI)", "Auto-rollback (smoke failed)". On a good deploy the first two are green and the third is skipped. |
| 2 | First job → step **Record what is serving now** (or `gh run view <run id> --log`, and look at that step's lines). | After the script, four lines: `api-service: api-service-000NN-xxx`, `agents-service: agents-service-000NN-xxx`, `gotenberg: gotenberg-000NN-xxx`, and `web app: Hosting version <id>`: what was serving before this deploy, which a rollback returns to. The version is a bare id, never `sites/…/versions/…`. A service with nothing serving reads `<service>: nothing serving`. If the web release can't be read, the line is the warning "Could not read the web app's live Hosting release, so a rollback of this deploy won't restore the web app." and the deploy goes on. |
| 3 | Step **Deploy all services**: find `--- prisma migrate deploy ---`. | Either Prisma's output, or "⚠  could not read the database-url secret from this runner. …" followed by "   → continuing deploy; migrations not auto-applied this run.". In the second case, if the release adds a folder under `apps/api/prisma/migrations` (`git diff --name-only <commit production ran> <this commit> -- apps/api/prisma/migrations`), tell the owner: the migrations must be applied by hand, or requests that need them will fail. |
| 4 | Same step, each service. | For gotenberg, agents-service and api-service: "Service [<service>] revision [<revision>] has been deployed and is serving 100 percent of traffic." followed by a traffic update of the same service to its latest revision, with no error. Then "--- deploy worker-service (always-on BullMQ workers) ---" (verify whether it deployed; if not, the line "⚠  worker-service deploy failed — continuing; the API still runs workers in-process." and the run goes on), "--- build + deploy web app (Firebase Hosting target=app) ---", "--- build + deploy marketing site (Firebase Hosting target=marketing) ---", each with Firebase's "Deploy complete!", and "Done.". |
| 5 | Job "Production smoke (API + UI)". | "API smoke (~60s, 49 checks)" ends "Smoke results: N pass / 0 fail / M skipped"; "UI smoke (~25s, real Chromium)" ends "UI smoke: N pass / 0 fail" (what they check: E2E-PROD-01). |
| 6 | Job "Auto-rollback (smoke failed)". | Skipped. If it ran, check TC-DEPLOY-03 on this run: the summary "⛔ Auto-rollback executed" lists step 2's revisions and web version. |
| 7 | Optional, with Cloud Run Viewer: `gcloud run services describe <service> --project <production project> --region us-central1 --format='value(status.traffic)'` for api-service, agents-service and gotenberg. | The entry with 100 percent has `latestRevision` true and is the revision step 4 deployed (TC-DEPLOY-02). |
| 8 | The next deploy's step **Record what is serving now**. | It names the revisions this run deployed: the "before" lines of successive runs are the deploy history. |

**Also check**
- A run started by hand with **skip-smoke** or **skip-rollback** ticked skips the smoke or the rollback (TC-DEPLOY-03 N2); a deploy job that fails by itself is not rolled back (N1).
- Deploys never overlap: a second push waits for the running one.
- Traffic changes and the manual rollback (TC-DEPLOY-03 P9–P11) need deploy rights and the owner's OK.

**Known limits**
- CI can't read the database secret, so migrations are not applied by the deploy; they are a manual step before code that needs them goes live.
- The step hides the production project id from its outputs as a secret, but the id is in the repository (`.firebaserc`, `env.api.yaml`, the smoke scripts' defaults, the marketing site's form address).

### E2E-PROD-03 · The hosted API is healthy, strict and serving the new build (read-only checks)

**Covers:** production `GET /marketing/contact/health` · the API's `/api/health`, `/health`, `/health/ready`, `/health/live` · the agents service's `/health` · the route-marker check (FIX_TRACKER FF3) · TC-DEPLOY-01, TC-SEC-03 (N6)
**Roles:** anonymous · **Needs:** internet · **Time:** ~10 min

**Preconditions**
```bash
PROD_APP=https://app.draft-legal.com                                  # the web app; /api/** goes to api-service
PROD_API_DIRECT=https://api-service-611770954192.us-central1.run.app
PROD_AGENTS=https://agents-service-611770954192.us-central1.run.app
```
- The services scale to zero: the first call after a quiet spell can take 5–10 s.
- Every check is a GET, a refused call, or one failed sign-in. Don't create, change or submit anything on production.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | `curl -s "$PROD_APP/api/health"` | 200 `{"status":"ok","checks":{"database":"ok","redis":"ok"},"timestamp":"…"}`. |
| 2 | `curl -s "$PROD_API_DIRECT/health"`, then `…/health/ready` and `…/health/live`. | `/health`: `status` "ok", both checks "ok", `latencyMs`, `uptime`, and `versions` `{"node":"v22…","env":"production","commit":"unknown"}`. `/health/ready`: `status` "ready". `/health/live`: `{"status":"ok","service":"clm-api",…}`. `commit` always reads "unknown" (the deploy doesn't set it): use step 5 to tell which build is live. |
| 3 | `curl -s "$PROD_AGENTS/health"`; then `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$PROD_AGENTS/agent/chat"` | `{"status":"ok","replayMode":null}` (never "replay" or "record" in production); the chat call without the service secret → 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}`. |
| 4 | `curl -sI "$PROD_APP/api/health"` and read `x-ratelimit-limit`. | `1000` (development says 10000): production runs strict (E2E-SEC-07). The API's security headers (E2E-SEC-06 step 1) are there too. |
| 5 | Which API build is live (the route marker): find a route the new build adds (command A) and call it with no credentials. | A route the live build has answers 401 (its auth check runs); a route it doesn't have answers 404 `{"message":"Route <METHOD>:<path> not found","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404}`. 401 = the new build is live; 404 = the old one still is. For the release that added `invoice_list` (FIX_TRACKER GG3): `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$PROD_APP/api/internal/ai/tools/invoice_list"` prints `{"detail":"Internal endpoint — bad secret"} 401` once it is live. |
| 6 | The control: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$PROD_APP/api/v1/qa-no-such-route"` | 404 with "Route GET:/api/v1/qa-no-such-route not found". |
| 7 | `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' "$PROD_APP/api/v1/metrics"` | 404 `{"detail":"Not found"}` (no `METRICS_TOKEN`) or 401 `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}`; never the metrics. |
| 8 | The marketing form's endpoint: `curl -s "https://draftlegal-prod-13353.web.app/api/v1/marketing/contact/health"`, then command B (a CORS preflight from the site's origin). | `{"ok":true}`. The preflight answers 204 with `access-control-allow-origin: https://draft-legal.com` and `access-control-allow-methods` including POST. (Don't submit the form: it files a real enquiry.) |
| 9 | Once only (each failure counts toward that email's 10 tries per 15 minutes): command C. | 401 `{"detail":"Invalid email or password"}`: the demo admin doesn't use the development password. If it answers 200, stop and tell the owner (TC-SEC-03 N6). |
| 10 | Which web build is live, without cloud access: command D. | The `index-<hash>.js` name changes with every web build. If the release changed a string in `apps/web/src`, grep the bundle for it: found = the new web app is live. With Firebase Hosting Viewer, TC-DEPLOY-01 commands J and K give the live release id. |

Command A (routes a range of commits adds; `<live>` = the commit production ran, `<new>` = the one deployed):
```bash
git diff <live> <new> -- apps/api/src/routes | grep -E "^\+\s*app\.(get|post|put|patch|delete)\('"
```
A route in `apps/api/src/routes/<file>.ts` is served under the prefix `apps/api/src/app.ts` gives that file (for example `/api/v1/contracts`, `/api/internal/ai`). Call it through `$PROD_APP` with no `Authorization` header; prefer a GET, or a POST with no body.

Command B:
```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X OPTIONS "https://draftlegal-prod-13353.web.app/api/v1/marketing/contact" \
  -H 'Origin: https://draft-legal.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type'
```
Command C:
```bash
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -X POST "$PROD_APP/api/v1/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@demo.com","password":"password123"}'
```
Command D:
```bash
curl -s "$PROD_APP/" | grep -o '/assets/index-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.js'
curl -s "$PROD_APP/assets/index-<hash>.js" | grep -c '<a string the release added>'
```

**Also check**
- `curl -sI "$PROD_APP/"`: `x-frame-options: DENY`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`, so a reload always gets the new release.
- `$PROD_APP/status` shows "System Status" / "Status page not bundled in this build.": there is no live status page.
- Trying a new revision before it takes traffic (the `candidate` tag FF3 used) changes traffic settings: only with the owner's yes.

**Known limits**
- `/health` can't say which commit is live; use the route marker, the Cloud Run revision (E2E-PROD-02 step 7), or a string in the web bundle.
- A route marker exists only for a release that adds an API route.

### E2E-PROD-04 · A test account signs in on the hosted demo and every main page loads

**Covers:** hosted `/login`, `/dashboard`, `/agent`, `/matters`, `/contracts`, `/contracts/:id`, `/requests`, `/counterparties`, `/approvals`, `/signatures`, `/review-queue`, `/obligations`, `/renewals`, `/invoices`, `/templates`, `/clauses`, `/playbook`, `/analytics`, `/diligence`, `/profile`, `/settings`, and the Admin pages including `/admin/integrations` · `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/logout`, `POST /telemetry/events`
**Roles:** the QA test account on production, from the owner · **Needs:** that account; a browser with DevTools · **Time:** ~15 min

**Preconditions**
- A test account the owner gave you for the hosted demo. Never the CI smoke admin (signing it in elsewhere ends its session), and don't register a new one without the owner's OK.
- Look, don't change: no uploads, edits, sends, approvals or Assistant messages on production unless the owner asks.

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Open `https://app.draft-legal.com`. | `/login` with "Welcome back — please enter your details." and the sign-in form. The first load after a quiet spell can take several seconds. |
| 2 | Sign in. | `/dashboard` with its figures; `POST /api/v1/auth/login` answered 200. |
| 3 | Open each sidebar page: Dashboard, Assistant, Matters, Contracts, Requests, Counterparties, Approvals, Signatures, Extraction Queue, Obligations, Renewals, Invoices, Templates, Clauses, Playbook, Analytics, Diligence. | Each shows its heading and its data or empty state; none shows "This page doesn't exist" or an error toast; no API call answers 5xx. |
| 4 | Open a contract from Contracts; look at the rail and tabs without editing. | The page loads with its panels. The header's collaboration badge reads "Connecting…" or "Offline", and the console shows a failed WebSocket to `ws://localhost:3030` (see Known limits). |
| 5 | User menu (initials, top right) → **Profile**, then **Settings**. If the account is an admin: Admin → Users, Roles, Organization, Integrations, Skills, Team. | Each loads. Integrations shows its four tabs for an admin, "Admin access required" otherwise. |
| 6 | The console on each page. | No red errors other than step 4's WebSocket. |
| 7 | User menu → **Sign out**; then open `https://app.draft-legal.com/dashboard`. | `/login`, both times. |

**Also check**
- The build you see is the one just deployed (E2E-PROD-03 steps 5 and 10).
- Telemetry: with DevTools → Network open, open a contract. Within a few seconds the hosted app sends `POST /api/v1/telemetry/events` (a beacon), answered 202 `{"accepted":<n>}`. Locally the app only logs `[telemetry]` lines to the console (§1).

**Known limits**
- Every contract page on the hosted demo tries to open a collaboration WebSocket to `ws://localhost:3030` on the visitor's own computer (no collaboration server address is set for production builds), so its badge never connects.

### E2E-PROD-05 · The live marketing site serves the new build, its sitemap and working links

**Covers:** `https://draft-legal.com` (every page of the marketing site, live) · `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` · TC-SITE-01, TC-SITE-02, TC-SITE-03
**Roles:** anonymous · **Needs:** internet · **Time:** ~10 min

**Steps**

| # | Do | Expect |
|---|----|--------|
| 1 | Command A, line 1. | The same meta description as E2E-WEB-01 step 1. |
| 2 | Command A, lines 2–3 (the sitemap). | `42`, and one `<lastmod>` date: the day (UTC) the site was last built and deployed. A deploy today shows today's date. |
| 3 | `curl -s https://draft-legal.com/robots.txt` | As E2E-WEB-09 step 7. |
| 4 | In a browser open `https://draft-legal.com/`, `/product#negotiate`, `/security`, `/contact`, one comparison page and one industry page. | They render as in E2E-WEB-01 to E2E-WEB-06; `/product#negotiate` lands on Stage 3; the comparison page shows "Last checked: May 2026. …"; images load; no console errors. |
| 5 | The links on the live site: E2E-WEB-09 steps 3–6. | Footer **Privacy** / **Terms** → `https://app.draft-legal.com/privacy` and `/terms`; the demo link is the mailto; no X, LinkedIn or Cal.com; the only footer icon is GitHub. |
| 6 | `https://draft-legal.com/no-such-page` | The site's 404 "That page got redlined out.". |
| 7 | `curl -sI https://draft-legal.com/` and `curl -sI https://draft-legal.com/sitemap.xml` | `x-content-type-options: nosniff` and `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; the page has `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`, the sitemap `cache-control: public, max-age=3600`. |
| 8 | `https://www.draft-legal.com/` | verify: it serves the site or redirects to `https://draft-legal.com/` (the API accepts both as origins for the contact form). |

Command A:
```bash
curl -s https://draft-legal.com/ | grep -A1 'name="description"'
curl -s https://draft-legal.com/sitemap.xml | grep -c '<loc>'
curl -s https://draft-legal.com/sitemap.xml | grep '<lastmod>' | sort -u
```

**Also check**
- Never submit the live contact form without the owner's OK: it files a real enquiry.
- A rollback never touches the marketing site (TC-DEPLOY-03 P7).

**Known limits**
- verify with the owner: `MARKETING_CONTACT_EMAIL` is not in the tracked `env.api.yaml` the deploy uses, so production enquiries may be saved with nobody emailed.

| 5 | E2E-NOTIF-03 | With the daily digest, approval emails wait and arrive together at 9am local time | | | |
| 5 | E2E-NOTIF-04 | Slack requests are checked by their signature, `/contract` search answers, and approval buttons fall back safely (no Slack workspace needed) | | | |
| 5 | E2E-NOTIF-05 | With a real Slack app, an approval request posts a card whose Approve and Reject buttons decide the step | | | |
| 5 | E2E-NOTIF-06 | Teams channels (and any webhook) get approval and signing events as Adaptive Cards | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-01 | Obligations are extracted from an executed contract and listed on its page | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-02 | The obligations extractor reads only the first 16,000 characters and returns at most 25 obligations | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-03 | An obligation is completed with a note and evidence, the evidence downloads, and it can be reopened | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-04 | The Obligations page shows every status in the right tab, with true counts, search, the drawer and CSV export | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-05 | The contract owner gets a reminder a week before an obligation falls due, from the daily scan or a manual run | | | |
| 6 | E2E-OBL-06 | The Assistant lists a contract's obligations with obligations_list | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-01 | The Renewals page lists executed contracts by month, the lapsed ones first, with auto-renewal and the notice deadline | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-02 | The daily renewal scan alerts the owner on expiry or on the notice deadline, once a week, until a decision is logged | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-03 | A signed amendment's notice period moves the deadline and is named in notice.setBy; an amendment is never a renewal of its own | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-04 | Renewal advice and a renewal decision are recorded from the contract page and shown on the Renewals page | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-05 | The renewals CSV export | | | |
| 6 | E2E-REN-06 | The Assistant answers renewal questions with renewal_advice | | | |
| 6 | E2E-INV-01 | An invoice entered by hand matches a payment obligation by vendor, date and currency, with the amount checked against the contract total | | | |
| 6 | E2E-INV-02 | Invoices move through Pending, Matched and Reconciled; reconciling closes the obligation, and the totals follow | | | |
| 6 | E2E-INV-03 | A dispute is filed with a reason, and a disputed invoice leaves the working queue | | | |
| 6 | E2E-INV-04 | The Assistant reports what a vendor billed with invoice_list | | | |
| 6 | E2E-DIL-01 | A diligence room is created and filled in batches of at most 50 files | | | |
| 6 | E2E-DIL-02 | The room's comparison table and CSV export show each document's extracted terms | | | |
| 6 | E2E-DIL-03 | Room documents stay out of the org's own search, renewals, obligations and figures | | | |
| 6 | E2E-DIL-04 | A room is renamed, archived and deleted (API only), taking its documents with it | | | |
| 6 | E2E-ANL-01 | Every card and chart on the Analytics page counts what its label says | | | |
| 6 | E2E-ANL-02 | A sales rep's analytics and post-signature pages count only their own contracts | | | |
| 6 | E2E-ANL-03 | Every CSV export in the product downloads the rows its page promises | | | |

| 6 | E2E-CMP-02 | The compliance package PDF carries the cover, the signatures, an audit trail checked against the hash chain, and the contract document | | | |

| 7 | E2E-AI-01 | The Ask panel is on every page, knows which contract you are on, and keeps its threads | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-02 | The composer's "/" actions, "@" mentions, Stop and follow-ups work from the panel | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-03 | The full-page Assistant keeps conversations you can search, reopen and delete, and shows who answered | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-04 | Answers about one contract come from its own text, name the section, and cite it on request | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-05 | Portfolio answers state the true total, say when a list is partial or a sample, and read dates, values and prices from the data | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-06 | Directory questions (counterparties, matters, requests, fields, templates, people, the org's positions) get real answers or a plain "none" | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-07 | A change the assistant proposes happens only after Apply, and a reversible one can be undone for 15 minutes | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-08 | Approvals from chat: routing is undoable, deciding is not, and nobody can decide a step that isn't theirs | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-09 | Redlines and new drafts from chat are proposals first, become a version or a contract only on Apply, and undo cleanly | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-10 | The assistant says when it found nothing, flags ids nobody gave it, keeps to its budget, and warns when a document talks to the AI | | | |

| 7 | E2E-AI-13 | Each role gets only the tools it may use, sees only what it may see, and can't reach another user's or org's threads | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-14 | The editor's AI (Draft new, the selection popover, the toolbar, Doc AI, ghost text and margin badges) suggests and changes nothing until you accept | | | |
| 7 | E2E-AI-15 | Asking a question about one contract (Q&A) answers from its clauses, with sources, and degrades honestly | | | |

| 8 | E2E-INT-10 | Teams: events arrive as Adaptive Cards through a Teams workflow webhook | | | |

| 8 | E2E-SEC-02 | A sales rep (own scope) sees and counts only their own contracts and requests | | | |
| 8 | E2E-SEC-03 | Sessions expire and rotate: stale or signed-out tokens are refused, and the app recovers cleanly | | | |

## Appendix A. Sample documents

Make each document once (§0.7). Replace the `<…>` dates relative to the day you test.
- `<START>` is 10 months before today.
- `<END>` is 75 days after today. That puts renewal and notice deadlines inside the windows the product watches.

The companies are fictional. The personal data in A.2 uses well-known example values, not a real person's: an
example SSN, the standard Visa test card, and the IBAN example from the IBAN standard. Never use real personal data.

>

>

>    least reasonable care, and disclose it only to employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by
>    similar duties.

## Appendix B. Bug report template

```
Title:        <what is wrong, in one line>
Journey:      E2E-<AREA>-NN, step <n>        (and any TC-… case it matches)
Environment:  local <git commit> | hosted demo <date/time>;  browser + version
Account:      <admin-a | counsel-a | …>  in Org A | Org B
Steps:        1. …  2. …  3. …
Expected:     <the plan's expected result, quoted>
Actual:       <what happened; exact message / HTTP status / screenshot>
Evidence:     screenshot; browser console errors; the failing request (DevTools → Network → Copy as cURL, token removed);
              API log lines around the time (from the `pnpm dev` terminal)
Severity:     P1 security / data loss / cross-organization / feature unusable
              P2 feature partly broken or wrong result
              P3 minor, wording, layout
Repeatable:   always | sometimes (n of m) | once
```

## Appendix C. Known issues found while writing this plan (30 Sep 2026)

Writing the journeys meant reading every screen and route, and that turned up defects. Each is marked in the journey
where it shows, as **Open bug** or **Known issue**, with what you'll see. Check that it still happens rather than filing
it again. The most important are listed here.

- **Verified** means checked against the code or with a test while this plan was written.
- **Reported** means found by reading the code. Confirm it on your first run.

### Verified

| Issue | Where | Journey |
|---|---|---|
| The contract page's approval history never loads. It calls `GET /approvals?contractId=…`, a route that doesn't exist. The Approval tab shows no steps, comments or rejection reason, and the rail says "Not yet submitted for approval." | Contract page | E2E-APPR-05, E2E-APPR-06 |
| Any organization's admin can edit the built-in skills that every organization shares (`PATCH /skills/:id` accepts `orgId: null` rows). On the hosted, multi-organization service, one customer changes another's prompts. | Admin → Skills | E2E-SKL-03 |
| The API's rate-limit bypass for the agents service doesn't exist. `@fastify/rate-limit` 9.1.0 has no `skip` option, so in production the agents service counts against the per-IP limit. | API | E2E-SEC-06 |
| Invites send no email. The link is shown once, in a banner, and can't be sent again; re-inviting the same email answers 409. | Admin → Users | E2E-ADM-01 |
| The app's Privacy and Terms pages are placeholders ("Privacy policy content not bundled in this build."), and the marketing site's footer links to them. | `/privacy`, `/terms` | E2E-WS-06, E2E-WEB-01 |
| Every contract page on the hosted app tries `ws://localhost:3030` with an empty token for live editing. `collab.ts` reads a token key the app never writes, and production sets no `VITE_COLLAB_URL`. | Contract page | E2E-SEC-06 |
| The UI smoke test checks the Assistant at `/assistant`, which isn't a route, so that check can't fail. | `scripts/smoke-ui.mjs` | E2E-PROD-01 |
| The Renewals page's cards and CSV counted an amendment as a renewal of its own. | Renewals | Fixed on this branch (GG4); E2E-REN-03, E2E-REN-05 |

### Reported

| Issue | Journey |
|---|---|
| An admin can't reset a forgotten password. "Forgot password?" tells admins to send a temporary password, but no screen or route does that. | E2E-ACC-04 |
| "Save Profile" drops the user's roles from the session until they sign in again, so the Admin menu disappears and writes are refused. | E2E-ACC-05 |
| A deactivated user keeps access for up to 15 minutes (the access token isn't checked against the user's status). | E2E-ADM-04, E2E-SEC-04 |
| Emails are case-sensitive at sign-in and registration: `Admin@Demo.com` can't sign in. | E2E-ACC-01 |
| A failed re-extraction of obligations deletes the contract's open obligations first. A model error then leaves none. | E2E-OBL-01 |
| No CSV export neutralises cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` (spreadsheet formula injection). | E2E-ANL-03, E2E-REPO-03 |
| Contracts and requests the Assistant creates never finish processing: they show "Processing starting…" or "Classifying" indefinitely. | E2E-DRAFT-04, E2E-REQ-04 |
| A request converted to a contract has no current version, so Send for Signature refuses it. | E2E-REQ-03 |
| The chat may use the platform's provider instead of the organization's own model routing when keys for two providers exist. | E2E-AIADM-01 |
| A new version made while a contract is out for signature may make its seal fail on every retry. | E2E-SIGN-09 |
| The "Message (optional)" in Send for review is discarded, and approval decisions are never emailed. | E2E-APPR-01, E2E-NOTIF-01 |
| The counterparty portal's Comments tab never lists any comment, and portal comments notify no one. | E2E-PORT-02 |
| Governing-law clauses are checked against the anti-bribery ("Compliance with Laws") playbook positions. | E2E-REV-03 |
| Webhook retries create new delivery rows with a new delivery id each time, so receivers can't spot duplicates. | E2E-INT-08 |
| `MARKETING_CONTACT_EMAIL` is missing from the deploy's environment, so enquiries may be saved without anyone being emailed. Check with the owner. | E2E-WEB-04 |
| The seeded "Wayne Enterprises — Partnership Agreement" is stuck in Approval with no approval behind it. | E2E-APPR-10 |
